author: thetriumphantfox
body:
Every region already scatters a signature open-ground landmark into its clearings (mossy boulder, sandstone obelisk, ice/cloud/storm/obsidian spire, standing stone, shadow monolith, tombstone, light pillar, driftwood), but only the mana forest's landmark — the colossal trees — was drawn as a big multi-tile overlay. The rest rendered at a single tile. This makes the other regions match: each landmark is now blown up ~3× about its foot into a multi-tile giant that overhangs the clearing, the elemental/non-forest answer to the colossal trees.

## How it works

The landmarks are placed on a tile whose whole 8-neighbourhood is open ground (`addRegionLandmarks` / `addTombstones` / `addLightPillars`), so drawing them oversized can't collide with walls. All the landmark art is vector canvas drawing parameterised by tile size, so it scales up crisply — no redrawn art.

- **`render-tiles.js`** — a `landmarkOverlayPass` flag lets `drawTileProcedural` split each landmark tile into two halves: the flat ground fill (normal tile pass) and the object art (overlay pass). New `drawBigLandmark()` re-issues the landmark's own art through `drawTileProcedural`, scaled ~3× about its foot, with the ground square suppressed so the giant sits on the real clearing floor. Same after-entities overlay treatment as `drawColossalTree`, so the hero and enemies pass *behind* the overhang.
- **`render.js`** — `BIG_LANDMARK_TILES` set + `mapBigLandmarkTiles()` (cached per map, sorted top-to-bottom for painter's order), and an overlay loop alongside the colossal-tree pass that draws each giant once its foot tile is unfogged.

The poison region's `FALLEN_LOG` is intentionally left alone — it's already a seamless multi-tile run and enlarging it per-tile would break its joins.

## Verification

Loaded a desert overworld in the preview, warped onto an obelisk, and sampled canvas pixels on a real rendered frame: the enlarged obelisk draws as continuous sandstone ~2.5 tiles tall (apex) from its foot, no console errors. `node --check` passes on both files.

---
Stacked on the render.js split (`render-tiles.js` only exists on that branch), so this PR is based on `claude/perf-collision-scans` and shows the landmark change alone.

## Summary

Adds a second real LLM provider (OpenAI) alongside Anthropic to demonstrate that the codebase depends only on the `LLMClient` protocol, not any single vendor SDK. ### Key changes:
- **OpenAI adapter** (`src/aih/llm/openai_adapter.py`): Implements `LLMClient` protocol for OpenAI Chat Completions API, with lazy SDK import and API key validation

body: ## Problem `apps/web/src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/messages/page.tsx` has two Supabase-driven promises in its load effect (the client-profile lookup and `resolveConversation()`) with no rejection handler. If either rejects (network blip, transient RLS/PostgREST error), it becomes an unhandled promise rejection and the page can get stuck without ever setting `client`/`conversationId`, with no error surfaced to the user. This is the exact same bug already fixed in the client-side counterpart page, `my-nutritionist/messages/page.tsx`, in #83 — that fix was never applied to this coach-side page. ## Fix Add rejection handlers to both `.then()` calls, matching the established pattern from #83: ```diff .single() - .then(({ data }) => { - if (!cancelled && data) setClient(data as UserProfile) - }) + .then( + ({ data }) => { + if (!cancelled && data) setClient(data as UserProfile) + }, + () => {} + ) ... -resolveConversation().then((cid) => { - if (!cancelled) setConversationId(cid) -}) +resolveConversation().then( + (cid) => { + if (!cancelled) setConversationId(cid) + }, + () => {} +) ``` No behavior change for the happy path; only the rejection path is now handled instead of throwing unhandled. ## Verification - `npm run lint -w apps/web` — passes (pre-existing `` warnings only, none in the changed file) - `npm run build -w apps/web` — passes, `/clients/[id]/messages` route compiles cleanly --- _Generated by Claude Code_ --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01GzTxSDNVFfeqqGMdCgFt1o)_

author: tedyoogrammarly
body:
## What

Replaces the Calendar page's OAuth-based Google Calendar connection with a **shareable-link** flow.

**Before:** create a Google Cloud OAuth Client ID → paste it → sign-in popup → grant `calendar.readonly` (tokens expire ~1h, silent re-auth).
**After:** make a calendar public in Google Calendar → copy its shareable link (`…?cid=…`) → paste it. Events read anonymously via Calendar API v3 using a shipped, HTTP-referrer-restricted API key (`window.GOOGLE_API_KEY` in `config.js`).

## Why it's safe / minimal
- **No new network grants** — `www.googleapis.com` was already in the CSP; `accounts.google.com` is now *dropped* (GIS removed).
- **No OAuth, no expiring tokens, no server proxy.**
- Preserves v4.72 features: `normalizeEvent` (week-grid times) and per-calendar **Work/Personal** category tagging + the Work/Personal/Family filter.
- Admin-only + read-only unchanged.

## Notes for the maintainer
- **Add your API key:** the repo ships `window.GOOGLE_API_KEY = ''` (integration stays dark until set). Create a referrer-restricted key in Google Cloud (enable Calendar API) and paste it into `config.js`. See `supabase/SETUP.md` §8.
- **Public calendars only** — a non-public link is rejected with guidance. Private calendars aren't supported (that needed the removed OAuth flow or a proxy).
- **Existing OAuth connection resets** on load (legacy config is cleared by `GoogleCalendar.migrate()`); re-add each calendar once via its shareable link. No stored events are lost (events were always fetched live).

## Verification
Headless Chrome: clean boot (no console/CSP errors), `parseCalendarLink` across `?cid=`/iCal/raw forms, `addCalendar('junk')→BAD_LINK`, empty-key modal (disabled + notice), and configured modal (calendars list, category selects, remove, add-another). `tools/test-parse-calendar-link.mjs` covers the parser.

author: jdrumgoole
body:
## What

Both servers now build dates from calendar components with **`$dateFromParts`**: `{$dateFromParts: {year, month, day, hour, minute, second, millisecond, timezone}}`.

Components default to month/day = 1 and time = 0, and out-of-range values **roll over** exactly as mongod does — month 13 → next January, month 0 → previous December, day 0 → last day of the previous month, hour 25 → next day, millisecond 1500 → +1.5 s. `year` is required (1–9999); a `timezone` interprets the components as local time (local→instant); any null component yields null.

## Validated against real MongoDB (three-way probe)

Semantics matched to **real `mongod` 6.0** via a three-way probe (mongod vs Rust server vs Python server): **all value cases match mongod exactly** — every rollover, integral-double parts, both tz-offset directions, null-propagation. The validation error paths (non-integral component → `40515`, missing `year` → `40516`, `year` out of 1–9999 → `40523`) match mongod on the **Python server**; the Rust server errors too but with a generic code (the documented cross-cutting `Fallback` gap, `tasks/backlog.md` §7.5).

## How

- `expressions.py` / `secantus-core`: `_op_date_from_parts` / `op_date_from_parts` — month-carry (`year*12 + month-1` → divmod) plus a day/time `timedelta` from the first of the month, so components roll over across month/year boundaries. The Python server also resolves **named IANA zones** via `zoneinfo`; the Rust server computes fixed-offset zones natively and defers named zones to the Python oracle (the local→instant direction is DST-ambiguous, as with `$dateFromString`). The ISO-week form (`isoWeekYear`/`isoWeek`/`isoDayOfWeek`) is not yet supported.
- Tests: +18 curated parity cases, a Rust unit test, a pymongo integration test.
- Versions: Python `0.5.4b190`, all Rust crates `0.5.3-beta.141`.

## Verification

- Three-way probe: all values match mongod; Python matches error codes.
- `./inv rust-gate` green; full Python suite **5021 passed, 4 skipped**.

This is **PR 1** of a phased rollout (see `.kiro/specs/unified-auth/`). It contains only the `skawr-auth` library changes — consuming services (analytics, indexer, marketplace) adopt these in follow-up PRs.

## What's included

### Schema (8 Alembic migrations, additive only)
- Extended `users` (subscription_tier, nullable password_hash)
- New `product_enrollments` (user ↔ product with roles)
- New `connected_stores` (Salla/Shopify OAuth data + legacy_client_id)
- Enhanced `user_sessions` (device, ip, product)
- Extended `api_keys` (user_id, product, resource_id, resource_type)
- Dormant future-ready tables: `organizations`, `organization_members`, `user_identity_providers`
- `subscription_tier_audit` (append-only tier change log)

### Backend logic
- **Dual-auth**: `detect_token_format()` + `verify_token_for_product()` handle unified, legacy_indexer, and legacy_analytics token formats simultaneously (90-day transition window)
- **Config standardization**: `SKAWR_AUTH_SECRET_KEY` with backward-compat aliases (`SECRET_KEY`, `JWT_SECRET_KEY`)
- **Sync + async** dependency factories (indexer uses sync SQLAlchemy, analytics uses async)
- **Role-based access**: `require_product_role()` with admin > member > viewer hierarchy
- **Resource resolver**: maps user UUID → connected stores / projects / API keys; resolves legacy `client_id` → user
- Services: enrollment, session management, guest account claim
- Internal subscription tier endpoint (for the upcoming Polar.sh payment integration)
- **Data migration scripts**: analytics users, SaaS APIClients, marketplace Supabase users (idempotent, batch-commit)

### Key generation CLI
```bash
python -m skawr_auth --env          # generates SKAWR_AUTH_SECRET_KEY + SKAWR_AUTH_STORE_ENCRYPTION_KEY
skawr-keygen --env | pbcopy         # if installed via pip
```

### Frontend (`@skawr/auth-frontend`)
- Extended `AuthClient` (product-aware login, `getEnrolledProducts()`, `hasProductAccess()`)
- `ProductSwitcher` component (accessible, role badges)
- `SharedLoginPage` component (login/signup tabs, error handling)
- New TypeScript types (ProductEnrollment, ConnectedStore, UserSession)

## Testing

94 unit tests, all passing:
- Token format detection (all 3 formats + invalid)
- `verify_token_for_product` (deadline enforcement, edge cases)
- Role hierarchy + `require_product_role`
- Session lifecycle (create, list, revoke, cleanup)
- Subscription endpoint (updates, audit, validation)

## Backward compatibility

- Old tokens (without `product_enrollments`) accepted for 90 days
- Existing factory API (`create_user_models`, `create_auth_router`, etc.) unchanged
- `@skawr/auth-frontend` public API preserved (AuthProvider, useAuth)
- Legacy env var names still resolve via priority chain

## Deployment notes

Before deploying, generate and set on the VPS (same value for **all** services):
```bash
SKAWR_AUTH_SECRET_KEY=<generated>
SKAWR_AUTH_STORE_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<generated>
```

## Follow-up PRs (not in this PR)
- PR 2: skawr-analytics adoption
- PR 3: skawr-search — Indexer dual-auth + dashboard
- PR 4: skawr-web — Unified auth frontend
- PR 5: Legacy token removal (day 91)

author: gamboiuwu
body:
## Summary

Adds a **Target Green Number** control — the IIDX **"float hi-speed"** workflow — to the Game Preview. Type the reaction window you want (in ms) in the new *target ms* field next to the **Green#** readout, press **Set** (or Enter), and the preview solves for and applies the **HiSpeed that yields that window** at the current BPM, scroll mode and practice rate. A chartist can now pick a reading window numerically instead of nudging the HiSpeed slider by feel.

This implements **Point 38(c)** from `Upcoming Changes.rtf`, building directly on yesterday's v0.0.56 **Green Number** readout. It was verified absent before building (no prior target/inverse solver), and yesterday's v0.0.56 work was confirmed fully integrated and unbroken first.

It is **render-only** — the chart is never modified; only the visual HiSpeed changes.

## What it does

- **Target ms field + Set button** next to the *Green#* readout. Enter a target and press Set (or Enter in the field) to apply the solved HiSpeed.
- **Scroll-mode aware:** solves against the constant **dominant BPM** in C-mode (so the lock is constant across soflan) and the **BPM at the playhead** in M-mode. Also honours the practice **Rate**.
- **Round-trips exactly:** the solved speed is snapped to the HiSpeed slider's granularity + range, so the resulting *Green#* reads back the target. Targets below the window achievable at the slider max clamp honestly to the achievable value.
- Persists via **Save Config** (`prefs.reactionTargetMs`).

## Changes

- **`js/chart.js`** — `hispeedForReactionMs(targetMs, bpm, rate)`: a DOM-free, unit-tested single source of truth. The exact inverse of v0.0.56's `reactionWindowMs()` — given a target reaction window it returns the HiSpeed that yields it (`fullSpanTicks / (targetMs·rate·bpm·TICKS_PER_BEAT/60000)`), guarded so non-positive/NaN input returns `0`.
- **`js/app.js`** — `applyTargetReaction()` resolves the reference BPM by scroll mode, solves, snaps to the slider and dispatches the existing HiSpeed input handler so both render paths and the readout update in one place. Set-button + Enter wiring; Save Config persistence + restore. `APP_VERSION` → `0.0.57`, CHANGELOG entry.
- **`index.html` / `style.css`** — target-ms number field + Set button in the HiSpeed section; new `.pvc-num` input style.
- **`js/i18n.js`** — `preview.setHispeed` added across all 5 locales (en/es/fr/ja/zh).
- **Docs** — `vibe-editr-docs.html` Updates section + version banner; `Upcoming Changes.rtf` (Point 38c marked **SHIPPED**, new **Point 39** recommendations, dated UPDATES entry).

## Testing

- **106-assertion node round-trip identity test** against the real `chart.js`: `hispeed → ms → hispeed` is exact across hispeed/BPM/rate grids, plus target/BPM/rate monotonicity (higher BPM ⇒ lower hispeed for a fixed window, half rate ⇒ double hispeed) and guard cases (0/neg/NaN/undefined → 0, bad BPM/rate stay finite).
- **10-assertion real-browser Playwright run** driving the live UI: target `800 ms` → HiSpeed `6.7×` reads back `796 ms`; target `1200 ms` → HiSpeed `4.4×` reads back `1212 ms`; unreachable sub-533 ms targets clamp to the slider max and honestly report the achieved window; the Enter path applies; the full app boots and enters Game view with **zero page errors**.
- All 20 JS modules pass `node --check`; the dev server serves the app reporting `APP_VERSION = '0.0.57'`.

## Verification of prior work

Confirmed yesterday's **v0.0.56 Green Number** is fully integrated and unbroken before starting — `chart.js` still exports `reactionWindowMs`, `app.js` `updateReactionReadout()` writes `#pvc-reaction` + `gameView.reactionMs`, and the new solver reuses that same engine and BPM-resolution logic.

body:
## Why this exists

**PR #10 (Phase 6 — offline PWA) was never actually merged.** It is still OPEN, its commit `631db29` is not an ancestor of `main`, and its files never reached production (prod \`/sw.js\` returned **404**, prod \`app.html\` still shipped the base64 data-URI manifest with **0** SW registrations). Phase 7 + WO2 + PR #13 were all built on top of a main that silently lacked Phase 6.

This PR recovers Phase 6 by **re-implementing it against today's `app.html`** (not a stale cherry-pick of `631db29`, which would conflict with the Phase 7/WO2/PR13 divergence) and restoring the static assets. **PR #10 will be closed with a link to this PR.**

## What's in it

- **manifest.json + icons** (`icon-192`, `icon-512`); `<head>` links the real manifest + `theme-color` + `apple-touch-icon`, replacing the base64 data-URI manifest.
- **sw.js** (`tio-shell-v1`): precaches the shell + **all vendored libs** (opencv, jscanify, tesseract core+worker+traineddata, jspdf, pdf-lib). Stale-while-revalidate for same-origin GET; **network-only for `/api/*`**; navigation falls back to the cached shell offline. Replaces the old blob-URL "SW" that deleted all caches and unregistered itself.
- **Vendored jspdf 2.5.1 + pdf-lib 1.17.1**; `loadJsPDF`/`loadPdfLib` load `/vendor` first with CDN fallback (new `loadScriptWithFallback`). Offline PDF build.
- **IndexedDB outbox**: completing a form offline (or on a failed server call) queues it (fields + filled-PDF/scan/signature) and shows "Saved on device — will upload when you're back online"; history shows a **pending-sync** badge. `flushOutbox()` runs on load, on SW register, and on the `online` event.

## Precache ↔ vendor contract (per Q)

The `sw.js` `PRECACHE` list matches the **current** `vendor/` contents exactly — **nothing from WO2b** (pdf.js is not vendored here and not precached). WO2b's SW-precache line lands only once this PR is merged + device-verified.

## CSP ↔ SW interaction

- SW is same-origin `/sw.js` → satisfies Phase 7 `worker-src 'self'` (the retired blob-URL SW is what needed `blob:`).
- `/vendor/*` scripts are same-origin → `script-src 'self'`; CDN fallbacks (cdnjs, unpkg) already allow-listed.
- `vercel.json` already carries `/sw.js` `no-cache` + `/manifest.json` short-cache (folded in during Phase 7).

## Verification

- Guard: app.html inline JS parse **OK**; `6608 → 6694` (no shrinkage). `sw.js` + vendored libs pass `node --check`.
- Preview headless: SW registers at origin scope, manifest valid, **no CSP console violations**, all precache assets 200, offline fns defined. _(pending — results appended below.)_
- **Human gate (Q, on device):** SMOKE_TESTS.md "Offline PWA" — install prompt / Lighthouse installable; airplane-mode complete → "Saved on device" + pending-sync badge; reconnect → outbox uploads, badge clears, form appears server-side.

body:
Touches migrations/, .github/workflows/, or web/prisma/schema.prisma: **NO** — route handler + tests only.

## Summary
- `GET /api/deals/:id/properties` returned raw Prisma rows to any deal participant, so buyers received `tracked_properties.agent_private_note` over the wire even though the agent UI labels it "Private note (only you see this)".
- Rows now pass through an explicit `serializeProperty()` before `json()`: `agent_private_note` is included only when the caller is the deal's owning agent (`deal.agent_id === userId`); for every other participant the key is absent from the payload entirely (not just null).
- All other fields are passed through unchanged, so buyer-visible data (address, status, agent_note, buyer_note, offer_requested, etc.) is byte-for-byte identical to before.

## Files changed
- `web/app/api/deals/[id]/properties/route.ts` — added `serializeProperty()` + owning-agent check in `GET`; no longer returns raw rows.
- `web/tests/api/properties.test.ts` — new `GET` describe block (TDD, written first and watched fail): buyer-absence, owner-presence, shared-fields-intact.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI: `npm test` green (911 tests / 92 files locally), `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` clean.
- [ ] New tests: buyer participant GET → `agent_private_note` key absent and note text nowhere in the JSON; owning agent GET → field present with value; buyer GET → all shared fields intact (id, deal_id, address, status, agent_note, buyer_note, offer_requested + presence of city/state/price/beds/baths/sqft/thumbnail_url/source_url/added_by/created_at/updated_at).
- [ ] UAT: as an agent add a private note to a tracked property; as the buyer participant open the network tab and load the properties list → the response JSON contains no `agent_private_note`.

## Assumptions
- "Non-owner" = anyone whose `userId !== deal.agent_id`. TC/admin don't pass `hasDealAccess` today unless they are the owning agent or a participant, so no special-casing was added for them — a TC/admin added as a participant is treated as non-owner and does not receive the private note (safe default).
- No client changes needed: `web/hooks/useProperties.ts` already maps the field optionally (`p.agent_private_note ?? undefined`), so an absent key degrades to `undefined`; the buyer UI (`web/components/pages/buyer/BuyerView.tsx`) never references `agentPrivateNote`; the agent UI (`web/components/pages/agent/DealDetail.tsx`) keeps working because the owning agent still receives the field. Both files were listed in the ticket as context and verified — neither required an edit.
- `POST /api/deals/:id/properties` and `PATCH/DELETE .../:propId` were left as-is: all three are gated to the owning agent (`agent_id` check), so their responses can't leak to a buyer. Buyer write authz is explicitly out of scope per the ticket.
- `agent_private_note` is the only agent-only field on `tracked_properties` (`agent_note` is the buyer-visible shared note; the schema has no other private columns).

author: edbertchan
body:
## Summary

Three UI polling hooks (useQueueStatus, useWorkerStatus, useActionGraphSnapshot) invoke setState on every 2s response, even when the response is byte-identical to the previous one.

That churns the returned object reference, invalidates downstream useMemo dependencies, and cascades into full App re-renders in the Running view.

This slice exposes a small helper, packages/ui/src/hooks/useDedupedState.ts::areStructurallyEqual, and each hook now returns the previous object reference when the incoming payload matches it structurally.

## Review Claim

Each polling hook returns the previous object reference when the incoming payload matches it structurally.

## Review Lane

refactor

## Review Unit

activation-surface

## Safety Invariant

Behavior unchanged; equal payloads already carried the same data, so downstream consumers observe the same values.

## Slice Rationale

Smallest change that removes the 2s identity churn in three independent polling hooks. Write-side only, no consumer file is touched.

## Architecture

### Before

Every 2s poll writes a fresh object, so downstream useMemo dependencies invalidate on identity even when the payload is byte-identical.

```mermaid
graph LR
    P["Poll (2s)"] --> S["setState(newPayload)"]
    S --> H["hook returns newRef"]
    H --> M["useMemo dep changes"]
    M --> R["App re-render"]
```

### After

The hook returns the previous object reference when the incoming payload matches structurally, so downstream useMemo dependencies stay stable across unchanged ticks.

```mermaid
graph LR
    P["Poll (2s)"] --> C{"areStructurallyEqual(prev, next)"}
    C -->|"equal"| K["keep prev ref"]
    C -->|"different"| S["setState(newPayload)"]
    K --> H["hook returns prevRef"]
    S --> H2["hook returns newRef"]
    H --> M["useMemo dep stable"]
    H2 --> M2["useMemo dep changes"]
    M --> N["no re-render"]
    M2 --> R["App re-render"]
```

## Non-goals

- No behavior change.
- Sidebar memoization (later slice).
- Shared clock extraction (later slice).
- Gating polls on relevance (later slice).
- Replacing polling with push projections (deferred to Phase 2).

## Test Plan

<details>
<summary>Test Plan</summary>

- [x] cd packages/ui && pnpm test

</details>

## Revert Plan

<details>
<summary>Revert Plan</summary>

- Safe to revert? Yes
- Revert command: `git revert <sha>`
- Post-revert steps: None
- Data migration? No

</details>

body:
## Summary

Found by dogfooding a live goal-supervised build: the goal chip never appeared. Backend was flawless (session JSON and `goal.set` event both correct) — the inspector sourced goal state *only* from the event stream, whose replay cursor starts at the global high-water seq, so a `goal.set` predating the browser connection was never replayed. Messages survived only because they're fetched on select; goals had no equivalent bootstrap.

Fix: `selectSession` seeds goal state from `GET /session/{id}.goal` alongside the message fetch. New pure helper `goalFromSession` with test coverage (bootstrap gap is the exact scenario asserted).

author: davidfernandezcast-lab
body:
## Bug
Al elegir el plazo, el vencimiento se derivaba de **hoy + N años** (`new Date()`), no de **fecha de inicio + N años**. Un plan iniciado en 2022 con plazo 15 mostraba "Vence" ~2041 (hoy+15) en vez de 2037 (inicio+15). Además, cambiar la fecha de inicio no recomputaba el vencimiento.

## Fix
- Nuevo `useEffect` en el parent: `maturityDate = startDate + termYears`, recomputado cuando cambia **cualquiera** de los dos (solo para `plan_inversion`).
- El `onClick` de los chips de plazo deja de calcular el vencimiento (solo setea el plazo); el `useEffect` se encarga.

## Alcance
Un archivo: `src/modules/wealth/components/add-holding-wizard.tsx` (+10/-3). Typecheck limpio.

## Verificación
1. Plan con inicio `2022-06` + plazo 15 → "Vence" muestra **2037-06** (no 2041).
2. Cambiar la fecha de inicio → el vencimiento se recalcula solo.
3. Cambiar el plazo (15 → 20) → se recalcula desde la fecha de inicio.
4. El input manual de `maturityDate` de cashflow (perfil B) queda intacto.

body:
## Summary

App already memoizes the workflow, attention, and running collections at the top level, but the sibling LeftStatusColumn recomputes them from raw inputs on every render.

That amplifies wasted work whenever App re-renders. This slice wraps the three collection computations inside LeftStatusColumn in useMemo so unchanged inputs return an identical reference.

## Review Claim

LeftStatusColumn returns identical workflow, attention, and running collection references across renders when its inputs are unchanged.

## Review Lane

refactor

## Review Unit

activation-surface

## Safety Invariant

Behavior unchanged; the produced collections already had value equality on unchanged inputs, so downstream rendering observes the same output.

## Slice Rationale

Isolated to a single component and only the three collection computations. No cross-file touches. Kept apart from the polling hook change so each fix reads in isolation.

## Architecture

### Before

LeftStatusColumn recomputes the three collections on every render from raw inputs, so every parent re-render produces new array references even when the inputs are unchanged.

```mermaid
graph LR
```

author: dixitsa
body:
## Summary
Previously, patron requests and upvotes only ever lived in Firestore — nothing pushed those songs onto the venue's actual Spotify playback (this was surfaced as "the queue doesn't apply to the output device"). This adds a continuous sync so votes actually drive real playback.

**Design decision (confirmed with the user):** chose continuous top-vote syncing over a simpler "queue on approval" model, to keep votes influencing play order for as long as possible.

**Hard constraint:** Spotify's Web API only supports *appending* to the playback queue — no reorder/remove endpoint. So the sync loop maintains "at most one committed-but-not-yet-playing track in Spotify's queue at a time," minimizing how much gets locked in:
1. If the currently playing track matches a song still in Firestore's approved queue, that song has started — remove it from "Up Next" so the next most-voted song can take its place.
2. If Spotify's real queue is empty, push the current top-voted approved song.

## Changes
- `lib/spotifyAdmin.ts` — new admin-gated `getPlaybackQueue` (GET `/v1/me/player/queue`) and `queueTrack` (POST same endpoint), same `requireAdmin` pattern as `skipTrack`/`transferPlayback`. `getNowPlaying` now also returns `spotifyTrackId`.
- `types/index.ts` — `spotifyTrackId` on `NowPlaying`, new `PlaybackQueueState` type.
- `components/admin/AdminPlayer/AdminPlayer.tsx` — sync loop piggybacks on the existing 5s now-playing poll; small "Auto-queued next: {title}" status line so this isn't a silent black box.

## Known limitations (Spotify API constraints, not solved here)
- Requires the admin dashboard tab to stay open (client-side polling, same as existing `skipTrack`/`getNowPlaying`; no new server/cron infra).
- Once a track is pushed to Spotify's queue, later votes can't reorder or remove it.
- Multiple simultaneously-open admin tabs could each queue near-simultaneously in rare cases; worst case is an occasional duplicate.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 errors
- [x] `npm run build` succeeds
- [x] Signed into the real admin dashboard with Spotify connected but no active device — confirmed the dashboard renders correctly (no crash) and `queueTrack`'s 404 ("no active device") is caught and logged properly, not silently reported as success (caught and fixed a real bug during review: the initial version didn't check `response.ok`)
- [ ] **Needs verification from the operator**: confirming a song actually starts playing on a real connected speaker/device requires a live active Spotify session, which only they have

## Summary

Cosmetic time strings in the UI each owned a private setInterval that called setState to advance a relative-time display.

Multiple tickers at the same cadence ran independent timers and paid independent React re-renders.

This slice exposes packages/ui/src/hooks/useNow.ts. It activates one setInterval per interval value at module scope; new callers attach to the existing timer, and the timer clears when the last caller unmounts.

Two existing tickers migrate: TimelineView (1s bar-width advance, only while a task is running) and HeartbeatTimingSection (5s heartbeat-age display, only while the task is running with a lastHeartbeatAt).

## Review Claim

TimelineView and HeartbeatTimingSection observe the current time via the exposed useNow hook instead of owning their own setInterval and tick state.

## Review Lane

refactor

## Review Unit

activation-surface

## Safety Invariant

Behavior unchanged; each component re-renders at the same cadence and shows the same relative-time strings.

## Slice Rationale

One migration slice covering both consumers of the shared clock. Same pattern applied to both, so one conceptual unit.

## Architecture

### Before

Every cosmetic-time component owns a private setInterval and setState pair. N components at the same cadence run N independent timers and pay N independent React re-renders per tick.

```mermaid
graph LR
    TV["TimelineView"] -->|"setInterval(1000)"| TA["tick TV"]
    HB["HeartbeatTimingSection"] -->|"setInterval(5000)"| HA["tick HB"]
    TA --> RA["render TV"]
    HA --> RB["render HB"]
```

### After

useNow(intervalMs, enabled) keeps one setInterval per interval value at module scope. Callers attach as subscribers; the timer clears when the last subscriber unmounts.

```mermaid
graph LR
    TV["TimelineView"] -->|"useNow(1000, hasRunning)"| C1["clock[1000]"]
    HB["HeartbeatTimingSection"] -->|"useNow(5000, running && heartbeat)"| C2["clock[5000]"]
    C1 -->|"one setInterval"| S1["subscribers -> setState(now)"]
    C2 -->|"one setInterval"| S2["subscribers -> setState(now)"]
    S1 --> R1["render TV"]
    S2 --> R2["render HB"]
```

## Non-goals

- No behavior change.
- Migrating other UI intervals (DAG watchdogs, delta perf reporter). Those are functional intervals, not cosmetic time displays.
- Polling hook or sidebar memo changes (their own slices).

author: merlimat
body:
## Problem
Under a max-throughput run (thousands of in-flight requests) the etcd driver's worker OOMs. jetcd defaults to an **unbounded cached thread pool** for its async callbacks, which grows to ~9k threads under high concurrency and exhausts the worker's native memory (pthread `EAGAIN`).

## Fix
Pin jetcd's callback executor to a bounded pool (`Executors.newFixedThreadPool(64)`) via `Client.builder().executorService(...)`, and shut it down in `close()`. `executorService()` is part of jetcd's stable core builder API (unlike `connectTimeout`), so it's safe against the shaded-jetcd ambiguity already noted in this file.

## Verification
etcd completed the full YCSB throughput comparison on a real cluster with 0 failures and no OOM (previously OOMKilled mid-run).

* Related to Automattic/jetpack#50222 (original Stats admin-bar link, front-end only)
* Related to Automattic/wp-calypso#112405 (client-side Stats-node injection in the Calypso omnibar)

No.

body:
## Summary

useQueueStatus and useWorkerStatus polled every 2s forever, even on an idle app with no tasks and no queue view open.

This slice exposes an optional enabled parameter on both hooks so their internal 2s setInterval only activates when the data is worth fetching.

App wires the parameter from a runtime-relevance predicate: any known task exists, or the queue view is currently open.

Together with slices (1)-(3), an idle app now performs effectively zero background re-renders in the Running view.

## Review Claim

useQueueStatus and useWorkerStatus accept an optional enabled parameter; when false, their internal setInterval does not activate; App drives the value from a runtime-relevance predicate.

## Review Lane

refactor

## Review Unit

activation-surface

## Safety Invariant

Behavior unchanged when enabled is true or omitted; App activates polling whenever any task exists or the queue view is open, which covers every case the polled data currently drives.

## Slice Rationale

Foundational hook-signature change plus its App activation. Kept together because the predicate is trivial and the signature is not consumed by any other file today.

## Architecture

### Before

useQueueStatus and useWorkerStatus start their 2s setInterval unconditionally on mount, so an idle App with no tasks and no queue view open still pays two polls every 2s.

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["App mount"] --> Q["useQueueStatus()"]
    A --> W["useWorkerStatus()"]
    Q --> QI["setInterval(2000) always"]
    W --> WI["setInterval(2000) always"]
    QI --> QP["poll queue status"]
    WI --> WP["poll worker status"]
```

### After

Both hooks accept an optional enabled parameter. App wires it from a pollingRelevant predicate ("any known task exists, or the queue view is open"), so the timers only exist when the polled data is worth fetching.

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["App render"] --> P["pollingRelevant = tasks.size > 0 || viewMode == queue"]
    P --> Q["useQueueStatus(2000, pollingRelevant)"]
    P --> W["useWorkerStatus(2000, pollingRelevant)"]
    Q --> QG{"enabled?"}
    W --> WG{"enabled?"}
    QG -->|"true"| QI["setInterval(2000)"]
    QG -->|"false"| QN["no timer"]
    WG -->|"true"| WI["setInterval(2000)"]
    WG -->|"false"| WN["no timer"]
```

## Non-goals

- No behavior change when polling is active.
- Replacing polling with push projections (deferred to Phase 2).
- Broader sidebar-based gating (requires reordering hook calls in App).
- Any consumer file changes beyond App.

author: joey-huckabee
body:
## Problem (team review, item 7)
Every poetry command in the docs uses `-C python <cmd>` except the wheel build, which uses `poetry -P python build`. The comment flagged the inconsistency and that `-P` requires Poetry ≥ 2.0 — suggesting a version note or standardizing on `-C`.

## Analysis (verified, not assumed)
The `-P` is **deliberate and still necessary** — `poetry -C python build` doubles the source path on Windows and the wheel build fails. Reproduced on the current Poetry (2.3.4):

```
poetry -C python build → [WinError 3] ...\python\src\src\mie_decoder\__init__.py   (src doubled; wheel fails)
poetry -P python build → builds sdist + wheel cleanly
```

So standardizing on `-C` (the other suggested option) would **reintroduce a broken build on Windows**. The right fix is the version note.

## Change
Documents the rationale at each `-P python build` site — a full note in `python/README.md`, and a one-line inline comment in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `docs/MAINTAINER-GUIDE.md`: `-P` (`--project`, Poetry ≥ 2.0) is used only for the build to avoid the `-C build` src-path-doubling bug on Windows. **No command changed** — only the rationale is now recorded.

author: ivanium
body:
## Purpose

`get_mooncake_dp_engine_index` asserted `data_parallel_rank_local is not None` under external/hybrid DP LB. This crashes on headless wide-TP follower nodes: they go through `run_headless` → `MultiprocExecutor` directly, which never populates `data_parallel_rank_local`.

Preferring `data_parallel_rank_local` was also inconsistent: for a replica launched with `--data-parallel-rank N` (N > 0), head-node processes computed `rank_local = 0` while follower-node workers would compute the global index N, so TP ranks of the same replica disagreed on their DP index.

Fix: use `parallel_config.data_parallel_index` unconditionally. It is populated in every launch path (`ParallelConfig.__post_init__`, `run_engine_core`, Ray actor), is identical on head and follower nodes, and unlike `data_parallel_rank` is not reset to 0 for dense-model DP engines. That reduces the helper to a one-line accessor, so it is inlined at its two call sites (`MooncakeStoreWorker.__init__`, `get_zmq_rpc_path_lookup`) and removed; the lookup IPC path stays unique per node since co-located engines have distinct global indices.

## Duplicate check

No open PR touches this helper (searched `mooncake dp index`, `get_mooncake_dp_engine_index`, `mooncake wide TP`, `data_parallel_rank_local mooncake`; open Mooncake PRs #47317 / #41093 are unrelated).

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) via commit hooks.
- Wide-TP (multi-node TP, headless followers) × DP deployment with MooncakeStoreConnector, which crashed on the assert before this change.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py` (monkeypatch replaced by `data_parallel_index=0` on the fake parallel_config).

## Test Result

Wide-TP DP serving comes up and serves traffic; previously every follower node died at engine init with `AssertionError` in `get_mooncake_dp_engine_index`. No model-output/accuracy impact (side-channel identity only).

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change; the diff was reviewed and the deployment validated by the submitter.

body:
## Summary
Ships the **V5 BP+search225 step-12000** CP-detector model as the browser/product default, aligns the benchmark defaults with the production decode, removes a misleading benchmark column, makes the browser decode defaults a single Rust-sourced value, and modernizes the stage-inspector toolchain.

Paired with **zacharyfmarion/create-pattern-detector#13** (model registration + dated report).

## Model promotion
- `scripts/cp-detect/current-model.json` → v5 (model_id, ONNX SHA `399e6078…`, versioned/stable dirs, checkpoint + manifest). ONNX copied into the stable `cp-detector-v3/` dir the browser loads (assets gitignored; `current-model.json` is the tracked source of truth; verified with `check-local-model-assets.mjs`).
- Stage-inspector (`DEFAULT_DENSE_MANIFEST`) + `rederive-junction-recall.py` defaults repointed at the v5 native dense cache.
- Native-cp-v1 `solve_recovered_original` **121 → 231** (deterministic replay), **204** browser-onnx.

## Benchmark ↔ production alignment (root-caused a baselining trap)
- New `oristudio-cp-detect::defaults` — single source of truth for default decode sources (candidate strategy `junction-first-v1`, line evidence `source-image`, junction source `dense-model`).
- `compare_exact_solve_benchmark` + `compare_candidate_coverage` now default to the **production** decode (was `legacy` + `model` — a weaker path that measured a different pipeline than the product and produced misleading baselines) and **require `--dense-manifest`** (no silent stale cache). `--candidate-source legacy` kept as an explicit historical baseline; a guard test asserts the default is never legacy.
- **Dropped the always-on `legacy` output column** (misleading once the default is junction-first). Verified no metric change: deterministic native replay still recovers 121/17.
- Documented that the headline `solve_recovered_original` comes from the replay harness (`--threads 4`, deterministic) rather than the 16-core full benchmark (wall-clock-timeout-noisy near the boundary).

## Single-source browser defaults (codegen + guardrails)
- The browser `CP_DETECT_DEFAULT_*` constants are now **code-generated from Rust** (`emit_cp_detect_defaults_ts`) into a gitignored generated TS file on every `build:wasm` — structurally can't go stale. `cpDetectTypes.ts` imports it (the typed assignment also guards union membership). The wasm crate exports the same constants; a Rust test + a vitest test assert *generated-TS == the wasm the product ships*.

author: endle
body:
Reviews and modernizes the five GitHub Actions workflows, and removes a
dead code path found along the way.

## Commits

### `003eb94` — rust-cache + cargo-deny-action, `cargo --locked`
Replaces sccache and six hand-rolled `Get Date` + `actions/cache@v3` registry
blocks with `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`, and swaps `cargo install cargo-deny`
(which compiled cargo-deny and its whole dep tree from crates.io on *every*
run) for the prebuilt `EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2`.

Both shift dependency-fetch traffic off crates.io onto GitHub's cache/releases
backend. sccache never helped here — it caches rustc output, but cargo
downloads crate sources *before* rustc runs, so only the registry cache
reduces crates.io traffic.

`--locked` on every cargo invocation makes the committed `Cargo.lock`
authoritative, so no index re-resolution hits the network.

Coupled migration (the old scaffolding was being rewritten anyway):
- `actions-rs/toolchain@v1` (archived, uses removed `set-output`) → `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`
- `actions/checkout@v2`/`v3` → `@v4`; dropped a duplicated sccache step
- llamafile model cache `actions/cache@v3` → `@v4`

cargo-deny is behaviour-identical (`check licenses advisories`, `arguments: ""`
to override the action's `--all-features` default).

### `a3af29e` — remove dead keyword highlighter
`/highlight` is now fully LLM-based. The old tree/keyword highlighter in
`post_query::highlighter` was left behind: all 12 of its public functions were
referenced only within the module itself and two 2024 test files. It's also a
remnant of the server-side HTML rendering approach the project explicitly
abandoned.

Those two test files were independently broken — an `assert_eq!(4,4)`
tautology, assertion-free tests, a "didn't finish the test" stub, and
commented-out cases.

Removes ~618 lines of Rust + 124 KB of fixtures. `cargo test --locked
--all-targets` stays green.

### `b35090e` — trigger scoping + concurrency
Replaces inconsistent, hand-maintained push allowlists (`rust`: `llm_candidate`;
`llm-backend`/`llamafile`: `backend_llm`; `quality`: every branch) with one
uniform model: **push → master only, pull_request → all PRs, plus
`workflow_dispatch`**. This eliminates the double-run where `push` and
`pull_request` both fired for a commit on a branch with an open PR.
`workflow_dispatch` is the manual escape hatch for testing a branch pre-PR.

Adds a top-level `concurrency` block that supersedes stale PR/branch runs.
`master` is excluded via `github.run_id` (unique per run), so every
default-branch commit still gets its own full, independent run — bisect-friendly.

### `7dc3581` — restrict `GITHUB_TOKEN` to `contents: read`
The repo's `default_workflow_permissions` is `write`, so every run got a
read/write token that **no step uses**. That token is reachable:
`actions/checkout` persists it into `.git/config`, and cargo executes arbitrary
`build.rs` and proc-macros from the dependency tree — a compromised crate or
`uses:` action could scrape it and push.

Declaring `permissions: contents: read` sets every unlisted scope to `none`.
Nothing regresses: the Actions cache and artifact upload use the runtime token,
not the `contents` scope; cargo-deny only reads.

## Verification

All five workflows parse; the live proof is this PR's own run. Expect **exactly
one run per workflow** (no double-run), and a follow-up push should cancel the
prior run.

## Not included (deliberately)

Still open from the review, each independent: turning the `rustfmt`/`clippy`
steps into real gates (today `rustfmt` is installed but `cargo fmt --check`
never runs, and `clippy` has no `-D warnings` so it can't fail), and the
`release` job in `rust.yml` that is mislabeled — it uploads a *debug* binary on
every push and PR. Also not touched: the repo-level
`default_workflow_permissions` setting, which could be flipped to `read` as a
backstop for future workflows.

## 개요
모든 도메인을 최상위 모듈로 평탄화하고, 게시글 확장(텍스트 블러) 저장/조회 파이프라인을 구성했습니다.

author: fgarofalo56
body:
## Live gap (browser-verified 2026-07-08)

`/thread` (the Loom Thread / Weave lineage graph) still rendered orphaned edges referencing items deleted in the 2026-07-08 UAT purge (Demo lakehouse, E2E Weave Model/Report, adventureworks-mirror-e2e, etc.). The merged LIN-GC work (#1732) wired delete-time cleanup and a **Purview-only** orphan reconcile, but the reconcile sweep never covered Thread edges — so pre-existing edge debris (from before delete-time reconciliation was wired) persisted, and `POST /api/admin/lineage/reconcile` had no way to clean it.

## Changes

- **`lib/thread/thread-edges.ts`** — new `listAllThreadEdges()` (deployment-wide, cross-partition, includes tombstoned edges so stale-flagged orphans are still caught) and `removeThreadEdge(tenantId, edgeId)` as the shared single-edge removal primitive. `reconcileThreadEdgesOnDelete(mode:'remove')` now delegates to it.
- **`lib/azure/lineage-gc.ts`** — new `findThreadEdgeOrphans()` resolves each edge's source **and** non-external target against live Cosmos items via the existing batched `liveItemIds` check (fail-safe: unprovable ⇒ treated live, never purged). Recycled/soft-deleted items remain in the items container, so their tombstoned—recoverable—edges are correctly **not** flagged. `purgeThreadEdgeOrphans()` reuses `removeThreadEdge` with per-edge outcomes.
- **route** — response gains `threadEdges: { scanned, orphans[] }` (dry-run) and `threadEdges.purged[]` (purge). Both planes are swept; a non-dry-run purges both. The Thread sweep runs **even when Purview is unconfigured** (the /thread graph has its own debris).
- **Reconcile dialog** — dry-run table now has two sections (Purview catalog entities + Weave/Thread edges), purges both on confirm, and the description + Purview-unconfigured note were updated to reflect the two planes.

## Delete-path verification (task step 3)

`reconcileThreadEdgesOnDelete` is confirmed wired into all three delete paths, so the /thread copy "Deleting an item automatically removes its lineage here" holds:
- per-item delete → `deleteOwnedItem` (direct) + workspace item route `cleanupItemMetadata`
- workspace cascade → `cleanupWorkspaceMetadata`
- bulk-delete → `cleanupWorkspaceMetadata`

No path missed; no new wiring needed.

## Tests & guards

- **Vitest (38 passing)** across the 3 affected suites: orphan detection (both endpoints live ⇒ kept; one endpoint missing ⇒ orphan with correct `missing[]`; external target never counted missing), `listAllThreadEdges`/`removeThreadEdge` primitives (404 = success, real error = false, best-effort no-throw), and the route dry-run/purge shape (incl. Purview-unconfigured still sweeps Thread edges).
- **Guards** — `check-no-raw-px`, `check-route-guards`, `check-env-sync`, `check-no-bare-client-fetch`: **zero** violations.
- Typecheck: touched source files clean (remaining tsc noise is the pre-existing repo-wide test-mock `(...a:any[])` spread pattern, excluded from the build tsconfig).

author: codestronger
body:
double_quoted_string and quoted_array wrapped values in double quotes without escaping an embedded " or \. Any caller that passes user-controlled input as a WhereOp.contains / WhereOp.in / WhereOp.phrase argument could break out of the string literal and inject arbitrary YQL into the where clause. The free-text model.queryString (userQuery()) path is a bound parameter and was never affected.

Escape " and \ at the single quoting chokepoint so every WhereOp string literal is inert regardless of the caller. Ordinary values (law keys, ltree paths, numerics, booleans) are unchanged.

## Problem

Claude Code uses `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` for internal background tasks (context summarization, token counting) independently of `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`. It was missing from Osprey's `MANAGED_ENV_VARS`, so a stale value in the user's shell would survive the scrub and override the project's provider config.

**Concrete failure scenario:**

A user with a Bedrock model ID set in `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` (common at AWS-enabled facilities) would have that ID used for every background Claude Code call, even when the project is configured to use a vLLM endpoint via hpc-as-api. vLLM rejects Bedrock model names with HTTP 404 ("model does not exist").

Example `config.yml` for a vLLM endpoint on an HPC cluster:

```yaml
claude_code:
  provider: hpc-as-api

api:
  providers:
    hpc-as-api:
      api_key: ${HPC_AS_API_API_KEY}
      base_url: https://relay.stream.acer.uic.edu:8001/v1
      models:
        haiku: gemma4-31b
        sonnet: gemma4-31b
        opus: gemma4-31b
```

With this config, every user message generated two vLLM requests: one for the main response (correct model) and one background call using the stale Bedrock model ID (404 error). The 404 was harmless after the companion fix to hpc-as-api's buffer proxy, but it added latency and log noise on every request.

## Fix

Two changes in `claude_code_resolver.py`:

1. Add `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` to `MANAGED_ENV_VARS` so it gets scrubbed from the shell before launch, like the other model selectors.
2. Set it to the haiku-tier model inside `ClaudeCodeModelResolver.build()` so the provider's correct model ID gets injected at runtime.

`settings.json` stays env-block-free, consistent with the existing design and the `TestProviderEnvBlock` tests.

## Test plan

- [ ] All existing `TestProviderEnvBlock` tests pass (settings.json has no env block)
- [ ] `TestClaudeCodeResolver` tests pass
- [ ] Configure a project with a vLLM provider (e.g. hpc-as-api with `gemma4-31b`)
- [ ] Confirm no 404 background calls appear in vLLM logs after launch
- [ ] Confirm both the main response and background calls use the correct model

author: jameopotato
body:
## Problem
The deferred transport-clear synth (`FireDeferredTransportClearSynth`) fires on the first post-transition player `UpdateObject` whenever the **destination** is off a transport — but that includes mage-teleport / cross-continent / BG-exit transitions where the player was **never on a transport at the source**. There the fabricated `MoveTeleport(TransportGUID=empty)` leaves the client unable to walk (WASD dead; camera-rotate + casting still work), recoverable only by `/reload`. This is the **#329 / #331 / #332** wedge — reproduces at EU latency (~35 ms), not NA.

## Fix
Gate the synth on the **source** transport state (already in scope as `prevTransport`):

| source (prev) | dest on transport | action |
|---|---|---|
| observed **empty** | no | **skip** ← *new* (the wedge) |
| non-empty | no | fire (boat/zep stale-attach clear, dc39c39) |
| null (unobserved) | no | fire (login gate-release; fail-safe) |
| any | yes | skip (unchanged) |

The decision is extracted to a pure `TransportClearGate.ShouldFire(source, dest)` predicate; the arm sites, `FireDeferredTransportClearSynth`, and the guard-flag machine are untouched.

## Why it should help
Those transitions **should no longer** wedge, since the proxy no longer fabricates a transport-clear teleport for a player who wasn't on a transport at the source. The change is **fail-safe** — it only removes fabrications that the 6/6 healthy captures proved were no-ops, and preserves every believed-load-bearing case (boat/zep clear, login release).

## Validation
- **Pre-ship:** `TransportClearGateTests` — a deterministic truth-table unit test over the predicate (4 cases, passing). Full solution builds clean.
- **Post-ship:** the wedge is client-internal and EU-latency-only (not NA-reproducible), and a healthy transition produces no distinguishing "success" log — so real-world validation is the **absence of further #329/#331/#332 reports**.

Base: `beta`. Addresses #329, #331, #332 (intentionally not auto-closing — fail-safe but not yet field-verified).

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [cert-manager](https://cert-manager.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager)) | minor | `v1.20.3` → `v1.21.1` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>cert-manager/cert-manager (cert-manager)</summary>

### [`v1.21.1`](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/tag/v1.21.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/compare/v1.21.0...v1.21.1)

cert-manager is the easiest way to automatically manage certificates in Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters.

v1.21.1 fixes a controller panic for Certificates with `spec.renewal.policy: Disabled`, a regression in 1.21.0 which caused log spam and dropped Secret informer events, Issuers and ClusterIssuers getting stuck at `Ready=False` (`InvalidSolver`) when a referenced ACME DNS-01 solver Secret is created after the Issuer, and the commented Gateway API example in the Helm chart values. It also updates several dependencies to fix reported security vulnerabilities.

All users should upgrade.

#### Changes by Kind

##### Bug or Regression

- Avoid controller panic if a Certificate sets spec.renewal.policy=Disabled ([#​9038](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9038), [@​sklirg](https://redirect.github.com/sklirg))
- Fix Issuer/ClusterIssuer stuck at Ready=False/InvalidSolver after a missing ACME DNS-01 solver Secret is created ([#​9083](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9083), [@​SebTardif](https://redirect.github.com/SebTardif))
- Fix log spam and dropped Secret informer events for non-cert-manager Secrets, caused by a generics regression introduced in 1.21.0. ([#​9037](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9037), [@​wallrj-cyberark](https://redirect.github.com/wallrj-cyberark))
- Fixed the commented Gateway API config example in the Helm chart values to use `gatewayAPI.enabled` instead of the invalid `gatewayAPI.enable`. ([#​9012](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9012), [@​mateenali66](https://redirect.github.com/mateenali66))

##### Other (Cleanup or Flake)

- Bump `golang.org/x/text` to v0.40.0 to fix a reported security vulnerability ([#​9039](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9039), [@​wallrj-cyberark](https://redirect.github.com/wallrj-cyberark))
- Bump `google.golang.org/grpc` to v1.82.1 to fix a reported security vulnerability ([#​9063](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9063))
- Bump `github.com/google/cel-go` to v0.29.0 to fix a reported security vulnerability ([#​9072](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9072))
- Bump `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` to v1.44.0 to fix a reported security vulnerability ([#​9073](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9073))
- Update distroless base images ([#​9000](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9000), [#​9025](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9025))

### [`v1.21.0`](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/tag/v1.21.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/compare/v1.20.3...v1.21.0)

cert-manager is the easiest way to automatically manage certificates in Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters.

cert-manager 1.21 brings ACME Renewal Information (ARI) support, AWS IAM authentication for the Vault issuer, several security hardening changes, and continued improvements to Gateway API integration and cainjector. There are three breaking changes related to Helm chart RBAC and metrics values — review them carefully before upgrading.

#### Known Issues

- **Controller crash-loops when a Certificate sets `renewal.policy: Disabled`**: the new Certificate renewal policies feature ([#​8258](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8258)) causes a nil pointer dereference panic in the trigger controller whenever a Certificate's `spec.renewal.policy` is set to `Disabled` — `pki.RenewalTime()` returns `(nil, nil)` for that policy, but the caller unconditionally dereferences the result. This crashes the controller process (crash-loop) for any cluster with such a Certificate. **Workaround**: do not set `renewal.policy: Disabled` on any Certificate until this is fixed; remove the field (or set a different policy) from any Certificate that already has it, and restart the controller if it is currently crash-looping. See [#​9031](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9031) for details.
- **Log spam for non-cert-manager-labelled Secret events**: the typed predicates refactoring ([#​8407](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8407)) causes `filteredEventHandler` type assertion failures (`"OnAdd missing Object"`, `"OnUpdate missing ObjectOld"`, `"OnDelete missing Object"`) for every non-cert-manager-labelled Secret event, multiplied by 7 certificate sub-controllers. **This is cosmetic only** — the affected controllers only need events from cert-manager-labelled Secrets (which arrive via the typed informer); the metadata informer events were always filtered out by predicates in previous versions. Issuer and ClusterIssuer controllers are not affected. See [#​8994](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8994) for details.
- **Issuer/ClusterIssuer can get stuck at `Ready: False, Reason: InvalidSolver` and never self-correct**: new eager validation of ACME solver Secrets ([#​8255](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8255)) means an Issuer/ClusterIssuer referencing a solver Secret (e.g. a DNS01 provider credential) that doesn't exist yet will correctly report `Ready: False`, but creating the missing Secret afterwards does not trigger re-reconciliation — the controller's Secret-watch logic was never updated to recognise solver Secrets. It will only recover on the next 10-hour informer resync, a change to the Issuer/ClusterIssuer's own spec, or a controller restart. **Workaround**: after creating the missing Secret, make a trivial edit to the Issuer/ClusterIssuer spec (or delete and recreate it) to force reconciliation. See [#​9036](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9036) for details and a fix proposal.

#### Major Themes

##### Default `tokenrequest` RBAC removed from Helm chart

> ⚠️ Breaking change

The Helm chart no longer creates a default `Role` and `RoleBinding` granting the cert-manager controller permission to create tokens for its own ServiceAccount (`serviceaccounts/token: create`). No documented workflow requires this RBAC — the Route53 docs section that motivated it was removed in 2024.

If you use `serviceAccountRef.name` pointing at the controller ServiceAccount, you must now either create your own `Role`/`RoleBinding` granting `serviceaccounts/token: create`, or migrate to a dedicated ServiceAccount (recommended — see the [Vault](https://cert-manager.io/docs/configuration/vault/) or [Route53](https://cert-manager.io/docs/configuration/acme/dns01/route53/) documentation).

##### Restrict Challenge and Order RBAC in `cert-manager-edit` ClusterRole

> ⚠️ Potentially breaking change

The `cert-manager-edit` aggregate ClusterRole no longer grants `create` for `challenges.acme.cert-manager.io` or `create`, `patch`, `update` for `orders.acme.cert-manager.io` ([`GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258`](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/security/advisories/GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258)). These resources are internal to cert-manager's ACME workflow. Challenge `patch` and `update` are retained because users may need them to remove stuck finalizers.

This change was already shipped in v1.20.3 and v1.19.6, so if you are running one of those versions this will not be a breaking cha

author: nickpismenkov
body:
## What

The liquidation fire paths only acted on **USDC-debt** positions. The Save census showed roughly half of the liquidations we missed were USDC-debt — the other half (USDT / SOL debt) were simply un-fireable. This widens the debt scope to **USDC / USDT / wSOL** on the two flash-capable protocols (marginfi + Kamino).

## How

**marginfi** (liquidation *absorbs* the liability — no borrow needed):
- `marginfi::payback_asset` — generic over the debt bank; `payback_usdc` now delegates.
- `liq_fire` — swaps seized collateral → `debt_mint`, repays the actual debt bank.
- `liq_executor::try_arm` + `is_v1_fireable` accept any liability bank whose mint is USDC/USDT/wSOL; the profit gate prices the debt asset (its decimals + USD price) instead of assuming USDC `1e6`/$1.

**Kamino** (flash-borrows the debt asset from Jupiter Lend):
- `flashloan.rs` generalized from the single hardcoded USDC market to a per-asset market lookup (`borrow`/`payback` take a mint; `has_market` gates unwired assets).
- The USDT/wSOL JupLend flash-market account sets were reverse-engineered and pinned as constants:
  - `reserve` = `PDA(["reserve", mint], vault-program)`
  - `rate_model` = `PDA(["rate_model", mint], vault-program)`
  - `vault` = `ATA(liquidity-global, mint)`
  - `token` = the 120B account linking the global lending admin ↔ mint (looked up live; not a clean PDA)
  - The derivation **self-checks against the live SDK-captured USDC constants** (reproduces them exactly).
- `kamino_fire` + `liq_kamino_executor` flash-borrow / swap-to / repay the debt mint; repay math priced in the debt asset.

**Same-mint edge** (SOL collateral / SOL debt, USDC/USDC): skip the swap — the seized collateral already *is* the debt asset. Jupiter rejects equal in/out mints, so the old code 400'd on these. Now handled in both fire paths.

## Verification (live mainnet sim)

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `flashloan_probe` | USDC + USDT + wSOL self-repaying flash loans **all simulate clean** |
| `kamino_fire_probe` (USDT debt) | real obligation runs full flashloan-wrapped tx through borrow + refreshes + liquidate, reverts at Kamino health/close-factor gate (custom 6016) — **wiring proven** |
| `kamino_fire_probe` (wSOL debt) | same — **wiring proven** |
| `liq_fire_probe` (wSOL, same-mint) | reaches inside marginfi `LendingAccountLiquidate`, reverts at oracle/eligibility gate — **wiring proven** |

No live non-USDC single-position *marginfi* liquidatable account existed at fresh prices to get a full `err:null`, but the widened path is generic and reaches marginfi's internal liquidate gate.

## Scope

Touches only marginfi/Kamino/flashloan + their probes. Does **not** touch Save (`save*.rs`) or Jupiter (`jupiter.rs`) — those are separate PRs.

body:
## 这个 PR 做什么

战略 30 天清单第 2 项：**匿名 opt-in 遥测（Aptabase）**。在此之前所有阶段门槛（1 万安装、D30>20%）都是盲猜。

## 原则

- **Opt-in，默认关**。全部事件走唯一出口 `utils/telemetry.ts` 的 `track()`，门控在 `telemetry_enabled` 设置上（默认 `false`）。用户不打开，一个字节都不发。
- **匿名 by construction**。属性只允许枚举值和数字——没有 session id、路径、prompt、昵称。事件字典进代码前必须先进 spec（`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-08-telemetry-aptabase.md`）。
- **插件零自动采集**。tauri-plugin-aptabase 官方保证不自动上报，所以前端单点门控覆盖 100% 事件。

## 事件字典（v1，共 4 个）

| 事件 | 属性 | 回答什么 |
|---|---|---|
| `app_started` | mode | 安装、DAU、D1/D7/D30 |
| `agent_task_complete` | source (cc/codex/cursor) | 日均 agent 任务量 |
| `meal_fed` | tier (snack/meal/feast) | token 喂养参与度 |
| `approval_response` | awarded (0/2) | 审批单是否改变响应行为 |

## UI

- **设置 → 隐私**：新增「匿名使用统计」开关（en+zh 文案）。
- **Onboarding**：模式卡片下方一个**默认不勾选**的复选框——新用户是安装数主要来源，这是唯一自然的询问时机。勾选后 `app_started` 在选完模式后补发。

## 密钥注入（@Azealoo 需要做的事）

1. 到 [aptabase.com](https://aptabase.com) 注册（或自托管），创建 app，拿到 `A-US-xxx` / `A-EU-xxx` 密钥。
2. 仓库 Settings → Secrets → Actions 新增 **`APTABASE_APP_KEY`**。

密钥经 `option_env!` 编译期烘焙进二进制（release.yml 已透传 secret）。**没有密钥的构建（本地 dev、fork CI）完全不注册插件**，前端静默吞掉 missing-plugin 错误——开发环境天然零上报，CI 不需要任何改动就能继续跑。

## 验证

- vitest **223/223**（新增 5 个门控测试：默认关、关时不发、开后转发、`telemetry_enabled` 键名持久化、keyless 构建的 rejection 吞掉）
- svelte-check 0 错误；biome 干净（仓库既有 1 个无关警告）；cargo check 通过
- 注：本地未设密钥无法端到端验证真实上报——密钥配好后第一个 release 构建即可在 Aptabase 面板看到 `app_started`

body:
## Problem
The no-raw-motion-values ESLint rule missed seven motion anti-pattern classes (transition:all inline, ease-in, scale(0) entries, >300ms durations, interaction-triggered keyframes, unguarded :hover CSS, Framer Motion x/y shorthands). Fixes #13641.

## What changed
- Extended apps/web/eslint-rules/no-raw-motion-values.js with 8 new messageIds, all at error severity (the rule was already wired 'error' in eslint.config.js; the stale 'warn-level Wave 1c' header comment was corrected):
  - transitionAllInline — inline style transition: 'all …' and transitionProperty: 'all'
  - easeInClass / easeInInline — Tailwind ease-in class (ease-in-out excluded), inline 'ease-in' timing, and Framer ease: 'easeIn'
  - scaleZeroEntry — scale-0 class, transform: 'scale(0)', and Framer initial/animate scale: 0 (suggests scale(0.95) + opacity)
  - rawSecondsDuration — raw Ns seconds durations in inline styles (mirrors the existing raw-ms ban; subsumes the >300ms cap for inline styles)
  - longFramerDuration — Framer transition duration > 0.3s
  - interruptibleKeyframes — arbitrary animate-[…] keyframes bound to hover/focus/active/data-[state] interaction variants (keyframes restart from frame 0 on re-trigger; transitions interpolate)
  - hoverWithoutMediaGuard — literal CSS :hover blocks without @media (hover: hover)
  - framerAxisShorthand — Framer x/y shorthands on motion.*/m.* components (suggests transform strings)
- New unit test apps/web/eslint-rules/no-raw-motion-values.test.ts (RuleTester, vitest) — 22 valid FP-guard cases + 23 invalid cases covering every new messageId.

## Assumptions
- Spec file (/Users/timwhite/.openclaw/workspace-veronica/tasks/motion-lint-eslint-13641.md) is a local path unreachable from this environment; built from the dispatch's inline check list.
- 'Keyframes on dynamic/interruptible UI' is scoped to interaction-variant-triggered keyframes (hover:/focus:/active:/data-[state]:animate-[…]). Infinite loaders and one-shot menu open/close keyframes are explicitly allowed by .claude/rules/ui.md, so a blanket animate-[…] ban would flag canon-approved code (MobileNav, onboarding progress) and blow the <1% FP budget.
- 'Hover without media guard' is scoped to literal CSS :hover blocks (style tags / CSS strings). Tailwind v4 hover: variants are framework-guarded already; flagging them would be ~100% FP.
- Grandfather ratchet: 20 pre-existing files (14 Framer x/y consumers, home-demo/billing raw-seconds/long-duration call sites, one :hover email block, HomepageV2 float keyframes) are listed in GRANDFATHERED_PATH_FRAGMENTS applying ONLY to the three checks they already violate. New code errors immediately; the list is decrementing-only (matches the repo's ratchet pattern, JOV-3577 lineage). Migrating those 20 files is motion-design work out of scope for a lint PR.
- The >300ms Framer ceiling intentionally coexists with the DS cinematic token (420ms): cinematic motion should ride the token path, not raw Framer durations.

## Verification
Sandbox npm registry access is blocked (403; network-access request pending), so the full local gate could not run. Executed locally:
```
$ node -e "require('./eslint-rules/no-raw-motion-values.js')"   # rule loads OK; 15 messageIds
$ node regex smoke tests: ease-in-out excluded ✓, 150ms not seconds ✓, 0.6s caught ✓, transition:all caught ✓, tallness excluded ✓, tw hover: variant excluded ✓, css :hover caught ✓
$ repo-wide grep replay of every new pattern: zero non-grandfathered hits
```
Remaining gate deferred to CI: pnpm turbo lint typecheck test:fast --affected && pnpm run build:web. PR stays DRAFT until CI is green.

## Dispatch
motion-lint-eslint-13641 · Fixes #13641

author: myinisjap
body:
## Problem

The SQLite DB holds everything users can't regenerate — run history, per-run cost data, label-history audit trails, agent notes, diff review comments. There's no backup endpoint, no documented backup procedure, and a naive `cp` of a live SQLite file under write load can produce a corrupt copy. \"Self-hosted\" implies the user owns their data; right now they own a file they can't safely copy.

## Proposal

Two cheap layers, either alone is a big improvement:

- **Built-in**: `GET /api/v1/backup` streams a consistent snapshot via SQLite's online backup API (`VACUUM INTO` a temp file, stream, delete). Admin-token-gated once named tokens (#45) exist; plain bearer until then.
- **Docs**: a short `docs/backup.md` covering the volume layout, `sqlite3 .backup` / `VACUUM INTO` from inside the container, and a Litestream sidecar example (compose snippet) for continuous replication to S3-compatible storage.
- Restore path documented and tested once: stop backend → replace file → start (migrations tolerate old snapshots by design).

_Imported from https://github.com/myinisjap/agent-task-editor/issues/89_

### What changed

## Code review agent (this session)

Reviewed the branch against the specific prior-review feedback: "shouldn't we also include some way in the UI to initiate the backup also maybe a way to setup an automatic backup".

### Verified implementation

**UI-initiated backup** — `frontend/src/pages/HealthPage.tsx`:
- New "Backup" section with a "Download backup" button that `fetch()`s `GET /api/v1/backup` (with `Authorization` header via `VITE_API_TOKEN`), turns the response into a Blob, and triggers a browser download using the filename from `Content-Disposition` (with a sane client-side fallback).
- Loading/disabled state and error surfacing (`backupError`) are handled.

**Automatic/scheduled backup**:
- `backend/internal/backup/scheduler.go`: a `Scheduler` that ticks on a configurable interval, writes a timestamped `VACUUM INTO` snapshot (`agent-task-editor-<UTC ts>.db`) to a configured directory, and prunes down to a configured retention count, touching only its own filename pattern (safe to point at a shared/non-empty directory). Tested (`scheduler_test.go`): write, prune-keeps-newest, keep<=0 disables pruning.
- Config: `BACKUP_DIR` (empty = disabled), `BACKUP_INTERVAL` (default 24h), `BACKUP_KEEP` (default 7) — env-var driven in `internal/config/config.go`, with defaults and invalid-value warnings, covered by `config_test.go`.
- Wired into `cmd/server/main.go`: scheduler only started when `BACKUP_DIR != ""`, run in a background goroutine tied to the app's shutdown context.
- Visibility: a new `auto_backup` health check (`internal/health/health.go`) reports whether the scheduler is enabled and its settings — surfaced on `GET /api/v1/health/providers` and thus on the Health page, so a disabled/misconfigured scheduler isn't a silent gap.
- `docker-compose.yml` / `docker-compose.release.yml` ship a commented-out `BACKUP_DIR=/data/backups` example reusing the existing `db_data` volume (no new volume needed).
- `docs/backup.md` documents the on-demand endpoint, the UI button, the automatic scheduler (table of env vars, health-check visibility), manual `VACUUM INTO`, a Litestream sidecar example for offsite continuous replication, and a tested restore procedure.

### Endpoint security
Confirmed `GET /api/v1/backup` is registered inside the `r.Group` wrapped with `middleware.BearerAuth(bearerToken)` in `internal/api/router.go` — it is bearer-gated like the rest of `/api/v1`, consistent with the task's "plain bearer until admin tokens exist" proposal.

### Checks run (all green)
- `go build ./...`, `go vet` implied by build — pass
- `go test -count=1 ./...` — all packages pass, including `internal/backup` and updated `internal/config`, `internal/health`, `internal/api/handlers`
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — pass
- `npm run build` — pass
- `npm run test -- --run` — 63/63 pass
- `npm run lint` (oxlint) — pass

### Verdict
The specific review feedback (UI backup trigger + automatic backup setup) is fully and cleanly implemented, well-tested, and documented. No medium/high/critical issues found. Approving.


### Commits

- SQLite backup/restore story (safety-net commit)

author: edugabriel12
body:
## Contexto

PR-2 (final) do plano de expansão de cobertura. O deep-research verificou que a África **não tem modelo de previsão regional** (só globais), e que a "verdade" do Open-Meteo archive lá é **ERA5 reanalysis (~9-25 km, não a estação)**, com viés que **excede o tick de 1°C** dos mercados. O operador decidiu um **piloto pequeno e alto-risco só nas cidades desérticas/subtropicais**, com salvaguardas, e **não operar** a zona de monção/ITCZ (Lagos/Acra/Dacar/Addis/Nairobi), onde o skill de previsão despenca e a verdade é não-confiável.

Este PR entrega esse piloto e **cerca o resto do continente**. Separado do PR-1 (#167, já mergeado) por ser mais pesado (novo caminho de resolução) — revisão isolada e revert fácil.

## Mudanças

**Config — 5 cidades-piloto** (`weather-cities.json`):
- Cairo `HECA`, Casablanca `GMMN`, Argel `DAAG`, Túnis `DTTA`, Joanesburgo `FAOR`, cada uma com `resolution_source: "metar"` + `pilot: true` e **sem `om_models`** (não há modelo regional → trio global default).
- Casablanca/Argel/Túnis adicionadas ao `world` (Cairo/Joanesburgo já existiam) para parsear; `station_names` dos aeroportos; doc `_africa_pilot_doc`.

**Resolução via METAR real** (`weather_edge_helpers.py`, `force_resolution_sweep.py`):
- `fetch_metar_daily_extremes(icao, date)` — max/min observado do dia via `aviationweather.gov` (observações **reais da estação**, grátis, sem key). Fail-open.
- `_observed_value_for` roteia estações-piloto para o METAR e **NUNCA cai no arquivo ERA5**. METAR ausente → `(None, "metar_unavailable")` e o mercado **fica irresolvido de propósito** (o ERA5 é justamente o que o piloto evita).

**Judge — revisão LLM obrigatória** (`weather_edge_judge.py`, `weather-judge-prompt.md`):
- `_entry_is_pilot` + gate em `_judge_route`: entradas-piloto **nunca** pegam rota determinística (nem auto-approve nem cheap_convexity) → sempre revisão LLM completa (guards determinísticos são menos confiáveis na África).
- `review_proposal` injeta `evidence["africa_pilot"]` (high-risk); o prompt instrui a exigir corroboração independente e **preferir ADJUST (tamanho reduzido)** a um APPROVE seco.

**Bot — cerca geográfica** (`weather_edge_bot.py`):
- `_africa_pilot_gate` + caixa continental (lat ∈ [-35, 37], lon ∈ [-18, 52]): candidato africano fora da allow-list → skip `africa_non_pilot` + `insert_discovery_skip`. Operacionaliza "piloto só nas desérticas" (allow-list dentro da África, não bloqueio total).
- Stash `pilot: true` em `discovery_meta_json` para o judge.

**`verify_eu_stations.py`:** lista default estendida com as 5 cidades-piloto (o operador confirma station/coords das Rules antes de operar).

## Verificação (offline; aviationweather/Gamma/Open-Meteo bloqueadas pelo proxy → mocks)

- **Novos:** `--test-metar-resolution` (sweep, 8 casos: parse por-dia, non-200/vazio/sem-obs → None, roteia piloto p/ METAR sem tocar ERA5, `metar_unavailable` sem fallback, EU segue no archive) e `--test-africa-pilot-gate` (bot: caixa, allow-list, fence por-nome, e **piloto força judge full** via `_judge_route`).
- **Regressão completa PASS:** helpers (M6-M8 + suíte), judge (brightsky/ipma/metno/autoroute/cc-route/rule6/sibling-gate/group-sweep/prejudge/anomaly), bot (atomic/orphan/outcome/ladder-cap/cc-discovery/phantom-cashout/dup-token/side-adjust/expired-execute), db (6/6). `py_compile` de todos; JSON válido; todos os valores de `stations` são dicts.

## Ação do operador antes de operar

`python polymarket-analyzer/scripts/verify_eu_stations.py` no host (Gamma acessível) confirma quais dessas cidades a Polymarket lista e a estação real das Rules. Coords atuais são o aeroporto primário padrão — ponto de partida, não verdade confirmada.

## Riscos

- **Verdade de resolução na África:** mesmo nas desérticas, se o METAR faltar o mercado fica irresolvido (deliberado — nunca ERA5 no piloto). Piloto pequeno e alto-risco por design.
- **Coords/estação erradas = trade perdedor** → tudo gated no `verify_eu_stations.py` do operador; pré-preenchimento é só ponto de partida.

Paper-only; §1/§2 da constituição intocados; **nenhuma key nova** (aviationweather é grátis, sem key).

author: gmoro
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The daemonization logic in `proxydhcpd/cli.py` used `os.umask(0)`, which clears the process's file mode creation mask, causing newly created files (like logs) to be world-writable by default (CWE-732).
🎯 Impact: Local attackers could potentially modify daemon log files or other files created by the service, leading to log spoofing or tampering.
🔧 Fix: Changed `os.umask(0)` to a secure file creation mask `os.umask(0o022)` during daemonization.
✅ Verification: Ran full pytest test suite to ensure no regressions in daemonization. Tested using Python 3.12.

body:
## What & why
When someone fills out a website lead form, the `lead.new` notification previously said only "New lead · <form name>" — the admin had to open the app to learn who submitted or what they wanted. This enriches the alert so the **bell, Web Push, and email** all carry the actual submission, with the email formatted as a UPR-branded card.

## Scope
- **In:** `functions/api/form-submit.js` — a pure content builder (`buildLeadNotificationContent` / `leadNotificationRows`) that turns the submitted form fields into a title (with the lead's name), a plain-text body for the bell + OS push (every answered field, long free-text truncated), and a design-system HTML card for the email (`#1e293b` brand header, white card, `--text-*` / `--accent` palette, a "View lead" button). Wired into the existing `notifyNewLeadFromForm` hook + its call site.
- **Deliberately out:** No change to the dispatcher (`notify.js`), the event catalog, audience/prefs, or any other notification type — this only enriches the payload the `lead.new` form hook already sends. No schema/migrations (the form data is passed in-process, not re-queried). CallRail-call leads keep their existing body (separate hook, unchanged).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Bell + push body lists the submitted fields (name, phone, email, message, etc.)
- [x] Email renders a branded UPR card with the full submission and a link to the lead
- [x] Consent + honeypot fields are omitted; multi-select answers join cleanly
- [x] All submitted values are HTML-escaped in the email (untrusted public input)
- [x] Degrades to the prior generic line if no schema/data is available

## Tests
- [x] Tests added/updated: `functions/api/lead-notify.test.js` — content across channels, HTML escaping of a `<script>` value, multi-select join, consent/honeypot skip, and the schema-less fallback (5 new cases; 10 total in the file)
- [x] `npm test` green — 934 passed / 137 skipped

## Verification actually run
- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [x] `npm run lint` — `eslint` on both changed files: no errors (no new baseline errors)
- [x] Rendered the email HTML from a representative submission and eyeballed the branded card + verified the plain-text body
- Notes: No live-data/schema work — this is a payload-formatting change; the form data flows in-process from the submit handler.

## Docs
- [ ] `UPR-Web-Context.md` — no table/RPC/component/page/worker surface changed (same worker, same `lead.new` event); left untouched. Will add a note if reviewer prefers.
- [x] Other docs updated (if relevant): none needed

## Risk / not done
- Low risk: the hook is fire-and-forget (a notify failure never breaks form intake) and the enrichment degrades gracefully. The `lead.new` type is already enabled (Session B); this changes only what the notification says, not whether it fires.
- The email card visual is best confirmed on the Cloudflare branch preview / a real send, since a real Resend send needs the deployed env.
