body:
## What

The `SwissSet<T, THasher>` class remarks describe it as a drop-in peer of `CeleritySet` sharing "the same `IEnumerable<T>` surface". `SwissSet` actually implements `ISet<T>` (and thus exposes `UnionWith`/`IntersectWith`/`IsSubsetOf`/etc.). This changes the cref to `ISet<T>`.

## Why

All three sibling specialized sets describe the shared surface as `ISet<T>` — `HashCachingSet` ("the same `ISet<T>` surface"), `RobinHoodSet` (same), and `PooledCeleritySet` ("the full `ISet<T>` set-algebra surface"). The type `SwissSet` claims parity with, `CeleritySet`, is itself declared `: ISet<T>`. The `IEnumerable<T>` wording is a copy-adapt slip from `SwissDictionary`'s remarks (which reference `IReadOnlyDictionary`), understating the documented surface. Doc-only, no code change.

- [x] `dotnet build` (Celerity) — succeeds
- [ ] `dotnet test` — not run (XML-doc-only change, no runtime effect)

author: merlimat
body:
Improvements to `scripts/run-comparison.sh` surfaced by running the comparison on an EKS spot cluster.

- **Tolerate transient `CrashLoopBackOff`.** Spot-node preemption / OOM during Karpenter scale-up briefly crash-loops pods; the old fail-fast bailed on the *first* `CrashLoopBackOff`. Now it bails immediately only on unrecoverable **image** errors (`ImagePullBackOff`/`ErrImagePull`/`InvalidImageName`), and treats `CrashLoopBackOff` as terminal only once a container has restarted `CRASH_RESTART_LIMIT` times (default 5).
- **Dump the crashing pods before the sweep.** When it does bail on a crash loop, print each crashing pod's container states + `--previous` logs, so the failure reason lands in the run output instead of being swept away.
- **`WORKER_CPU` knob** to override the per-backend worker CPU request/limit, mirroring the existing `WORKER_REPLICAS`.

## Verification
Used across the YCSB comparison + scaling sweeps: the tolerance let oxia survive transient spot churn (a run that previously aborted), and the restart limit correctly distinguished a genuine crash loop from a transient one, dumping its reason.

author: awwaiid
body: Follow-up to #8 (ENG-629), from an install on hermes-cloud. ## Problem On Docker/cloud images the gateway runs under an s6 supervisor (`s6-supervise gateway-`). The setup wizard's `hermes gateway restart` can't reliably cycle it there — the wizard runs inside the gateway's own process tree, so the supervisor keeps (or respawns) the **old** process, which started before the plugin was installed and never loads the Filament adapter. The install looks successful, but the gateway never picks up the plugin or the saved `.env`. ## Change After the setup wizard finishes, ask the supervisor directly: for each live gateway service slot under `/run/service` (`gateway-*` / `hermes-gateway-*` with a `supervise/control` FIFO present), send `s6-svc -t` so the supervisor SIGTERMs and respawns the service with the plugin loaded. Details matched against upstream `NousResearch/hermes-agent`: - `-t` (SIGTERM + respawn) is the same action as upstream's `S6ServiceManager.restart`. - s6-overlay keeps its binaries in `/command`, which is rarely on PATH — probed explicitly after `command -v`. - Only slots the supervisor has actually brought up are poked (control FIFO check), skipping half-built registration slots. - On non-s6 systems the whole block is a silent no-op, and `s6-svc` failures never fail the installer (`|| true`). ## Testing Exercised the block in isolation under `bash -euo pipefail` against a simulated tree: plain host with no s6 (silent no-op, exit 0), a live `gateway-default` slot alongside a half-built slot and an unrelated service (only the live gateway got `s6-svc -t`), and an `s6-svc` that exits non-zero (installer still exits 0). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) 🌒 Run on Niteshift: [View Task](https://niteshift.dev/repo/filament-dm/filament-hermes/task_vz6iycj887mtsd8j) > [!NOTE] > ### Force a supervised gateway restart after setup on s6 images > - Adds a post-setup section to [install.sh](https://github.com/filament-dm/filament-hermes/pull/11/files#diff-043df5bdbf6639d7a77e1d44c5226fd7371e5259a1e4df3a0dd5d64c30dca44f) that detects `s6-svc` (from `PATH` or `/command`) and sends `SIGTERM` via `s6-svc -t` to restart the supervised gateway for the current Hermes profile. > - Tries profile-specific service slots (`gateway-` and `hermes-gateway-`) under `/run/service`, falling back to any live matching `gateway-*` services if neither slot exists. > - Adds `warn()` and `restart_slot()` helpers: `restart_slot()` treats `s6-svc` failures as non-fatal warnings, only returning failure when no live slot is found. > - No-op on systems without `s6-svc`. > > > > Macroscope summarized 238e508. > >

body:
## What this is (the C7 analog for detection — closes P-D)
`host/events/detection_bench.py` runs ALL 5 real detectors (contact / current_spike / impact / slip / vibration) over the labeled scenario suite, scores each via D1 `score_events` vs `ground_truth_events` into a frozen `DetectionReport` whose P/R **re-derive at construction** (a forged report can't load). `gate(reports, thresholds)` — explicit per-detector min precision/recall; an ungated report or a threshold for an absent detector **raises** (no always-pass by omission); determinism enforced. CLI `python -m events.detection_bench --out DIR` writes `docs/bench/P-D-DETECTION.{json,md}` and exits 0 iff the gate passed.

## Provable failure
`--cripple` swaps the detectors for `noop` → every recall drops to 0.0 → gate **FAILS, exit 1**. Proven in-test and by CLI.

## MEASURED (committed `docs/bench/P-D-DETECTION`, seed 7)
| detector | scenario | kinds | precision | recall | f1 | neg FP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| contact | slip_recovery | contact_start/release | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0 |
| current_spike | current_spike_jam | current_spike | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0 |
| impact | slip_recovery | impact | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0 |
| slip | slip_recovery | slip | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0 |
| vibration | slip_recovery | impact | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0 |
| vibration | slip_recovery | slip | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0 |

All deterministic; all negative-scenario false-positives = 0.

## Evidence
- **53 tests** both directions: gate passes the real suite AND fails `--cripple`; CLI exit 0 vs 1 (incl. `python -m` subprocess); `from_dict` rejects forged counts / missing / unknown keys; determinism byte-identical.

## What & why

OpenSpec change `dedupe-night-vibe-suggestions` (archived in this PR): "Suggest from your cooking" piled up 48 redundant pending `add_vibe` proposals in production (one member had six chicken-stir-fry paraphrases, four fish-taco variants). The derivation now dedups **every** candidate source (clusters and cold start alike) in phrase space against the palette, pending proposals, rejected proposals, and within the run — one batched, KV-cached embedding call at threshold 0.85. author: nrdptel
body:
## What

The `Segmented` control — the app's most-used control, behind the **mode**, **system**, **diameter**, and **sort** toggles — was built as a `role="group"` of `aria-pressed` toggle buttons. That's valid and axe-clean, but for a **mutually-exclusive single-select** the correct WAI-ARIA pattern is a **radio group**. This switches it over:

- `role="radiogroup"` with `role="radio"` options and `aria-checked` (screen readers now announce "radio, checked, N of M" instead of a pile of independent toggle buttons).
- **Roving tabindex** — only the checked option is in the tab order, so the whole group is a single tab stop.
- **Arrow / Home / End** move the selection, with focus following — so keyboard users don't tab through every option to get past the toggle.

## Why

It's a concrete accessibility improvement to a primitive used everywhere in the tool, and the more idiomatic pattern for the single-select toggles. Purely a hardening change.

## Notes

- **No API or visual change.** Every consumer (mode / system / diameter / sort) is untouched — the props are identical and the styling is the same.
- Guarded against focus traps: if nothing is selected, the first option stays tabbable.

## Verified

Local gate green: eslint clean, **104 unit** tests, `next build` (634 static pages), **25 Playwright e2e** — the toggles are now selected by their `radio` role, plus a **new keyboard-navigation test** that drives the mode toggle entirely with Arrow keys (asserting `aria-checked` moves, focus follows, and the view switches). The **axe WCAG audit stays green in light and dark**, including on the populated result view where the toggles live.

author: jmg698
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #46. That PR fixed the `sigstore` provenance crash (it worked — provenance now signs), but the next publish attempt failed with a different, misleading error:

```
npm error code E404
npm error 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/font-lab - Not found
npm error 404  'font-lab@9.23.3' is not in this registry.
```

The package exists and is ours (`font-lab`, `latest: 0.12.2`), so a 404 looks nonsensical — but the **job log is conclusive**:

```
npm: 10.9.8                                   # setup-node's bundled npm
Preparing npm@11.16.0 for immediate activation...
10.9.8                                        # `npm -v` AFTER corepack — unchanged!
...
npm error code E404 ... PUT .../font-lab - Not found
```

**Root cause:** `corepack prepare npm@… --activate` does **not** override the npm that setup-node put on PATH — Corepack's shims lose PATH precedence, so the publish ran on **npm 10.9.8**. npm 10.x can't perform the npm **OIDC trusted-publishing handshake** (requires ≥ 11.5.1). When the handshake fails, the registry treats the request as **anonymous**, and an anonymous publish returns a misleading **E404** rather than a 401/403. (Confirmed the `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` in the log is the empty `XXXXX` placeholder, so auth genuinely depends on the OIDC handshake.)

Separately, the log shows the version input was `v09.23.3` → npm "cleaned" the leading zero to `9.23.3`. That's a manual-input slip, not the cause of the 404, but worth guarding against.

## Fix (three parts)

1. **Pin npm with `npm install -g npm@11.18.0`** — the mechanism that *actually* replaces the bundled npm (it's what upgraded 0.12.0–0.12.2). Drops the Corepack lines that silently no-op'd. Exact pin, never `@latest` (that pulled the broken npm 12.0.0 behind #46's sigstore failure).
2. **Bump the publish job to Node 24** — its bundled npm is OIDC-capable, and it's immune to the Node 22.22 in-place-upgrade corruption ([npm/cli#9151](https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/9151)) that caused the original sigstore break. Node 22's bundled npm 10.9.x was the trap.
3. **Assert `npm -v` ≥ 11.5.1 as a named step** — so a silent version miss (like Corepack's) fails loudly *here* instead of resurfacing as a cryptic E404 at publish.

Also tightens the "Derive version" regex to reject leading zeros (`09.23.3` → clear error up front).

## Verification

Both shell snippets unit-tested locally:
- Regex rejects `09.23.3`, `00.1.2`, `0.012.3`; accepts `0.12.3`, `1.0.0`, `0.9.2-beta.1`.
- Version gate fails `10.9.8`/`11.5.0`, passes `11.5.1`/`11.18.0`.
- `npm@11.18.0` confirmed to exist on the registry; YAML validated.

Full end-to-end (the OIDC PUT) can only be exercised by a real release run.

## How to re-release 0.12.3 after merge

Nothing has published — `0.12.3` is still free. Recommended: **delete the existing `v0.12.3` release + tag on GitHub, then recreate the release tagged `v0.12.3`.** The `release: published` trigger runs this fixed workflow and derives the version from the tag (`0.12.3`) — so there's no manual version box to fat-finger. (A manual *Run workflow* also works now; just type `0.12.3`, not `09.23.3`.)

author: jf888trade-creator
body:
## Problem

BUG-001 reports that newly added expenses don't appear at the top of the expense list. Steps to reproduce confirmed it: add an expense dated today, and it can land anywhere in the list instead of at the top.

Root cause, in `Api::ExpensesController#index`:

```ruby
expenses = Expense.includes(:category).order(created_at: :desc)
...
expenses = expenses.where(created_at: start_date.beginning_of_day..end_date.end_of_day)
```

Both the ordering and the month/year filter used `created_at` (when the row was inserted) instead of `date` (the expense's actual date, which is what the calendar UI is keyed on and what users pick in the form). Two concrete failure modes:

1. **Ordering**: if you add an expense for today but it's not the most recently *inserted* row overall (e.g. you also just edited an older expense, or seed data was inserted out of order), it won't sort to the top, even though its `date` is the most recent.
2. **Filtering**: navigating to a given month/year on the calendar filtered by `created_at`, so an expense entered late for a *past* month would show up under the *current* month instead of the month it's actually dated for -- and vice versa.

## Fix

Changed both the `order` and the `where` clause to use the `date` column (with `created_at` as a secondary sort key to keep ordering stable for same-day entries):

```ruby
expenses = Expense.includes(:category).order(date: :desc, created_at: :desc)
...
expenses = expenses.where(date: start_date..end_date)
```

This is a one-line-per-clause fix, but it aligns the API with how the rest of the app already treats `date` as the source of truth (the calendar view, the expense form's date picker, etc.).

## Tests

- Replaced the existing ordering spec (which only asserted ordering between two same-day expenses and happened to pass under the old `created_at` ordering too) with a spec that creates an expense whose `date` is in the past but whose `created_at` is the most recent, asserting it now sorts *after* today's expenses.
- Added a new spec for the year/month filter asserting it's scoped by `date`, not `created_at`, by creating an expense dated last month but created just now, and confirming it's excluded from the current month's results.

## Note on scope

This branch also includes a handful of small, unrelated Docker fixes (see #2) that were necessary just to get `docker compose up` working at all on this machine -- they're included here only because the reviewer needs them to actually run the app; I opened a separate PR for them (#2) so it can be reviewed on its own merits.

author: fullmetal-fred
body:
## SHIP REVIEW — feat: principal lifecycle console UI (archive rename + IAM form hardening)

**Closes #146, completes #143 (epic #27).**

**Outcome:** an operator runs the full principal lifecycle from the user blade (suspend → archive → purge), the verbs read pause → remove → destroy, and the IAM create/edit forms validate inline and populate in one flow.

**Verdict:** ready-pending-your-call (two naming confirmations below).

### Scope
- **Lifecycle console UI (#146).** The user blade's footer presents the lifecycle by state: the left slot is the reversible toggle (**Disable / Enable**, or **Restore** for an archived account); the kebab holds the escalating red steps (**Archive** when live, **Purge** when archived and the caller holds `principal:purge:admin`), each confirmed. A **Show archived** toggle on the Users directory (`include_archived` param) surfaces hidden accounts; the detail fetches the principal by id so a just-archived user stays resolvable.
- **Rename deactivate → archive.** "Disable" and "deactivate" read as synonyms. Renamed the soft-delete step **deactivate → archive** and **reactivate → restore**, end-to-end for API-first coherence: column `deactivated_at → archived_at` (new idempotent migration), storage `ArchivePrincipal` / `RestorePrincipal`, endpoints `:archive` / `:restore`, capability `principal:archive`, list param `include_archived`, console labels, regenerated OpenAPI + client + CLI. Recorded in ADR-0016.
- **Blade closes on removal.** Archiving, purging (and a group delete) close the blade first, drop the dead detail query, then refresh the list, so the blade never lingers on a stale or 404 view of the entity it just removed.
- **Impersonation reboots to Home.** Starting or stopping impersonation hard-reloads (`window.location`) so the permission-driven sidebar and route guard rebuild from the new identity. (Self-impersonation stays blocked: a 422, unconditional, plus hidden in the UI.)
- **Inline form validation (API-first).** A username and a group name are lowercase handles (`pattern:^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$`, no capitals or spaces); an email must be well-formed (`format:email`). Enforced on the server create body (Huma, 422) and mirrored in the forms: an invalid field shows an inline error and disables the submit before the round-trip. A new `valid` gate on the blade edit contract disables the footer **Save** the same way.
- **Create in one flow.** A newly created **user or group** opens directly in edit mode with the grant builder (and, for a group, the member picker) live, so grants and members are added right away and one Save commits them, rather than a create-then-edit second step.
- **Copy consistency.** The group create Drawer title read "New principal_group" (leaked the resource key) and now reads **New group**; the group create form gained the subtitle the user form has; placeholders are consistent across create and edit.

**Thin cut:** `principal:archive` rides admin's existing `principal:*` wildcard (no roles.yaml change). Group *edit* does not validate a name (that form edits only display-name + description; name is not renamable there). **Deferred:** group-scoped principal administration (#149).

**Surfaces:** API `:archive` / `:restore` / `:purge`, `include_archived`, `pattern`/`format` on the create bodies · CLI `principal archive` / `restore` / `purge` (generated) · UI Users + Groups directories, the blade footer, and both create forms (live).

### Proof (ran fresh)
- `go test -count=1 ./...`: **green**, all packages (api 23.1s, storage 17.2s, e2e 13.6s, migrate 9.3s exercising the rename migration, seed/devseed, plus the unit tiers). New `TestPrincipalCreateValidation` (a malformed username, group name, or email is a 422; a valid one is accepted).
- Web: `vitest` **195 tests / 26 files**; `tsc --noEmit` clean; `make gen` clean.
- Load-bearing web tests: the blade closes without an orphan refetch on archive/purge/delete; an invalid field blocks create and the footer Save; a created user and group land in edit mode.

### Visual confirmation (live, isolated Postgres)
**Lifecycle** — live user (Disable + Archive, no Purge) · Show archived (red badge) · archived user (Restore + Purge):
![live](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c4e7b3f9-a77a-4032-a3f9-136842bff51a)
![show archived](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/150df5f9-2c68-4944-89cd-4114a81dffdf)
![restore purge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6fde77a1-63db-40e9-85c9-ddbc8e775ccb)

**Inline validation** — invalid username (error + disabled Create) · group drawer fixed to "New group" with subtitle + the same handle rule:
![user validation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46908164-a7e9-445f-a53d-27d91dd9f522)
![group validation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9b8c756-2b0b-4d97-b7bf-96ac6220a958)

**Create in one flow** — new group and new user both open directly in edit mode:
![group create in edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c93ae8c5-047a-41b8-a16b-8b784268abef)
![user create in edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52e13a8d-d895-45ea-a71e-7b2f582eb5da)

### Docs
identity-access (lifecycle verbs), ADR-0016 (archive terminology + a Naming note recording the rename), console guide (lifecycle footer, Show archived, username/group format + inline validation, create-in-edit), CLI guide, status.mdx (lifecycle + hardening entries). Arch-of-record consistent.

### Decisions I made (your veto window)

author: rrhester
body:
Third and final surface for "make the dark sidebar reach the top."

## The real cause (for the ChromeOS install)
The screenshot is the **installed PWA on a Chromebook**, running in plain `standalone` display mode — **not** window-controls-overlay and **not** the Electron desktop app. In standalone mode there's no WCO band; Chrome paints the **entire window title bar from the manifest `theme_color`**, which was light rail-blue (`#EFF6FF`). That's the light strip — the earlier WCO band (#3631) and Electron (#3634) fixes don't touch it.

## Change
- `manifest.webmanifest` `theme_color` and the `index.html` `<meta name="theme-color">` → **`#071E2F`** (the dark rail navy, `--rr-nav-bg` = the sidebar's top color).
- Chrome now paints the title bar navy and auto-switches the min/max/close glyphs to light for contrast, so the sidebar reads as reaching the very top of the window.
- `SW_DEPLOY_NONCE` bumped so installed apps refresh.

## Notes
- No CSS/JS logic changed; the title bar is browser chrome, so **render pixels are unaffected** — visual-regression baselines and the design-lint ratchet are untouched.
- **Timing:** Chrome applies a new `theme_color` when it next re-reads the installed app's manifest (a background update, or immediately on reinstall) — so this may take a app relaunch or two to appear, or you can reinstall the PWA for it right away.

Together with #3631 (WCO band) and #3634 (Electron desktop), all three install surfaces now render the dark rail to the top of the window.

author: hardlydifficult
body:
## Summary

Enforce source-security lifecycle invariants on current `main`: known issuance quantities cannot be reduced below zero, terminal events retire their source, and lifecycle events cannot predate issuance.

Covered reductions:

- stock cancellations, repurchases, transfers, conversions, reissuances, consolidations, and retractions
- warrant cancellations, transfers, exercises, and retractions; unknown issuance quantities still preserve terminal-event semantics
- equity-compensation cancellations, transfers, exercises, releases, and retractions

Direct stock-class splits are applied chronologically to stock issuances and equity-compensation issuances with an explicit `stock_class_id`. Because OCF records calendar dates without intra-day ordering, same-day events use the lowest-balance valid ordering: a same-day reverse split is included when it may reduce the issuance balance, while a same-day forward split is excluded when the issuance may already be post-split.

## Deliberate exclusions

This PR does not validate successor identity, `balance_security_id` materialization, resulting-security continuity, predecessor graphs, terminal completeness, or inferred stock-plan class lineage. Those remain separate rules.

Warrant issuances with no quantity cannot be numerically balance-checked. A warrant exercise with omitted quantity is treated as a full retirement of the source security.

## Version and branch

- Base: `main`, including merged #280
- Exact head: `bec4cfd5f85059c099acb579d6b58aba7f9896bb`
- Contract package: `OpenCapTable-v34 0.0.3`
- The single undeployed mutable `0.0.3` DAR and lock entry were rebuilt from the combined source.

## Validation

- multi-package DAML build: passed
- full DAML script suite: passed, including same-day and later-date split regressions
- DAML lint: no hints
- DAR integrity and version policy: passed
- ESLint: 0 errors, 2 pre-existing warnings
- Prettier: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- read-only same-day issuance/split audit: 0 matches in dev, 0 matches in production
- exact-head dev replay: **passed** ([run](https://github.com/Fairmint/open-captable-protocol-daml/actions/runs/30019707087)); every source object passed strict OCF schema validation and the cap table converged on LocalNet
- exact-head production replay: **baseline-equivalent failure** ([run](https://github.com/Fairmint/open-captable-protocol-daml/actions/runs/30019708939)); failure phases are unchanged from current main: `batch`, `conversion`, and `schema`

## Dev data correction

Four old Protelicious equity-compensation issuances recorded `quantity: "4"` while their vestings totaled `7.9998` and their sole exercise consumed `8`. With approval, dev-only version 3 rows were appended changing only `quantity` to `"8"`; version 2 remains preserved. Independent read-only verification passed, and the definitive exact-head dev replay subsequently converged without any failure.

<!-- OCP_REPLAY_ARTIFACTS_START -->
## Exact-head replay artifacts (2026-07-23)

- Contract SHA: `bec4cfd5f85059c099acb579d6b58aba7f9896bb`
- Dev: [passed](https://github.com/Fairmint/open-captable-protocol-daml/actions/runs/30019707087) with zero failure phases; every source object passed strict OCF schema validation and converged; replay duration 12m32s
- Production: [failed](https://github.com/Fairmint/open-captable-protocol-daml/actions/runs/30019708939) in the same `batch`, `conversion`, and `schema` phases as the [current-main baseline](https://github.com/Fairmint/open-captable-protocol-daml/actions/runs/29974148252); replay duration 4m48s
- Traffic: dev 8.244 MB / $137.43 equivalent; production 3.663 MB / $61.07 equivalent
- Review: exact-head CI, DAR integrity, Copilot, Codex, and Cursor are clean; no unresolved review threads

<!-- OCP_REPLAY_ARTIFACTS_END -->

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core cap-table acceptance logic for all stock, warrant, and equity-comp lifecycle batches; incorrect split or retirement ordering could reject valid production data or miss invalid states.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **post-batch validation** on `UpdateCapTable` so a known issuance quantity cannot be driven below zero by recorded lifecycle events on that `security_id`.
> 
> The contract introduces `SecurityBalanceEvent` (reductions, retirements, class splits as multipliers), aggregates events for **stock**, **warrant**, and **equity compensation** issuances, and runs `validateSourceSecurityBalances` after each batch. It rejects cumulative overdraws, pre-issuance reductions, further reductions after **retraction / reissuance / consolidation / full warrant exercise**, and ambiguous **same-day** split vs reduction ordering (OCF has calendar dates only). Splits on a **later** date scale balances; same-day forward splits on issuance are not assumed to inflate pre-recorded quantities.
> 
> **DAML script coverage** is expanded across cancellations, transfers, exercises, releases, repurchases, conversions, and split edge cases, with small test-helper tweaks (e.g. configurable EC grant size). **`OpenCapTable-v34` 0.0.3** DAR and lock metadata are updated to ship the new rules.

Wave 1B of the post-#196/#197 continuation — hardens the `preview-ui-walk` skill against the false green its own docs warned about, and ships the authed path it previously only described in prose. **Skill-only** (no app code).

## 1. Playwright authed-login driver — `references/playwright_walk.mjs` (new)
The preview MCP blocks 302s, so a cookie/redirect login silently stays on the pre-login page (false green). This driver drives the box's **cached Chromium directly via `playwright-core`**:
- Mints the session cookie server-side with `curl -c jar -L` (curl follows the login redirects and keeps the `Set-Cookie` the MCP block drops).
- Auto-discovers `playwright-core` from the npx cache via `createRequire` (ESM `import` ignores `NODE_PATH`), and the newest cached chromium build (probing the real `chrome-linux64/chrome` layout, with `PW_CHROMIUM`/`PW_CORE` overrides).
- Injects the cookie, then navigates / screenshots / collects console+network per page, read-only.

**Verified end-to-end** against a throwaway redirect-login server: cookie mint + authed pages PASS, and a page that bounces to `/login` correctly **FAILS** (report shows "redirected to…").

## 2. Per-page landed-URL verification (both drivers)
`playwright_walk.mjs` reads `page.url()`, `walk.py` reads the observed current URL; each **FAILs a page when the landed URL doesn't match** its `lands_on`/`path`. A gated page bounced to `/login` no longer PASSes on a 200 + screenshot alone — the core false-green fix. `walk.py` surfaces the redirect in its HTML report.

## 3. Second worked manifest — `references/authed-admin-example.json` (new)
Demonstrates the `login.type: "cookie"` + per-page `lands_on` shape for the Playwright driver, alongside the existing session-inject `onebackend-v3-superadmin.json`.

`manifest-schema.md` + `SKILL.md` updated: document `login.type: "cookie"`, `pages[].lands_on`, and route the login step to the right driver by auth model.

author: anderdc
body:
## The real bug is the duplication

#127 fixed `toFixed(2)` in the dashboard's `RatesTicker`. The miners page's `StickyNetworkHeader` carried a **byte-identical copy** of the same eyebrow markup, so it kept rendering a BTC quote (~`0.0021` SOL) as a flat **`0.00`**. Its own comment even admitted the relationship — *"Mirrors the miners-page StickyNetworkHeader eyebrow"* — but they were copies, so fixing one silently skipped the other.

So: fix the duplication, not the copy.

## Shared component

Extracted **`CrownDirectionSegment`** — the `👑 sol → btc  uid 2 @ 0.0021 SOL` segment — now used by both `StickyNetworkHeader` (miners) and `RatesTicker` (dashboard). They differed in exactly two ways, both now props:

- the no-holder wording (`none` vs `no crown`) → `emptyLabel`
- the dashboard's trailing EMA rate → `children`

Rate formatting lives in one place, so the next fix can't miss a caller. **Net −73 lines.**

## Remaining rate sites → `formatRate` (RATE_SIG_FIGS = 5)

| site | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| `MinerDetailHeader` — `QUOTE · SOL → BTC` tiles | `0.00` | `0.0021` |
| `CrownGridHoverCard` — hover `rate` line | `0.00` | `0.0021` |
| `OrderbookDepth` — price-level key | `0.00` | `0.0021` |

**`OrderbookDepth` was not cosmetic.** That value is the bucket key: it groups miners into price levels, sorts the book, is the React key, *and* is rendered verbatim as the level. At 2dp every BTC-scale quote rounded to `"0.00"`, so the whole book **collapsed into a single bogus level with summed capacity**. Distinct levels now survive:

```
0.0019 / 0.0021 / 0.00215 / 0.0022     (all four were "0.00")
```

`parseFloat`-based sorting still works on the formatted key (`parseFloat("0.0021") === 0.0021`).

## Deliberately left alone

Amounts and percentages are not rates — collateral, volume, success rate, crown share keep their `toFixed`. `CrownRateChart`'s axis formatter is already magnitude-aware (`abs >= 0.001 → toFixed(4)`), so `0.0021` renders correctly there.

## Verification

`tsc -b`, `eslint --max-warnings 0`, prettier clean. Driven in a browser against the **live test API**:

- miners page header → `SOL → BTC uid 2 @ 0.0021 SOL` (was `@ 0.00 SOL`)
- miner drilldown → `QUOTE · SOL → BTC  0.0021 SOL` (was `0.00 SOL`)
- dashboard ticker → still `0.0021`, and the `healthy` / `last refresh` segments are intact — regression check that the extraction didn't change the dashboard

6/6 assertions pass, including `"@ 0.00 SOL"` appearing nowhere on any of the three pages.

author: pierrel
body:
Implements `docs/2026-07-08-research-audit.org` (Part 5), guidance-first. The audit's key finding: the two asks **converge** — search-unavailability was the trigger for the worst redundancy runaways (peptides 78×, b37c712b 108k), so honest partial handling is also the top redundancy fix.

## Changes
- **Searcher guidance** (`sub_research.txt.j2`): keyed on a *checkable* condition — if an earlier search this turn returned results, **use them** (only what they contain, **never from memory**) + one honest sentence that some searches couldn't complete; else stop + relay. (Fixes the 2026-07-02 "gave up and discarded a good result" failure.)
- **Orchestrator** (`research_instructions.txt.j2`): write the best report from *any* usable findings (carry the caveat); **dispatch the research-agent exactly once** — dropped the ambiguous "genuinely failed" re-dispatch loophole (the multiplier behind the peptides runaway).
- **`SearchUnavailableBreaker`**: rewritten from strip-to-dead-end (which discarded gathered results — the 2026-06-05 volume-cap anti-pattern) to **finalize-not-kill** (`wrap_tool_call` + a corrective ToolMessage, the reread-breaker pattern): refuse further searches, nudge the model to answer from what it gathered. No `jump_to` needed.
- **Removed** a per-call "PARTIAL RESULTS" note from `search_internet`: real-SearXNG data showed 3/4 healthy queries have a throttled engine (brave/ddg) yet return 17–32 results, so it would falsely caveat nearly every report + self-throttle the searcher.
- `sub_critique.txt.j2`: removed a dead "use the search tool" line (the critique agent has no tools).

## Review + eval
- **Design-review + 2-lens code-review**: the correctness/breaker lens came back clean (the `wrap_tool_call` rewrite is the proven pattern — no dangling-tool_call hang); the guidance lens caught the b1 misfire (removed) + a missing never-from-memory guard (added). All addressed.
- **Eval** (`edd/eval/test_research_partial_results.py`, mocked search): mixed-burst (first search good, rest rate-limited) keeps the good result + refuses memory-fabrication; all-unavailable relays without fabricating. Eval-first, N≥3 in progress.
- 1012 unit tests green.

Audit doc + design decisions (prose caveat over sentinel; guidance over tool-serialization; dispatch-once) on the branch. Not deployed/merged — for review.

## Slice 3b — the DnD port + reorder + preview-click selection sync

The **sanctioned legacy code port** (CANVAS_RULES §7, the ONE exception to never-port-legacy) lands in `finalBuilderCanvas`:

- **Capture-phase gatekeeper** owns `preventDefault` + edge auto-scroll — a stable native cursor, no flicker (highlights are applied imperatively, never via re-render).
- **One validity predicate** feeds cursor AND highlight: palette fields only into parent-context field sections (never repeaters, never gaps — §1), elements only between sections sharing a data-context signature (§2, hooks ready for repeaters), sections/pages anywhere. Rejection = native no-drop, **no toasts**.
- Adaptations: spec ids; the palette is a separate component now, so the drag kind rides a **typed dataTransfer marker** (drag data is protected until drop — types aren't); gap drop zones between sections; `bc-` prefixed highlight classes.

**Studio mutations** behind canvas intents (all through the one `_mutate`/autosave path, read-only-guarded): `dropfield` at position (incl. page-chip drops that ensure a section + switch the blueprint there), `moveelement` (within/between sections, cross-page via chips), `movesection` (gaps/reorder/cross-page), `movepage` (blueprint keeps showing the page you were on).

**Preview-click selection sync** (P3 requirement): clicking an element in the live preview selects it on the blueprint, switches to its page, and opens properties. Org QA caught the fun one: **synthetic shadow retargets `composedPath`**, so the viewer can't resolve clicks itself (jsdom said yes, LEX said no) — the section renderer announces a composed `elementclick`, an `authoring` viewer re-emits `elementselect`, guest renders swallow it. No nav shell knows.

**Deferred to the properties/blocks slice**: content-block gap drops + the repeater flow (§4) — picker/inspector/renderer don't exist yet; context signatures are already enforced (jest covers the repeater-refusal rule).

**Tooling fixes riding along**: lint-staged serialized (`--concurrent 1`) + jest `--maxWorkers=2` — the default config SIGKILLed itself on this machine; eslint test-file override for `no-async-operation`/`prefer-custom-event` (standard jest patterns); viewer's last `catch (e)` debt paid. The pre-commit hook now passes clean — no `--no-verify` anywhere.

## Verification
- jest **402/402** (6 new canvas DnD tests incl. gatekeeper matrix + repeater refusal, palette marker test, studio mutation tests, viewer authoring-click pair).
- Deployed to revcloud@dev.com; Playwright end-to-end **ALL PASS**: reorder swap + restore, palette drag-in (append via header, insert-before via row), preview-click opens the right properties, cleanup removal; owner's draft left exactly as found. Screenshots eyeballed.

author: russfellows
body:
## Summary

Multi-agent bug audit fix release. Closes a coordinated 7-issue, 39-bug audit of s3dlio HEAD (post-v0.9.108), spanning the Rust core (S3/Azure/GCS backends, multipart upload lifecycle, range GET/RangeEngine, URI parsing) and the Python DLIO integration layer.

The audit fanned out 8 specialized reviewers by subsystem, then adversarially verified every finding with an independent skeptic that defaulted to refuting. Every surviving finding lands in this PR, organized into six phases by severity/blast-radius, plus internal version bumps at the two natural boundaries (v0.9.109 after Phase C, v0.9.110 after Phase F):

| Phase | Theme | Bugs | Landed as |
|-------|-------|------|-----------|
| A | Silent data corruption / silent commit | 4 | v0.9.109 |
| B | Wrong data returned to caller, reachable from public API | 10 | v0.9.109 |
| C | Silent failure elimination | 6 | v0.9.109 |
| D | Backend correctness / hygiene | 9 | v0.9.110 |
| E | Edge cases / low severity | 4 | v0.9.110 |
| F | Env-var/config-ignored, plus one docs fix | 4 | v0.9.110 |
| **Total** | | **39** | |

Every fix landed with a RED-then-GREEN regression test: written first, verified to fail against unmodified code for the exact reason the bug describes, then verified to pass after the fix — per this repo's CLAUDE.md §6 policy.

**Test count: 748 passing** across the full suite (every `cargo test` binary — lib unit tests plus every `tests/*.rs` integration file — across the relevant feature combinations), up from 689 at the start of this work, plus the Python DLIO integration suite (`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `python -m compileall`, `uv run pytest`) all clean.

## Issues closed

This PR was filed as 7 coordinated issues from one audit pass. All 7 are fully closed by this PR:

| # | Issue | Bugs | Area |
|---|-------|------|------|
| [#151](https://github.com/russfellows/s3dlio/issues/151) | Multipart upload lifecycle: silent partial-commit and staged-block leaks | 6 | Rust multipart drop/abort/complete paths (S3 + Azure) |
| [#152](https://github.com/russfellows/s3dlio/issues/152) | Range GET and range engine: silent data corruption and length=0 handling | 8 | Rust range/get_range paths (all backends) |
| [#153](https://github.com/russfellows/s3dlio/issues/153) | Python DLIO integration: silent failures and API correctness | 10 | `python/s3dlio/integrations/dlio/` |
| [#154](https://github.com/russfellows/s3dlio/issues/154) | S3 core correctness: URI parsing, list filter, delete_objects error semantics | 5 | Rust S3 protocol layer |
| [#155](https://github.com/russfellows/s3dlio/issues/155) | GCS backend: retry backoff, cache poisoning, delete accounting, community stub | 4 | Rust GCS backends (native + community) |
| [#156](https://github.com/russfellows/s3dlio/issues/156) | `direct://` backend: panic on missing length + URI scheme round-trip | 2 | `src/file_store_direct.rs` |
| [#157](https://github.com/russfellows/s3dlio/issues/157) | Environment variables: dead knobs, doc/code mismatches, missing clamps | 4 | Env-var handling across code + docs |

Also closes the mlcommons/storage#715 seed bug (B10, hardcoded multipart threshold), which triggered this audit in the first place.

## Behavior changes — read before merging

- **`parse_s3_uri_full` endpoint-detection heuristic narrowed (B8, #154).** Previously, an `s3://` URI's first path segment was treated as a custom endpoint hostname if it merely contained 2+ dots, started with a digit, or contained `minio`/`ceph`/`localhost` as a substring — misrouting legitimate bucket names using those shapes. Now only fires on a colon (port), a dotted-quad IPv4 address, or a recognized hostname-like suffix (configurable via `S3DLIO_S3_ENDPOINT_HINT_TLDS`).
- **`round_robin` DLIO endpoint selection now rank-based (B9, #153).** Uses MPI/SLURM/PMI rank instead of a static per-process PID hash, falling back to the old pid-based behavior (now logged) only when no rank var is available.
- **DLIO storage `create_node`/`delete_node` no longer swallow arbitrary errors (C1–C3, #153).** Only a genuine already-exists / not-found signal is treated as success; everything else propagates. If your code depended on silent `[]`/`True`/`False` on real errors, you will now see exceptions.
- **`S3DLIO_OPLOG_BUF`'s code default corrected from 256 to the documented 8192 (F3, #157).** The previous 256-slot channel silently dropped op-log entries under a moderate burst.
- **`mp::Runner.max_http_connections()`/`.optimized_http()` now actually take effect (F1, #157).** Previously silent no-ops (wrote env var names nothing read); now write the real, wired `S3DLIO_POOL_MAX_IDLE_PER_HOST`/`S3DLIO_ENABLE_HTTP2` vars into spawned workers.

Full detail on every behavior change: [`docs/Changelog.md`](docs/Changelog.md).

## New environment variables

| Variable | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `S3DLIO_S3_ENDPOINT_HINT_TLDS` | Extra suffixes for the narrowed endpoint-detection heuristic (B8). |
| `S3DLIO_MULTIPART_THRESHOLD_MB` / `S3DLIO_MULTIPART_PART_SIZE_MB` / `S3DLIO_MULTIPART_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` / `S3DLIO_DISABLE_MULTIPART` | Configurable multipart threshold for both DLIO storage integrations, replacing a hardcoded constant (B6/B10 — the mlcommons/storage#715 seed bug). |
| `S3DLIO_S3_ENDPOINT_TLS_PORTS` | Marks additional ports as TLS-terminated for per-endpoint S3 clients addressed via `s3://host:port/...` (E2). |

See [`docs/Environment_Variables.md`](docs/Environment_Variables.md) for defaults and full semantics.

## All 39 bugs

| # | Phase | Bug | Issue | File | One-line summary |
|---|-------|-----|-------|------|-------------------|
| A1 | A 🔴 | 2.1 | #152 | `range_engine_generic.rs` | Range engine tolerated a length-mismatched chunk with a warning and truncated the buffer instead of erroring — silent data corruption on a short/over read. Now a hard error. |
| A2 | A 🔴 | 1.1 | #151 | `multipart.rs` | `MultipartUploadWriter`'s `Drop` let the coordinator commit a partial object even when `abort_on_drop=false`. Coordinator now always cancelled on drop. |
| A3 | A 🔴 | 1.2 | #151 | `multipart.rs` | `abort_blocking()` discarded its result via `let _ = ...` and never stopped the coordinator — an explicit `.abort()` could still race to commit. Now always cancels first and logs on best-effort-abort failure. |
| A4 | A 🔴 | 4.5 | #154 | `s3_ops.rs`, `s3_utils.rs` | `delete_objects` treated any HTTP 200 as full success, ignoring S3's per-object `<Error>` list. Now inspects `.errors()` and surfaces per-key failures. |
| B1 | B | 2.2 | #152 | `s3_utils.rs` | `get_object_range_uri_async` had no retry wrap (a #148 regression) — a mid-body connection failure aborted the whole GET. Now wrapped in `retry_get_body`. |
| B2 | B | 2.3 | #152 | range-header builder | `length=Some(0)` silently downloaded the entire remainder of the object instead of zero bytes. Now short-circuits to `Ok(Bytes::new())`. |
| B3 | B | 2.4 | #152 | HEAD handling | Missing `Content-Length` was treated as size `0`, silently truncating reads and poisoning the size cache. Now a proper error / cache-safe fallback. |
| B4 | B | 2.5+2.6+2.7 | #152 | S3/Azure/GCS `get_range()` | `offset + length - 1` underflowed when `length=Some(0)` (panic in debug, wrap in release) across all three backends. Fixed via a shared checked helper. |
| B5 | B | 3.6 | #153 | DLIO storage `get_data()` | AND-guard only routed through `get_range()` when BOTH offset and length were given, silently returning the full object for offset-only/length-only calls. |
| B6 | B | 3.2 | #153 | `s3_torch_storage.py` | `S3PyTorchConnectorStorage.put_data()` had no multipart path at all — every write hit the S3 5 GiB single-PUT limit. |
| B7 | B | 4.4 | #154 | `object_store.rs` `list_with_client` | Regex filter was `re.is_match(key) \|\| key.starts_with(prefix)` — always true (dead code) since every returned key already starts with the query prefix. |
| B8 | B | 4.1 | #154 | `s3_utils.rs` `parse_s3_uri_full` | See "Behavior changes" above.

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [cert-manager](https://cert-manager.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager)) | minor | `v1.20.3` → `v1.21.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>cert-manager/cert-manager (cert-manager)</summary>

### [`v1.21.0`](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/tag/v1.21.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/compare/v1.20.3...v1.21.0)

cert-manager is the easiest way to automatically manage certificates in Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters.

cert-manager 1.21 brings ACME Renewal Information (ARI) support, AWS IAM authentication for the Vault issuer, several security hardening changes, and continued improvements to Gateway API integration and cainjector. There are three breaking changes related to Helm chart RBAC and metrics values — review them carefully before upgrading.

##### Known Issues

- **Log spam for non-cert-manager-labelled Secret events**: the typed predicates refactoring ([#​8407](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8407)) causes `filteredEventHandler` type assertion failures (`"OnAdd missing Object"`, `"OnUpdate missing ObjectOld"`, `"OnDelete missing Object"`) for every non-cert-manager-labelled Secret event, multiplied by 7 certificate sub-controllers. **This is cosmetic only** — the affected controllers only need events from cert-manager-labelled Secrets (which arrive via the typed informer); the metadata informer events were always filtered out by predicates in previous versions. Issuer and ClusterIssuer controllers are not affected. See [#​8994](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8994) for details.

##### Major Themes

##### Default `tokenrequest` RBAC removed from Helm chart

> ⚠️ Breaking change

The Helm chart no longer creates a default `Role` and `RoleBinding` granting the cert-manager controller permission to create tokens for its own ServiceAccount (`serviceaccounts/token: create`). No documented workflow requires this RBAC — the Route53 docs section that motivated it was removed in 2024.

If you use `serviceAccountRef.name` pointing at the controller ServiceAccount, you must now either create your own `Role`/`RoleBinding` granting `serviceaccounts/token: create`, or migrate to a dedicated ServiceAccount (recommended — see the [Vault](https://cert-manager.io/docs/configuration/vault/) or [Route53](https://cert-manager.io/docs/configuration/acme/dns01/route53/) documentation).

##### Restrict Challenge and Order RBAC in `cert-manager-edit` ClusterRole

> ⚠️ Potentially breaking change

The `cert-manager-edit` aggregate ClusterRole no longer grants `create` for `challenges.acme.cert-manager.io` or `create`, `patch`, `update` for `orders.acme.cert-manager.io` ([`GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258`](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/security/advisories/GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258)). These resources are internal to cert-manager's ACME workflow. Challenge `patch` and `update` are retained because users may need them to remove stuck finalizers.

This change was already shipped in v1.20.3 and v1.19.6, so if you are running one of those versions this will not be a breaking change. If you have tooling that creates Challenge or Order resources directly, you will need to grant those permissions explicitly.

##### Metrics port name and path Helm values removed

> ⚠️ Breaking change

The Helm values `prometheus.servicemonitor.targetPort`, `prometheus.servicemonitor.path`, and `prometheus.podmonitor.path` have been removed. The controller Service metrics port has been renamed from `tcp-prometheus-servicemonitor` to `http-metrics`. Because the Helm values schema uses `additionalProperties: false`, users who still have any of the removed keys in their values overrides will see a schema validation error on upgrade — remove them before upgrading. ([#​8952](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8952))

##### ACME and Certificate Management

- **ACME Renewal Information (ARI)**: experimental support for [RFC 9773](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9773) behind the `ACMEUseARI` feature gate. When enabled, cert-manager queries the ACME server's `renewalInfo` endpoint for the recommended renewal window, allowing servers like Let's Encrypt to proactively prompt renewal during mass revocations or CA key rollovers. ([#​8798](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8798))
- **`waitInsteadOfSelfCheck` solver option**: skip cert-manager's own self-check and instead wait a configured duration before asking the ACME server to validate. An escape hatch for split-horizon DNS and NAT hairpin environments. See [configuration details](https://cert-manager.io/docs/configuration/acme/#skip-the-self-check-with-waitinsteadofselfcheck). ([#​8858](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8858))
- **AWS IAM authentication for Vault**: the Vault issuer now supports IRSA, EKS Pod Identity, and ambient EC2/ECS credentials, removing the need for long-lived AWS Secrets. ([#​8422](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8422))
- **Certificate renewal policies**: a new `renewalPolicies` field on the Certificate API provides more expressive control over renewal scheduling, complementing `renewBefore` and `renewBeforePercentage`. ([#​8258](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8258))
- **Configurable CertificateRequest retry backoff**: the new `--certificate-request-maximum-backoff-duration` flag (default: 32 hours) caps the exponential backoff for failed CertificateRequests, useful for environments with scheduled CA maintenance windows. ([#​8893](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8893))
- **Modern2026 [PKCS#12](https://redirect.github.com/PKCS/cert-manager/issues/12) profile**: a new FIPS 140-3 compatible encoding profile using AES-256 + SHA-256 KDFs instead of legacy 3DES/RC2. ([#​8841](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8841))
- **Webhook certificate renewal after system suspend**: the webhook now detects missed certificate renewals after system suspend (S3/S4) or VM live migration by polling wall-clock time, recovering within one minute of resume. ([#​8464](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8464))

##### Gateway API and cainjector

- **HTTP01 ListenerSet parentRef fallback**: the `acme.cert-manager.io/http01-parentreffallback: "true"` annotation causes cert-manager to use the parent Gateway for solver HTTPRoutes instead of the ListenerSet, enabling TLS-only ListenerSets to use a shared HTTP listener for ACME challenges. ([#​8749](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8749))
- **`cert-manager.io/ignore-tls-listeners` annotation**: exclude specific Gateway TLS listeners from certificate management. ([#​8727](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8727))
- **Additional listener protocols**: configurable listener protocols beyond the default set. ([#​8683](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8683))
- **`enableGatewayAPI` configuration restructure**: `enableGatewayAPI` and `enableGatewayAPIListenerSet` are deprecated in favor of `gatewayAPI.enabled` / `gatewayAPI.enableListenerSet`. The old fields continue to work. ([#​8732](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8732))
- **`CAInjectorMerging` promoted to GA**: unconditionally enabled; will be removed in a future release. ([#​8583](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8583))
- **cainjector server-side apply unconditional**: the `ServerSideApply` feature gate is deprecated. ([#​8692](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8692))
- **cainjector `--ignore-namespaces` flag**: skip specified name

author: willgriffin
body:
## Slice

L2 persona **learning & adaptation loop** with a human-in-the-loop approval gate, on top of the merged `AgentPersona` (#1887) + `LearningMemory` / `Learning` trait (#1886) foundation. Design defaults are locked: human approval is required for all behaviour changes, the surface is a review queue, auto-proposals are limited to instructions text, and there is a single approver.

### What it builds (all in `packages/personas`)

- **Behaviour + memory scoping** — a persona's `instructions` apply through a per-persona registered prompt key + a tenant-scoped `prompt_override` (`persona-prompt.ts`); `memoryScope` routes `LearningMemory` (via `owner_id`) so different personas learn independently (`persona-memory.ts`).
- **`Feedback`** (`agent_feedback`) — human `accept`/`reject`/`correction`/`rating` and autonomous `outcome`/`metric` signals, each with a required **correlation-id** back to the AI call / dispatch / job. `toLearningOutcome()` feeds the confidence-scored reinforcement from #1886; `reinforceFromFeedback()` applies it (automatic, ungated).
- **`ReflectionRunner`** (schedulable) — runs under the autonomous reflection principal, reinforces recent feedback, then consolidates episodes + feedback via an injected `reflect` boundary (the AI call) into pending **`DirectiveProposal`** rows (`directive_proposals`) with rationale + evidence, deduped by fingerprint.
- **The gate = a permission split** — activating a directive requires the `personas.activate-directive` slug (contributed to the manifest permission catalog via `registerPermissionDefinitions`). The reflection principal **lacks** it and can only propose. `DirectiveApprovalService.approve`/`reject` calls `assertCanActivate` first; approval writes the persona-scoped override through `PromptOverride.save()`, so `validatePromptOverride` still refuses a non-editable template. A rejection is recorded as a signal and the same proposal is never re-surfaced. Confidence-only reinforcement stays automatic.
- **Minimal review-queue UI** — `@happyvertical/smrt-personas/svelte` `DirectiveReviewQueue` (presentational Svelte 5): pending proposals with a current-vs-proposed diff and Approve/Reject, delegating to callbacks a host wires to the gated service.

### Tests

Real in-memory SQLite; only the AI/reflection boundary is stubbed. Covers every acceptance criterion: two personas behave differently and learn in separate memory scopes; `Feedback` (human + outcome) carries a correlation-id and adjusts reinforcement; the runner emits pending proposals it cannot activate (its principal lacks the slug); a human holding the slug activates one; a rejection is recorded and not re-surfaced; a non-editable prompt template cannot be overridden; the slug is present in the catalog. 43 tests pass.

### Notes

- New acyclic package edges: `personas → smrt-prompts`, `→ smrt-users`, `→ smrt-ui` (Svelte only), `→ @happyvertical/sql`. DAG + no-smrt-peer guardrails pass.
- Svelte-package tests can't run locally on Darwin/vite8; the UI is built (`svelte-package`) and typechecked locally, and relies on CI for the Svelte runtime.
- This wave runs in parallel with #1888 / #1890, which also touch `packages/personas` + `packages/agents`; additions are kept modular. **Governance surface — do not merge without review.**

Closes #1889
Part of #1885

author: seokminhong
body:
### Motivation
- Make the CLI parser robust and safe against malformed/fuzzing-style inputs and support both `--flag value` and `--flag=value` forms while allowing multiple path arguments and globs.
- Support glob/multi-path usage and include/exclude filtering without adding external crates in this environment.
- Improve stability of query compilation and scanning for invalid UTF-8, control characters, and non-Korean inputs by treating them conservatively as literals in `auto` mode.
- Improve code organization by modularizing the monolithic binary into focused units to make further enhancements and tests easier.

### Description
- Split the single `src/main.rs` into modules `cli`, `query`, `scan`, and `walk`, and simplified `main` to orchestrate parse → compile → walk → scan → output flow.
- Reworked CLI parsing in `src/cli.rs` to validate inputs, support `--flag value` and `--flag=value`, handle multiple `PATH`/glob arguments, and reject empty/oversized/invalid values (e.g., NUL/control chars, overly large numeric options); added `MmapMode` and bounded parsing utilities.
- Added glob-like path expansion, `include`/`exclude` filtering, hidden-directory skipping, dedup/sort of results, and a byte-level wildcard matcher in `src/walk.rs` to accept glob patterns without external crate dependencies.
- Hardened query compilation in `src/query.rs` with seed validation limits, conservative `auto` → `literal` handling for non-Korean input, `--derive` support, and retention of nominal/predicate/ modifier/particle seed generation and irregular class handling.
- Implemented UTF-8-safe scanning and hit deduplication in `src/scan.rs`, added char-boundary checks, safe `line/column` extraction from raw bytes, and JSON-safe escaping for control characters.
- Added unit tests covering CLI parsing and validation, non-Korean literal handling, irregular predicate surface generation, invalid-UTF-8 scanning safety, JSON escaping, and wildcard matching; fixed Clippy warnings surfaced by the refactor.
- Note: an attempt to switch to external crates such as `clap`, `globset`, `ignore`, or `aho-corasick` was blocked by crates.io network access in this environment, so the PR strengthens the in-repo parser/walker instead of adding those dependencies.

### Testing
- Ran `cargo test` and all unit tests passed (test suite completed successfully).
- Ran `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and fixed issues so the linter check passes with no warnings.

author: zhouguangming
body:
## Background In our deployment, we integrate **Higress with Knative** using VirtualService-based routing. The architecture includes: - **Two Gateway CRs**: `public-gateway` (for external traffic) and `internal-gateway` (for internal traffic) - **Two separate sets of Istio data-plane proxies**: one fleet serving public internet traffic, another fleet serving internal network traffic - **Knative Services (ksvc)** that need to switch between public and internal network exposure Knative generates VirtualService resources for each ksvc. When toggling a service between public/internal access, we update the ksvc's gateway label, which causes Knative to update the VirtualService's `gateways` field binding (e.g. from `internal-gateway` to `public-gateway`). ### Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Kubernetes Cluster" subgraph "Control Plane" Istiod["Istiod (Pilot)"] RDSCache["RDS Cache"] end subgraph "Data Plane - Public" PubGW["Public Gateway Proxies
(Gateway CR: public-gateway)"] end subgraph "Data Plane - Internal" IntGW["Internal Gateway Proxies
(Gateway CR: internal-gateway)"] end subgraph "Knative" KSVC["Knative Service (ksvc)"] VS["VirtualService
gateways: [public-gateway]"] end end Internet["Internet Traffic"] --> PubGW InternalNet["Internal Traffic"] --> IntGW PubGW --> KSVC IntGW --> KSVC Istiod -->|"xDS Push"| PubGW Istiod -->|"xDS Push"| IntGW KSVC -->|"generates"| VS VS -->|"watched by"| Istiod Istiod --- RDSCache ``` ### Race Condition (The Bug) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant K as Knative participant VS as VirtualService participant Istiod as Istiod + RDS Cache participant IntGW as Internal Gateway participant PubGW as Public Gateway K->>VS: Update gateways: internal → public VS->>Istiod: Config change detected Istiod->>IntGW: Full Push (RDS) Istiod->>PubGW: Full Push (RDS) Note over Istiod,IntGW: Internal GW computes first (~T+0s) IntGW->>Istiod: buildHostRDSConfig() Note over Istiod: VS not bound to internal-gateway
→ vHost = nil → blackhole (404) Istiod->>Istiod: ❌ Cache.Add(key, blackhole_route) Note over Istiod,PubGW: Public GW computes later (~T+0.8s) PubGW->>Istiod: buildHostRDSConfig() Note over Istiod: Cache HIT on same key!
Returns blackhole from internal GW Istiod-->>PubGW: ❌ Returns cached 404 (blackhole) Note over PubGW: Public gateway permanently
serves 404! 💥 ``` ## Problem After switching a ksvc's gateway label (e.g. internal → public), the **public gateway permanently returns 404** for that service, even though the VirtualService is correctly configured to bind to the public gateway. The issue persists until the Istio control plane is restarted or the RDS cache is manually cleared. ## Root Cause The VS `gateways` field update triggers a **full push** to all gateway proxies. A race condition in the RDS cache causes cross-gateway cache pollution: 1. Knative updates the VS (`gateways: internal-gateway` → `public-gateway`), triggering a full push to **both** gateway proxy fleets 2. Internal gateway data-plane computes RDS first — since the VS no longer binds to it, `VirtualServicesForGateway` returns empty, `selectedVirtualServices` is empty, `vHost` becomes `nil`, and a **blackhole (404) route** is generated 3. This blackhole result is **cached** in the RDS cache 4. Public gateway data-plane computes RDS ~0.8s later — **cache HIT** on the same key (the cache key does not include proxy/gateway identity), returns the blackhole entry written by the internal gateway 5. Public gateway **permanently serves 404** until the cache is manually cleared The fundamental issue: the RDS cache key does not distinguish between different gateway identities, so a result computed for one gateway can poison the cache for another. ## Fix Skip caching when `vHost` is `nil` (blackhole result). A blackhole/404 route is always a transient, negative result — it means "this route does not apply to this gateway right now." Such results should **never** be cached because they can poison the cache for other gateways that share the same route name and cache key space. ```go - if features.EnableRDSCaching && cacheable { + if features.EnableRDSCaching && cacheable && vHost != nil { configgen.Cache.Add(routeCache, req, resource) } ``` **Performance impact:** Negligible — only blackhole results (rare, transient) skip the cache; normal routes with valid vHosts continue to benefit from RDS caching as before. ## Verification Verified in production-like environment: after this fix, switching gateway labels (public → internal → public) no longer causes permanent 404 on the target gateway.

author: changfazhi
body:
Closes #52.

## The bug

Stripe delivers webhooks at-least-once. It retries any delivery that doesn't return 2xx, resends from the Dashboard button, and — as the issue notes — may send the same event more than once even when nothing failed.

The PayNow branch of `checkout.session.completed` is *relative*: it reads `users.access_expires_at` and adds a billing period on top of it.

```js
let baselineMs = Date.now();
const existingExpiryMs = row?.access_expires_at ? new Date(row.access_expires_at).getTime() : null;
if (existingExpiryMs !== null && existingExpiryMs > baselineMs) {
  baselineMs = existingExpiryMs;   // reads back what the first delivery just wrote
}
```

So a redelivered event reads the expiry the *first* delivery wrote, treats it as pre-existing credit, and stacks another 30 or 180 days. One payment, two periods — and it isn't capped at two, since Stripe backs off and retries for up to ~3 days until it gets a 2xx.

The `mode: 'subscription'` branch was never affected: `grantPaidTier` writes absolute values, so replaying it is a no-op. Only additive arithmetic is replay-unsafe.

## The fix

**`stripe_events` ledger** (migration `030`), keyed on `event.id`. `claimEvent()` inserts the row before *any* side effect runs — including the `cancel_at_period_end` Stripe API call, not just the Supabase write. The primary key makes the claim atomic without a lock, the same shape as the existing `welcome_email_sent_at` claim in `middleware/auth.ts`.

The row carries `'processing'` / `'completed'` rather than a bare "seen" marker. A naive seen-marker would ack an event *before* knowing the work succeeded, so a process dying mid-handler would cause the retry to be skipped and the customer's payment silently dropped. Instead: `'processing'` is written up front, promoted to `'completed'` only after the handler fully succeeds. A duplicate of a completed event returns early → 200 → Stripe stops. A duplicate hitting a live claim throws → 500 → Stripe backs off. A claim older than `CLAIM_LEASE_MS` (5 min) is assumed dead and taken over via a conditional update.

**Unchecked writes.** `grantPaidTier`, `grantPayNowTier`, `revokePaidTier`, and the `customer.deleted` handler all did `await supabase.from('users').update(...)` without inspecting `error`. supabase-js reports failures on the result object rather than throwing, so a failed write returned normally, the handler marked the event completed, and the user was left holding a `tier: 'paid'` custom claim with no matching row state — with no retry to correct it, since the webhook returned 2xx. All four now go through `updateUserOrThrow()`.

**Route.** A new `WebhookSignatureError` gets a 400 (the payload isn't from Stripe; there is nothing to retry). Everything else is a 500, so Stripe redelivers and the claim re-runs the work. The handler no longer echoes `String(err)` back to the caller.

## Verification

`billingService.test.ts` drives the real `handleWebhookEvent` against an in-memory fake of the two tables, following the `vi.mock('../db/supabase.js')` pattern already used in `payNowExpiryReminder.test.ts`. Six cases:

- first delivery grants exactly one period
- **redelivery of the same `event.id` grants nothing further** — the regression
- a genuine second purchase (distinct `event.id`) still stacks to 60 days, so the intended behaviour survives
- a delivery arriving against a live claim is rejected so Stripe retries
- a stale claim left by a dead process is taken over
- a failed tier write throws and leaves the event `'processing'`, i.e. replayable

I confirmed these actually catch the bug rather than passing vacuously: with the `claimEvent` guard disabled, the redelivery test reports `expected 60 to be 30` and the live-claim test stops rejecting.

`tsc --noEmit` clean; full suite 121 passing.

## Deploy note

**Run `030_stripe_events.sql` in the Supabase SQL Editor before deploying.** Until the table exists, `claimEvent()`'s insert fails and every webhook returns 500. Stripe will retry and recover once it's there, but there'd be a window of unprocessed payments.

author: flwizkid
body:
## Summary

Contact-form emails were not arriving in `contact@encountive.com`. Investigation found the root cause is **outside this repo** (see below), but it also surfaced a real **lead-loss bug** in the edge function that this PR fixes.

The `send-contact-email` edge function sent the Resend notification **before** persisting the submission, and returned a `502` **without saving anything** when Resend rejected the send. Because the Resend sending domain is currently unverified, every submission was being lost entirely — neither emailed nor stored (the `contact_submissions` table had 0 rows).

## Changes

- **Capture-first flow** in `supabase/functions/send-contact-email/index.ts`:
  1. Persist the submission to `contact_submissions` immediately — a lead is never lost even when email delivery is down or misconfigured.
  2. Attempt the Resend notification as a best-effort step.
  3. Record the delivery outcome (`sent` | `failed` | `skipped`) and any error detail on the stored row.
- The visitor now gets a success response whenever their message is captured, so an email outage no longer blocks the form or shows a confusing error. Failures are logged and stored for follow-up/retry.
- **New migration** `20260709015021_add_email_status_to_contact_submissions.sql` adding `email_status`, `email_error`, and `email_sent_at` columns.
- Brings the repo's edge-function source back in sync with what is deployed (the two had drifted).

## Verification

- Migration applied to the `bolt-native-database` Supabase project.
- New function deployed (v9, `verify_jwt: false`) and exercised end-to-end: a submission returned `{"ok":true}` and was persisted with `email_status = failed` and the exact Resend error captured, confirming no lead is lost. Test row was removed afterward.

## Root cause of the email delivery failure (requires action outside this PR)

`encountive.com` is verified under a **different Resend account/team** than the one whose API key the function uses. Resend returns *"This domain has been claimed by another team and can no longer be verified,"* and the DKIM key published in DNS does not match the key this account expects. **Fix:** set `RESEND_API_KEY` in the Supabase project's Edge Function secrets to a key from the Resend account where `encountive.com` shows **Verified**. No code change needed once the correct key is in place; this PR ensures submissions are captured in the meantime.

body:
## What

When the price book's Grout & Caulk sheet lists the **same SKU for every color row** of a matrix column — Custom Epoxy Grout **Part B** (SKU shared across all colors) — the import was keeping the first row's item, so it showed up as "Custom Epoxy Grout Part B — **Antique White**".

Now, when `parseGroutMatrix` sees a SKU a second time under a different color in the same matrix, it strips the color from the item: it imports as just **"Custom Epoxy Grout Part B"**, with an empty `color`.

## Why the color must go (not just the label)

`groutFamilies` (ADR 0007) treats any Grout & Caulk item with a `product` + `color` as a pickable grout color. A color-carrying Part B would pose as a one-color "Custom Epoxy Grout Part B" family in the job color dropdown. Colorless, it drops out of the family list and behaves like what it is: a base-type item.

## Evidence

- Parser change only — no UI or print surface touched, so nothing for a preview to show; the node:test suite is the proof.
- Extended the existing grout-matrix test: SKU `28865` (Part B, shared across Antique White and Light Smoke rows) now asserts `description = "Custom Epoxy Grout Part B"`, `color = ""`, and the Part B column price.
- `npm test`: **111 pass, 0 fail** (was 111 before — one test tightened, none added/removed).

Note for after merge: SKU 28865's description/color change will appear as 1 changed item in the next import's diff preview — expected.

body:
## BUG-048 — Appium `TakeOverFirstIdleVehicle` precondition flakes under full-suite load

### What was built

Fixes a load-dependent `NoSuchElementException` flake in the Appium shared helper `TakeOverFirstIdleVehicle()`. The idle-vehicle list rows and take-over screen elements are populated by async REST + SignalR data loads that arrive after the take-over screen mounts; under full-suite load, bare `Driver.FindElement(...)` calls raced those loads and intermittently failed, causing whichever scenario happened to invoke the helper to redden the Appium suite with a non-deterministic failure. The fix routes all four async-loaded element lookups in `Login()` and `TakeOverFirstIdleVehicle()` through the existing bounded `WaitForSignalR(...)` poll (15 s timeout / 500 ms interval), the same convention BUG-046 applied to `ActiveJobTests`, eliminating the race without touching any production code.

### Acceptance Criteria → Test Coverage

| # | Acceptance Criterion | Test Method(s) | Level | Status |
|---|---------------------|----------------|-------|--------|
| AC-1 | `TakeOverFirstIdleVehicle()` + dependent scenarios green in the full Appium suite under load, across 2–3 consecutive runs, no `NoSuchElementException` from this helper | Full-suite live run via `scripts/local/test-appium.sh` — 3× consecutive, 26/0/1 each; zero `NoSuchElementException` from L282/315/316/319; flaky `HeartbeatGoOffDutyTests` scenario green all 3 | Live E2E | Covered |
| AC-2 | Waits remain genuine bounded gates — time out and fail, not no-ops / unbounded sleeps | Code inspection: `WaitForSignalR` (L239) = `WebDriverWait(Driver, AppiumConfig.SignalRWait)` with `SignalRWait`=15 s (L40), 500 ms poll, `wait.Until(...)` throws `WebDriverTimeoutException` on timeout; no `Thread.Sleep` or unbounded wait added | Inspection | Covered |

Previously-flaky `HeartbeatGoOffDutyTests` passed all three; zero `NoSuchElementException` from L282/315/316/319. Pre-fix the same suite was 25/1/1. Finding cleared; APPROVED at cycle 2. |
