author: dcruzf
body:
This pull request addresses a critical bug in the P-FRB rule base initialization logic, ensuring that rule consequents are correctly aligned with the sampled training points when subsampling is used (i.e., when `pfrb_max_rules < n_samples`). The changes introduce a deterministic sampling utility, update all relevant estimator logic to use it, and add regression tests to guarantee correct behavior. The version is bumped to `0.23.5`.

**Bug fix and alignment improvements:**

* Added a new `_select_pfrb_indices` utility to deterministically sample the subset of training indices used for P-FRB rule construction, ensuring reproducibility and alignment between rule centers and their corresponding labels.
* Updated `_build_pfrb_input_mfs` to use `_select_pfrb_indices` for consistent rule center sampling.
* Refactored `_pfrb_aligned_labels` and related hooks in base and derived estimator classes to always use the correctly sampled indices, ensuring that rule consequents match the actual sampled points, not just the first `max_rules` labels. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-145939309810b585b1434b946973d939cf15b87776d6b471d9cb89cbe65f6325R619-R643) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d5a0a3210e24ab5fbaf93dc0dec12594ed5ec12cd567b2fdf62139269c73c0f7R198-R205) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-cc72d12d90d51b3ce0a6647607566fd6403c63dd5944a8b4f7a273fe920f223dL251-R251) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-cc72d12d90d51b3ce0a6647607566fd6403c63dd5944a8b4f7a273fe920f223dL535-R537)
* Overrode `_effective_pfrb_max_rules` in DG-ALETSK to support data-dependent defaults, maintaining alignment with rule sampling.

**Testing and versioning:**

* Added regression tests to verify that P-FRB consequent labels always align with the sampled rule centers, and that DG-TSK fits correctly when subsampling is active.
* Bumped package version to `0.23.5`.

author: hbleiberg
body:
## Summary

Pure UI reorganization of the node-edit ("Edit points") panel in `Hebrew_Font_Maker.html` — **zero behavioral change**. Every handler function, keyboard shortcut, mode, toggle, and undo path is untouched; only the panel template (`nodeEditPanelHTML()`), panel-scoped CSS, and the keyboard-shortcuts sheet content changed.

### What changed

- **Sticky header** — "Edit points · `<glyph>` — `<name>`" + **Done editing** merged into one row that stays pinned (with a faint depth shadow) while the left column scrolls. Replaces the old `ws-side-title` line; names the panel like the Trace/Align titles do, so it doesn't duplicate the tabs-row "Editing:" indicator. The glyph preview reuses the `updateCurrentGlyphLabel` idiom, and the name now passes through `esc()`.
- **Mode segmented control** — ↖ Select / ▭ Marquee / ✒ Pen as one mutually exclusive control (`role="toolbar"` + `aria-pressed` + roving tabindex, `aria-keyshortcuts`; arrows move focus, Enter/Space activates). M / P / Esc shortcuts unchanged — the buttons dispatch to the existing `togglePenMode`/`setMarqueeMode` setters only on actual state change.
- **Contextual zone** — renders by selection state instead of greying everything, laid out as an aligned two-column grid (joined **Smooth|Corner** and **To curve|To line** pairs share the left column; Retract and the delete cluster right-align). 0 selected shows stacked full-width Select all / Paste / Remove specks (selection-dependent controls hidden, not disabled); pen mode swaps in a "Placing points" status card + full-width **Cancel path** (the existing discard path). A fixed `min-height` (125px desktop / 176px touch, measured) keeps the panel from jumping between states, and each state's content fills its reserve so there's no dead area.
- **Delete split button** — default click = `doNodeDelete()` (unchanged); the ▾ caret opens a keyboard/touch-accessible menu with "Delete points" and "Delete contour" (`doDeleteContours()` — same code path and confirm rules as Shift+Delete). Danger styling (`#c0392b` / dark `#ff8a7a`, matching the app's `.warn` accent). Escape closes the menu without reaching the node-mode Esc handler (selection stays intact).
- **Disclosures** — Transform / Round corners / Contours get uniform chevron chrome and now **persist open/closed state** in `hebrewFontMaker_uiPrefs` (`nodeXformOpen` / `nodeFilletOpen` / `nodeContoursOpen`, same mechanism as the waterfall preview). The module vars remain runtime truth so the Contours stage-tinting readers are untouched; the Contours `ontoggle` keeps its `renderStage()` side effect.
- **Hint system** — the wall-of-text paragraph is replaced by a one-sentence tip that rotates by state (select / has-selection / marquee / pen) plus a **[?]** button that opens the shortcuts sheet pre-scrolled to the Point-editing section (`openShortcuts(sectionId)` gained an optional param; existing no-arg callers unaffected). Every fact documented only in the old paragraph was migrated into the sheet: Shift-click add, drag-box select, selection-box move/scale (Shift = uniform, snapping), segment-dot line↔curve, double-click ○/□ toggle, Alt-click point insert, exact 5/25 nudge steps, pen close-on-first-point, and the contour-inside-a-shape-becomes-a-hole rule. Also fixed: reopening the sheet previously kept the prior scroll position (scrollTop writes are no-ops while `display:none`).
- **Accessibility / mobile** — zones are labeled `role="group"`s, the readout line (only) is `aria-live="polite"` and styled in the app's uppercase label voice (CSS-only), and a `@media (pointer: coarse), (max-width: 820px)` block gives all panel controls ≥44px targets (net-new, panel-scoped).
- **Release chores** — `FONT_MAKER_VERSION` 4.1 → 4.2 with one combined changelog entry; `sw.js` cache `v240` → `v241`. All new CSS uses `.npnl-*` class names — no shared classes modified.

### Element IDs

No control IDs changed. The panel's only three IDs (`nodeRotAngle`, `nodeScalePct`, `filletRadV`) are preserved verbatim; the only new IDs are the `sc-*` group anchors in the shortcuts sheet. The only visible label change: "Retract handles" → "Retract" (full phrase kept in its tooltip).

## Testing

Headless Playwright against the real page (light + dark, 1280×900 + 800×1000, zero `pageerror`s across all scenarios):

- All 20 handler names still present in the rendered panel across selection states; the three IDs still resolve; Transform's dynamic "— N selected points / — whole glyph" label intact.
- Selection transitions 3 → 0 → 1: correct show/hide, Paste disabled without clipboard, To curve disabled at 1 point with reason, contextual-zone `offsetHeight` identical across select/pen/empty states at both widths; empty-state buttons verified full width; menu items verified single-line.
- Mode transitions via buttons **and** M/P/Escape keys, including pen auto-exit on contour close; arrow keys move focus in the segmented control without changing mode.
- Delete dropdown: opens with focus on first item, ArrowDown cycles, Escape closes with selection intact and focus returned to the caret, outside click closes, "Delete contour" routes through the same `askModal` confirm.
- Sticky header pinned at viewport top when scrolled; disclosure states persist across reload via `localStorage`; Contours-open stage tinting still renders.
- [?] opens the sheet pre-scrolled to `#sc-nodes`; the `?` key still opens it from the top; all nine migrated facts present in the sheet.
- 44px touch targets verified at 800px; dark-mode danger color verified; trace/align panels screenshot-checked for shared-CSS inertness.

author: kibukx
body:
Closes #146

### Problem

The item-bearing checkpoint lists were hand-defined **four** times (store.`_ITEM_LISTS`, serializer.`iter_items`, recall's kind maps, carry's carried kinds) and had drifted: `iter_items` omitted `contradictions_flagged` — those items got ids and redaction but skipped `first_seen` inheritance, importance sanitization, quote verification, and GC importance pinning.

### Fix

New leaf module `schema.py` owns the descriptor (`ItemField`: section, key, singleton, kind, scoring_type, carries). Import-free by design — the chain runs serializer ← store ← recall ← carry, so a leaf is the only cycle-safe host. All four consumers now derive their views from it.

Review verified the derived views **element-by-element against the old literals — value-identical including ordering**. `recall`'s contradiction→`recent_decision` scoring fallback preserved exactly (`scoring_type=None` omits the key, `.get` default intact). `store._ITEM_LISTS` stays as an alias — briefing/cli iterate it unchanged.

Behavior change is exactly the issue's intent, contradictions-scoped: they now flow through `first_seen`, sanitize, `verify_quotes`, `_max_importance`, and the quote audit like every other list. No load-time downgrade risk: `verify_quotes` runs only at serialize time for new checkpoints.

### E2E test

`test_serialize_brief_e2e.py` populates one item per descriptor field, writes through real disk I/O (`write_checkpoint` → `read_latest`), renders a brief, asserts id + trust tag + first_seen per item. Driven by `ITEM_FIELDS`, so a future field is auto-covered and a consumer dropping it fails the test. TDD red first — the red output was the issue's exact claim (`first_seen missing`, `importance: 99` unsanitized on contradictions).

### Found while here (not touched, follow-up material)

- `anchor.py:81 _all_items` is a **fifth** hand-rolled copy, also missing `contradictions_flagged` — left alone (module is deliberately stdlib-only/import-free).
- `briefing._iter_trusted_quotes` covers the five lists but excludes `active_topic` from LLM-render quote validation.

### Also

Second commit: coverage now omits `daimon_briefing/_hooks/` — byte-identical mirrors of drift-guarded tested sources, executed only as subprocesses under the host's Python; in-process line coverage can never see them (they showed as 299 permanently-0% lines distorting the total).

### Verification

Full suite **1099 passed** (+2). Ruff clean on all changed files. Both commits signed.

author: moov-son-of-ben[bot]
body:
## What
New custom `go/analysis` analyzer in `analyzers/testify-subtest-assertion/`. Walks `*_test.go` files, finds every `t.Run(...)` / `s.Run(...)` (including `s.T().Run(...)`) call, inspects the closure body, and reports any SelectorExpr→CallExpr where the receiver chain contains `.Assert` or `.Require` above the leaf selector.

## Why
4 review comments on 2026-07-08 PR batch surfaced the pattern (transfersbff2#945 ×3, accounts#901 ×1): suite-level `s.Assert.Equal` / `s.Require.NoError` called inside a `t.Run` subtest closure misattribute failures to the outer test, masking which subtest actually broke.

The companion chapter change is `moovfinancial/agent-skills#49` — adds a one-line rule to `moov-test-scaffold/SKILL.md` telling humans to bind assertions to `assert.New(t)` scoped to the inner `*testing.T`. This analyzer enforces the same thing mechanically at lint time.

## Example
```go
func (s *MySuite) TestThing(t *testing.T) {
    s.Run("nested", func(t *testing.T) {
        s.Assert.Equal(t, 1, 1)   // want: bind to assert.New(t).Equal(...)
        s.Require.NoError(t, err) // want: bind to require.New(t).NoError(...)
    })
}
```

Permitted: clean variant with locally-constructed `assert.New(t)`-style helpers; suite-level `Assert.X` calls outside any `t.Run` closure (legitimate single-level test).

## Mechanics
- Restricts to `*_test.go` (the pattern only makes sense in tests).
- Recognizes both `t.Run` and `s.T().Run` call shapes via the suite/embedded-*testing.T pattern.
- Walks the selector chain looking for `.Assert` / `.Require` above the leaf — catches `s.Assert.X`, `s.Require.X`, `s.Suite.Assert.X`, etc.
- Reports a single diagnostic per offending call with the position of the call site and a message naming the suite accessor.

## Diff
- `analyzers/testify-subtest-assertion/testify-subtest-assertion.go` — analyzer implementation.
- `analyzers/testify-subtest-assertion/testify-subtest-assertion_test.go` — analysistest harness.
- `analyzers/testify-subtest-assertion/testdata/testifysubtestassertion/suite_test.go` — fixture covering flagged variants (assert+require inside `s.Run`), clean variants (local binding), and top-level suite-method calls outside any subtest.
- `analyzers/testify-subtest-assertion/testdata/go.mod` — module fixture so the testdata loads in module mode.
- `plugin.go` — analyzer registered in `BuildAnalyzers()`.

## Verification
`- go build ./...`: clean.
- `go test ./...` (all 4 analyzers, including this one): PASS.
- Analysistest harness matches `// want` comments for positive cases and skips negative cases.

Executes goal G1 (docs/GOALS.md). Closes the account-attribution gap found in the 2026-07-08 diagnosis, plus the deeper orphaned-reference break found during verification.

## The real state of the data

- 1,158/2,835 transactions had no `ownAccountId` (headers defeated the 20-line extraction window).
- The other 1,677 pointed at account ids that **no longer existed** — every profile re-seed minted fresh ids (`delete` + re-insert with time-based ids), silently orphaning all references. The eval counted these ghosts as attributed, reporting 59.2% when live attribution was **0%**.

## Changes

**Parser** — header scan covers the whole pre-table region (bounded at the first dated row with a money token, cap 80 lines); a standalone masked-number rule handles ICICI card statements (`4375XXXXXXXX9012` on its own line, mask required). Both are scoped so transaction narrations can never match (the 74693e3 lesson — negative tests included; the old 20-line window could actually match `A/C XXXX9999` inside a txn row). Card statements are detected from the document text and override the assumed docType.

**Resolver policy** (`src/ingest/account-reconcile.ts`, documented + tested): `header_match` → `institution_unique` → `stub` → manual, with issuer-family matching (`hdfc-bank` ↔ `hdfc-bank-cards`) and recorded `own_account_source` provenance (new column, migration 0006). The no-last4 fallback never force-attributes zero-transaction docs (demat/TDS/T&C mailers). Stubs raise a review item — an unregistered account is never a silent NULL.

**Profile re-seeds** upsert banks/cards by natural key (institutionId + last4), keeping ids stable; rows dropped from the seed are deleted only when unreferenced; learned last4s are never wiped. Regression-tested.

**Assign flow** — the triage "No account detected" badge now opens `AssignAccountPanel`: lists the source **documents** behind the group (account identity lives at the document altitude), assigns a registered account or registers a new one, stamps the document plus all its transactions as `user_assigned`.

**Repair backfill** (`scripts/backfill-account-ids.ts`) re-stamps both broken populations from stored rawText via the live functions, corrects docTypes, completes a registered account's missing last4 on unique match (ICICI card ··5005), and registers the owner-confirmed HDFC card ··1567. Idempotent.

**Eval** now reports orphaned ids so ghost references can't fake health again.

## Verification

- Rehearsed on a DB copy, then ran on the real DB after a `VACUUM INTO` snapshot (`exports/pre-g1-backfill-2026-07-08T18-37-09.db`).
- `npm run eval:ledger`: **[accounts] 100.0% (2835/2835), missing 0, orphaned 0** (from true 0%). Re-run is a no-op.
- Attribution audit on the copy: 9 HDFC savings docs → ··9563 (including two whose txn narrations mention ··2840 — the trap case), 12 HDFC card docs → ··2663/··1567, 20 ICICI savings docs → ··2840, 6 ICICI card docs → ··5005; 18 zero-txn docs stay honestly unassigned.
- UI driven end-to-end on a scratch server: one document assign cleared 29 triage groups' chips; DB rows confirmed `user_assigned`.
- Suite: 186 pass / 0 fail; lint 0 errors; production build clean; fresh-DB migration chain passes under `PF_DB_STRICT_MIGRATE=1`.

author: douglasichen
body:
## Bug: unbounded frame-stream decompression in `decodeAsciiv` (embed viewer DoS)

**Where:** `src/codec.ts` — `decodeAsciiv` → `gunzip`.

**Failure scenario.** The `.asciiv` container ends with `gzip(frame stream)`. `decodeAsciiv` did `await gunzip(framesGz)` which fully materialized the decompressed buffer into memory *before* `decodeFrames` read a single byte. The header caps (`MAX_CELLS` / `MAX_FRAMES` / `MAX_TOTAL_CELLS`) — whose comment states they exist "so a tiny malicious file can't OOM the viewer" — only bound the decoded *frame objects*, not the intermediate decompressed byte buffer.

So a file with a **valid, tiny header** (e.g. `cols=2,rows=2,frameCount=1` → 4-byte legit frame stream) but a frame blob that is a few hundred bytes of gzip decompressing to gigabytes sails through `validHeader`, balloons in `gunzip`, and OOMs/crashes the tab. `decodeFrames` then reads only the first 4 bytes and would "succeed" — the damage is done in `gunzip`.

**Remotely reachable.** Anyone can `POST /api/save` to mint a presigned S3 upload (`same_origin` only checks Origin/Referer, both absent on curl → allowed) and upload arbitrary bytes up to the 25 MB *compressed* cap under a key of their choosing, then share `embed.html?id=<key>`. A ~1000× compression ratio turns 25 MB into ~25 GB decompressed.

**Adversarial check.** Confirmed with a probe: a 229-byte gzip'd blob decompressing to 200 000 bytes decodes "fine" today under a header whose legitimate max is 4 bytes.

## Fix

`gunzip` now stream-reads the `DecompressionStream` and aborts with `frame stream too large` once cumulative output exceeds a caller-supplied cap. `decodeAsciiv` computes that cap from the already-validated header as the exact worst-case legit stream size: `N + (frameCount-1)*(4 + 5*N)` (keyframe + per-delta-frame budget, `count <= N`).

- **Byte-compat preserved.** A legit stream is always `<= maxStream`, so every already-published embed keeps decoding byte-identically (all existing codec round-trip tests still pass). Only oversized/malicious streams fail closed.
- No encode-side change; `.asciiv` output format is untouched.

## Test

`tests/embed.test.ts` gains a case in "fail closed" that builds a valid tiny-header file, swaps in a gzip decompressing far past the 4-byte header budget, and asserts `decodeAsciiv` rejects with `/frame stream too large/`. **Fails before / passes after** (verified by stashing the fix: 1 failed → all pass).

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` clean
- `npm test` → 5 files, 11 tests pass
- `npm run build` clean
- `python3 tests/test_api.py` → OK

author: gaurav
body:
## Context

Babel has four developer tools plus a pair of commit-split shell scripts. They are "tools" in one consistent sense: they help you work with Babel outputs and Babel runs, but are not part of the compendium pipeline.

They were scattered. Three lived in a top-level `tools/` package; `source-impact-report` lived alone in `src/cli/`. Two unrelated modules were both named `clique_diff`, each with its own JSONL compendium loader. `docs/tools/README.md` indexed three of the four tools and was half index, half clique-diff reference manual. And `docs/Development.md` proposed five *more* tools at a third namespace, `src/scripts/`, which never existed.

## The organizing principle

**A tool is a thin CLI frontend.** Logic that models Babel data — cliques, compendia, concords — belongs in `src/`, beside the code it models, where a second tool or a future pipeline rule can reuse it. A tool must never reimplement pipeline functionality.

Every tool now lives at `src/tools/<tool>/`. Being inside `src/` means tools inherit coverage, lint, and test conventions structurally rather than by configuration.

## What changed

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `src/cli/source_impact_report.py` | `src/tools/source_impact_report/cli.py` |
| `tools/clique_diff/diff.py` (360 self-contained lines) | `src/model/compendium_diff.py` + `src/tools/clique_diff/cli.py` (~60 lines) |
| `src/model/clique_diff.py` | `src/model/glom_diff.py` |
| `tools/slurm/`, `tools/memory/` | `src/tools/slurm/`, `src/tools/memory/` |
| `tools/commit-split/` | `scripts/commit-split/` |

Top-level `tools/` is gone. `[tool.setuptools.packages.find] include` collapses to `["src", "src.*"]`. Console script names are unchanged, so `reports.snakefile`'s `uv run source-impact-report` invocation is untouched.

### Naming

The two `clique_diff` modules are now named for what they diff: `glom_diff` takes the union-find output of `glom()`; `compendium_diff` takes finished JSONL compendia.

### `scripts/` keeps its name, and gains a README

`tools/` was a bad name because it named a *purpose* `src/` already served. `scripts/` names a *form*, and the form is the real discriminator: bash invoked by path, never imported, installed, or tested. Nothing in `src/tools/` is any of those.

### Documented exceptions

`slurm` and `memory` stay self-contained: `parse.py` models Snakemake `benchmark:` TSVs and SLURM `.err` files, the memory estimator models pyoxigraph RSS. Neither reads Babel data. Noted in the convention alongside #759/#736, which may eventually give them something to reuse.

## Notable behavior change

The two compendium loaders are deduplicated into one. `glom_diff`'s used `jsonlines`, which raises `InvalidLineError` on a blank line; the tool's skipped them. The surviving shared `load_compendium` skips — strictly more permissive, and it fixes a latent crash.

`babel-clique-diff`'s CSV and JSON output was verified **byte-identical** to the pre-split implementation on a fixture exercising `leader_changed`, `dropped`, `moved`, `kept`, and unchanged cliques.

## Coverage

Because the tools now live under `src/`, the existing `source = ["src"]` picks them up with no config change. This immediately exposes real gaps that were previously unmeasured:

| Module | Coverage |
|---|---|
| `src/tools/memory/estimate_rdf_load_memory.py` | 0% |
| `src/tools/slurm/resources.py` | 51% |
| `src/tools/slurm/errors.py` | 57% |
| `src/tools/source_impact_report/cli.py` | 67% |
| `src/model/compendium_diff.py` | 99% |
| `src/model/glom_diff.py` | 100% |

## Docs

`docs/tools/README.md` becomes a one-screen index — a table of all five commands and what question each answers — followed by the convention for writing a new tool. The clique-diff reference material moves to `CliqueDiff.md`. `SourceImpactReport.md` is new, documenting the CLI, the `PIPELINE_CONFIG` registry, and what the report structurally cannot see.

`docs/Development.md`'s ~190-line "Ideas for Improvement" backlog is retired. It mixed an already-shipped tool (proposal #2, `diff_compendia.py` — it's `babel-clique-diff`), ideas that duplicated open issues, and genuinely untracked ones, all at a `src/scripts/` namespace that never existed. It's replaced by a one-line pointer to a new **`developer tooling`** GitHub label ("Tooling & workflow that helps develop, debug, and validate Babel without changing pipeline outputs"). The untracked ideas became issues [#919](https://github.com/NCATSTranslator/Babel/issues/919)–[#925](https://github.com/NCATSTranslator/Babel/issues/925) (check-prerequisites, per-type report targets, standalone `build-cliques`, intermediate-file cache, isolate semantic types, DuckDB intermediate store, per-source version manifest); the already-covered ones were mapped onto existing issues (#453, #515, #561, #562, #633, #634, #736/#759, #753, #763, #764, #914) and given the same label. `docs/Testing.md`'s now-dangling anchor into that section is repointed at #764.

Also fixes three stale references to `tools/babel-errors.py`, deleted long ago when it became `babel-slurm-errors`, and gitignores `*.egg-info/` and `.coverage`, neither of which was ignored.

## Agent instructions: scoped `CLAUDE.md` files, and an `AGENTS.md` bridge

The reorg was also the occasion to split up the monolithic root `CLAUDE.md` — the file loaded into every agent query. Two moves:

- **Scoped down.** Point-of-use conventions moved out of the root file to where they apply and load only when relevant: new `tests/CLAUDE.md` and `src/datahandlers/CLAUDE.md`, the per-tool `src/tools/*/CLAUDE.md`, and `docs/sources/CLAUDE.md`; subsystem gotchas moved into the relevant docstrings. The root file went from ~540 lines on `main` to ~250, with the architecture/convention detail now in `docs/` (read on demand) rather than loaded on every query.
- **Cross-agent.** The root instructions are now canonical in **`AGENTS.md`**, and root `CLAUDE.md` is a one-line `@AGENTS.md` import. Developers using other agents (Codex, Cursor, …) read the real instructions natively; Claude Code loads them via the import and keeps its on-demand loading of the nested `CLAUDE.md` files. No symlink (portable on Windows / `core.symlinks=false`), no duplicated content. Doc cross-references that named the moved root sections now point at `AGENTS.md`.

## Follow-on fix: fail loud on an unregistered bad-xrefs key

Unrelated to the reorg, but caught while reading the code. The disease/phenotype bad-xrefs filter is looked up by concord basename (`pref in badxrefs`), so a key that matches no concord silently never filters anything — the two-place-registration footgun (a typo, or `DEFAULT_BAD_XREFS` and the `disease_compendia` snakefile dict drifting apart) that the `DEFAULT_BAD_XREFS` docstring itself warned about. The failure mode was fail-*open*: no crash, just some bad xrefs sneaking through and a couple of cliques over-merging.

`compute_cliques_for_impact_report()` now raises `ValueError` — naming the offending key and the known concords — when a `badxrefs` key matches no concord basename. Validated against the full `concordances` list rather than the post-exclusion subset, so a `--source X` impact-report before-run (which keeps X's concord in the list but skips it inside the loop) doesn't trip on X's own entry. The two stale comments describing the old silent behavior are updated, and two tests cover the typo case (raises) and the excluded-source case (does not). `docs/sources/CLAUDE.md` notes the split — the guard catches a typo'd key, while two-dict drift or a forgotten key still fail open, so the recommended unit test remains the guard for those.

## Verification

- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `snakefmt --check`, `rumdl check .` — all pass
- 275 unit tests pass (up from 270; three for the shared loader and the CLI's CSV, two for the bad-xrefs guard)
- All four console scripts, the `python -m src.tools.slurm` dispatcher, and the memory script run
- `snakemake -n babel_outputs/reports/source_impac

author: sydlexius
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `realign` command that fixes lyric sidecars (`.lrc`/`.txt`) orphaned when an external tool (Lidarr, Picard, beets) renames the audio file, so the sidecar follows its track instead of stranding and triggering a redundant re-fetch.
- Resolves each orphan through a four-tier confidence ladder, recording the winning tier as a `method` in the JSONL backup and the dry-run/summary output:
  - **exact** - the orphan's `[isrc:]`/`[mbid:]` provenance header matches a unique audio file's embedded ISRC/MBID (read via the existing `dhowden/tag` readers; no new dependency). `identity_keys` default is `[mbid, isrc]`.
  - **heuristic** - one orphan + one sidecar-less audio in a directory, gated by a Jaro-Winkler name guard (`min_confidence`) comparing the orphan's `[ar:]`/`[ti:]` against the audio's artist/title.
  - **ambiguous** / **conflict** - reported and skipped, never guessed or clobbered.
- Adds a persistent `[realign]` config section wired through the registry (env vars + TOML + web settings UI): `enabled`, `on_scan`, `require_provenance`, `cross_directory`, `identity_keys`, `min_confidence`.
- Dry-run by default, `--yes` to apply, `--library` scoping, clobber-safe `os.Rename` + `fsyncDir` with a backup-first JSONL undo trail, preserving the sidecar's original extension (never converts `.txt` <-> `.lrc`).
- Ships an optional `contrib/lidarr-rename-sidecars.sh` Custom Script that prevents the orphan at Lidarr rename time.
- Note: the exact tier requires ISRC/MBID-tagged audio; untagged libraries fall back to the heuristic tier (conservative by design, tunable via `min_confidence`).
- Size override: single atomic feature (config -> helpers -> resolver -> command are interdependent; ~52% of the diff is tests and docs), shipped as one PR per the maintainer's everything-in-#444 scope decision.

## Linked issue

Closes #444

## Gates (run locally; CI enforces them)

- [x] gofmt / build
- [x] race tests (`go test -race ./...`)
- [x] patch coverage (Codecov parity; `internal/commands` +2%, `internal/scanner` +3%, floors met)
- [x] codecov report validation (dry-run)
- [x] golangci-lint (0 issues)
- [x] actionlint
- [x] govulncheck (0 vulnerabilities in called code)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit + end-to-end `realign_test.go`: exact-via-MBID, exact-via-ISRC (identity_keys order), cross-directory (on/off), heuristic + name guard, ambiguous, conflict (destination-exists / multiple-exact), require_provenance gating, extension-preserved, `--library` scoping, subcommand-recognition regression guard.
- [x] Helper unit tests: `IsAudioFile`, `ReadProvenanceTags`, `ReadAudioProvenance`.
- [x] Manual E2E against a seeded temp library: dry-run touches nothing; name guard correctly refuses a low-similarity pair; `--yes` renames + writes a method-tagged backup.

author: isitjeff
body:
## What

VIT (Endurance) already grows the HP/stamina **pools** (`advance_progression`) and speeds **stamina** recovery (`update_stamina`), but health regen was flat — the last unfinished quarter of VIT's *"governs the resources' capacity **and** regen"* role (the design's Toughness+Recovery pairing).

- `recover(Vital&, dt, boost=1.0f)` gains an optional multiplier; `regenerate_vitals` computes `boost = 1 + (endurance.level-1)*kHealthRegenPerEndurance` (its own knob, separate from stamina's) via `try_get<Attributes>` — null → 1.0, so creatures and bare entities are **bit-identical**. Mirrors `update_stamina`'s boost shape.

## The reconciliation (why VIT-regen was risky before)

A boosted regen (13.6/s at END 8) could **out-pace** starvation (12/s) and make it un-lethal. Instead of a fragile *"12 must stay above the fastest heal"* coupling, `regenerate_vitals` now **skips healing entirely while `hunger ≤ 0`**. Since `drain_hunger` runs first in `step()`, hunger is current — so starvation nets health strictly **downward at any regen rate**. A *structural* guarantee every future regen source (Medicine, rest tiers, healing gear) inherits for free. The stale coupling comment is retired.

## Balance (deliberate, flagged)

The gate deepens starvation: a wounded starver now nets **−12/s** instead of −4/s (no more clawing back the +regen). This applies to permadeath NPCs too — **by design** (player==NPC parity; "feeding everyone is the economy"). Hungry NPCs forage, hunger drains over minutes, food drops constantly; if it reads too harsh in play the knobs are food-drop / drain / NPC-regen rates — *not* a special-case (that would break parity). The existing "revive refills hunger" fix means a respawned player comes back fed — no re-death loop.

## Determinism

Pure per-tick float math on the pool, no RNG, no stream shift. No new component / command / system.

## Verification

- ci-strict `-Werror -Wconversion -Wshadow`: **0 warnings**
- **98 tests / 1750 assertions** pass (2 new: starving-never-heals invariant even at boosted regen; fed higher-Endurance heals strictly more)
- clang-format (**v18, CI-matching**) / includes-lint / docs-lint / mkdocs `--strict`: exit 0
- game **boots 180 frames on Metal, clean shutdown**
- 2-lens adversarial review (correctness+invariant / balance+regression+determinism): both **SHIP IT**, zero code defects (one balance nit noted + documented at the code site)
- `docs/engine/stats-system.md` updated

body:
## Context
Investigated a report of a "completely wrong transcript." I pulled the actual recordings from S3 and re-ran them through Deepgram: transcription is **accurate** (it even caught Hindi `दिव्या`). The wrong-content recording turned out to be one where the **"Capture call audio"** option had recorded a *video playing in the shared tab* instead of the user's voice — so the transcript correctly reflected that other audio.

(Separately: speaker diarization returns a single speaker on these clips across nova-2/nova-3/en/multi — that's a Deepgram limitation, being handled by testing with two real speakers, not a config change.)

## Change
Make the tab/system-audio capture option safer and self-explanatory so it can't silently record the wrong thing:

- **Reworded toggle** — spells out that it records a browser tab you pick, so anything playing there (a video, music) gets recorded instead of your voice; only for live video calls.
- **Prominent warning** (shown when the option is enabled) to pick your live meeting tab, tick "Also share tab audio", and close any videos/music first — replaces the small, easy-to-miss hint.
- Added a `.alert.warn` style.

Still off by default, mic-only remains the normal path.

## Testing
`npm run build` (tsc + vite + PWA) passes.

- Make `currentVertx()` reuse a managed default Vert.x instance outside Vert.x contexts instead of creating unowned instances per call.
- Add `defaultVertx()` / `closeDefaultVertx()` and managed default Vert.x HttpClient close support.

## What

Adds tracemill scenarios and a Splunk validation job for the ESCU detection **Windows AD Same Domain SID History Addition** (`5fde0b7c-df7a-40b1-9b3a-294c00f0289d`, T1134.005).

The detection fires on Security **EventID 4738/4742** where a same-domain SID is written into an account's `SidHistory` (the injected value's domain prefix matches `TargetDomainName`).

## Scenarios (`scenarios/windows/wineventlog/account-management/`)

- `sid-history-addition-user` (4738) — attack-positive: SID-History injection into a user account.
- `sid-history-addition-computer` (4742) — attack-positive: SID-History injection into a computer account.
- `account-change-no-sidhistory` (4738) — benign control: routine account change, no SID History.

## Job (`jobs/splunk/windows/wineventlog/account-management/`)

- `windows-ad-same-domain-sid-history-addition` — two attack workloads (`alert`) + benign control (`none`).

## Validation

Per-event correlation. Validated end-to-end against a local Splunk stack: both attack workloads fired and correlated; the benign control did not fire. Whole-library `validate` (0 errors) and the detection-coverage gate pass.

body:
### 🚨 Severity: HIGH

### 💡 Vulnerability
The dashboard endpoint (`/api/dashboard`) had several security weaknesses:
1.  **Hardcoded Secret**: A default fallback password was hardcoded in the source.
2.  **Timing Attack**: Password comparison was performed using standard equality, which is vulnerable to timing analysis.
3.  **Missing Rate Limiting**: The endpoint lacked specific protection against brute-force password guessing.

### 🔧 Fix
- Added `crypto.timingSafeEqual` with SHA-256 hashing for constant-time comparison.
- Enforced `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` environment variable (no fallback).
- Added `checkDashboardLimit` rate limiter (3 attempts / 10 mins).
- (Cleanup) Fixed `ChatWidget.tsx` lint/runtime errors discovered during verification.

author: codybrom
body:
Stacked on #117. Completes the localization work surfaced while auditing the string catalogs: gap backfill, a German quality pass, App Shortcut phrase localization, and dead-key cleanup. Four commits.

## 1. Gap backfill — `needs_review`
Every string missing a translation for a locale is now filled across all 11 non-English locales (de, es, fr, hu, it, ja, ko, pl, pt-PT, tr, zh-Hans), per the project's AI-backfill convention:
- **53 keys** in `Blankie/Localizable.xcstrings`, **13 keys** in `BlankiePresetPreview/Localizable.xcstrings` (accent-colour names + `System`), plus a new **`Remove %@`** accessibility key the artwork-tile remove buttons introduced.
- **`volume.deviceControlled`** now carries iPhone/iPad/other **device variations** for all 11 locales (German uses formal "Sie" and the real "Mix with Other Audio" setting name).

## 2. German quality pass
Reviewed the German `needs_review` backlog against Blankie's own human-approved German and the owner-set house style:
- **"sound" → „Geräusch"** (ambient/everyday) or **„Klang"** (musical — e.g. „Musikklang") — never the "Sound" loanword.
- Proper German over loanwords: Artwork → **„Motiv"**, Website → **„Webseite"**; kept genuine ones (App, Credits, CarPlay); **„Schnellmix"** for Quick Mix; formal **„Sie"** throughout; accent-colour names mirrored from the main catalog.
- **Promotion rule:** an AI string is promoted to `translated` only when its `(English → German)` pair **exactly matches an already-human-approved rendering** elsewhere (colour names, "System"). Everything else stays `needs_review` for a human pass — reviewing an AI string does not sign it off.

## 3. App Shortcut Siri phrases
New **`Blankie/AppShortcuts.xcstrings`**: the six App Shortcuts' Siri phrases localized into 12 locales (the 11 + en-GB). Each shortcut is a `stringSet` carrying **both phrase forms**, with the `${applicationName}` / `${preset}` / `${sound}` tokens preserved and a translator comment. Phrase keys were taken from Xcode's own extraction (`ExtractedAppShortcutsMetadata`), so they reconcile cleanly on build. The five intent **parameter-summary** forms in `Localizable.xcstrings` also received translator comments.

## 4. Cleanup
Removed four stale artwork-label keys — `Choose Artwork`, `Select Image`, `Remove`, `Remove Artwork` — superseded by the artwork-tile rework (Xcode-flagged `stale`, 0 source references, no surviving translations changed).

## Method & safety
- Native-language multi-agent workflows: one translator/reviewer per locale, each **prompted in its target language** (the approach that's worked best here), using Apple's platform terminology.
- Automated verification on every step: **every format specifier** (`%@`, `%lld`, `%1$@`/`%2$@`) and **every `${…}` token** preserved; backfill/review confirmed **additive** (no unintended edits to surviving translations); catalogs **compile** (`xcstringstool`, 0 errors).
- Everything stays `needs_review` for a human's final sign-off, except the corpus-matched promotions in §2.

_(The first commit is unsigned — 1Password was unavailable overnight; later commits are signed, and a squash-merge signs the final commit regardless.)_

author: fernanda-syafalam
body:
## Why

First-page load was heavy: `dist/assets/index-*.js` was ~536 kB raw / ~140 kB
gzip because **23 authenticated routes used `createFileRoute` with an inline
component**, bundling their pages (large data tables, the Leaflet topology map,
qrcode, etc.) into the eager entry chunk — downloaded even by the
unauthenticated **login** page. This also violated the repo rule "Lazy-load
route components. Always."

## What

Split each of the 23 routes into this repo's existing pattern:
- `<route>.tsx` keeps the eager options (`loader` / `validateSearch` /
  `beforeLoad`) via `createFileRoute`;
- `<route>.lazy.tsx` holds the component via `createLazyFileRoute`.

Auth guards stay eager (`_auth` `beforeLoad` is never lazified). Pure
code-splitting — no behavior change. `routeTree.gen.ts` regenerated by the
Vite plugin.

## Result

| | raw | gzip |
|---|---|---|
| Entry `index-*.js` before | ~536 kB | ~140 kB |
| Entry `index-*.js` after | ~333 kB | **~93 kB** |

~33% smaller entry; Leaflet (~154 kB) is now a lazy chunk off the critical
path, loaded only when the topology map is opened. `pnpm build`, `typecheck`,
`lint:ci`, and `size` (size-limit) all green (entry 93 kB vs 160 kB budget).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Convert the remaining eager routes / lazy-load vendor `radix`/`tanstack` off the login path.
- Subset the variable fonts (Inter/JetBrains Mono) and split the 95 kB CSS.

`TerminalProbeSupport.swift`; the four nested copies deleted. The Resolver's were
internal-only (no shim). The Probe keeps `typealias` shims so the qualified
spelling `TerminalSessionAttachmentProbe.GhosttyTerminalSnapshot` /
`.TerminalTabSnapshot` — used by `ProcessMonitoringCoordinator` + ~22 test sites —
keeps resolving.

Behavior-neutral: a pure verbatim type relocation.

## Linked Spec

`.octospec/tasks/dedup-terminal-snapshots/brief.md` **r2** (human-approved:
`lml2468` — both r1 and r2 entries). Discovery:
`.octospec/tasks/arch-quality-audit-r2/discovery.md` (#9, cluster A). Journal:
`.octospec/journal/dedup-terminal-snapshots.md`. Follows `terminal-jump-resilience`.

**r2 was a spec-changing iterate:** r1 wrongly framed the acceptance as
failing-first unit tests. A test referencing the moved top-level type fails to
*compile* (not assert) on the pre-move tree — an invalid Red — and a struct move
has no wrong-value to assert. So A1/A2 are `N/A(test)` and A4 (existing suites +
byte-identical diff) is the neutrality proof, mirroring the merged
`ui-decomposition` slice. See the brief's Iteration Log.

**Deferred cluster-A remainder:** AppleScript source-string constants →
`runAppleScript`/`isRunning` (need an injection seam) → `corrected*JumpTarget`
(Ghostty variant differs — Probe Zellij guard).

## How verified

- No new tests (pure relocation, per the approved `N/A(test)` acceptance).
- **Verbatim proof:** the moved struct bodies diff byte-identical (fields, types,
  order, `Sendable`) to the deleted nested copies; both probe files stripped their
  nested defs; `grep "struct GhosttyTerminalSnapshot|struct TerminalTabSnapshot"`
  returns exactly one hit each (the shared home).
- **Behavior-neutral proof:** the ~40 existing references +
  `TerminalSessionAttachmentProbeTests` (~40 cases) + `AppModelSessionListTests`
  compile and pass unchanged.
- **Independent Verify** (fresh-context reviewer): PASS — confirmed the verbatim
  diff, shim resolves without a cycle, module-collision workaround justified, no
  out-of-scope changes.
- Gate green: `scripts/harness.sh ci` — 434 tests / 54 suites, warnings-as-errors
  + `swiftlint --strict`, exit 0.

## COMPREHENSION

1. **What does this change actually do** to the load-bearing path?
   It relocates two identical snapshot structs to one shared definition and points
   both probe types at it (the Probe via typealias, keeping its qualified name
   working). No field, type, conformance, or usage changes — every producer and
   consumer of these snapshots sees the same shape.

2. **What could break** because of it (dependents + failure mode)?
   The risk in a type move is a reference that no longer resolves. Mapped
   exhaustively: Resolver's structs are internal-only (verified zero external
   qualified refs); the Probe's ~40 external refs are preserved by typealias
   shims. A module-name collision (`struct OpenIslandApp` @main shadows the module
   name) blocked a module-qualified alias, worked around with a file-scope
   `internal` alias. The whole app + test suite compiling and passing unchanged is
   the proof.

3. **How do you know it works** (specific test/repro/trace)?
   The moved bodies are byte-identical to the deleted ones (git diff), the
   duplicated struct now exists in exactly one place (grep), and the ~40
   references + heavily-tested Probe suite pass unchanged. Independent reviewer
   confirmed all four. Gate exit 0.

author: chrisbewithyou
body:
## Problem

Importing a Guitar Pro file with a **constant** authored tempo produces a chart whose tempo **drifts slightly per bar** in the editor/timeline — e.g. a 140 BPM song shows bars at 139.94 / 140.02 / … (reported by testers on GP5 and GP8 files). Guitar Pro itself stores one exact tempo; we don't match it.

## Root cause

The editor/timeline **derives** per-bar BPM from beat spans (`bpm = beats·60 / span`). `gp2rs` computes beat times *exactly* from the GP tempo map, but writes them to the arrangement XML at **millisecond (3-decimal)** precision. Deriving BPM from ms-rounded spans amplifies the ±0.5 ms rounding into a **~0.05–0.7 BPM per-bar wobble** — worse for fast/odd meters (a 1-beat bar at 200 BPM can drift ~0.7). Most bar lengths don't land on a ms boundary, so nearly every constant-tempo import wobbles (125 BPM is a lucky exception — its bars *do* land on ms boundaries).

## Fix

Write `<ebeat>` / `<startBeat>` times at **6-decimal (microsecond)** precision. That's the only change — the times are already computed exactly; we were just truncating them on the way out. Everything else stays at `:.3f` (only beat times drive the tempo derivation).

## Verification

Ran the real `convert_file` on GP5 imports; derived per-bar BPM collapses from two drifting values to the single authored constant:

| File | before (3-decimal) | after (6-decimal) |
|---|---|---|
| Highway to Hell | 115.998 / 116.054 | **116.0** |
| Equivalence | 139.942 / 140.023 | **140.0** |
| Living After Midnight | 137.931 / 138.01 | **138.0** |

Companion editor-side PR (`feedback-plugin-editor`) matches the precision on the editor's save path so the drift can't return on save/reload.

author: garymike
body:
Phase 1 of deepening the differentiator (the developer-execution surface).

**What changes.** `skill-testfile-gate` goes from *presence* flagging (filename `find`, which cries wolf on every honest test suite) to a **layered** gate:
- **inventory (low)** — an auto-executed skill file is present; reported, non-blocking.
- **malice (high, blocks)** — a first-party **Semgrep rule pack** (`toolbox/skill-audit/rules/agent-exec-surface.yml`, reusing the engine we already ship) flags credential reads, `curl|bash`, decode-and-exec, reverse shells, agent-memory writes, and obfuscation; plus an invisible-Unicode check. Emits **SARIF** to code scanning.

**Wider scope** per [where skills live](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#where-skills-live): nested `**/.claude/skills/` (monorepo), plugin skills, `.claude/commands/`, `.cursor`/`.agents`, symlink-following, and `.git/hooks` (a blind spot for 8/9 scanners per SkillCloak).

**Proof-fixture (the point).** `tests/gate-proof.sh` (wired into `dogfood-scan`, **blocking**) builds the image and asserts on every run: the gate **blocks** a defanged Gecko demo and **clears** a benign skill — so the presence→malice upgrade is continuously proven, and legit tests aren't false-positived.

**Also:** semgrep pinned explicitly in `skill-audit-toolbox`; ADRs 0010–0012; `threat-model.md` updated; CHANGELOG `[1.1.0]`.

Detection validated locally against the fixtures + FP probes (gecko→block, benign→clear, legit fetch/child_process→WARNING-not-ERROR). Merging republishes `skill-audit-toolbox:latest` via build-toolbox.

author: bvengerov
body:
## Summary

Lowercase German legal URLs now permanently (308) redirect to their capitalised canonical form:

- `/de/impressum` → **308** → `/de/Impressum`
- `/de/datenschutz` → **308** → `/de/Datenschutz`

German nouns are capitalised, so the canonical legal URLs under the `de` locale are `/de/Impressum` and `/de/Datenschutz` (from `routing.ts#pathnames`). People type URLs lowercase, though, and lowercase variants aren't manifest keys — they fell through next-intl's locale-segment fallback and got rewritten to the `/de` homepage (a silent 200 that reads as "the imprint doesn't exist" and creates SEO duplicate content).

**Where:** the redirect lives in `src/proxy.ts` (implementation hint 1, the preferred option) — that's where locale-related routing decisions and the age-gate rewrite already live, and the redirect *must* fire **before** next-intl runs its rewrite (order is load-bearing). A config-only `next.config.ts` `redirects()` would sit outside the proxy's routing chain and couldn't guarantee ordering relative to next-intl's middleware, so `proxy.ts` is the correct home.

**Extensibility (AC 3):** the new `canonicalGermanLegalRedirect` helper (`src/lib/legal/canonical-german-legal-paths.ts`) derives its lowercase → canonical map from the routing pathnames manifest rather than hardcoding two `if`s. Any capitalised German-localised pathname is picked up automatically, so adding a future capitalised German legal noun to `routing.ts` wires up its redirect with no change to this module. Scoped strictly to the `de` locale — English legal paths stay lowercase (`/en/imprint` untouched).

## Closes

Closes #97

## Review checklist

### i18n
- [x] All new user-facing strings live in `messages/{en,de}.json` (no inline JSX literals) — N/A, this PR adds no user-facing strings (routing/redirect only)
- [x] German catalogue is structurally identical to English (`messages-parity` test green) — unchanged
- [x] No forbidden promotional copy (`pnpm i18n:audit` clean) — no copy changes

### GDPR (per ADR-0009)

This PR touches **no personal data** — it is legal-page URL canonicalisation (routing only). No new processing, no vendor, no stored personal data exposed, no consent surface. The GDPR sub-items are therefore N/A.

### Verification
- [x] `pnpm lint` — clean
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm test` (unit) — 829 passed, incl. new `canonical-german-legal-paths.test.ts` (7 cases: lowercase→canonical for both paths, trailing-slash normalisation, no-loop on already-canonical, English-locale untouched, non-legal paths untouched, manifest-derived map)
- [ ] `pnpm test:e2e -- legal-pages` — **not run locally**: this worktree has no Playwright browsers installed and no `.env.local` to boot `pnpm dev` (Clerk/DB keys absent). The e2e coverage was added and is deferred to CI.
- [ ] `pnpm verify` (full chain) — not run locally for the same reason; deferred to CI.

### Deviations from spec

None. All four acceptance criteria are met. E2E was written per AC 4 but executed on CI rather than locally (environment can't boot the dev server here) — called out honestly above.

## Manual testing

`pnpm dev`, then (the redirect itself needs no auth/DB):

- `curl -sI http://localhost:3000/de/impressum`  → `HTTP/1.1 308` + `location: /de/Impressum`
- `curl -sI http://localhost:3000/de/datenschutz` → `HTTP/1.1 308` + `location: /de/Datenschutz`
- Browser (German locale): `/de/impressum` lands on `/de/Impressum` (200); `/de/datenschutz` → `/de/Datenschutz`.
- No loop: `/de/Impressum` stays 200 (no redirect). English untouched: `/en/imprint` behaves as before.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary A batch of UX/correctness improvements to the Home Sentinel telemetry dashboard (`index.html`). No backend changes — same `/ws` protocol (`backfill` / `metric` messages). **Ping gets its own Y axis.** CPU load and memory % (0–100) previously shared a single value axis with ping in milliseconds, so the percentage lines were squashed to the bottom whenever ping spiked. Ping now renders on a dedicated `opposite` (right-hand) axis: ``` pctAxis = ValueAxis() // CPU load, memory % pingAxis = ValueAxis({opposite}) // ping (ms) makeSeries(..., yAxis, tooltipText) // series now bound to the correct axis ``` **"Follow live" toggle.** Every incoming point used to force `xAxis.zoomToValues(min, max)`, snapping the view back to full range and making it impossible to pan/zoom into history. Auto-follow is now gated behind a checkbox (default on): ``` function followIfEnabled() { if (!followLiveEl.checked || !allData.length) return; xAxis.zoomToValues(allData[0].timestamp, allData.at(-1).timestamp); } ``` **Live numeric readout.** Three cards show the current CPU / memory / ping values, updated on each `metric` and from the last point of a `backfill`. **Data-freshness indicator.** A line under the status shows `updated Ns ago`, flipping to a "stream may be stalled" warning after 10s without data (`setInterval(refreshFreshness, 1000)`). This distinguishes "socket connected but device silent" from a healthy stream. **Fix unbounded series growth.** `allData` was capped at 720 points but the three amCharts series arrays were `push`ed to forever (memory leak on long sessions). The trim now also drops the oldest point from each series: ``` while (allData.length > 720) { allData.shift(); cpuSeries.data.removeIndex(0); memSeries.data.removeIndex(0); pingSeries.data.removeIndex(0); } ``` Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0df8b31c171c4f2daab650a686a18f31 Requested by: @Reddogg4200 ---

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
## What

Makes the honest pre-alpha distribution truth explicit for the three skills that carry `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` refs in shipped content — `re-frame2`, `re-frame2-setup`, `re-frame2-pair` — and neutralises the dead npm channel that produced dangling redirect pointers (rf2-517dsa, operator-ruled Option 3).

**Problem:** shipped leaves + `SKILL.md` route every deep-dive through the repo-root `SKILL-REDIRECT.md`. A `package.json` `files` allow-list cannot reach the repo root, so an npm-packed consumer gets dangling pointers for every deep link. The npm registry returns E404 for these packages (zero consumers), and no prepack machinery exists — the packaging is scaffolding only.

**Fix:** repo checkout (git clone + link) and marketplace-plugin are the supported channels; npm is dropped until a deliberate staged-publish design exists. A clone carries the repo-root `SKILL-REDIRECT.md`, so every redirect resolves.

## Changes

**Manifests (non-publishable) — commit 1**
- `skills/re-frame2/package.json`, `skills/re-frame2-setup/package.json`, `skills/re-frame2-pair/package.json`: add `"private": true`, drop `publishConfig.access public`.
- The `files` allow-list is **retained** — inert under `private` (npm refuses to publish), it keeps the repo-wide convention that every skill manifest carries an explicit allow-list and keeps the eval-packaging agreement gate meaningful. This reads the ruling's "remove **or disable**" as *disable* via `private`.

**Docs (repo-checkout is the channel) — commit 2**
- `re-frame2/README.md`, `re-frame2-setup/README.md`: Install sections now name repo-checkout + marketplace as the channels and note the `private` manifest; dropped the "no npm entry **yet**" (publish-forthcoming) framing and "published package" wording.
- `re-frame2-pair/README.md` + `SKILL.md`: the `re-frame2-pair.runtime` preload ships in the skill's own `preload/` dir (linked clone), not the now-private `@day8/re-frame2-pair` npm package; the MCP server (`@day8/re-frame2-pair-mcp`) is built/run from a clone. All `npm install` forms retained only as explicit **"Once published"** future paths, consistent with `docs/LOCAL_DEV.md` (which already frames both as pre-release clone routes).
- `re-frame2-pair/references/{mcp-transport,errors}.md`: same clone-first framing.
- `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` stays the single repo-root index; **no redirect targets inlined** into leaves.

## Scope notes
- Only the 3 skills carrying redirect refs in *shipped* content are in scope; `re-frame-migration` + `re-frame2-implementor` reference it only in non-shipped evals/spec — left untouched.
- `@day8/re-frame2-pair-mcp` is a separate `tools/` deliverable with its own release story (out of edit scope); its skill-doc references are softened to the clone route rather than rewriting that package's channel.

## Acceptance (rf2-517dsa)
- (a) no skill doc or manifest implies a *currently* installable npm package — npm forms are future-gated ("Once published"), manifests are `private`. ✓
- (b) all three affected skills state repo-checkout/marketplace as the install path. ✓
- (c) skill `package.json` manifests are non-publishable. ✓
- (d) `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` remains the sole repo-root index; all in-repo redirect refs resolve from a clean clone. ✓
- (e) no redirect targets inlined into leaf files. ✓

## Quality gates (foreground)
- `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` — **PASS** (all in-repo markdown links/anchors resolve)
- `python scripts/check_skill_redirect_anchors.py` — **PASS** (every `SKILL-REDIRECT.md -> *Label*` ref resolves)
- `python scripts/check_skill_eval_packaging.py --self-test` and corpus — **PASS** (re-frame2 + re-frame2-setup: files:OMIT / docs:EXCLUDE = agree)
- `bb skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj` — **PASS** (27 tests / 143 assertions)
- `bb skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/setup_drift_test.clj` — **PASS** (27 tests / 78 assertions)
- `bb skills/shared/tests/{retro_protocol,tool_pair_surfaces}_test.clj` — **PASS**
- `python scripts/{check_skill_mcp_drift,check_skill_pair_authoring_drift,check_skill_setup_counter_drift,check_readme_inventories}.py` — **PASS**
- grep-confirm: no skill doc/manifest implies a currently-installable npm package.

## Stance
Pre-alpha, no shims; CLARITY + CORRECTNESS + GOOD-PRACTICE. Making the current truth explicit and dropping dead publish scaffolding is the honest pre-alpha move; maintaining machinery for a nonexistent channel would be gold-plating.

author: erinepshovel-code
body:
### Motivation
- Provide the missing infrastructure to invert non-head (tail) right cells in successor-product cancellativity proofs by measuring tail elements against a common baseline instead of re-reading the right-head angle. 
- Expose a small arithmetic bridge from canonical floor-zero facts to `amod4` fixed points so canonical-range facts can be used to recover raw angles. 
- Keep the cancellativity proof path aligned with the `AlignedComplete` domain and thread induction over paired tail lists with concrete floor-zero / payload witnesses.

### Description
- Add `amod4_eq_self_of_floor_div_four_eq_zero` to turn floor-zero facts into `amod4` fixed-point equalities.  
- Introduce `multiplyRowWithBase` and `multiplyRow_cons_tail_eq_multiplyRowWithBase` to map a right row against an explicit baseline and to relate it to the original `multiplyRow` shape.  
- Add numerous lemmas that lift first-row equalities to equalities of the common-baseline mapped tails, including `tail_product_cells_eq_of_first_row_eq`, `tail_product_cells_eq_of_multiplyFuel_succ_eq`, and `tail_product_cells_eq_of_multiplyFuel_succ_eq_commonBase`.  
- Provide non-head inversion theorems for angle, face and payload under a common baseline, together with raw-angle inversion theorems parameterized by `amod4` fixed-point hypotheses and concrete floor-zero obligations.  
- Add `AlignedComplete`-scoped variants of the new lemmas so the cancellativity code follows the normalized-domain path, plus list-induction helpers and list-shaped witness types `commonBaseTailFloorZeros` and `commonBaseTailRecursivePayloadEqWitnesses` to thread floor-zero and payload evidence through tail walks.

author: douglaz
body:
## What

**The last go-live gate** (`lnrent-y4m.7` / PR-12, codex-endorsed as the right final gate before the `7qc` refund dogfood). The operator's BIP39 seed — which controls the operator identity AND all ecash — must never reach a recipe hook. Today `spawn_hook` inherits the daemon's full environment, so a seed supplied via `LNRENT_MNEMONIC` (the recommended path) is copied into every provision/suspend/resume/destroy/op hook process. This closes that in **code**, not just prose (SPEC §13).

### B — the load-bearing fix (`runner::spawn_hook`)
The single hook choke point now `.env_clear()`s the child and passes **only** a fixed base allowlist (`PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, TZ, TMPDIR`) plus the recipe's declared passthrough — each forwarded from the daemon env only when present. `LNRENT_*` never reaches a hook **by construction**. Threaded `&recipe.provisioning.env` through `run_hook` → `spawn_hook` and all five callers (provision ×2, reconcile, resume, op_dispatch).

### Recipe — declared passthrough
New `provisioning.env: Vec<String>` (serde default empty), validated by `Recipe::validate`: **≤16 entries, each `[A-Z0-9_]{1,64}`, and rejects any `LNRENT*` name** (the seed's namespace is never forwardable). `recipes/do-vps` declares `["DO_TOKEN","DO_REGION","DO_SIZE","DO_IMAGE"]` (the one documented exception — its hooks read all four); `dummy`/`wireguard` declare nothing.

### A — defense-in-depth (`main.rs` runtime restructure)
`#[tokio::main]` replaced with a **synchronous `fn main`** that loads config (consuming the seed/secret env into a zeroizing guard), `remove_var`s `LNRENT_MNEMONIC`/`FEDIMINT_INVITE`/`FEDIMINT_GATEWAY` **while still single-threaded**, then builds the Tokio runtime and `block_on`s the async entrypoint — so the scrub can't race a worker-thread `getenv`. It can't overwrite the kernel-placed env block (documented — `/proc/self/environ` may still show them), so B's `.env_clear()` is the real guarantee; A hardens the daemon's own process.

### Docs
SPEC §7.2 (child-env contract), §13 (secrets-via-stdin now **enforced**, not conventional), go-live.md §4 + README — the base-allowlist + recipe-env rule and the systemd-credential/stdin recommendation for a clean daemon environ.

## Tests

- **Pure allowlist logic** (`hook_env_from`, injectable getter — deterministic, no env mutation).
- **Real spawned env-dump hook**: with `LNRENT_MNEMONIC` + an undeclared var set in the daemon (test) env, the hook does **not** see them, but **does** see a recipe-declared var + base `PATH`. Proves the actual `.env_clear()` at the process level (serialized, restores prior env).
- **Recipe validate**: rejects `LNRENT_MNEMONIC`, non-`LNRENT` bad shapes, oversize/over-count lists; accepts the do-vps shape.
- **Part A scrub**: post-scrub `std::env::var(...)` returns `Err` for each secret.

Workspace **470 passed / 0 failed**, `clippy --workspace --all-targets` clean, wasm buyer clippy clean, `--no-default-features` mock build green — all in the nix devshell.

## Impact

Closes `lnrent-y4m.7`. With this merged, **`lnrent-7qc` (the fedimint refund staging dogfood) becomes ready** — the last step before an attended mainnet launch per the operator decision.

author: mrityunjaybhardwaj
body:
### Problem
`assignSoundToCursor` (in `WorkspaceShell.tsx`) decides where to write a sound name:

- **Note/roll chunk under the cursor** → set/replace its `.sound()` (chainMethod idiom, single-quoted so the name stays a literal).
- **No chunk under the cursor** → drop a fresh `s("…")` on its **own line**: insert at the *end of the cursor's line* (a raw offset would land mid-token or inside a comment — `// scratch` → `// scratchs("…")`), with a newline prefix only when the line already has content.

The reused primitives (`detectChunk` / `patternKind` / `readChainMethod` / `Writeback`) are unit-tested, but the line-aware decision itself was only covered by Playwright E2E — and it lived inline in a React closure reaching Monaco imperatively, so it couldn't be tested in isolation.

### Fix
Extract the whole decision into a pure helper **`planSoundAssignment(doc, offset, sound)`** that returns an offset-space edit (`replace` a range / `insert` at an offset) — mirroring the existing `detectChunk(doc, offset)` pure-helper idiom. `assignSoundToCursor` now computes the plan and applies it via `Writeback`, so **the tested code is the shipped code** (no duplicated logic to drift). Removed the three now-unused imports.

Behavior is identical for the project's `\n`-EOL documents: the planner's `indexOf('\n', offset)` resolves to the same position Monaco's `getLineMaxColumn` did, and the imperative write glue is unchanged.

### Test plan
- **New:** `soundAssign.test.ts` — 11 unit tests over both branches, asserting the **applied-document outcome**:
  - roll chunk → append `.sound('…')`, replace an existing `.sound()`, match the `.s()` alias
  - source insert → empty doc (no prefix), below a comment (the regression case), **mid-word cursor still writes at line end**, content line (newline prefix), blank line (no prefix), EOF without trailing newline, and a step/drum chunk left untouched
- `pnpm --filter @stave/editor test` → **578/578 pass** (incl. the new 11); no regression in the visualEdit suite.
- `pnpm --filter @stave/editor build` → DTS typecheck clean; editor `dist` rebuilt and committed with src.
- End-to-end sidebar-assign behavior remains covered by the existing Playwright specs (behavior-preserving refactor).

Closes #830

author: koopa0
body: The sidebar listed the whole vault while the reading route served only `.md`, so the vault root's `Makefile` rendered as a dead link. Every file the tree lists now opens, presentation per kind, inside the existing `/notes/` URL space. ## What it does - **Dispatch by content, not by trust in extensions.** A sniff (valid UTF-8, no NUL) decides text from binary. The extension only picks the chroma lexer, or the viewer for the kinds a browser draws. - **Text** → a read-only, escaped, chroma-highlighted source page in the shell: filename as title, no status face, no seal, no TOC, no diagnostics. - **Images** (png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/svg) → an `` over the raw bytes. **PDF** → the browser's viewer over the raw bytes. - **Binary without a viewer, or text past ~1 MB** → an information page: name, size, type, a link to the raw bytes. - **Raw bytes** (`GET /raw/{path...}`) serve with an explicit content type, `nosniff`, `no-store`, and a **bare** CSP sandbox. - **Unchanged**: search indexes markdown only; the graph's note set stays markdown-only; the write face touches nothing. ## The defense layer the `.md` gate was `TestReadingPageRejectsPathTraversal` records that the reading route's containment was three layers: the mux cleans dot segments, **the handler serves only `.md`**, and `vault.ReadNote` rejects non-local paths. Removing the gate removes a layer. `filepath.IsLocal(".git/config")` returns **true** — it rejects escapes above the root, not names beginning with a dot — and the vault's `.git` holds the history of every note in it. So both routes restate the scanner's own rule at their boundary: **a dot-leading segment is refused, and only a regular file serves.** Bytes are opened through an `os.Root`, which refuses every symbolic link — whether its target is outside the vault or inside it, and whether the link is the final path element or a directory buried in the middle, which a check on the last element alone would miss. ## Test plan Gates: `make verify` exit 0 · `make gen && make css` no-op · biome 2.5.2 + stylelint 17.14.0 exit 0 · hygiene greps clean. ### Kill-tests (red observed, then reverted) | Mutation | Result | |---|---| | Remove the CSP header from `/raw` | `TestRawServesBytesUnderASandbox` red: `Content-Security-Policy = ""` | | Remove the dot-segment guard from `servable` | `TestServable` red (3 cases) and `TestFileRoutesRefuseWhatTheTreeDoesNotList` red — **`GET /raw/.git/config = 200` and it leaked the sentinel** | | Remove the regular-file check | `GET /notes/Notes` (a directory) = 500, want 404 — red | | Drop the NUL check from `looksText` | `TestLooksText` red (NUL, ELF header) and the binary fixture stopped taking the information page | Each mutation was asserted to have actually applied before the run — an earlier attempt at the first two was **vacuous** (a bad regex, and a mutation that left imports unused so the package merely failed to build). A test that has never been red is a hope; so is a kill-test that never mutated anything. ### Defect found by the probe, fixed here A symlinked directory escaping the vault (`/raw/up/secret.txt`) answered **500**, not 404: `os.Root` rejects it with an error that is not `fs.ErrNotExist`. A 500 tells a caller that the path it guessed was special. Both routes now warn-and-404 on any open failure, matching the report-raw route's established shape, and the refusal tests assert **exactly 404**. ### The PDF decision ladder — step 1, resolved The ruling said: probe headed Chrome under the bare sandbox; uniform if the viewer renders, otherwise exempt `application/pdf` alone. **Chrome tolerates the sandbox; Safari does not.** Headless cannot answer this at all — it never paints PDF content, and the control with *no CSP* produced an identical blank area. Driving headed Chrome over the DevTools protocol, the viewer rendered fully under `sandbox`. But the owner reported the PDF blank in **Safari**, which is the browser he actually reads PDFs in. **Ladder step 2 taken: `application/pdf` alone drops the `sandbox` directive.** It keeps `frame-ancestors 'self'`, `nosniff`, `no-store`, and the server-wide `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy`, so only yomihon's own shell may frame it and no other origin may embed it. The exemption costs no safety: a PDF is handed to a viewer the browser isolates for itself, never rendered as a document in this origin, and the pinned type with `nosniff` keeps it from being read as anything that could script. Every other kind stays fully sandboxed, which `TestRawPDFDropsTheSandbox` pins from both sides. Verified: Chrome still renders the PDF after the change (no regression), and the raw headers are exactly as described. **Not verified by me: that this fixes Safari** — Safari's WebDriver needs "Allow Remote Automation", which I cannot enable. The owner re-tests; if it is still blank, the ruled fallback is ``/`

Release @primmel/primmel 1.2.0

Bump from 1.1.0 → 1.2.0. This release rolls up all the parser,
language, and tooling improvements that landed on main after the
1.1.0 cut.

## New features

- **`term` keyword** (MN 113-6): formal terminology modeling. Each
  term captures id, label, definition, optional symbol cross-ref,
  source clause refs.
- **`tokenizeWithPositions()`**: every token now carries source
  position (line, col, offset). All parse errors include `line X col Y`
  instead of `token N`.
- **Parse-time duplicate-ID detection**: via new optional `field`
  config on ParserConfiguration entries. Issues collected on
  ParseContext.issues and surfaced via new `loadWithIssues()` /
  `loadFileWithIssues()` API.
- **Post-parse `validate()`**: catches form-calculation-missing,
  form-subform-missing, form-conformance-process-missing,
  state-machine-{from,to}-missing, empty-id.

## Bug fixes

- **Bare-ID mangling**: `stripWrapping()` replaces `removePackage()`
  for ID-like fields. Previously, `conformance_process X` had its ID
  mangled (`DetermineMeasurementError` → `etermineMeasurementErro`).
  The R 60 model had 24 such mangled references; all now valid.
- **Dumper string escaping**: `escapeString()` applied to all 17
  dumper files. Round-trip is now lossless for any string content
  (including `\` and `"`).

## Refactors

- **DRY FormField parser**: extracted shared `field-parser.ts` module;
  eliminated 120 lines of duplication between form.ts and subform.ts.

## Public API additions

- `loadWithIssues(src)`, `loadFileWithIssues(path)`: returns
  `{ standard, issues }`.
- `validate(standard)`: returns `ValidationIssue[]`.
- Types: `Token`, `Position`, `ValidationIssue`, `ValidationSeverity`,
  `Term`.

type-check, lint, test, and build before publishing.

author: omkhar
body:
Part of A5 (signed session audit seals). First PR in a 4-PR stack.

Manages the per-host ECDSA **P-256** key used to sign A5 session audit seals: generate, load, and harden the private key and its public sidecar under an owner-secured (0700) signing directory. Distinct concern from the audit-chain recompute + sign/verify in package `auditseal` (stacked PR-B), which consumes `LoadOrCreateSigningKey`/`LoadPublicKey`.

**Containment.** The whole operation is anchored to one validated directory fd: the signing dir is opened `O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY` and fstat-validated (real dir, owner euid, 0700 via `unix.Fstat`), then every key/pub read and write is an `*at` syscall relative to that fd (`openat`/`renameat`/`linkat`/`unlinkat`), so a post-validation dir swap cannot redirect any read or write. Content files are `O_NOFOLLOW` + fstat-checked (regular file, owner euid, mode). Keys are **refused** (never repaired) if insecure/symlink/non-regular/wrong-owner/wrong-curve; the public sidecar is repaired atomically from the private key and bound to its key-id filename. Directory entries are made durable by fsyncing the dir and **its full ancestor chain**, independent of who won a first-use race.

**Core tests** here: key gen + stability + rotation, P-256 curve enforcement, one perms refusal, one durability (parent fsync) case, blank-dir guard. Dead-code clean standalone. The exhaustive hardening matrix (perms/symlink/FIFO/TOCTOU/durability/racers) is stacked test-only PR-A2.

Stack:
- **PR-A (this)** a5k1/keystore-core → main
- PR-A2 a5k2/keystore-hardening-tests → a5k1 (test-only)
- PR-B a5a2/auditseal-lib → a5k1
- PR-C a5b2/session-verify → a5a2

author: petergstfsn
body:
## What

Fixes "mesh generation isn't completing" on STEP uploads — the run log stopped at "Building Core volume mesh artifact…" with the mesh stuck at "Not generated" and no error anywhere.

- **Unhandled quality-gate rejections** (`WorkspaceApp.tsx`): `generateMesh` rethrows `MeshQualityError` by design so quality failures don't silently degrade to preset estimates — but the Generate-mesh handler never caught the promise, so the rejection died unhandled with zero UI feedback. The handler now catches and logs `Mesh generation failed: <reason>` (renders as an ERR line; status ticker flips to "Needs attention"). Thin curved shells routinely trip the minSICN ≥ 0.05 floor at coarse/medium presets, so this was the everyday path into total silence.
- **Heal CSP-era placeholder selections** (`stepFaceHealing.ts`, new): projects whose STEP upload happened while the CSP regression blocked occt-import-js fell back to generic box faces (`face-upload-*`); their persisted support/load selections can never map onto meshed geometry (`could not map selection …`). On opening such a project we now rebuild the real B-rep face registry, remap selections whose placeholder normal has a **dominant** match (alignment ≥ 0.8, ≥ 0.1 ahead of the runner-up), and explicitly name anything ambiguous for manual re-selection — no guessed physics.
- **Dev-server meshing** (`gmshWasmBinary.ts`, `vite.config.ts`): in-browser meshing under `pnpm dev` had never worked — vite's SPA fallback answered both the missing `assets/gmsh-wasm.json` manifest fetch and the Emscripten glue's `import.meta.url`-relative `gmsh-core.wasm` fetch with index.html + HTTP 200. The manifest loader now checks content-type before parsing, and `@loumalouomega/gmsh-wasm` is excluded from dev pre-bundling so the relative .wasm URL resolves to the real file.

## How it was diagnosed

Reproduced in real browsers against the production `dist`: drove the app UI (STEP upload → Generate mesh), staged the exact stale-project states via the autosave, and captured the swallowed rejection with an `unhandledrejection` listener — the failure fires in the worker immediately after the "parse" phase message, which is why logs end at "Building Core volume mesh artifact…".

## Verification

- Production build, real browser: healthy STEP studies mesh (static **and** dynamic, byFace selection mapping, ~2.2–2.5k nodes); stale-selection projects get healed faces + a clear remap/re-select message; quality rejections now surface with actionable guidance.
- `?meshProof=step` browser harness: full registry → mesh → attribution → solve passes (reaction = applied load).
- 613/613 web tests pass (6 new for `stepFaceHealing`); production build clean.

## Reviewer notes

- The two silent-failure modes look identical in the log; they're distinguishable by whether an ERR line appears (mapping failures were already caught and fell back to estimates — quality rejections were not).
- The heal deliberately refuses low-confidence remaps: a placeholder box face genuinely can't disambiguate parallel faces (e.g. inner vs outer wall), so those selections are named for re-picking instead.

author: omkhar
body:
Part of A5. Stacked on **a5k1/keystore-core** (PR-A). **Test-only — adds no production code.** Stays draft until PR-A merges (main-based-merge policy).

The exhaustive keystore security/durability matrix:
- **Perms/kind refusal:** insecure/symlink/FIFO/non-regular key and signing dir, trailing-slash symlink dir, cross-platform owner check (`unix.Fstat`, so it runs on Linux where `os.FileInfo.Sys()` is `*syscall.Stat_t`).
- **TOCTOU:** open-then-fstat and `O_NOFOLLOW` at the leaf; `*at`-anchored writes proven to land in the validated dir fd, not a swapped path.
- **Public key:** key-id binding (mismatched content refused), symlink/FIFO/missing/insecure `.pub` refused; drifted-mode/symlink/FIFO-symlink/corrupt `.pub` repaired atomically from the private key.
- **Durability:** parent + ancestor-chain fsync, key/`.pub` publish fsync, reuse-path fsync, EEXIST/concurrent first-use racers — all fail closed on a fsync error.

Uses the `withFsyncPhaseFailure` seam from `keystore_test.go`.

author: akeemjenkins
body:
Addresses the CLI-gap feedback from the inbox-cleanup session. All four features were built test-first: the test files were written and committed failing before any implementation.

## Feedback → what changed

**1. Classification results aren't queryable after the fact → `higgs state query`**
The state DB already persisted every per-message field (`suggested_labels`, `confidence`, `rationale`, `is_mailing_list`, apply status) — only a query surface was missing. `higgs state query [mailbox]` now exposes it, purely locally (no IMAP dial), as NDJSON: `--is-mailing-list true|false`, `--applied true|false`, `--min/--max-confidence`, `--label` (exact element match), `--failed`, `--limit`. Answering "which messages are non-mailing-list" is now `higgs state query INBOX --is-mailing-list false` instead of hand-aggregating saved NDJSON in Python.

**2. No stdin/pipe support for UID sets → `--uid -` everywhere**
Every command taking an explicit `--uid` list (`archive`, `trash`, `move`, `mark-read`, `flag`, `extract`, `unsubscribe`, `attachments`, `summarize`, and the new `verify`) accepts `-` to read the set from stdin. Stdin takes plain comma/whitespace-separated UIDs **or** NDJSON — each object row's numeric `uid` field is used, rows without one (summary lines) are skipped — so higgs output pipes straight back in:

```
higgs search INBOX --before 2025-07-01 | higgs archive INBOX --uid -
higgs state query INBOX --is-mailing-list false | higgs move INBOX Folders/Personal --uid -
```

UIDs are deduplicated; `--uid - --all-matching` still errors before consuming stdin.

**3. No verification/audit primitive → `higgs verify`**
`higgs verify <mailbox> --uid <set|-> --expect present|absent|exact` is a read-only diff of a mailbox against an expected UID set: one `{"type":"violation"}` row per mismatch (`exact` reports both missing and unexpected UIDs), a summary with `checked`/`ok`/`violations`, and a non-zero exit when the expectation fails — the "dump mailbox, diff against expected set" script, built in.

**4. The pick-one improvement → `extract --apply-as-label`**
`higgs extract ... --apply-as-label Needs-Reply --when needs_reply=true` stamps the extraction outcome directly as a persistent, searchable label (lazy `Labels/<name>` creation, same COPY mechanism as classify's apply mode). Rows gain `label_applied`, the summary counts `labels_applied`/`label_apply_failed`. With no `--when`, every successful extraction is labeled.

## Deliberately not addressed

Agreeing with the feedback's own assessment: the needs-reply heuristic (sender regexes, bulk-ESP domain lists, recency cutoffs) and exact-duplicate signature computation stay in the scripting layer on top — `--apply-as-label` plus `--uid -` piping now give that layer clean primitives to build on.

## Testing

TDD throughout: contracts pinned in `internal/state/query_test.go`, `cmd_state_query_test.go`, `uid_stdin_test.go`, `cmd_verify_test.go`, `cmd_extract_label_test.go` (committed failing first, red for the right reasons). Full `go test ./... -race -count=1` passes, `go vet ./...` clean, plus a manual smoke run of the built binary (`state query` against a fresh DB, `archive --uid - --dry-run` fed by a pipe).
