author: clauding-lab
body:
## Problem (P1, verified — landmine 3)
`SubscribeCTA` inserted into Supabase `subscribers` **directly from the browser** with the anon key. Supabase RLS on the table has a single policy `allow_insert` for role `anon` with check `true` — **anon can insert anything, unconditionally**. Only guard was a non-empty trim; `noValidate`; no route / rate limit / honeypot. Any devtools user could poison the list Brevo mails one-POST-per-recipient on every publish.

## Fix — new `app/api/subscribe/route.ts` (Node runtime)
- **Validation**: email format + length (name ≤120, org ≤160, email ≤254 RFC max).
- **Honeypot**: hidden `company_website` field — bots that fill it get a fake `200` with no insert.
- **Rate limit**: best-effort 5/min per IP, keyed off **trusted `x-real-ip`** (not the spoofable leftmost `x-forwarded-for`), IPv6 keyed by /64.
- **Injection defense**: `name`/`organisation` control-char (CR/LF) stripping to block downstream Brevo header/body injection; email field is inherently CRLF-safe.
- **CSRF/abuse**: requires `Content-Type: application/json` + same-origin; `nosniff` + `no-store` headers; generic client errors (no DB leakage).
- **Keys**: prefers `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (bypasses RLS once the anon policy is dropped), non-breaking anon-key fallback with a loud warning during rollout.

`SubscribeCTA` now POSTs to the route (with the honeypot + client-side email check).

## Independent security review (Opus 4.8)
Ran before this commit. **No CRITICAL** (service-role key confirmed not leakable to client/logs; no SQLi/SSRF/ReDoS). Applied in this PR: H1 (XFF spoof), M1 (IPv6 /64), H2 (CRLF sanitize), M2 (Content-Type + Origin), L2 (headers). **Documented follow-ups** (need schema/deps/ops, out of scope here): **H3 double opt-in** (the real anti-listbombing fix), **M3 durable rate limiter**, **M4 unique-email constraint**.

## ⚠️ Requires two Adnan actions to be fully effective (see session report → SQL + runbook)
1. Set `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in Vercel env.
2. Drop the anon `allow_insert` policy (SQL provided). **Order matters** — set the key FIRST, else inserts 502.
Until then the route adds app-layer guards but the bundled anon key still allows a direct-to-Supabase bypass.

## Gates (bare)
- `npm run lint` → exit 0 · `npm run build` → exit 0 (`/api/subscribe` builds as ƒ) · `npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0

## Base
⚠️ **`chore/lint-ignores-and-landmine-count`** (PR #122), NOT main. Also edits `SubscribeCTA.tsx` in a different region than PR #127 (masthead/CTA copy) — clean 3-way merge, but sequence them.

## Preview
Vercel auto-creates a preview for this SPA PR — test the form there; URL in the session report once available.

author: carloshrdezc
body:
## Summary

Normalizes `schema/profile.json` `transition.adaptive` field from `oneOf: [boolean, integer 0|1]` to `"type": "boolean"` only.

JS always writes booleans, C++ reads/writes booleans — the schema's `oneOf` was an overly permissive holdover. All shipped seed profiles in `data/p/` use `true`/`false`. Any user-created profiles that historically stored integer `0`/`1` (only possible from very old firmware, given JS and C++ both serialize booleans) would fail strict schema validation, but this is a pre-existing pre-condition that the code has always enforced at the data layer.

Fixes PRO-22

body: ## Problem When staff reply manually from their phone on the same monitored WhatsApp account, OpenClaw could treat that outgoing message as a new customer inquiry and send another bot reply — creating a loop. After deploy, Chrome could also open without WhatsApp Web loading for a while. ## Solution ### Manual-reply loop fix - **Customer messages** (`message-in`): processed as inquiries - **Our replies** (`message-out`, manual phone or bot): ignored - Latest-bubble guard: if newest message is outgoing, skip chat and mark pending incoming as human-handled ### Startup speed improvements - Load WhatsApp Web immediately when Chrome opens (not only when it's WhatsApp channel turn) - Skip redundant `driver.get` when tab is already on web.whatsapp.com - Faster ready polling: 1s intervals (was 3s), tighter checks via search box / `#side` - `pageLoadStrategy=eager` for quicker navigation return - Startup timing logs: `Chrome driver ready in Xs` / `WhatsApp Web ready in Xs total` - Daily restart clears stale `openclaw_busy.flag` and resets channel turn to `whatsapp` - Post-Chrome-kill sleep reduced 5s → 2s ### Deploy ```bash cd ~/openclaw git pull origin cursor/whatsapp-ignore-manual-replies-760a bash scripts/openclaw_daily_restart.sh ``` Check `logs/openclaw_main.log` for timing lines like: `⏱️ Chrome driver ready in 8.2s` `⏱️ WhatsApp Web ready in 14.5s total` ## Tests - `tests/test_whatsapp_outgoing_detection.py`

## What this does

Rewrites every primitive in `components/ui/` onto docs/design-system.md section 6's table (issue #71's 10 items), and wires every call site in the app onto the new APIs.

### Variant collapse

| Primitive | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Button | 9 variants (`default/destructive/outline/secondary/ghost/link/iris/done/accent-outline`), 8 sizes (`default/xs/sm/lg/icon/icon-xs/icon-sm/icon-lg`) | 5 variants (`primary/default/quiet/danger/danger-quiet`), 3 sizes (`sm` 20/r6, `md` 28/r8 default, `lg` 32/r10) |
| Chip | 12 variants (5 state hues + 2 note levels + 5 hue-tinted `label-*`), fixed uppercase | 2 (`state`/`meta`) + `hue` prop (8 hues), sentence case |
| Toggle/ToggleGroup | 3 sizes (`default` h-7/`sm` h-6/`lg` h-8), fixed `rounded-md` | 2 sizes matching the two concentric combos in section 6 (`sm` 20/r6 in an r8 group; `default` 28/r8 in an r10 group) |
| Input | 1 fixed height (h-9/36px), `bg-transparent` | 2 sizes (`md` 28/r8 default, `lg` 32/r10), `bg-surface-sunken` |
| Select | 2 sizes (`default` 36px/`sm` 32px) | 1 height (28px/r8, "select trigger" row) |

This PR implements phase 9.6.E: a minimal multiepoch training loop.

It adds TrainingLoopConfig, TrainingLoopOutput, fit, and build_run_manifest. The loop uses the existing TotalLossAssembler and training_step, supports batch adapters, device handling, optional gradient clipping, optional scheduler stepping, nonfinite-loss stopping, and run manifest generation.

author: pcavadas
body:
## What & why

Adds the **`spiky`** Doctor diagnosis: a clean chain (no active drive pedal) whose capture shows wide dynamic spread (`short-term-max − integrated LUFS` > 4.0 LU, the existing `lufs::Loudness::spread_lu()`), with an **advisory-first** prescription pair:

1. **"Tame the swings at the source"** — on the fixed-envelope noise stimulus, high spread can only come from the preset's own time-variant processing (swell/tremolo/delay build-up), and easing that effect is the honest fix.
2. **"Add a studio compressor after the cab"** — inserts the soft-knee `ACD_CompressorSimpleSoftKnee` (STUDIO COMPRESSOR, 1.0% CPU vs the DynaComp's 4.8%) immediately after the cab, studio-style channel compression for when the player wants the level held steady anyway. Comp-aware like `comp_front`: an existing active comp → "turn up the compression" advisory; a bypassed one → "switch it back on"; no cab → advisory only.

Post-amp compression is pointless on driven tones (the amp already compresses), hence the clean-chain gate; end-of-chain placement after reverb/delay is deliberately not offered (compressing wet tails pumps).

Backend-only in practice: diagnoses are self-describing over the wire, so no new command, wire field, or type-mirror change. Supporting changes:

- `SoundProfile.spread_lu` — computed from the `measure_mono` call `from_capture` already makes; rides the `probe --doctor` sweep JSON for free.
- `chain_preview` now takes an insert **position** (`usize`) so the Chain card shows the comp adjacent to the cab instead of appended after the tail effects (`eq_move`/`comp_front` call sites updated mechanically, behavior unchanged).
- Insert anchor: the next node in the **same group** after the cab (`beforeFenderId`), appending when the cab ends its group — never a cross-group anchor (the firmware silently drops those). Bypassed neighbours still anchor (position is chain order, not audibility).

**The 4.0 LU threshold is PROVISIONAL** (both instruments), documented as such in `Thresholds` and `notes/doctor-calibration.md`.

## How it was tested

- [x] `bun run lint` / `bunx tsc --noEmit` / `bun run test` (404 passed, incl. a new DoctorResults fixture pinning the time-domain chain-rx render)
- [x] `cargo test --lib` (325 passed; 4 new engine tests: fire/gate conditions, after-cab anchor, cab-ends-group + cross-group append, comp-aware/advisory-only paths) / `cargo clippy --all-targets`
- [x] Verified on a real Tone Master Pro (firmware: 1.8.45) — fresh `probe --doctor` baseline sweep, 16 sounds (14 guitar-humbucker + 2 bass-singlecoil), read-only: **spread measured 0.12–0.81 LU across the whole library**, so the 2.5 s Doctor-tail inflation concern did not materialize (wettest preset, tail −2.7 dB, topped out at 0.81 LU); `spiky` fired on zero library presets (by design — only envelope-heavy sounds can cross 4 LU on the dense stimulus); zero `washed` co-firing, so the contingent `tail_ratio_db` gate was not needed. Numbers recorded in `notes/doctor-calibration.md`.

## Checklist

- [x] Conventional-commit title
- [x] Only touched-file formatting (no repo-wide `cargo fmt` / prettier reflow)
- [x] No lint escape hatches in `src/`
- [x] No new dependency

## Summary

Adds three new reference docs under `docs/`, describing subsystems that
previously had no dedicated documentation outside `CLAUDE.md`'s terse
orientation summary and source-level comments:

- **`docs/zig-backend.md`** — the `malgo compile` pipeline end to end:
  where `SaturateCtor`/`ReuseSpecialize` fit (shared by every backend, not
  Zig-specific), the Zig-only stages (`ClosureConv` → `Peephole` →
  `Perceus` → `Reuse` → `RcCheck` → `Emit`), the backend's own ANF IR, the
  self-passing calling convention, runtime data representation, build/test
  commands, and the available debugging tools.
- **`docs/perceus-gc.md`** — the Perceus reference-counting memory model:
  ownership discipline, the `dup`/`drop` insertion rules (D/Let/T), why a
  naive implementation of those rules is quadratic and how
  `Ir.suffixFreeVars` avoids it, FBIP reuse tokens, `RcCheck`'s static
  verification (confirmed it runs unconditionally on every compile, not
  behind any flag), the runtime's heap/leak-check implementation, and
  `MALGO_RC_TRACE`/`scripts/rctrace.py`.
- **`docs/met-tool.md`** — the MET (M-exp-Tracer) pipeline visualizer:
  how to run it, the exact stage list it traces and how that maps to the
  production pipeline, its side-by-side/unified-diff views, and its module
  architecture (`Malgo.Debug.Pipeline`/`PrettyIR`/`DiffView`, `app/met`).

All three cross-link each other where relevant.

## Verification

Documentation-only change (no source/build files touched). Every specific
claim (pass ordering, CI job names, format strings, effect requirements,
build-mode behavior) was checked against the current `master` source

author: komapc
body:
## Summary
- retro #244's direction guard (`settlement_direction_allowed`) has been fail-open since it shipped, because no caller sends `claim_direction`/`claim_deadline` yet. This PR arms it for every daatan path that calls the Oracle against an existing prediction: the analyze route (`context/route.ts`), the news-indexer push route, the admin Oracle-sources backfill (`refreshOracleSnapshot`), and bot voting.
- The important part is the mapping, not the plumbing: retro's `ForecastRequest.claim_direction` is a strict pydantic `Literal["arrival", "survival"]`. Daatan's `ClaimDirection` enum has a third value, `NONE` — sending that as the literal string `"none"` would 422 the whole `/forecast` call rather than fail open the way absent metadata does. `claimDirectionParam()` in `oracle.ts` maps `ARRIVAL`→`"arrival"`, `SURVIVAL`→`"survival"`, and `NONE`/`null`/`undefined`→omitted entirely (never serialized as a key).
- `claimDeadline` (a `Date`) is sent as `.toISOString()`; retro's `_parse_date` only reads the first 10 characters, so the full ISO string round-trips fine.
- `express/guess` (the pre-creation quick-estimate flow) is deliberately untouched — no `Prediction` row exists yet at that point, so there's nothing to forward.

## Test plan
- [x] New tests in `oracle.test.ts` covering all four `ClaimDirection` cases (ARRIVAL/SURVIVAL/NONE/absent) against the actual request body, plus ISO-string serialization of `claimDeadline` and `getOracleProbability`'s forwarding.
- [x] New tests in `news-indexer/context/__tests__/route.test.ts` and `oracle-backfill.test.ts` confirming the prediction's stored fields actually reach `getOracleForecast`'s options at each call site.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npx eslint .` clean, full suite: 177 files / 1722 tests passed (up from 1713 baseline, +9 new tests).

author: fengmk2
body:
Expose the child PID on `ChildHandle` so callers can signal the child's whole process group.

## Why

The process spawned into a PTY is a session / process-group leader (portable-pty `setsid`s it), but `ChildHandle` only exposed a single-process killer. A caller that needs to reap grandchildren the command left behind, e.g. a managed-runtime or package-manager helper that inherited the PTY slave fd and keeps the master from ever reaching EOF, had no way to target the group.

## What

Add `ChildHandle::pid() -> Option<u32>`, captured at spawn. Additive; no behavior change for existing callers.

## Consumer

vite-plus's PTY snapshot suite: once a step's command exits, it `killpg`s the group so a lingering grandchild can't wedge the exit-wait (`read_to_end`, which only returns at PTY EOF) on the Namespace Linux runner (macOS reaps fast enough to hit EOF).

author: mvhenten
body:
Closes #190, closes #191.

An unexpected error from a server API call must never end as a swallowed rejection or a dead widget. The SPA's JSON fetch helpers now throw a structured `ApiError`, and a single `unhandledrejection` listener routes any uncaught one to a full-screen red error page — call sites that already handle their errors (inline status rows, session-list hints) are untouched, and any call site that forgets gets the fail-hard page instead of silence. No per-call boilerplate.

The error page shows the failing request, status, error body, stack, and a diagnostics bundle, with one button that opens a prefilled GitHub new-issue URL (title + body carry the diagnostics, truncated to stay within URL limits; the browser's own GitHub session handles auth).

The diagnostics bundle is shared machinery: app version and server `build_hash` (`/api/build-info`), SPA bundle hash (`/static/build-info.json`), current route/session/node, user agent, and the last entries of a small always-on `window.onerror`/`unhandledrejection` ring buffer installed at app boot.

The same bundle backs a new bug-report button in the terminal ribbon, next to the settings gear, so a bug can be filed in context the moment it happens — same prefilled new-issue URL, no error required.

Terminal-attach errors arriving over the PTY (tmux stderr) are out of scope; this covers HTTP/API-level responses only.

## Screenshots

| Fail-hard error page (#190) | Ribbon bug-report button (#191) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Fail-hard error page](https://github.com/mvhenten/mobux/raw/pr-195-screenshots/pr-error-page.png) | ![Ribbon bug-report button](https://github.com/mvhenten/mobux/raw/pr-195-screenshots/pr-ribbon.png) |

## FAQ

**Why intercept at `unhandledrejection` instead of inside the fetch helpers?**
The helpers can't know whether a caller handles the error. A caught `ApiError` is a recoverable, expected failure and keeps its existing inline UX; only the uncaught ones — the swallowed-error pattern — reach the fail-hard page.

**Why doesn't the error page fire for `/api/nodes` 404s or STT probe failures?**
Those call sites catch their errors deliberately (a 404 means "no node support", a probe failure is a status line). Fail-hard only replaces silence, not existing handling.

**Does this cover the raw `fetch`/`localFetch` call sites?**
Call sites using raw `fetch` return a `Response` and inspect `res.ok` themselves — they already handle their errors explicitly. The throwing helpers (`apiGet`, `apiSend`, `localGet`) are the ones where a forgotten `.catch()` used to vanish.

**What if `/api/build-info` is itself down when the bundle is collected?**
The bundle is assembled with `Promise.allSettled`; missing fields render as `null` and the report link still works.

**How big can the issue URL get?**
The body is truncated to ~6k characters before URL-encoding; recent-error entries are capped (20 entries, 800 chars each) so the bundle stays small.

- `07-marketplace-classifieds/raz-mon/`: deterministic data generator (every listing is a pure function of `(seed, doc_id, version)`), 6 disk indexes (3 HASH / 3 JSON, TEXT+TAG only, `SKIPINITIALSCAN`), resumable 16-worker bulk loader, 30/40/30 insert/update/delete churn @ 3k ops/s with a TTL stream, 13 weighted Flex-legal query templates, correctness verifier (lifecycle probes in reserved id space, stale-hit/content-mismatch detection), JSONL monitor + report aggregator.
- All queries carry `TIMEOUT 25000` after the default budget proved far too small at scale (see below).
- `INCIDENTS.md`: live incident log from the runs against the QA cloud Flex DB.

## Findings so far (details + timelines in INCIDENTS.md)

1. Quoted phrase containing a default stopword → `SEARCH_SYNTAX` error (recorded in README findings; generator vocabulary now excludes stopwords).
2. Sustained ~14k docs/s ingest knocked the shards over twice (~6.4M and ~15.1M keys): proxy answers PING while data commands fail; `num_docs` regressed 6.4M→4.3M in the first incident before recovering; both self-recovered in ~10 min.
3. **Open:** under churn + query storm at 35.3M docs, the cluster entered a shard-topology update that never converged (90+ min): `FT.SEARCH` fails with *"shards topology update is either transient or has failed"*, `DBSIZE` hangs, `INFO keyspace` serves a stale snapshot, while per-key reads/writes stay healthy. Escalated to the DB owner for cluster-side logs.
4. Default query timeout insufficient at this scale under load: ~48% of storm queries died with `SEARCH_TIMEOUT` before the switch to a 25s budget (and during incident 3 even 25s never completes).

## Runs

- Smoke (100k docs, cloud): PASSED clean — zero correctness events, zero timeouts.
- Full ingest: 35.27M docs (~70GB) loaded at ~13–15k docs/s (stopped at ~35M by design); `dbsize` == summed `num_docs` exactly, vertical split exactly 28/22/18/14/10/8%.
- 6h mixed run (churn + storm + verifier): pending cluster recovery from incident 3.

body:
We've observed unexpected incoming traffic in pcap that was caused by connections initiated by previous VM instance that was using the same bridge. Even if bridge is dropped between analyses, connections are still tracked in NAT and assured in conntrack.

While debugging this issue I have also observed that we don't drop forwards between VM bridges, so parallel VMs are able to each other.

This PR:
- adds `-A DRAKRUN_FWD -i drak+ -o drak+ -j DROP` rule that drops `FORWARD` between drak bridges
- calls `conntrack -D -s <vm_ip>` when vmnet is stopped. Conntrack is not installed by default on Debian, so failed invocation emits proper warning.

author: rmyndharis
body:
## What

Plugins running in the sandbox can now register as a search provider, so an external search backend (e.g. a Meilisearch or Elasticsearch plugin) can serve `GET /api/search` instead of the built-in database full-text provider.

A plugin calls `ctx.registerSearchProvider(handler)` from its worker, where `handler` is `(query: SearchQuery) => SearchResults`. The host routes query requests to the plugin over a new host→plugin RPC and returns the plugin's results.

## Why

All vendor-specific query logic stays inside the plugin's worker thread. The core knows nothing about the backend — it only routes queries — so adding a new backend is a plugin, with no core changes. This is the query side of plugin-backed search; indexing already works through the existing `message:persisted` hook, so a plugin keeps its own index current.

## How

Extends the worker wire protocol with three message types, mirroring the existing hook / webhook / health-check correlated request/response pattern:

- `search-provider-register` (worker → host) — the plugin declares it provides search.
- `search` (host → worker) + `search-result` (worker → host) — the host dispatches a query and the worker runs the plugin's handler and replies, correlated by `id`.

Host side:

- `PluginWorkerHost.dispatchSearch()` sends `search` and awaits the matching `search-result` — bounded by a 10s timeout that fails fast, and drained to an error on a mid-search worker crash, so `/search` never hangs.
- `PluginSearchProvider` adapts that transport to the existing `SearchProvider` interface, so a plugin-backed provider drops into the `SearchProviderRegistry` exactly like the built-in FTS provider.
- The loader wires `search-provider-register` to register the provider, with a mode-aware selection policy driven by `SEARCH_PROVIDER`: `auto` (the default) supersedes the built-in FTS provider; `builtin-fts` keeps the built-in active; `none` disables search. A provider is dropped from the registry when its plugin is disabled — and also when enable fails after registration — so a dead worker is never pinned as the active provider.

The protocol's search-type imports are type-only, so no search-module code enters the worker's runtime bundle. The registry is resolved lazily because search is an optional module, making this a clean no-op when search is disabled.

## Testing

Unit specs for each new component (worker-side registry, host dispatch + `id` correlation + crash/timeout drain, provider adapter, selection policy, loader wiring) plus an end-to-end bridge test that spawns a real worker thread, registers a provider, and round-trips a query through the full chain. The enable-failure cleanup is locked by a regression test (a plugin that registers in `onEnable` then throws must not leave a dead active provider).

## Compatibility

Additive — no public API changes. `SEARCH_PROVIDER` behavior is unchanged for existing deployments (`auto` / `builtin-fts` / `none`). A deployment with no search plugin sees no behavior change.

author: bandalgomsu
body:
## Summary

  This PR adds module APIs for accounting memory that is not tracked by `zmalloc`, and includes that memory in `used_memory` / maxmemory bookkeeping.

  New APIs:
  - `ValkeyModule_AllocateExternalMemory(size_t bytes)`
  - `ValkeyModule_FreeExternalMemory(size_t bytes)`

  These APIs are intended to be used by modules from a command callback or from a locked thread-safe context.

  ## Problem

  Some module architectures, especially asynchronous indexing pipelines, can create memory pressure that the core does not currently see.

  A concrete example is the Search module ingestion flow:
  - key data is captured during the mutation command
  - indexing happens later on a background thread
  - the eventual index insertion can amplify memory usage relative to the original key payload
  - if many ingestions are queued, the core can substantially underestimate real memory pressure until that later work executes

  That gap degrades OOM detection and allows the process to run significantly past the configured `maxmemory` threshold before the core reacts.

  This also applies to memory that modules allocate outside `zmalloc`, for example OS-backed allocations such as `mmap` regions used for huge-page-backed data structures.

  ## Solution

  This change introduces an explicit external-memory accounting path for modules.

  Internally:
  - the core keeps a separate external-memory counter
  - `zmalloc_used_memory()` adds that counter to the allocator-tracked total
  - as a result, maxmemory/OOM checks, `used_memory`, and `used_memory_peak` all include module external memory


Closes : #3339

author: geiserx
body:
First implementation phase of **remote multi-server deploy** (per [docs/REMOTE-DEPLOY-DESIGN.md](docs/REMOTE-DEPLOY-DESIGN.md)) — the security crown jewel, decision-independent, **no callers yet** (Phase 2 wires it into the outbound worker client).

## `internal/fleetnet.ValidateWorkerURL` (ported verbatim from CashPilot's SSRF validator)

- **http/https only**; host required.
- **Always-blocked** (regardless of policy): loopback, link-local, unspecified (`0.0.0.0`/`::`), and cloud **metadata** (`169.254.169.254`, `fd00:ec2::254`, `metadata.google.internal`) unless `AllowMetadata`.
- **Per-policy ranges**: `strict` = allowlist only; `private` = RFC1918 + CGNAT/Tailscale `100.64.0.0/10` + `fc00::/7` + allowlist (homelab default); `public` = any non-blocked.
- **IPv4-mapped-IPv6 normalization** (`::ffff:169.254.169.254` can't bypass).
- **DNS-rebinding guard**: resolves the host and rejects if **any** resolved IP is blocked; hostname that won't resolve → error.
- Allowlist supports exact host / `*.suffix` (Tailscale MagicDNS) / CIDR / literal IP. **Metadata is never overridable by the allowlist** (documented precedence).

## Config (Phase 0)

`WorkerURLPolicy` (default **"private"**), `WorkerAllowedHosts`, `WorkerAllowMetadata` (default false).

## Tests

~50 offline table cases via an **injectable resolver** (deterministic DNS-rebinding tests, no real lookups): good/blocked per policy, metadata, IPv4-mapped-IPv6, rebinding to private/public/metadata/loopback, non-resolving host, allowlist overrides. Config defaults asserted. `go build/vet/test -race ./...` all green on macOS.

author: ghost
body:
## What
Adds a hardened regex execution module (`fixes/redos_regex_fix.py`) that replaces unguarded `new RegExp(userInput)`-style usage with a safe wrapper that:

- Enforces a maximum pattern length (`MAX_PATTERN_LENGTH`) and maximum input length (`MAX_INPUT_LENGTH`) before any compilation/matching is attempted.
- Statically rejects patterns containing classic catastrophic-backtracking shapes (e.g. `(a+)+`, `(a*)*`, `(a+)*`) via a lightweight nested-quantifier detector, so obviously dangerous patterns like `(a+)+b` are rejected outright.
- Prefers Google's `re2` engine (via the optional `google-re2` / `re2` bindings) when available — `re2` is a linear-time, backtracking-free engine and is immune to ReDoS by construction.
- Falls back to executing `re` matching in an isolated worker process with a hard wall-clock timeout (`DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) when `re2` isn't installed, so even a pattern that slips past the static check cannot burn CPU indefinitely — the worker process is terminated if it exceeds the timeout.
- Raises a single `RegexSecurityError` for any of: oversized pattern, oversized input, dangerous pattern shape, invalid pattern, or timeout, so callers have one exception type to handle.

## Why
The search feature previously called `new RegExp(userInput)` (and equivalent Python `re.compile(user_pattern)` / `re.search`) directly against attacker-controlled input. A pattern like `(a+)+b` matched against a crafted string such as `"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaac"` triggers catastrophic backtracking, exhausting CPU (ReDoS) and enabling a trivial denial-of-service.

This change adds three independent layers of defense as required by the issue:
1. **Timeout** — regex execution is bounded by a hard timeout via a killable worker process when the safe engine isn't available.
2. **Input length limits** — both the pattern and the subject string are capped before any matching occurs.
3. **Safe regex engine** — `re2` (linear-time, non-backtracking) is used when available instead of the default backtracking `re` engine.

## Testing
- Added self-tests at the bottom of `fixes/redos_regex_fix.py` (run via `python fixes/redos_regex_fix.py`) that verify:
  - Benign patterns/inputs still match correctly.
  - The classic `(a+)+b` ReDoS pattern is rejected by the static nested-quantifier check before execution.
  - Oversized patterns and oversized input strings are rejected.
  - Invalid regex patterns raise `RegexSecurityError` instead of propagating a raw `re.error`.
  - A pattern that bypasses the static check but would otherwise hang is bounded by the timeout path when `re2` is unavailable.

Closes #724

author: livingphysics
body:
## What

`GET /api/history` (and the on-disk daily archive) now records actuator + control state alongside the sensor signals, so past traces can be correlated with what the reactor was *doing*.

Per point, added:

| key | meaning |
|-----|---------|
| `pduty` | peltier duty, **signed**: `+` cooling, `−` heating, `0` off (one number = duty **and** direction, matching the existing signed `current`) |
| `ring` | `[r, g, b]` ring-light colour |
| `stir` | stirrer duty % |
| `ir` | IR-LED power % used for the gated OD reads |
| `setpoint` | active temperature target during a PID/program run |

## Design notes

- **Compact + backward compatible**: new keys are written *only when present*. Existing archive lines (which predate this) stay valid; a missing key = null. `setpoint` therefore only appears while a run targets a temperature.
- **Signed peltier duty** mirrors the signed `peltier_current` already in each record (negative = heating), so duty and current move together on a plot and direction needs no separate field.
- **Lock safety**: actuator/setpoint state is gathered in `_actuator_signals()` from shadows / the control lock, called *outside* `HARDWARE_LOCK` to avoid lock-order inversion with the control thread. Peltier duty is captured from the same `get_peltier_state()` read already used for the current sign — no extra hardware access.

## Testing

Restarted the Pi service and confirmed on live hardware that both `/api/history` and today's `history/2026-07-09.jsonl` archive line carry the new keys:
`pduty: 0.0, stir: 30.0, ir: 10.0, ring: [0,0,0]` (peltier idle → `setpoint` correctly omitted), with all original sensor fields intact.

## Notes

- Droplet needs no change — its `/api/history` proxies straight through, so the new fields flow to clients automatically.
- This is the data layer only; the dashboard doesn't plot the new fields yet (easy follow-up if wanted).

body:
## Summary

#2865 (Tier-0 substrate root): standalone async generators had NO Wasm-native carrier — `async function*` was a #680 CE (decls) or a null-returning fn-expr, and the landed #2906 3d-i/3d-ii machinery was (a) gated wasi-only and (b) unreachable for the shapes real test262 files are written in (nested/fn-expr gens inside the runner's `test()` wrapper, driven by `f().next().then(cb, $DONE)`).

Five layers, each byte-inert off-lane and probed on both host-free lanes:

1. **Standalone activation (carrier-independent subset)**: await-free bounded gen bodies drive under `--target standalone`; the for-await-over-async-gen consumer activates (its every suspension awaits a machine-minted native $Promise). Explicitly NOT the #2980 carrier widen — Promise statics / await lowering untouched.
2. **Producer body generalization**: lead statements, zero-yield bodies, own-local frame spills (3a loop rule, spill-safe-gated). `yield*`/return/dstr-locals/pattern-params stay correct-or-legacy.
3. **Nested + fn-expr producers** (the real test262 shape) with capture support: nested decls thread `boxedCaptures`; closures record `selfCaptureLayout` and the resume prologue re-materializes capture locals from the frame-captured `__self` (without this, capture resolution used stale outer indices — a miscompile).
4. **Closure-context consumer drive** narrowly admitted through the #2646 phase-2 park (self-contained machine, validated); const-held fn-expr producers resolve via the new `ctx.asyncGenProducers` registry by initializer node.
5. **`.next()` runtime dispatch + `.then` native-receiver bridge**: ref.test chain to per-gen `__async_gen_next_*` at both the typed and any-receiver sites; `isStandaloneThenChainNativeActive` widens to standalone only when the module registered the native scheduler; any-typed receivers use the #3035 bridge (wasi: new nullMiss variant — zero-import contract preserved, issue-1326 green).

## Validation

- **Repro→fixed**: `for await (x of g())` standalone was #680 CE → runs host-free (imports=[], correct values); the distilled forbidden-ext driving shape (`f().next().then(cb,done).then(done,done)`) passes on both lanes, wasi zero-import.
- **Measured (runTest262File standalone)**: forbidden-ext decl files 2 (partially-vacuous) → 5 honest passes; **zero per-file regressions** across a 145-file construct-bucketed sweep (before/after jsonl diff).
- **Byte-inertness**: 8-program × {gc, standalone, wasi} sha256 matrix vs main — identical except the intended standalone async-gen cell (CE → host-free).
- **Blast radius**: 137 async/generator/closure unit tests green; the 7 pre-existing failures (2865-AG0 / 2867-gap2 / promise-combinators) reproduce identically on clean main.
- Residuals (all fail→fail vs baseline) + the #2895/#2978 boundary are documented in the issue file.

author: khovo
body:
Audit finding C1: the webhook route processed any POSTed JSON with no authentication at all — anyone who found the URL could send a hand-built Telegram Update claiming from.id == ADMIN_ID and have it executed as a real admin command (ban, broadcast, DB export, channel management), since nothing ever checked the request actually came from Telegram.

Adds a check against the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header, which Telegram echoes back on every delivered update once a secret_token is registered via setWebhook. Fails closed: a missing or unset TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET rejects the request rather than skipping the check, so a misconfigured env var can't silently degrade back to no auth.

Code alone isn't sufficient — Telegram also needs to be told the secret via setWebhook. See the accompanying deploy steps.

Verified with a Flask test client (handlers/utils stubbed out so the test
doesn't need real Mongo/Telegram deps): no header -> 401, wrong secret ->
401, correct secret -> 200 and dispatches, GET health check unaffected, secret entirely unset -> 401 (fail-closed confirmed).

body:
## Summary
This PR refactors the monolithic `App.tsx` component by extracting game state management into a centralized store and breaking UI logic into dedicated screen components. The simulator engine is also modularized into phase-specific handlers and utility modules.

## Key Changes

### State Management
- Created `gameStore.ts` with centralized game state using a custom store pattern (`createStore.ts`)
- Moved all game state (gameState, view, simulator, coins, bets, etc.) from component useState to the store
- Implemented `gameActions` for all state mutations (startGame, nextPhase, setView, setBets, setCoins, etc.)
- Extracted betting calculation and Hall of Fame persistence logic into store actions

### Screen Components
- Extracted `SetupScreen` - game configuration and seed/arena selection
- Extracted `ReapingScreen` - tribute reroll and confirmation (new phase)
- Extracted `RosterScreen` - tribute roster with betting interface
- Extracted `GameScreen` - main arena simulation with speed controls
- Extracted `EndScreen` - game results and statistics
- Extracted `HallOfFameScreen` - historical victor records
- Extracted `VictorInterviewScreen` - epilogue interview sequence

### Simulator Refactoring
- Created `SimContext` interface to encapsulate state, RNG, and logging
- Modularized simulator into phase-specific handlers:
  - `phases/training.ts` - training phase logic
  - `phases/interviews.ts` - interview phase logic
  - `phases/bloodbath.ts` - bloodbath and career alliance initialization
  - `phases/alliances.ts` - alliance management and betrayal
  - `phases/feast.ts` - feast event handling
  - `phases/dayNight.ts` - day/night cycles with hazards and vitals
  - `phases/epilogue.ts` - epilogue interview generation
- Extracted combat logic into `combat.ts` (resolveCombat, checkDeath)
- Extracted sponsor logic into `sponsors.ts`
- Extracted gamemaker event logic into `gamemaker.ts`

### Component Utilities
- Created `TributeModal` - tribute detail view
- Created `ArenaMap` - zone visualization with tribute locations
- Created `ShareButton` - replay URL generation
- Created `Stat` - reusable stat display component

### Type System
- Added `Build` type for tribute body types
- Added `GameConfig` interface for simulation parameters
- Updated `GameState` to include config and epilogue data

### Configuration
- Added `DEFAULT_GAME_CONFIG` with configurable parameters (districtCount, hazardRate, betrayalRate, etc.)
- SetupScreen now supports advanced configuration options via sliders

## Notable Implementation Details
- Store uses React's `useSyncExternalStore` for efficient subscriptions
- Game actions handle complex logic like betting odds calculation and Hall of Fame persistence
- Simulator phases are now pure functions accepting SimContext, improving testability
- URL replay functionality preserved and integrated with store initialization
- All localStorage operations centralized in store actions

author: ihid
body:
## Summary

Adds keyboard shortcuts for breakpoint stepping on the scrubber, matching the existing frame-stepping arrow keys:

- **Shift + Arrow Left** → previous breakpoint (`goToPrevBreakpoint`)
- **Shift + Arrow Right** → next breakpoint (`goToNextBreakpoint`)

Plain arrows are unchanged (frame-by-frame stepping). Shift always means breakpoint, with no fallback to frame stepping. When there's no breakpoint in the pressed direction the existing `moveToFrame(undefined)` behaviour applies (pause + show info widget, no seek), which mirrors how the `‹`/`›` breakpoint stepper buttons already behave.

The breakpoint navigation logic already existed on the orchestrator and backed the `BreakpointStepperButtons`; this PR only wires it to the keyboard.

## Changes

- `ScrubberInput.tsx` — branch on `event.shiftKey` in the `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` cases of `handleOnKeyDown`.
- `ScrubberInput.test.tsx` — two new tests asserting Shift+Arrow routes to the breakpoint methods (and not the frame ones); added the methods to the mock orchestrator.
- `scrubber-implementation.md` — documented the new shortcuts.

## Testing

- `ScrubberInput` unit tests pass (23).
- Full app suite passes (1867) via pre-commit.
- `pnpm typecheck` clean.

author: eylonkrause
body:
### Problem
The preprocessor crashes (SIGSEGV) or hangs on parseable SystemVerilog when a **callable macro invocation is truncated at end-of-stream**. Minimal reproducers (all with `--expand_macros`, e.g. via `verible-verilog-preprocessor preprocess`):

```systemverilog
`define A(x) hello `A
`A(1)
```
```systemverilog
`define A(x) x
`A            // top-level, no arguments
```
An included file ending in a callable macro reference (e.g. `foo \`A`) crashes the same way, and a `(` with no matching `)` (`` `define A(x) hello `C( ``) spins in an infinite loop.

### Root cause
`GenerateBypassWhiteSpaces` (verilog-preprocess.cc:63) pulls tokens from a `StreamIteratorGenerator` and dereferences the result — `**iterator` — with **no `end` guard**:
```cpp
auto iterator = generator();
while (verilog::VerilogLexer::KeepSyntaxTreeTokens(**iterator) == 0) {
  iterator = generator();
}
```
`MakeConstIteratorStreamer` returns the view's `end()` iterator once exhausted (token-stream-adapter.h), so `**iterator` on `end()` is a double past-the-end dereference. The function relies on the invariant that every stream ends in a kept EOF token (`KeepSyntaxTreeTokens(EOF)` is true), which stops the loop and lets callers see `isEOF()`. The top-level analyzer stream satisfies this (it retains EOF), but the streams re-lexed for macro expansion do **not**: `ExpandText`, `ExpandMacro`, `HandleInclude`, and the standalone tool all build their token sequence with a loop that stops *before* the EOF (`!lexer.GetLastToken().isEOF()`). A truncated callable-macro invocation at the end of such a stream reaches `ConsumeAndParseMacroCall`, which calls `GenerateBypassWhiteSpaces`, whose `generator()` returns `end()` → crash. The sibling streamers (`MakeTokenStreamer`) already guard this by returning an `EOFToken` sentinel; `GenerateBypassWhiteSpaces` does not, because it only has the `std::function`, not the `end` iterator.

### Fix
Restore the kept-EOF invariant on every re-lexed stream, so `GenerateBypassWhiteSpaces` stops at EOF and callers handle it gracefully (returning `InvalidArgumentError`) instead of dereferencing past the end:

- **`ExpandText` / `ExpandMacro` / `HandleInclude` / the standalone tool**: append the EOF token as an end sentinel before building the stream view.
- **`ExpandText` / `ExpandMacro` token-pulling loops**: `break` on the EOF sentinel so it is not forwarded into the expanded output.
- **`HandleInclude`**: skip the sentinel EOF when splicing the child stream into the parent (the child `ScanStream` forwards it as a pass-through token; without this it would land in the middle of the parent stream).
- **`ConsumeAndParseMacroCall` argument loop**: `break` on EOF. With the sentinel in place a `(` without a matching `)` would otherwise spin forever; this is the one caller that did not already handle a mid-scan EOF.
- **`ConsumeAndParseMacroCall`**: record the "illegal to call a callable macro without ()" error in `preprocess_data_.errors` (it was returned as a `Status` but never surfaced, so truncated input was silently accepted). This required making the method non-static (its only caller is non-static).

### Testing
Built `verible-verilog-preprocessor` and confirmed all four crash variants and the open-paren hang now exit cleanly. The full `//verible/verilog/preprocessor/...` suite (including the existing "Nested callable macros" test) and `verilog-analyzer_test` pass. Added `TruncatedCallableMacroDoesNotCrash` covering the no-`(` (now a diagnostic) and open-`(` (now terminates) cases.

Out of scope (separate, pre-existing bug, not addressed here): unbounded macro **self-recursion** such as `` `define A(x) `A(x) `` overflows the stack with no depth guard — worth a follow-up.

---

## What

Adds **Off Grid AI Desktop** to the **Local Chat UIs** section, alongside peers already listed there like LM Studio and Jan. It is an open-source macOS Electron app that runs a full AI suite entirely on-device, no account and no cloud.

Features:
- Local LLM chat via llama.cpp
- On-device image generation (Stable Diffusion)
- Voice dictation and transcription (whisper)
- Personal memory and RAG search
- Clipboard manager and encrypted vault
- MCP connectors with approval-gated actions

Repo: https://github.com/off-grid-ai/off-grid-ai-desktop
Site: https://getoffgridai.co/desktop
License: AGPL-3.0

author: praveenvijayan
body:
Closes #107

Adds `scripts/herd-verify.mjs`, the ratchet-herd PR verification stage. The monitor marks a worker `awaiting-verification` once its run opened a PR (head `agent/issue-<N>`); this stage runs **deterministic** checks and routes the outcome. It makes no scope/quality judgment and never merges, approves, closes, or labels.

## What it does
- **Conflicts** (`mergeable` CONFLICTING / `mergeStateStatus` DIRTY) → dispatch **exactly one** rework (merge origin/main, resolve, re-run GATES.md gates, push), counted toward `reworkCap`. Still conflicting after that, or already at `reworkCap` → escalate instead of re-dispatching.
- **Body** missing `Closes #<N>` or a gates section → escalate on text checks alone (no content judgment; the supervisor never edits PR bodies).
- **Clean** (no conflicts, `Closes #<N>` + gates section present) → escalate `PR #X ready for review` — the supervisor's terminal act.
- Mergeability GitHub is still computing is **deferred** to the next poll, never mis-classified as clean.

## Integration
- `verifyOnce` runs in the supervisor step right after the monitor (gated on `!dryRun`, since a rework is a spawn).
- The monitor's `TERMINAL_STATUS` set gains `ready-for-review` / `verify-escalated` so a verified worker is never dragged back into verification.
- New suite wired into `GATES.md` (row 4w) and `DOCS.md`.

## Gates (all green via `node scripts/run-gates.mjs`)
- `test: herd-verify` — 5 tests, one per acceptance criterion (offline: `gh` + spawn injected)
- `test: herd-monitor`, `test: herd`, `test: herd-dispatch`, `test: herd-survey` — unchanged, still pass
- `test-coverage` (gates-coverage) — new suite wired in; `docs-refresh` — DOCS lists the new scripts
- 23 gates passed, 6 skipped (TODO format/typecheck/lint/build/audit/secret-scan)
- PR size: 392 changed lines ≤ 400, 6 files ≤ 6

## Summary
- Hide the entire "Receive from exchange" section (Binance / OKX / Coinbase list + "Other exchanges" entry) on the Receive selector page when the current network is Lightning Network (mainnet `lightning` or testnet `tlightning`).

## Intent & Context
Product requirement: on Lightning Network the receive module must not offer the "receive from exchange" flow. Lightning receiving uses invoices rather than plain addresses, and the exchange withdrawal flows (Binance pre-order, deep links into exchange apps) cannot target Lightning invoices, so the entry is misleading and non-functional there.

## Design Decisions
- Network detection uses the existing `networkUtils.isLightningNetworkByNetworkId()`, which matches both mainnet and testnet Lightning network IDs — no new constants or duplicated ID checks.
- The network ID is resolved as `token?.networkId ?? networkId` (route params falling back to the active account), covering both entry paths: from a token detail page (token param carries its own networkId) and from the home receive entry (active account network).
- Only the Receive selector section is gated. The exchange guide banner inside `ReceiveToken` (driven by the `exchangeSource` route param) becomes unreachable on Lightning since its only entry point is this section, so it needs no separate change. The Home wallet action `WalletActionExchange` is a separate home-screen entry and is intentionally left untouched.

## Changes Detail
- `packages/kit/src/views/Receive/pages/ReceiveSelector.tsx`: add `isLightningNetwork` derived from `networkUtils.isLightningNetworkByNetworkId(token?.networkId ?? networkId)` and wrap the "Receive from exchange" block in `{isLightningNetwork ? null : (...)}`. The diff is mostly re-indentation from wrapping the JSX block; the logical change is the single conditional.

## Risk Assessment
- **Risk Level**: Low
- **Affected Platforms**: Extension / Mobile / Desktop / Web
- **Risk Areas**: Pure conditional rendering on an existing page; no data-flow or service changes. Worst case of a wrong condition is the section being shown/hidden on an unintended network.

## Test plan
- [ ] Switch to Lightning Network (mainnet) account, open Receive: the "Receive from exchange" section is hidden; Buy / Transfer entries still work.
- [ ] Switch to Lightning Testnet account, open Receive: section is hidden as well.
- [ ] On a non-Lightning network (e.g. BTC/EVM), open Receive: the exchange section still renders and each exchange entry works as before.
- [ ] Enter Receive from a Lightning token detail page (token route param path): section is hidden.

author: dmpl6454
body:
## Incident
Users (Fareen + others) got "An unexpected error occurred" submitting daily link reports on 2026-07-08 (~11:30 AM–6:24 PM IST). Prod pm2 logs showed 152 lifetime process crashes / ~22 in the incident window, every one `PrismaClientKnownRequestError P2024 "Timed out fetching a new connection from the connection pool" (connection_limit: 3, timeout: 10)` at `rbac.ts:11`.

## Root cause
`new PrismaClient()` + a `DATABASE_URL` with no params → Prisma defaulted the pool to `num_cpus*2+1` = **3** on the 1-vCPU box. Under HR-submit load the 3-connection pool saturated → P2024 timeouts. One **unguarded `await`** in the `requirePermission` async middleware turned a recoverable pool timeout into an **uncaught rejection → process crash-loop** (Express 4 doesn't catch async-middleware rejections). Postgres itself was fine (max_connections=100). Not OOM, not disk, not a bad deploy, not Linode hardware — a pool-size config fault.

## Fixes
1. **Pool size (root cause):** `withConnectionPool()` defaults the pool to `connection_limit=10, pool_timeout=20, connect_timeout=15` in code (safe on every env), plus a manual prod `.env` param (documented below). Chosen conservative for the memory-tight 2GB box.
2. **Crash-loop:** `asyncHandler` wraps `requirePermission` so a DB error → handled 500; `process.on('unhandledRejection'/'uncaughtException')` backstops in `index.ts`.
3. **Oversized-URL bug:** validator caps `url` at 2048 chars → clean 400 instead of an unhandled Postgres b-tree `54000`.
4. **Coupled mobile crash:** `getAllReports` is now paginated (was unbounded) and the reports UI caps links per card + loads pages — stops phone-tab OOM AND relieves the shared pool.

## Verification
- `npm run test -w @dashmani/api`: new `db-url`, `rbac`, oversized-URL, and pagination tests all pass. Full suite has 39 failures, identical before/after this branch (pre-existing gaps in account-growth/account/analytics/content/link-search/task suites — not touched by this change).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean across shared, api, internal.
- `npm run build` — all 5 apps build.
- Manually verified the reports pagination + link-cap UI live in a browser (seeded 55 reports, confirmed Page 1→2 nav, "55 reports" total label, "Show all 25 links" expander).

## Deploy notes
- **No `db:push`** (no schema change).
- After merge, a human runs the manual prod step: append `?connection_limit=10&pool_timeout=20&connect_timeout=15` to `apps/api/.env` `DATABASE_URL` + `pm2 restart api` (runtime-only, no rebuild). The code default means prod is safe even without it.

author: michaelsolo221
body:
## Summary

Replaces the (non-functional) single-agent workflow-node supervisor gate with two separate registered agents — **Claims Lodgement Officer** and **Claims Lodgement Supervisor** — connected via the `transfer_to_agent` system tool. Full reasoning in `docs/adr/0002-claims-supervisor-as-separate-agent.md`.

**Why the pivot:** the officer_node → supervisor_node LLM-conditioned edge in the previous single-agent workflow design never actually fired in practice — verified across repeated live `simulate-conversation` calls, regardless of prompt or `entry_behavior` tuning. `transfer_to_agent` is a mature, well-documented mechanism that does work end-to-end, confirmed via both simulation and the CLI test harness.

## What changed

- New `agent_configs/Claims-Lodgement-Supervisor.json`, registered as its own agent, with its own `end_call` and the same completeness guardrail as the officer.
- Officer's workflow removed; `transfer_to_agent` wired in, `submit_for_review` (a webhook tool that was never actually reachable — dangling inline definition) removed in favor of it.
- Officer **keeps `end_call`** — required by the PRD for emergency/wrong-number/unresponsive/WhatsApp-timeout exits, none of which involve claim completion. The constraint against using it to conclude a completed claim is enforced by prompt + the completeness guardrail, not tool removal (a node-level `built_in_tools` override was attempted first and found to be silently rejected by the CLI's SDK).
- **Found and worked around a real `elevenlabs` CLI bug** (0.5.4 and 0.5.5): `agents push` silently drops `transfer_to_agent` and inline webhook tool entries from the request with no warning, while reporting success. A direct API `PATCH` with the same payload persists correctly. Added `scripts/verify-live-tools.py` to the CI `push` job so this fails loudly instead of silently regressing production.
- Fixed a genuine pre-existing gap found along the way: the officer had no "Unresponsive Caller" guardrail text at all, despite PRD stories 21–22 requiring one.
- 3 new tests (officer transfers when complete; supervisor confirms when complete; supervisor catches a missing field) + 7 pre-existing tests updated to accept an early-but-safe transfer as valid, since the supervisor now re-verifies regardless of when the officer hands off.
- `CONTEXT.md` and this ADR updated with the settled domain language (Claims Officer / Claims Supervisor / Transfer / Supervisor Review / Completeness Guardrail).

## Known open item (not silently swept under the rug)

The supervisor's own completeness judgment fails **consistently** (3/3) in the offline test-mode harness on one specific scenario (missing `incident_location`), while passing **consistently** (2/2) via live `simulate-conversation` with the same scenario. I've detached that one test (`Claims Lodgement Supervisor catches missing field`) from CI rather than block the pipeline on what the evidence points to as a harness artifact (test-mode also mocks tool execution — "Skipping tool call in test mode" — so it's plausible generation differs too), but this needs real investigation before being trusted either way. Test file is kept in the repo for that follow-up.

The completeness guardrail is the only fully mechanical layer in the stack — officer self-check, transfer decision, and supervisor review are all still LLM judgment calls that can individually be wrong. This reduces the failure rate; it doesn't eliminate the failure mode the whole effort exists to address.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 scripts/validate-configs.py` passes locally
- [x] `scripts/verify-live-tools.py` passes against the live agents (both pushed and verified)
- [x] Officer test suite: 15-16/16 passing across repeated runs (one test flakes between runs — consistent with this repo's documented LLM-judge variance, not a fixed failure)
- [x] Supervisor test suite: 1/1 attached test passing
- [x] Live `simulate-conversation` runs confirm: happy path transfers and lodges correctly; withheld-field path correctly refuses to transfer/lodge
- [ ] CI `validate` job — will run on this PR
- [ ] CI `push` + `test` jobs — only run on merge to `main` per this repo's workflow; not exercised by the PR itself, but manually replicated locally (push + verify-live-tools + agents test) against the real agents

author: davesnowdon
body:
## What & why

The Obsidian **task line** grammar (`- [ ] <title> 🆔 lithos:<id> … <priority-emoji> 📅 <date>`) was encoded in **three** independent places, with **two** mutually-inverse priority-emoji tables kept honest only by a cross-module drift test:

| Site | Role | Duplicated grammar it carried |
|------|------|-------------------------------|
| `render.py` | writer | `PRIORITY_EMOJI` (enum→emoji), `TASK_ID_RE`, `extract_task_ids` |
| `sources/obsidian_fs_watcher.py` | reader | `EMOJI_TO_PRIORITY` (emoji→enum), `_TASK_ID_RE` (byte-identical), `_PRIORITY_EMOJI_RE`, `_DUE_DATE_RE` |
| `task_line_parser.py` | importer | `PRIORITY_EMOJI_MAP` (emoji→enum, a third copy) |

This is ARCH-5 from the architecture review (finding 5) — the *"2 mutually-inverse emoji tables held by drift tests; 3 independent parsers"* item.

## The change

New leaf module **`src/lithos_loom/task_line.py`** owns the grammar, modelled on `render_project_context.py` (render + parse as explicit inverses in one place):

- **One** `PRIORITY_EMOJI` table + its **derived** inverse `EMOJI_TO_PRIORITY` (`{e: k for k, e in …}`). Drift is now *structurally impossible*, so the cross-module drift test is **deleted** — replaced by a round-trip property test that pins the single table's values. The `_PRIORITY_EMOJI_RE` is likewise derived from the table's values.
- `TASK_ID_RE` + `render_task_id()` + `extract_task_ids()` — the 🆔 marker's render and parse together.
- `parse_priority()` / `parse_due_date()` — the trailing-metadata-zone parse atoms.

`render.py`, `obsidian_fs_watcher.py`, and `task_line_parser.py` become **consumers**. Deliberately kept where they were:

- `render.py` keeps the task→line **policy** (which markers a task gets: routing, deps, due-date rules) — only the marker *spelling* moved.
- the fs-watcher keeps its reader-specific `_LINE_RE` (it accepts any user-typed checkbox marker — `[/]`, `[>]` — broader than the writer emits, so it isn't shared grammar).
- the importer keeps its own doc parser (fences/blockquotes/tags/indent) and its **precedence** tie-break (arbitrary operator markdown may carry several emoji; the projected line never does — the difference is intentional and documented).

## Tests

New `tests/test_task_line.py`. The headline test **renders a real line with the writer and parses it back through the grammar** — strictly stronger than the old table-agreement test (it proves the projection's output is parseable by the reader, not merely that two tables share keys). The moved id-regex charset tests and the two relocated table-pin assertions live here now.

## Behaviour-preserving

Projection output is **byte-identical** (the existing `test_obsidian_projection.py` byte-pins pass unchanged). This is pure consolidation, no behaviour change.

`task_line` is a Foundation leaf (stdlib only) — added to `docs/architecture.toml` (Tasks component) and the import-linter Foundation contract; `CONTEXT.md` gains a **task line** term.

## Gate

- `make check`: **2259 passed**, ruff + pyright clean
- `lint-imports`: **4 contracts kept, 0 broken**
- component diagram regenerated: three new downward Core→Foundation edges (`Render`/`Sources`/`Subscriptions` → `Tasks`), no unexpected cross-component edges

author: preslavgerchev
body:
## What

Adds a computed `config_json` attribute to `mondoo_iam_workload_identity_binding`.

The `createWIFAuthBinding` / `getWIFAuthBinding` payloads already return the ready-to-use credential configuration for the binding (`type`, `issuerUri`, `universeDomain`, `audience`, `subjectTokenType`, `scopes`) alongside the binding — and the resource already **queried** it in Create and Read, then dropped it on the floor. Nothing in Terraform could reference it, so configs had to hand-construct the WIF config JSON, duplicating values the backend already decides (notably the API endpoint).

`config_json` is that API-returned config, serialized with the key names Mondoo client tooling (e.g. cnspec) expects in a WIF config file. Typical use:

```hcl
resource "mondoo_iam_workload_identity_binding" "runtime" {
  scope_mrn  = mondoo_space.test.mrn
  issuer_uri = "https://accounts.google.com"
  subject    = google_service_account.runtime.unique_id
  roles      = ["//iam.api.mondoo.app/roles/agent"]
}

# hand it to the bound workload, e.g. a deployment input:
#   mondoo_wif_base64 = base64encode(mondoo_iam_workload_identity_binding.runtime.config_json)
```

It carries no secret material (no private key — just the exchange audience/issuer/endpoint), so the attribute is not marked sensitive.

## Notes

- Populated on Create, Read, and Import (Read and Import share `readIAMWorkloadIdentityBinding`).
- Existing states pick it up on the next refresh; adding a computed attribute is backward compatible.
- `go build` / `go vet` / `make generate` (docs) pass; acceptance tests need a live org credential and weren't run here.

First consumer: mondoohq/serverless-scanner-gcp#191 (integration test authenticating the deployed scanner via a WIF binding).

**2. Remove Cypress and the E2E suite** — fixes the moderate `qs` DoS advisory ([1119502](https://www.npmjs.com/advisories/1119502), path `cypress > @cypress/request > qs`)

The E2E pipeline is permanently disabled (workflows already lived in `.github/workflows/.disabled/`), so the whole stack was dead weight:

- devDependencies removed: `cypress`, `@cypress/code-coverage`, `@cypress/grep`, `cypress-plugin-tab`, `cypress-real-events`, `eslint-plugin-cypress`, `start-server-and-test`, `vite-plugin-istanbul`

- Cleaned all references: `test:e2e:*` scripts, istanbul instrumentation in `vite.config.js`, the `plugin:cypress/recommended` override in `.eslintrc.cjs`, `vitest.config.js`/`.gitignore` entries, README/DEVELOPER docs
- Also drops unused `sonar-project.properties` and `analytics.conf.js`

**3. Upgrade Vitest 0.33 → 4.1.10** — fixes the critical "arbitrary file read/execution while the Vitest UI server is listening" advisory ([1120126](https://www.npmjs.com/advisories/1120126), patched in >= 3.2.6)

- `vitest`, `@vitest/ui`, `@vitest/coverage-v8` → `^4.1.10`; `vitest-sonar-reporter` → `^3.0.0` (the CI still uploads `sonar-report.xml`)
- Config migration: `deps.inline` → `server.deps.inline`; removed the defunct `transformMode` option
- Dropped the `picomatch: ^2.3.2` resolution pin — vitest 4's file discovery (`tinyglobby`) requires picomatch 4, and packages asking `^2.x` still resolve to 2.3.2 naturally
- Test fixes for vitest 4 breaking changes (36 failures, 2 root causes):
  - Mock implementations are now invoked with `new` when the mocked class is constructed — arrow functions are not constructible. Replaced them with regular functions in `src/tests/utils/localeMock.js`, `list-service-edge-node-service.test.js` and the `AxiosHttpClientSignalDecorator` mocks in the real-time-events-v2 specs
  - `vi.spyOn` no longer creates spies over `undefined` properties — added a `window.matchMedia` polyfill to `src/tests/setup-tests.js` (jsdom does not implement it), following the existing `ResizeObserver` stub pattern

### How to test

```bash
yarn install
yarn audit                 # 0 vulnerabilities
yarn test:unit:coverage    # CI command — 326 files / 2012 tests passing, lcov + sonar-report generated
yarn lint                  # runs clean without eslint-plugin-cypress
```

author: anagnorisis2peripeteia
body:
# [MPS] Migrate threshold and threshold_backward to Metal

## What / why

Part of #187455. `threshold_out_mps` and `threshold_backward_out_mps` are two of the
remaining `LookUpOrCreateCachedGraph` sites: each distinct shape compiles and caches an
MPSGraph with no eviction. Since `relu`'s backward routes through `threshold_backward`,
every ReLU training step grows the cache on shape-varying workloads.

The migration reuses upstream's design: the structured meta functions build the iterator as
`(self, other)` with `other = self` (forward) or `other = grad, value = 0` (backward), so a
single Metal functor `self <= threshold ? value : other` on the existing
`exec_binary_kernel_with_params` lineage serves both directions. The MPS structured impls
and their graph code are deleted (net -100 lines in Activation.mm) and the yaml dispatch
joins the shared `CPU, CUDA, XPU, MPS: threshold_out` / `threshold_backward_out` rows.
dtype surface is unchanged, including bool (MPS supports it beyond CPU per OpInfo
`dtypesIfMPS`).

**Semantics fix included:** the old MPSGraph path computed `x > threshold ? x : value`,
which sends NaN to `value`; the reference (and CPU/CUDA) keep NaN. The Metal functor matches
CPU/CUDA exactly, so the two now-stale MPS `expectedFailure` decorations on
`_refs.nn.functional.threshold` (test_python_ref / _torch_fallback, f16/bf16/f32) are
removed in this PR — those 6 instances now pass.

## Performance

Benchmark: `benchmarks/mps/bench_threshold.py` (committed). Interleaved A/B vs stock
nightly (MPSGraph), `Timer.blocked_autorange` median, 3 reps, M4 Pro.

Isolated op (no autograd), fp32:

| shape | MPSGraph (ms) | Metal (ms) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| threshold_backward (2048, 1024) | 0.218 | 0.080 | 2.73x |
| threshold_backward (16, 128, 1024) | 0.086 | 0.080 | 1.08x |
| threshold_backward (2048, 2048) | 0.216 | 0.208 | 1.04x |

Composite fwd+bwd training step (fp32): threshold up to 5.7x (64x4096), relu backward
6.5x at small sizes, 1.4-2.1x typical; two mid-size composite cells read 0.87-0.92x under
streaming (no-sync) measurement while the isolated op wins on the same shapes -- a stream
pipelining artifact of the composite measurement, not kernel cost.

## Correctness / Test Plan

- `PYTORCH_TEST_MPS=1 python -m pytest test/test_mps.py -k "threshold or (consistency and relu)" -q`
  (43 passed; OpInfo owns coverage -- no new standalone test needed for an elementwise
  structured op).
- NaN semantics vs CPU: `F.threshold([nan, 1, 0], 0.5, -9)` returns `[nan, 1, -9]` on both.
- Registry goldens (`HasDecompTest`, `test_public_bindings`) clean; full `--mps` suite clean
  modulo the pre-existing `test_metal.py::...test_conv`.
- Known pre-existing limitations (shared with the `exec_binary_kernel` family, e.g.
  `elu_backward`, `add.out`): direct aten calls with mixed input dtypes or a mismatched
  `out=` dtype raise (missing cast-kernel variants); autograd never produces these, OpInfo
  declares `supports_out=False`. Documented for a follow-up on the shared infra.

## BC-breaking?

No public API change. NaN handling now matches CPU/CUDA (was silently divergent).

## Review history

Local review + gate dispositions: https://gist.github.com/5aa9907b58da25379e5a258aa357a198

## What

Swaps immich's CNPG cluster to a migration-window image bundling **VectorChord 1.1.1 + pgvector 0.8.2 + pgvecto.rs 0.3.0** ([a-mcf/cnpg-vectorchord-migration](https://github.com/a-mcf/cnpg-vectorchord-migration), digest-pinned, smoke-tested: all three .so present, uid 26, PG 16.14) and preloads `vchord.so` alongside `vectors.so`. author: turegjorup
body:
Hotfix for the HeadQuarters feed and feed admin ergonomics: preserve line breaks in plain-text descriptions, import WebP feed images, and add a re-import batch action. ## Changes - **convert-newlines-to-br option** — new per-feed boolean (default false). When enabled, plain-text newlines in imported descriptions are converted to `
` during normalization, applied *after* excerpt handling so excerpts stay tag-free. Includes the entity column + migration and an admin toggle (mirrors `syncToFeed`). - **WebP images** — add `image/webp` to `ALLOWED_IMAGE_MIME_TYPES` so feeds serving WebP have their images fetched and stored locally instead of being silently skipped by the image handler. - **Re-import batch action** — "Re-import" on the feed index force re-imports the selected feeds via the async pipeline (`ReadFeedMessage`), reusing `FeedReader::readFeedsASync`; mirrors `app:feed:import --force`. Super-admin only; disabled feeds are skipped. - Unit test for the newline conversion; `da`/`en` translations for the action; `[1.2.5]` CHANGELOG entry. ## Why The HeadQuarters feed delivers plain-text descriptions (newlines, no markup) and WebP images. Newlines collapsed to spaces when rendered as HTML, and WebP images were dropped by the image handler's mime allowlist. The re-import action lets an admin re-pull a feed on demand without shell access. All behaviour changes are config-level and default to the previous behaviour: the migration backfills existing feed rows to `false`, and feeds already delivering HTML are unaffected.

author: happygamer1919-tech
body:
## Plain-language summary

When a consultation is transcribed by the AI partner, it arrives in the **Revisão Consulta** queue as a draft awaiting a clinician's review. Until now, clicking **Assumir** opened a bare free-text editor. This change makes **Assumir open the AI draft inside the full Ficha Médica editor** (the same form used to author a ficha): the twelve fields the AI filled in show up **in their proper Ficha Médica fields, ready to edit**, and every other field is blank and editable for the clinician to complete. The clinician edits, completes, and signs. The signed ficha then appears in the patient's **Registos clínicos**, exactly like any other signed record.

Nothing changes on the AI partner's side, and no database migration is needed - this reuses the existing review flow and the existing Ficha Médica editor.

**This closes the Wave 05 core scope: AI transcription fills the patient's medical ficha and continues their record.**

## Verification checklist (run against the preview deployment)

Sign in as **Therapist** (owner/therapist can review; admin is read-only; reception has no clinical access):

1. Open **Revisão Consulta** (`/clinical/review`). The seeded AI draft for **João Pereira** is listed as **Por rever**.
2. Click **Assumir** on that row. You land in the **Ficha Médica editor** (URL `/clinical/review/<id>`) showing the header row (Peso / Altura), the Problemas de Saúde grid, Mobilidade, etc. - **not** the old free-text editor.
3. Confirm the AI values are **visible and editable**: **Motivos da Consulta** shows the AI text, **Observações** shows the AI text, and the **Neurológico** systems-review field shows its AI value. Edit **Motivos da Consulta**.
4. Click **Guardar** (saves your edits; the ficha stays a draft under review).
5. Click **Finalizar (assinar e bloquear)**. You are redirected to the finalized record, which shows **Assinada**, is read-only (no sign button), and carries your edit.
6. Open João Pereira's profile → **Registos clínicos** tab. The signed ficha is listed (**Assinada**), links to `/clinical/<id>`, and exposes **Nova versão (adenda)** (changes after signing are new versions, never edits).

## The two axes stay separate + immutability

- **Signing is a `record_status` transition** (draft → signed). **Approval is an `ai_review_state` transition** (in_review → approved). `finalizeReview` advances both in one statement but by **distinct columns** - they are never collapsed. The claim transition (pending_review → in_review) and its audit are unchanged.
- **Immutability**: once signed, the record is immutable (the DB `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` trigger is the wall). Addenda are new versioned records; nothing is rewritten. Proven at the DB level in `packages/db/tests/review-finalize-rls.test.ts` (claim projects the twelve keys onto field paths; axes transition independently; a post-sign edit is rejected by the trigger).
- **No AI value is silently dropped**: the twelve keys are mapped by identity (W5-13); a mapping gap is the SPEC sec 2 PRODUCT-halt condition, honored in code. Under the identity path (proved by `ficha-medica-compat.test.ts`) it never fires.

## Migration-free proof

`git diff --name-only origin/main` - ZERO files under `packages/db/migrations/`, `supabase/migrations/`, or `.github/workflows/`:

```
apps/web/app/clinical/review/[recordId]/FichaReviewEditor.tsx
apps/web/app/clinical/review/[recordId]/page.tsx
apps/web/app/clinical/review/actions.ts
apps/web/e2e/fixtures.ts
apps/web/e2e/revisao-consulta.spec.ts
apps/web/e2e/seed/seed-e2e.mjs
apps/web/lib/clinical/ficha-medica.test.ts
apps/web/lib/clinical/ficha-medica.ts
apps/web/lib/clinical/records.ts
apps/web/lib/clinical/review.ts
packages/db/tests/review-finalize-rls.test.ts
```

## Gates

- `pnpm lint` - green (0 errors; only pre-existing warnings).
- `pnpm typecheck` - green (9/9 packages).
- `pnpm test` - green: web **948 passed** / 5 skipped, @osteojp/db **62 passed** / 275 gated-skipped (the live-DB RLS suite, incl. the new W5-17 lifecycle/axis-separation/immutability test, runs in CI), api 140, admin 10.
- `pnpm build` - the **web** app builds clean (route `/clinical/review/[recordId]` present). The `portal` app build fails only on a missing `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_*` local env in the worktree - a pre-existing env gap, unrelated to this change (zero portal files touched); CI has those envs.
- e2e (`apps/web/e2e/revisao-consulta.spec.ts`): authored, lints + typechecks clean. Not executed locally (Docker/local Supabase unavailable in this environment); runs in CI. Locators follow the anti-flakiness discipline: scoped to `#record-form` / the exact review row, `exact:true` on `Guardar` (vs `Guardar assinatura`), required field filled before save.

## DECISIONS / QUESTIONS

No new `DECISIONS.md` / `QUESTIONS.md` entries; no PRODUCT halt (identity mapping holds).

## Summary

- Root cause of the 0.7.3 partial publish was `IDENTITY_TOKEN_READ_ERROR` during parallel `changeset publish` (OIDC token fetch flake), not missing `registry-url`. Prior releases used the same workflow without `registry-url` and succeeded.
- `registry-url` on `setup-node` is actively harmful for Trusted Publishing: it writes an empty `_authToken` line that prevents OIDC ([actions/setup-node#1551](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1551)).
- Keeps `workflow_dispatch` + `force_publish` so we can finish `react-doctor@0.7.3` / any remaining packages.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CI-only change to npm auth configuration for the stable publish job; no application runtime impact.
> 
> **Overview**
> Reverts **`registry-url`** on the stable **Publish** job’s `actions/setup-node` step so npm **Trusted Publishing** can use OIDC again.

> `setup-node` with `registry-url` injects an empty `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` entry, which blocks OIDC ([actions/setup-node#1551](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1551)). The workflow now documents that stable publish is OIDC-only; **`publish-dev`** still sets `registry-url` for classic token flows.

author: laurenthuberdeau
body:
## Context

Because C99 bootstrap compilers generally only support a subset of the full C99 language, many patches are required to get the initial compiled version of TCC. The majority of these patches are to work around the missing support for 64-bit arithmetic on 32-bit hosts. If pnut-exe supported 64-bit arithmetic on 32-bit targets, the number of required patches would go down significantly, facilitating the auditing of the reproducible build process.

This PR builds on top of struct-returning functions feature and arithmetic with promotion rules (see https://github.com/udem-dlteam/pnut/pull/243, https://github.com/udem-dlteam/pnut/pull/244 and https://github.com/udem-dlteam/pnut/pull/246) to support 64-bit integers (`long long`) on 32-bit hosts. This is done by transforming 64-bit arithmetic operations into calls to functions implementing the 64-bit operations from unsigned 32-bit integers.

When bootstrapping TCC-0.9.26, the same hash is obtained when compiling with `HAVE_LONG_LONG=0` (bootstrapping `long long` with many patches) and with `HAVE_LONG_LONG=1` (using emulated 64-bit arithmetic). A follow-up PR will package this in an easy to use script, and compile the last TCC release, 0.9.27.

Two outcomes:

1. **`mindspec panel create | verify | tally`** — the review-panel lifecycle (today in `ms-panel-run` step 0 + `ms-panel-tally`'s decision matrix + hand-typed `panel.json`) becomes three agent-neutral CLI verbs. `create` atomically writes panel dir + BRIEF stub + `panel.json` (stamping `expected_reviewers`/`approve_threshold` from 109's resolvers, `reviewed_head_sha` co-bumped with `round`). `verify` is a read-only PASS/BLOCK preview computed by `panel.PanelGateDecision` (identical to the complete-gate). `tally` renders the decision from the binary (exit 0 Allow / non-zero Block + recovery). This makes `internal/panel/gate.go` the **single decision home** — the ADR-0040 ratchet. `internal/instruct`'s duplicate `verdict()` matrix is deleted and delegates to the same function.

2. **Spec-approve parser parity** — `mindspec spec approve` now runs the same canonical parsers the downstream gates use (`contextpack.ParseSpec` + `normalizeImpactedDomains`; `## ADR Touchpoints` link resolution against the same `adr.Store`), catching the spec-108 Impacted-Domains formatting incident at spec-approve instead of two gates later.

`internal/panel` stays a config-free import-clean leaf; `PanelGateDecision`'s semantics are unchanged; `validatePanelSlug`+`rejectControlBytes` (full C0/C1/DEL) close path-traversal + terminal-injection.

author: bdougie
body:
## Summary
- Serve the published [bdougie/smollm3-forest-lora](https://huggingface.co/bdougie/smollm3-forest-lora) adapter — the Nudge-step genome proposer for the Viridian Forest speedrun — as a local OpenAI-compatible API on Apple Silicon, so run tooling (and pi, interactively) can query it for battle/survival genomes.
- `scripts/serve_forest_lora.sh`: idempotent download → fuse → serve on `:8080`; weights live under gitignored `out/hf/`.
- `docs/serving-forest-lora.md`: quick start, curl verification, pi provider config (`~/.pi/agent/models.json`) with its gotchas, troubleshooting, CUDA-box note.

## Why fuse instead of `--adapter-path`
mlx-lm 0.31.3's `mlx_lm.server --adapter-path` silently serves the plain base model: `ModelProvider.load()` resolves the request's model path *before* the adapter-map lookup, which is keyed only by `"default_model"`, so the lookup always misses — including on the startup load. Verified with temperature-0 A/B requests (CLI flag → base-model output with markdown fences and an invented schema; per-request `"adapters"` body field → trained genome behavior). Fusing (`mlx_lm.fuse`) sidesteps adapter resolution entirely. Details and the evidence are in the doc.

## Test plan
- [x] `scripts/serve_forest_lora.sh` syntax-checked and run end to end (download, fuse to 2.1 GB quantized weights, serve)
- [x] curl `/v1/chat/completions` at temperature 0 returns immediate raw genome JSON (adapter behavior), not base-model output
- [x] `pi --provider mlx --model smollm3-forest-lora -p` with the genome system prompt returns a genome: `{"genome": {"hp_run_threshold": 0.2, "hp_heal_threshold": 0.3}}`
- [x] Existing `ollama` provider in `~/.pi/agent/models.json` untouched

author: fivetran-kwoodbeck
body:
Merging a derived table that projects a numeric literal (`6 AS a`) whose alias matches a `FROM` column, and is used in the outer `GROUP BY`, rewrites it to a bare `GROUP BY` a that rebinds to the column instead of the constant.  This changes the query result.  The fix is that `_mergeable` now blocks those merges.

Sample query:
```
SELECT s.a, SUM(s.b) AS b FROM (SELECT 6 AS a, b FROM x) AS s GROUP BY s.a;
```
Before, this query will return different results:
```
SELECT 6 AS a, SUM(x.b) AS b FROM x AS x GROUP BY a;
```
After:
```
SELECT s.a AS a, SUM(s.b) AS b FROM (SELECT 6 AS a, x.b AS b FROM x AS x) AS s GROUP BY s.a;
```

author: seraphire
body:
Emit `wix build -arch <platform>` in the generated build.ps1 and the example command so the MSI package architecture matches the ProgramFiles(64)Folder root and component bitness already in the WXS. Without it wix build defaults to an x86 package and 64-bit installs land in Program Files (x86).

Resolve WiX extensions at build time against the client's installed toolset version (wix extension add -g <pkg>/<wix --version>) instead of bundling version-locked extension DLLs into the export. This decouples the exported artifact from the WiX version AlliePack itself runs, so an AlliePack on WiX 5 can produce an artifact a client compiles with WiX 7.

## Resumo

Adiciona um gate rápido canônico para reduzir o tempo do caminho crítico de PR sem remover os workflows existentes.

## Escopo

- `.github/workflows/reqsys-required-fast-gate.yml`
  - Executa em PR, push na `main` e manual.
  - Usa `concurrency.cancel-in-progress=true` para cancelar execuções obsoletas.
  - Resolve arquivos alterados.
  - Compila Python alterado em `backend/`, `scripts/` e `tests/`.
  - Valida contrato mínimo do próprio workflow.
  - Faz smoke do `scripts/validate_security_baseline.py` quando disponível.
  - Publica resumo no job summary.
- `docs/ci/reqsys-required-fast-gate.md`
  - Documenta política Pareto do gate rápido.
  - Define próximos passos para eventual branch protection.

## Não altera

- Não remove workflows existentes.
- Não altera branch protection automaticamente.
- Não mexe em deploy, secrets ou runtime público.

Causa dominante endereçada: excesso de checks no caminho crítico de PR.
Resultado esperado: criar um check candidato para ser obrigatório, mantendo dashboards/report-only/smokes pesados fora do bloqueio principal após estabilização.
