author: gholie
body:
## What & why

Clicking an album track now **plays that exact song**, and each row gains **Play Next / Play Last** buttons. Previously, clicking a track only *opened* its album and left the user to press play — the original bug report.

The Apple Music Windows app **never autoplays from a deep link**, and SMTC exposes no play-this-track or queue verb, so driving the app's own UI through **Windows UI Automation** is the only way to choose a track or touch the queue (verified live against the shipping app).

## How

- `AppleMusicPlaybackController` navigates to the album via the existing deep-link launcher (also the graceful fallback), then finds the track's row and invokes its `Play …` / `Play Next` / `Play Last` menu item.
- The pure row/menu matching lives in `AppleMusicUiMatcher` (unit-tested); the UIA adapter is a thin OS-surface wrapper, like `SmtcTrackWatcher`.
- Every failure mode degrades to "album left open" — never worse than the prior behavior, never an exception surfaced to the UI.

## Opt-in (this is the key safety point)

Driving the app is **intrusive** — it takes over Apple Music and brings it to the foreground — so it's gated behind a new setting, **Settings → Playback → "Play songs from the album list (experimental)"**, **off by default**:

- **Off:** clicking a track just opens its album (prior behavior); the Play Next / Play Last buttons are hidden.
- **On:** clicking plays the track; the queue buttons appear on hover.
- The controller reads the toggle **live**, so it applies without a restart.
- Older `settings.json` files deserialize the flag to **off**, keeping the feature opt-in on upgrade.

The in-app warning is deliberately simple:
> When on, Samklang briefly takes over the Apple Music app to play a song (or add it with Play Next / Play Last), so the app pops to the front for a moment. When off, clicking a song just opens its album so you can press play yourself.

## Caveats (all fail *soft* → left on the open album)

- **Menu labels are English** — "Play Next"/"Play Last" match on English text (the plain Play item matches on song title, so it's language-agnostic).
- **App-update risk** — if Apple restructures its UI tree, automation degrades to navigate-only rather than breaking.

## Tests

- 402 passing (8 new): `AppleMusicUiMatcher` matching, the opt-in gating in `DashboardViewModel` (queue commands disabled/hidden when off, row-click still opens the album, live toggle), and the new setting's persistence + back-compat deserialization.
- Verified end-to-end against the real Apple Music app (play, Play Next, Play Last) with the app backgrounded, driven from Samklang's own buttons.

author: asbuyrylw
body:
## Summary

- **`notebooklm_client.py`** — Thin, fail-closed Google NotebookLM / Semantic Retrieval API client: creates ephemeral corpora, ingests text/URL sources, generates Audio Overviews (two-host podcast), and synthesises notes (study guide, FAQ, briefing doc). Falls back gracefully when no key is set. All URL sources are SSRF-guarded; third-party text is fenced as untrusted DATA before corpus ingestion.
- **`rich_media_generator.py`** — New orchestration module producing 9 rich-media asset types per cycle: `podcast`, `report_audio`, `explainer_video`, `slide_deck`, `infographic`, `research_brief`, `deep_article`, `blog_series`, `newsletter`. Gated by `AGENT_RICH_MEDIA_IN_CYCLE=1`. All output lands in a new `rich_media_drafts` table as `pending_review` — nothing auto-publishes. Runs the same deterministic compliance gate as Module 6.
- **`strategy_generator.py`** — Six new canonical capabilities (`podcast_creation`, `slide_deck`, `infographic`, `explainer_video`, `research_brief`, `deep_content`) and matching TOOL_REGISTRY entries: `notebooklm_api` (SEMI, five rich-media pathways), `llm_deep_content` (AUTO, in-house LLM for written content), `veo` (SEMI, Google Veo for video clips from production briefs). NotebookLM entry upgraded to document the API-vs-browser distinction.
- **`config.py`** — Three new settings: `NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY`, `NOTEBOOKLM_BASE_URL`, `RICH_MEDIA_TYPES`.
- **`orchestrator.py`** — `AGENT_RICH_MEDIA_IN_CYCLE` opt-in cycle step (mirrors the existing `AGENT_PRODUCTION_BRIEFS_IN_CYCLE` pattern).
- **`content_generator.py`** — `deep_article`, `blog_series`, `newsletter` asset types added to `GENERATABLE`, `TITLE_HINTS`, and `specs` so Module 6 can draft them via the in-house LLM path when NotebookLM is not configured.
- **`.env.example`** — All new env vars documented with usage notes and commented-out examples.

## How NotebookLM fits alongside Gemini and Veo

| Content type | Previous path | New path |
|---|---|---|
| Articles, FAQ, bio, schema | Module 6 in-house LLM (single-topic prompt) | Unchanged — Module 6 remains the primary path |
| Video production briefs | `production_brief.py` (prompt → spec) | Unchanged; Veo entry added to tool registry for clip generation |
| Podcast / Audio Overview | Not available | `rich_media_generator` → `notebooklm_client.synthesise_audio` |
| Slide deck brief | Not available | NotebookLM study-guide synthesis → formatted brief |
| Infographic brief | Not available | NotebookLM FAQ synthesis → structured visual brief |
| Explainer video script | Not available | NotebookLM study-guide synthesis → script wrapper |
| Research brief (PR/content) | Not available | NotebookLM briefing-doc synthesis |
| Deep article / blog / newsletter | Not available | In-house LLM structured path (NotebookLM optional) |

## Configuration

```bash
# Minimum: set one of these (same Google AI Studio key works for both)
GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key          # already used by GeminiEngine in audits
NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY=your_key      # optional dedicated key

# Enable the rich-media step in the monthly cycle
AGENT_RICH_MEDIA_IN_CYCLE=1

# Optionally limit which types to generate each cycle
RICH_MEDIA_TYPES=podcast,slide_deck,infographic
```

No key is required for `deep_article`, `blog_series`, and `newsletter` — those fall back to the in-house LLM path automatically.

## Test plan

- [ ] `python -m rep_engine.rich_media_generator generate --business-id 1 --types deep_article,blog_series,newsletter` — in-house LLM path, no NotebookLM key needed
- [ ] With `NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` set: run all types including `podcast` and `slide_deck`

author: benjackwhite
body:
## Problem

The CDP events consumer uses the Node HogVM to evaluate hog-function filters and find which functions to queue for an event. We want production evidence on how the Rust HogVM (`@posthog/hogvm-node`) compares on that path — both latency and whether it agrees with Node — before considering it for real work. Filters are pure Hog (no host functions), so this can stay small and observation-only.

## Changes

- Adds `RustVmFilterShadow` (`nodejs/src/cdp/services/rust-vm-filter-shadow.ts`): for a sampled filter execution it re-runs the same bytecode + globals on the Rust HogVM off the JS event loop, records how long each VM took, and compares the boolean match. Fire-and-forget — the Node result stays authoritative and nothing here can affect it or the hot path.
- Wired into the shared `filterFunctionInstrumented` utility and enabled only by the `HogFunctionInvocationPipeline` (the events consumer's filtering path). Every other caller leaves the shadow undefined, so nothing extra runs.
- Gated by `CDP_HOG_RUST_VM_SHADOW_FILTER_SAMPLE_RATE` (default 0). The native addon is optional; if it isn't built the shadow disables itself.
- Metrics: `hogvm_filter_shadow_duration_ms{vm=node|rust}` and `hogvm_filter_shadow_comparison_total{outcome=match|mismatch|error}`.

## How did you test this code?

- `rust-vm-filter-shadow.test.ts` (native module mocked): outcome classification (match / mismatch / non-boolean-as-no-match / rust error / missing result), that `compare` runs the same bytecode + globals and records the outcome, that a rejected native call is swallowed as `error` rather than thrown, and that a 0 sample rate never loads the addon or calls it.
- Added cases to `hog-function-filtering.test.ts`: the shadow is handed the real Node boolean, bytecode and globals for a bytecode-executing filter, and is not invoked on the pre-filter / no-filter short-circuits.
- `hogli` / `ci:preflight` weren't available in this environment; ran eslint, prettier, tsc (changed files clean) and the affected jest suites directly.

## Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Built with PostHog Code. An earlier revision buffered captures and ran them as rayon-parallel batches with bytecode grouping, plus geoip/bot-list init; since filters are pure Hog and the goal is just timing + correctness observation, that was simplified to a single inline per-invocation `compare()`. The `/writing-tests` skill was used to gate the test changes.

---

author: th0rgal
body:
## Summary
- Reorder the generated container `resolv.conf` so public resolvers (`1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8`) come **before** Tailscale MagicDNS (`100.100.100.100`), with the tailnet `search`/`domain` line preserved in between so tailnet hostnames still resolve.
- Reuse the same resolver generation in the API one-shot/preflight nspawn path (`build_nspawn_command` in `src/api/workspaces.rs`) so it no longer binds the host MagicDNS-first `/etc/resolv.conf` directly.

## Root cause
On a Tailscale (tailnet) host, `/etc/resolv.conf` is a systemd-resolved stub and the generated container resolver listed MagicDNS (`100.100.100.100`) first. Provider preflight (e.g. `api.anthropic.com`) can run **before** `tailscaled`/MagicDNS is healthy, so DNS resolution failed before the mission prompt ever started (`DNS resolution failed for api.anthropic.com`). The `workspace_exec` path generated the reordered file, but the API preflight/one-shot nspawn path still bound the host stub resolver directly, preserving MagicDNS-first ordering.

## Changes
- `src/workspace_exec.rs`: extract `build_container_resolv_conf` (public DNS first, then `search`/`domain`, then MagicDNS only for tailnet domains); add `resolv_conf_bind_arg()` shared helper.
- `src/api/workspaces.rs`: `build_nspawn_command` uses `resolv_conf_bind_arg()` for both shared-network and non-tailscale bind sites instead of hardcoding `--bind-ro=/etc/resolv.conf`.

## Tests
`cargo test --lib workspace_exec::` — 5 passed, incl. new:
- `generated_resolv_conf_prefers_public_dns_before_magicdns`
- `generated_resolv_conf_omits_magicdns_without_tailnet_search_domain`

## Runtime note
Existing keepalive containers that bind-mounted the previously-deleted resolver file will keep the stale bind until restarted. They need a restart (not done here) to pick up the corrected resolver.

author: redam94
body:
## Summary

Auto-generated draft post for review — **not to be merged until Matthew approves**. The post is marked `draft: true` and will not appear on the published site.

## Post overview

**Slug:** `geo-experiment-contamination-detection`  
**Title:** "What to Do When Your Geo Experiment Gets Contaminated"  
**Tags:** experimental-design, marketing-mix-modeling, bayesian, measurement  
**Length:** ~870 words

The post covers a concrete, previously un-blogged problem: what happens when a geo experiment's stationarity assumption breaks mid-wave due to a differential shock (competitor promotion, supply disruption, regional event), and what to detect and do about it.

Key points:
- Why randomized holdout designs cancel *common* shocks but not *differential* ones
- Why contamination is invisible to standard posterior diagnostics (R-hat, ESS, divergences all look fine)
- **Bayesian online changepoint detection** (Adams & MacKay 2007) on the treatment-minus-control residual as a real-time within-wave alarm
- **CausalImpact-style counterfactual divergence check** (Brodersen et al. 2015) at readout to audit the full window
- Decision rules: censor contaminated periods, extend the wave, or repeat — and why folding contaminated data into the posterior corrupts the ENBS stopping criterion
- A pseudocode sketch of where the guard would live in Augur's `loop.py`

## Sources

1. **Email seed (primary):** `m.reda94+blogtopic@gmail.com`, July 4 2026 — subject "Augur Continuous Learning Math: Gap-by-Gap Technical Audit and R" — a technical audit document attached as a markdown file. This post covers **Gap I** (within-wave non-stationarity detection) from that audit. Gap E from the same audit was already published as the sequential-stopping post on July 7.

2. **mmm-framework repo** (`redam94/mmm-framework`): `continuous_learning/planner.py` (ENBS / `should_stop` implementation), `loop.py` (Eq. 22 forgetting-rate), and the technical-docs continuous-learning spec — used to ground the code pseudocode and describe exactly where the guard would plug in.

3. **Literature cited:**
   - Vaver & Koehler (2011), Google Research pub38355 — geo experiment common-shock cancellation
   - Kerman, Wang & Vaver (2017), Google Research pub45950 — GBR/TBR framework
   - Brodersen et al. (2015), *Ann. App. Stat.* — CausalImpact counterfactual check
   - Adams & MacKay (2007), arXiv:0710.3742 — Bayesian online changepoint detection
   - Fearnhead & Liu (2007), *JRSS-B* — multiple changepoints extension

## Existing posts NOT duplicated

Checked all 27 existing posts. No prior post covers mid-experiment data contamination, within-wave stationarity guards, or changepoint detection in the geo-experiment context. Related posts linked from the draft: [Designing Experiments to Maximize Information](/posts/designing-experiments-to-maximize-information/), [Wiring Your MMM to Your Experiments](/posts/closing-the-loop-mmm-calibration/), [The Sequential-Stopping Worry Is a Frequentist Problem](/posts/bayesian-sequential-stopping-likelihood-principle/).

## Build check

`pnpm run build` fails on `/og.png` (missing system fonts) — confirmed pre-existing on `main` before this branch was created. The new markdown file itself introduces no build errors.

author: jussisaurio
body:
The runner injects a random PRAGMA integrity_check on the active connection after successful queries. When the draw lands right after BEGIN DEFERRED, the hidden read pins the engine's WAL snapshot at that point, while the shadow model takes its snapshot lazily at the transaction's first plan-level statement. A commit from another connection landing between the two produces a false "table should have the expected content" mismatch (and spurious BusySnapshot errors) even though the engine behaves correctly.

Keep the RNG draw so seed streams are unchanged, but only run the check when the connection is in autocommit; the hidden read is harmless there because its read transaction ends with the statement.

Tests: seed 14376183891491691549 (faultless profile, memory IO) failed with "expected 9 rows but got 4" before this change and passes after.

Phase 1 gave us the accounts table and cookie-file routing by account_id. This PR wires that into the Jadwal Post scheduling UI so a creator can say "post this to Channel A on YouTube and Account B on TikTok" — not just "post to YouTube." ## Overview Adds a `platform_accounts` JSON column to `scheduled_posts` (additive migration, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, safe to run on existing data). The schedule API stores and returns the chosen account IDs alongside the existing `platform_urls`. When the user schedules or edits a post in the dashboard, a small account dropdown appears under each selected platform chip — populated from the existing `GET /accounts?platform=

` endpoint Phase 1 already shipped. If a platform has no accounts configured yet, a hint appears pointing to the Accounts page. ## Features & Fixes - `pipeline-api/main.py`: additive DB migration, `ScheduleCreate` / `ScheduleUpdate` accept `platform_accounts`, `_row_to_schedule` deserializes it, `PATCH /schedule/{id}` merges it the same way `platform_urls` merges. - `dashboard-svelte/src/pages/Jadwal.svelte`: three new reactive state vars (`platformAccounts`, `newPlatformAccounts`, `acctsByPlatform`), lazy account list fetching, account select per chip in both the edit modal and the create-flow step 2, account label shown read-only for already-posted platforms. - `pipeline-api/tests/test_schedule.py`: 20 new unit tests covering `_row_to_schedule` deserialization, patch merge semantics, and `_cookie_file` path resolution for both legacy and per-account modes. ## How to test 1. Start `pipeline-api` and open the dashboard Jadwal page. 2. Create a schedule, select a platform — if you have accounts configured (via the Accounts page) you should see a dropdown to pick one. If not, you see "Belum ada akun — tambah di Accounts." 3. Save the schedule, re-open it — the chosen account_id round-trips through the API (`platform_accounts` field in the GET response). 4. Confirm the posted platform shows its account label (read-only) next to the URL once posted. 5. Run backend tests: `cd pipeline-api && python -m pytest tests/test_schedule.py -v` — 33 pass. 6. Confirm build: `cd dashboard-svelte && npm run build` — "built in X.XXs", zero errors. ## Release Notes Jadwal Post now lets you choose which account (channel) to post to for each selected platform. The choice is stored per post and will be used by the upload flow to pick the right cookies. Existing scheduled posts are unaffected — if no account is chosen the system falls back to the legacy per-platform cookie file.

author: patel-bhavin
body:
This PR fixes a field-mapping issue in the suspicious process executed from container file detection.

The detection previously extracted the file launched from inside the archive into process_name, which could overwrite or conflict with the CIM process_name field. Since process_name should represent the actual process image, such as wscript.exe, this update renames the extracted archive member field to container_file_name.

This keeps CIM process fields accurate while still capturing the suspicious file executed from the compressed container.

Updated behavior:
```
process_name = actual executing process
file_name = compressed container file
container_file_name = file launched from inside the container
```

author: empireenglishcommunity-glitch
body:
This pull request was created by @kiro-agent on behalf of @empireenglishcommunity-glitch :ghost:

Comment with **/kiro fix** to address specific feedback or **/kiro all** to address everything.
<sub>[Learn about Kiro Web](https://kiro.dev/web/)</sub>

---
## The real problem this solves
Two prior training crashes cost fully-lost progress because a plain training run has zero memory of its own state — recovery depended entirely on someone staying connected via a fragile Cloudflare tunnel to notice the crash happened at all.

## What this does
`train_supervisor.sh` wraps `sdxl_train_network.py` in a self-healing loop:
- `train_config.toml` now has `save_state = true` — saves full optimizer state + step count every 300 steps, not just LoRA weights
- On ANY crash, the supervisor detects it immediately, finds the latest saved state, and relaunches with `--resume`, continuing from that exact step instead of step 0
- Applies `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` — targets the likely root cause of this project's dual-GPU SIGKILL crash (Kaggle T4 pairs have no NVLink; forcing CPU-mediated GPU sync avoids the P2P timeout)
- Writes `supervisor.log` (full crash/recovery history) + `supervisor_status.json` (current attempt, last step seen) so reconnecting after any gap shows the full story immediately
- Gives up after `MAX_ATTEMPTS=8` consecutive crashes — a safety valve so a real unrecoverable config error doesn't loop forever burning GPU quota

## Tested before push (with a fake training script + fake `accelerate`, no real GPU needed to verify logic)
1. **Crash-and-resume**: simulated crash at step 150 (attempt 1, before any state existed) and step 450 (attempt 2, after step-300 state was saved) → confirmed attempt 3 correctly resumed from step 300 (not step 0) and completed. Verified via `supervisor.log` and `supervisor_status.json` output.
2. **Give-up safety valve**: simulated an always-crashing script with `MAX_ATTEMPTS=3` → confirmed it stops after exactly 3 attempts with exit code 1 instead of looping forever.

## Not yet run on real Kaggle GPU
This needs to be launched in the live Kaggle session next (via the remote bridge) to confirm it holds up against the real SIGKILL failure mode.

## Summary
- classify MCQ generation failures as `provider_error` vs `invalid_output` in server logs while keeping the client-facing `generation_failed` response unchanged
- add OpenAI-compatible adapter hardening for Gemini: `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` with one 400 fallback, prose-wrapped JSON extraction, and empty-content diagnostics for finish/refusal/candidate details

- Google direct base URL + invalid/transcribed key: `POST /api/v1/generate` returned `502 generation_failed`; logs now show `class=provider_error status=400` with provider message `Please pass a valid API key`.
- Google direct base URL + vendor-prefixed gateway model slug: startup logs a GenAI config mismatch warning; request returns `502 generation_failed`; logs show `class=provider_error status=404` because Google direct treats `google/gemini-2.5-flash` as a literal missing model.

The deployed failure is most likely provider configuration or credential value, not MCQ schema validation. With the corrected Google direct pairing below, local generation succeeds. Do not use a Vercel AI Gateway vendor-prefixed slug with the Google direct base URL. For Vercel AI Gateway instead, the expected pairing is `CODEGYM_GENAI_BASE_URL=https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1` and a vendor-prefixed model such as `google/gemini-2.5-flash`.

body:
## Что это

Новый **read-only орган самоанализа** — «орган размера». Агент теперь **сам замечает** свои раздутые файлы и докладывает, какие стоит разбить на модули. Это прямой ответ на задачу «он должен написать нам, что дальше улучшать».

## Строго только-отчёт (безопасно)

Цель кандидата — **абстрактная** `split:<файл>`, для которой нет детерминированного маппера. Поэтому:

- `:self-build-produce` **назовёт** раздутый файл в причине отказа,
- но **никогда не станет авто-переписывать** его.

Проверено: `map_backlog_candidate("split:core/loop.py") → decision=no_target, ok=False`.

Разбиение крупного «органа» — рискованный многофайловый рефакторинг; он остаётся за человеком (авто-режим — «потом», как договаривались).

## Изменения

- `core/backlog_signals.py` — `oversized_module_candidates(files)`: чистая, детерминированная; порог 800 строк; сортировка worst-first; лимит 25; новое поле `SignalRecord.rank_hint` (по умолчанию `0.0` — на существующие органы не влияет).
- `core/backlog_selector.py` — провод в `load_backlog`/`build_backlog`; вес источника самый низкий (`0.9`), поэтому advisory **никогда не вытесняет реальную работу**.
- `tests/test_backlog_oversized_module.py` — чистый сканер, ранжирование, интеграция на реальном репо.

## Что покажет на этом репозитории

11 раздутых модулей; первым — монстр `core/loop.py` (~4500 строк), затем `planner.py`, `verifier.py`, `model_router.py` …

## Проверка

- Полный прогон: **4031 тест пройден**.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Read-only scanning and advisory backlog entries only; abstract targets avoid automatic split refactors via the existing mapper.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **read-only “oversized module” organ** so the self-build backlog can surface bloated `*.py` files (≥800 lines in `core`/`cli`/`tools`) as grounded advisories, without turning them into auto-producible work.
> 
> `oversized_module_candidates` emits `SignalRecord`s with abstract `split:<path>` targets, worst-first ordering (cap 25), and small `rank_hint` bumps. `load_backlog` / `build_backlog` wire in a filesystem scan; the new source sits at the **lowest score tier** (0.9) so it stays below tech debt, TODOs, and other actionable signals. `SignalRecord.rank_hint` lets within-source ordering affect final ranking without changing other organs’ tiers.
> 
> New tests cover the pure scanner, ranking vs tech debt, and repo integration (e.g. `split:core/loop.py`).

author: yanai-taketo
body:
## 概要

`YaguraConfigurationOptionsCloner.Clone` の Viewer セクション複製に ADR-0007 由来の `Viewer:ReverseDns:Enabled` が含まれておらず、クローン経由の経路で当該設定値が失われる不具合を修正する。

Closes #186

## 影響経路の調査結果

`YaguraConfigurationOptionsCloner.Clone` は 2 箇所の実処理から呼ばれている。いずれも「読み込んだ原本をクローン → 一部フィールドのみ変更 → クローン全体を `yagura.json` に上書き保存」という同一パターン。

1. **`SetupWizardService.ApplyAsync`**（`src/Yagura.Host/Administration/SetupWizardService.cs`）: 初期セットアップウィザードの確定操作。`ApplyValues` が `Clone(before)` で `after` を作り、受信ポート・閲覧ポート・公開範囲・保持期間などウィザードが扱うキーだけを上書きしたうえで、`after` 全体を保存する。
2. **`PromotionWizardService.ApplyAsync`**（`src/Yagura.Host/Administration/PromotionWizardService.cs`）: SQL Server への本番昇格ウィザード。同様に `Clone(snapshot.Options)` で `after` を作り、`Storage:*` のみ上書きして保存する。

**実害**: 利用者が `yagura.json` を手編集して `Viewer:ReverseDns:Enabled` を設定済み（例: 逆引き DNS クエリの発生を止めるため `false` に設定）の状態で、上記いずれかのウィザードを実行すると、Cloner が `Viewer.ReverseDns` を複製しないため `after.Viewer.ReverseDns` が `null` のまま保存される。結果として、ウィザードとは無関係な ReverseDns 設定が読み込み時の既定値（有効）へ静かに戻ってしまう。ReverseDns は「外向き DNS クエリを発生させる機能」（ADR-0007）であるため、意図せず有効化される方向に倒れる点で実害がある。

なお、`ConfigurationChangePlanner.Compare` も現状 `Viewer:ReverseDns:Enabled` を比較キーに含めていないため、この設定喪失は変更検出（「この変更には再起動が必要です」等の通知）にも現れない。これは本 Issue の対象（Cloner）とは別の既存ギャップのため本 PR では扱わないが、関連する同期漏れとして記録しておく。

## 変更内容

1. `YaguraConfigurationOptionsCloner.Clone` に `Viewer.ReverseDns` の複製を追加
2. 再発防止テストを追加（`tests/Yagura.Host.Tests/Administration/YaguraConfigurationOptionsClonerTests.cs`）
   - `Clone_ReverseDnsConfigured_IsCopied` / `Clone_ReverseDnsNull_RemainsNull` / `Clone_MutatingClone_DoesNotAffectSource`: 本 Issue の直接の再現・修正確認
   - `Clone_FullyPopulatedSource_CopiesEveryProperty`: リフレクションで `YaguraConfigurationOptions` の全プロパティ階層を機械的に列挙し、`Clone` 前後で一致することを検証する網羅性テスト。個々のキー名を知らなくても、将来 `YaguraConfigurationOptions` に新しいプロパティが追加されて `Cloner` の更新が漏れた場合に自動で検出できる（`RetentionTests` の `KnownKeys` ⇔ `ConfigurationKeyMetadata` 双方向同期テストと同じ狙い）
   - `Clone_SourceWithAllSectionsNull_ReturnsAllSectionsNull`: 全セクション未設定時の境界ケース
   - 検証済み: 修正前のコードに一時的に差し戻して実行し、上記 3 テストが正しく FAIL することを確認した（テストが実際にバグを検出することの裏取り）

## 検証

- `dotnet build Yagura.sln` 成功（警告 0）
- `dotnet test tests/Yagura.Host.Tests/Yagura.Host.Tests.csproj` 成功（197 件全合格）

author: raysubham
body:
## Summary

Adds a detector that inventories **Agent Skills** installed for AI coding agents, at both global and per-project scope. It covers Claude Code skills and skills.sh-managed installs (including plugin-provided skills).

For each discovered skill the scan records:
- Metadata: skill name, agent, scope, and source
- A SHA-256 hash of the skill's `SKILL.md` (for drift detection)
- skills.sh provenance from lock files (source, ref, install/update timestamps)
- A stat-only census of the skill folder (file counts and sizes — contents are not read)

Lock entries with no corresponding folder on disk are dropped — a lock entry is not an install, so the inventory is limited to on-disk skills.

### Privacy

- Skill file contents are never read beyond `SKILL.md`, and are never transmitted.
- Only a single SHA-256 hash of each `SKILL.md` is recorded — never its contents.
- For local skill sources, the on-disk source path is never serialized; only the lock alias is recorded.

### Notes

- `SKILL.md` discovery is case-sensitive (exact `SKILL.md`).
- The `~/.claude.json` project-registry discovery is shared with the MCP detector.
- Enabled by default.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `gofmt` are clean
- `go test ./...` passes for the affected packages

author: jjstwerff
body:
Makes `store_load_url_trusted(r, url) -> boolean` work under `--html` (the browser wasm target) with the **same internal API** as native — one synchronous loft call; only the fetch underneath is target-cfg'd.

## The problem
A browser `fetch()` is async, so a synchronous call would deadlock the single-threaded event loop (the program blocks waiting; the fetch can never run). And the whole HTTP path (`registry_index`/`ureq`) is `#[cfg(feature="registry")]`, absent from the wasm shape (`--features random`) — so the function wasn't even compiled in.

## The fix — asyncify bridge, same as `loft_web.ws_yield`
The async→sync bridge is **asyncify**: calling the host import unwinds the whole wasm stack back to the event loop; `AsyncifyCtrl` runs `await fetch(url)`, then rewinds with the bytes — the loft call returns synchronously and the page never freezes.

- **Rust:** `net::fetch_bytes(url)` — browser → the `loft_io.loft_host_http_get` asyncify import; native → `ureq`; gated to exist exactly where `load_url` does. `Stores::load_url` un-gated (registry OR browser) + routed through it; `n_store_load_url_trusted` un-gated + registered for the browser build; the import added to the wasm-opt `--asyncify` allowlist.
- **JS shell:** the `loft_host_http_get`/`_copy` double-call suspend import (unwind → start `fetch()` + suspend; rewind → return the byte length / `0xFFFFFFFF` on error). `AsyncifyCtrl` extracted from `loft-gl-wasm.js` into a shared `doc/loft-asyncify.js`; the **headless** `--html` page (which store-loading programs get) now drives asyncify (resumes are event-driven by each `fetch().then()`).

## Validation — all five steps green (`doc/claude/plans/97-layout-contract/`)
- **V1a/V2b** — the emitted page carries the imports + the asyncify driver.
- **V1b/V3** (`harness/run.sh`) — the REAL 355 KB wasm driven in node with a mocked fetch: valid image → `url keys=7,13,42`; fetch error / corrupt image → `false` (fail-closed).
- **V5 parity** — the same program native via `file://` → byte-identical output.
- **V4 — the real browser** (`harness/run_browser.sh`) — serve the `.store` over HTTP, load the page in **headless Chromium**; the rendered DOM shows `<pre id="out">url keys=7,13,42` (absent from the page source → runtime output of a real `fetch()` + asyncify unwind/rewind).

Compile-verified on native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown`; all JS blobs pass `node --check`. Design + verifiable steps: `WASM_STORE_LOAD_URL.md`.

## Notes
- WASI (`wasm32-wasip2`) is separate (no `fetch()`) — a documented follow-on.
- `store_load_url` (SHA-verified) stays native-only until `verify_sha256` moves out of the `registry` gate; the *trusted* variant (this PR) needs no SHA.

body:
## Description

Adds a **Transfer Only** rebalance mode — paired origin→destination fund movements without buy/sell operations. Designed for jurisdictions where fund transfers between same-category vehicles are tax-exempt (e.g. Spain's *traspasos*).

### Why

In Spain (and other EU countries), transferring between funds doesn't trigger capital gains tax. Users can rebalance by moving money between funds rather than selling and rebuying — preserving their tax-deferred status.

### Algorithm

- **Two-tier supply**: draws from overweight categories first, then taps in-band headroom only if needed. Never worsens at-target funds.
- **Tolerance-aware**: minimizes transfers to bring categories within the configured drift band — not to exact target.
- **Northwest-corner transport**: supply sorted DESC for minimum transfer pairs. Deterministic output.

### Changes

**Backend (Rust)**
- `ScenarioMode::TransferOnly` variant + `SuggestedTransfer`, `ResidualGap` types
- `TransferOptimizer` (new module) with 8 unit tests
- `RebalanceService` routing + integration test

**Frontend (React)**
- 4th mode button in `ModeSwitch` (responsive 2×2 grid on mobile)
- `TransferPairRow` cards showing origin → amount → destination
- `ResidualGapBanner` when plan is approximate (insufficient supply)
- CSV export and copy-to-clipboard adapted for transfer pairs (fully i18n)
- i18n keys for all 5 locales (EN, ES, DE, FR, ZH)

### Bug fix (included)

Fixed drift-driver sentence displaying actual allocation instead of deviation amount (e.g. "1% below" → "2% below").

/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This PR adds cost t-digest accumulator to the `datalayer` to memory-efficiently store actual cost of inference distribution. The `CostDigest` is stored per model in the models `AttributeMap`.

The intended usage:

**Consumer**: `CostGuard` scorer or another cost scorer or visualization: read-only, works on clones from the `AttributeMap` via `Get()`. 
**Producer**: specialized `requestcostextractor` that maintains live authoritative `CostDigest` per model, reacts to `ResponseEventType` events, and publishes snapshots to `AttributeMap` for thread-safe consumption by scorers (CostGuard, etc.). 

This is an infrastructure setting PR, nothing is wired yet.

`tessera.dflash.x86_attention_fn`, the x86 counterpart to `rocm_attention_fn` (#330) / `apple_gpu_attention_fn`, routing `block_diffusion_attention`'s rank-3 `flash_attn(+attn_bias)` core onto the native AVX-512 online-softmax flash lane. This **completes the DFlash Phase-2 seams on both of this box's backends** (ROCm + x86).

## Changes
- New **`_x86_flash_attn(q,k,v,*,scale,causal,attn_bias)`** convenience wrapper (runtime.py) — the CPU analog of `_rocm_flash_attn`: builds a minimal sub-artifact and calls `_execute_x86_compiled_flash_attn` (which already treats operand[3] as the additive bias).
- `x86_attention_fn` is the **simplest seam** — the AVX-512 kernel is **f32-native with no head-dim constraint**, so there's no dtype cast and no head-dim gate (unlike the f16 / multiple-of-16 ROCm WMMA lane). Falls back to `ops.flash_attn` when the x86 elementwise lib isn't built.

## Verification (AVX-512)
`test_dflash_x86_e2e.py`:
- **Seam parity** to **f32 epsilon (~2e-7)** for head_dim **16 and 8** (the head_dim=8 case proves the no-WMMA-constraint path the ROCm lane can't take).
- **Whole-draft**: logits match numpy to 1e-5 **and greedy tokens identical**.

mypy + ruff clean; 51 DFlash tests green; docs 19/19 in sync. Plan doc + `dflash.md` updated — both DFlash seams (ROCm/x86) now done; the CUDA seam remains gated on the emit/ FA bias operand (Phase 1 CUDA, sm_120 box).

Next buildable-now cell: the **x86 MSA `msa_sparse_attention` lane** (the one x86 gap in the family) — reuse `flash_attn_ext` + NSA-style host-select.

body: ## What One **dense MP3 per conversation** + a **spans manifest**, replacing the client-stitched N-per-part playback model (backend half; app PR follows). - New artifact `playback/{uid}/{conversation_id}/conversation.mp3` (same 30-day lifecycle prefix): captured audio only — intra-part gaps (<90s) stay silence-filled exactly as per-part artifacts do; the >90s inter-part gaps are **collapsed**. - The audio-merge Cloud Tasks handler (schema_version 2, task name `amc-{conv}-{fingerprint}`) builds it and stamps the doc with `conversation_audio`: spans (`{file_id, wall_offset, artifact_offset, len}`, wall offsets on the `TranscriptSegment.start` basis), `duration` (wall), `captured_duration`, and the `audio_files_fingerprint` it was built from. Upload precedes the stamp, so a stamped fingerprint always implies a servable blob. - `/v1/sync/audio/{id}/urls` gains a top-level `conversation_audio` object (`cached`/`pending`/`unavailable` + signed URL + spans). The per-part `audio_files` list is unchanged — old app versions are unaffected. - **Staleness is self-healing:** late chunks (pusher post-completion flush, offline sync, conversation merge) change the fingerprint → call sites and the `/urls` poll re-enqueue under a fresh fingerprint-named task (defeats the named-task tombstone). Live conversations never churn builds (no stamp → no-op). - Fixes the **duration estimate bug**: `database/conversations.py` divided by 16000 (8kHz) instead of 32000 (PCM16 mono 16kHz), ~2× overstating the last-chunk contribution. ## Why Segment-tap seeking is broken across parts today (the app's offset formula ignores inter-part gap time, which exists in no file), displayed duration disagrees with playback, and client-side stitching caused the WAV/RIFF failure class. One artifact + exact span arithmetic retires all of it. Design discussed and approved (wall-clock timeline with gap knowledge kept in metadata, dense CBR MP3 for exact seeking). ## Tests - New `test_conversation_playback_artifact.py` (span math with fixed vectors — mirrored in the upcoming Dart mapper test — /urls states, handler structure) and `test_conversation_audio_fingerprint.py` (fingerprint determinism/sensitivity, invalidation rules). - `test_audio_merge_tasks.py`: `amc-` naming; made the `tasks_v2` mock robust to import order. - Updated stub lists in `test_sync_playback_service.py` / `test_batch_upload_storage.py` / `test_merge_validation.py` for the new imports. - **259 passed** across the touched suites; zero branch-only failures vs main on identical sets; `scan_async_blockers.py` clean. ## Rollout Additive; gated by existing `AUDIO_MERGE_DISPATCH_MODE=cloud_tasks`. Old app + new backend: extra `/urls` key ignored. New app + old backend: falls back to per-part. No backfill job — the first `/urls` poll builds on demand. Docs updated per repo rules (`AGENTS.md` service map, `listen_pusher_pipeline.mdx`).

﻿## Summary

Fixes a Zod validation bug that prevented users from saving a bet when the result was set to "Pendiente". 

The Shadcn `<Select>` component was using `"pending-_"` internally as its value to avoid empty string selection issues. However, the `betSchema` did not include `"pending-_"` as an allowed value. This caused a validation error to immediately block submission before the form's `onSubmit` handler could clean it back to `""`.

## Changes
- Updated `betSchema` in `src/features/bets/schemas/bet.schema.ts` to allow `"pending-_"`.
- Bumped version to `1.0.3` and committed `package-lock.json` alongside `package.json`.
- Updated `CHANGELOG.md` accordingly.

- [x] All tests passing
- [x] Conventional commit format
- [x] Version bumped in package.json & CHANGELOG.md updated

## Summary

Implements Agent Bounties Flywheel v6 across the public distribution surfaces:

- makes `Post your own bounty` the default CTA on the static website, `/llms.txt`, discovery manifest, hosted public proof/bounty/template/agent/funding surfaces, and contributor templates
- positions Agent Bounties as a network where AI agents earn money by continuously finding, claiming, solving, and getting paid for verified digital bounties
- adds machine-readable flywheel fields to `assistant_acquisition` and updates the discovery schema
- adds shareable proof-card copy while preserving the evidence boundary: proof/sharing/star/upvote never imply payment without reconciled settlement evidence
- updates GitHub proof/funding/check copy to ask users to post their own bounty and star/upvote after value is delivered

Public notice: #108

- #24 by @qilu13, `feat: add Python and TypeScript SDK examples`: open, `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, mergeability `UNKNOWN`, no status checks reported by `gh pr view`. Expected impact is low because this PR changes public positioning/discovery copy and hosted renderers, not SDK example APIs. If #24 touches `/llms.txt`, discovery docs, or public copy, rebase on `main` and preserve the new default CTA.

## Compatibility / Repair Path

No active PR is expected to be invalidated. Contributors changing public site, discovery, proof, bounty, template, or profile pages should keep:

- default CTA: `Post your own bounty`
- agent-facing rule: `The more good bounties you post and share, the more users join, and the more future bounties you can solve.`
- payment boundary: no funding or payout claim without verified Stripe webhook evidence or indexed Base escrow/payout evidence

author: ridashamasneh
body:
Adds client support for SMB2 server-side copy: request a resume key for an open source file (FSCTL_SRV_REQUEST_RESUME_KEY), then copy chunks into an open destination file (FSCTL_SRV_COPYCHUNK / _WRITE). New API: smb2_request_resume_key(), smb2_copychunk(), and a smb2_server_side_copy() convenience wrapper that does both steps in one call, each with sync and async variants.

Two correctness bugs were found and fixed while wiring up the IOCTL reply path for these ctl codes:

- struct smb2_ioctl_reply was left partially uninitialized when a reply carried no output body, so smb2_copychunk()/smb2_server_side_copy() could memcpy/smb2_free_data() a garbage pointer on any copychunk error that didn't come with limit info attached.

- FSCTL_SRV_COPYCHUNK{,_WRITE} report the chunk-count/size limit-exceeded error as STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER but still shape the reply as a normal IOCTL response (limits in the output buffer), not the generic SMB2 error format. The reply dispatcher routed it to the generic error parser regardless, desyncing the read. The request's ctl_code is now retained on the pdu (mirroring the existing info_type/file_info_class fields kept for QUERY_INFO) so the dispatcher can tell the two reply formats apart.

Also includes:
- smb2-server-side-copy-sync example and prog_ssc test program, covering sync/async and direct-copychunk/server-side-copy-helper paths for both FSCTL variants
- negative tests that provoke real server-side rejections (chunk count over the server's limit, overlapping source/destination ranges) rather than only client-side argument validation
- reuse a single resume key across all batches of a copy instead of re-requesting one per batch

author: oaralabs
body:
## What

Lets Prometheus authenticate to `api.x.ai` with a **SuperGrok / X Premium+ subscription** instead of a metered `XAI_API_KEY`. The `/xai` provider gains a device-code OAuth credential source; the inference wire path is unchanged (an OAuth access token is just a `Bearer`).

Ported from [NousResearch/hermes-agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) (`hermes_cli/auth.py`) — the shared public Grok-CLI `client_id`, scope, and device-code flow. **Verified live end-to-end** on a real SuperGrok account: built through `ProviderRegistry` → `OpenAICompatProvider`, streamed a call to `api.x.ai`, HTTP 200, model complied. `grok-3` requests are served as `grok-4.3` on the OAuth surface.

## How

- **`providers/xai_oauth.py`** — device-code login + auto-refresh + owner-only (`0600`) token store at `~/.prometheus/xai_oauth.json`. `get_access_token()` refreshes within 120s of expiry and returns `None` (→ caller falls back to the key) on refresh failure.
- **`providers/openai_compat.py`** — `api_key` may now be a zero-arg **callable resolved per request**, so a rotating OAuth bearer isn't frozen at construction (providers are cached/long-lived). The static-string path is unchanged and covered by tests.
- **`providers/registry.py`** — xai bearer resolution **prefers OAuth over `XAI_API_KEY`**, with a per-request fallback to the key if an OAuth refresh ever fails.
- **`scripts/xai_oauth_login.py`** — interactive login / `--status` / `--logout`. Device-code = no loopback, works on a headless box (open the printed URL in any browser).

## Notes / decisions

- **Precedence:** OAuth wins over `XAI_API_KEY` when both are present (spend the subscription, not the metered key). Direct `config["api_key"]` still wins for tests.
- **No model-preset change:** the OAuth surface accepts `grok-3` and serves `grok-4.3`, so nothing downstream changes.
- **`GET /v1/models` is 403-gated** for standard SuperGrok subs (documented xAI behavior). It's never on this path — the model list is configured, not enumerated. `/v1/chat/completions` works.

## Tests

14 new (`tests/test_xai_oauth.py`): store lifecycle, expiry-triggered refresh, refresh-failure degradation, registry precedence, callable-bearer-per-request. Full provider sweep green (85 passed: new + cloud + api-provider-keys + force-search).

## Not included / follow-ups

- Beacon `/api/providers` login button + OAuth status in the keys catalog (daemon-side surface).
- The daemon must be restarted to pick this up for a live xai session (set OAra maintenance mode first).

author: ctate
body:
Fixes the Windows report of aliasing around round elements (buttons) in default `native dev` apps. Two defects compounded:

## Rounded-primitive anti-aliasing (engine, all software-raster hosts)

Rounded-rect fills and strokes tested pixel centers with a binary in/out check, so curved edges stair-stepped — most visible on Windows and Linux, whose hosts present the software raster directly. They now blend fractional edge coverage derived from the signed corner distance:

- Coverage ramps only inside corner squares with radius > 0; straight edges and radius-0 rects keep the binary test and stay bit-identical
- Squared-distance short-circuits keep the cost to the ~1px boundary band; `bench-render --check` passes all budgets
- The macOS GPU path already anti-aliases via its path rasterizer, so this improves cross-engine consistency; parity pixel signatures re-pinned from test output (chart goldens reviewed in both themes)

## Per-Monitor V2 DPI on Windows

Apps were DPI-unaware: on >100% display scaling Windows virtualized DPI to 96 and bitmap-stretched the window, blurring everything and amplifying the aliasing. Now:

- The embedded app manifest declares `PerMonitorV2` DPI awareness
- The Win32 host creates windows at physical size for the monitor's scale (800×600 points opens 1000×750 at 125%), frames child views/webviews in physical pixels, reports logical size + real scale, and handles `WM_DPICHANGED` by adopting the suggested rect and re-rasterizing surfaces at the new density

## Verification

- Full test suite, validate, and all seven smokes green; render budgets pass
- Before/after pixel inspection on real Windows 11: DPI context probe flips UNAWARE → PER_MONITOR (PMv2), window geometry identical at 100% (no regression), button corners go from a hard 255→23 step to a proper coverage ramp
- macOS 1x captures show the same staircase→ramp on curved edges with straight edges unchanged

Adds the first working implementation of NEST.

- **`nest.sftda`**: Spin-flip TDA/TDDFT (SF-TDA/SF-TDDFT) on UKS/ROKS references,

- **`nest.nttda`**: Noncollinear Tensor TDA (NT-TDA) on ROKS references,

author: paulrobertlloyd
body: Jira issue: [MAV-1753](https://nhsd-jira.digital.nhs.uk/browse/MAV-1753) This PR adds support for multiple seasonal flu programmes and introduces sub-statuses for the ‘Not eligible’ programme status. ## Supporting multiple (flu) seasons When showing a seasonal programme status (i.e., for flu), the following rules apply: - When a flu programme is in progress (1 September-31 March), the child record shows details of the current season - Children will have multiple programme statuses (but not **Not eligible**) - When a flu programme has ended (1 April-31 July), the child record shows details of the last season - Vaccinated children will have a **Fully vaccinated** programme status - Unvaccinated children will have the **Not eligible** (No longer eligible) programme status - During the preparation period (1-31 August), the child record shows details for the upcoming season - All children will have the **Not eligible** (Not eligible yet) programme status Any previous (and/or future) seasons are shown on the child’s flu record, linked to from the bottom of a seasonal programme page. ## Introducing ‘Not eligible’ programme sub statuses Supporting multiple seasons of flu (and considering support in the future for fine-grained eligibility vaccination statues) means we need to introduce sub-statuses for ‘Not eligible’: - **Not eligible yet** - Season programmes (flu): the season hasn’t started yet - Other programmes: the child is not old enough for the programme yet - **No longer eligible** - Season programmes (flu): the season has concluded - Other programmes: the child is too old for the programme We can also move the ‘Children aged out of programmes’ advanced filter and make it a ‘Not eligible’ sub-status. The ‘Not eligible’ status is shown on all lists of children, except those for school sessions (because all children in a school session are eligible). ## Screenshots ### Child record Only shows the current (or most recent or upcoming) season. ### Flu record (current season) ### Flu record (previous season) Consent was refused so the overall programme status is now ‘Not eligible’. No actions can be performed on this record (i.e. can’t record a previous vaccination or invite to a clinic).

author: tehsmash
body:
## Description

Adds a new `claude-agent-a2a` application — an A2A protocol server that wraps the [Claude Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python), making Claude accessible to any A2A-compatible agent or orchestrator.

Key design decisions:
- **A2A `context_id` = Claude `session_id`**: uses `list_sessions()` to detect existing sessions and resume them, otherwise starts a new session pinned to the A2A-supplied UUID, giving multi-turn conversation continuity across tasks in the same context.
- **A2A task = one `query()` call**: each task runs until `ResultMessage` is received.
- **`add_artifact` MCP tool**: a custom in-process MCP tool lets Claude attach structured output as A2A `TaskArtifactUpdateEvent`s.
- **Config-driven binding registration** via `agent.yaml`: each transport (JSON-RPC over HTTP, SLIM RPC) has an `enabled` flag; only active bindings are registered and advertised in the AgentCard.
- **SLIM RPC support** via [slima2a](https://github.com/agntcy/slim-a2a-python): connection details (node address, app name, auth) are loaded from `slim.yaml` using the config loader from [slim-bindings#21](https://github.com/agntcy/slim-bindings/pull/21).

### Example `agent.yaml`

```yaml
agent:
  name: "Claude Agent"
  organization: "agntcy"

bindings:
  jsonrpc:
    enabled: true
    host: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 45000
  slimrpc:
    enabled: true   # reads connection details from slim.yaml
```

### Usage

```bash
cd claude-agent-a2a
uv sync
uv run a2a-claude-agent
```

author: houseme
body:
## Related Issues

Tracked by rustfs/backlog#1105

## Summary of Changes

Multi-node startups (Kubernetes StatefulSets, bare-metal, VMs) can hit transient DNS/local-host resolution failures while peers and headless-service records are still coming up. Previously endpoint resolution retried DNS for a fixed 90s window and then returned an error, which propagated out of `run()` and exited the process; in Kubernetes this drove repeated kubelet restarts even though the cluster eventually converged, which reads to operators as an unstable service.

This adds a startup topology convergence policy so recoverable DNS/topology errors surface as "process Running, readiness=false, waiting" instead of a process exit, while genuine configuration errors still fail fast. The policy has three modes:

- `orchestrated`: wait effectively indefinitely for recoverable DNS/topology errors so the process stays Running (readiness stays false) instead of exiting; also defer the DNS-IP cross-port validation because headless-service records can still be flapping.
- `bounded`: wait a finite window (default 3m) then fail with an action-oriented error listing host, stage, attempts, elapsed, last error and remediation hints.
- `fail-fast`: fail on the first non-transient resolution error (CI/local debugging).

Mode is auto-detected (Kubernetes via `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST` -> orchestrated; distributed URL endpoints on non-Kubernetes -> bounded; local path endpoints -> fail-fast) and can be overridden via `RUSTFS_STARTUP_TOPOLOGY_WAIT_MODE`, `RUSTFS_STARTUP_TOPOLOGY_WAIT_TIMEOUT` and `RUSTFS_STARTUP_TOPOLOGY_RETRY_MAX_DELAY`.

Additional behavior: divergent local/remote verdicts for endpoints that share a `host:port` are normalized (local wins), retry warnings are throttled (first attempt plus at most once per 30s), and DNS-independent checks (local same-path, physical-disk independence) still run in every mode. The change is confined to endpoint resolution in `crates/ecstore/src/layout/endpoints.rs` plus new env constants in `crates/config`; public API signatures (`from_volumes`, `create_server_endpoints`, `create_pool_endpoints`) are unchanged, and the fix stays inside the Rust startup chain (no `entrypoint.sh` dependency and no forced TCP/RPC preflight).

Files:

- `crates/config/src/constants/app.rs`: new env constants (`ENV_STARTUP_TOPOLOGY_WAIT_MODE` / `_WAIT_TIMEOUT` / `_RETRY_MAX_DELAY`, `ENV_KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`) and defaults (180s wait, 8s retry cap).
- `crates/ecstore/src/layout/endpoints.rs`: `StartupTopologyWaitMode` / `StartupTopologyPolicy` (env-resolved via `rustfs_utils::get_env_opt_str`, test-injectable), duration parser, per-policy DNS retry deadline/backoff cap, same-host local normalization, orchestrated deferral of DNS-IP validation, throttled/action-oriented logging, and a one-line convergence summary.
- `crates/utils/src/envs.rs`: minor cleanup — simplify the `log_once` poisoned-lock branch to `unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)`, matching the existing convention in `crates/obs` and `crates/iam`.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p rustfs-ecstore --lib layout::endpoints` (17 tests pass, including 5 new ones; uses injectable policy/sleep/deadline, no real long sleeps)
- `cargo test -p rustfs-utils --lib envs` (13 tests pass; covers the simplified `log_once`)
- `cargo clippy -p rustfs-ecstore -p rustfs-config -p rustfs-utils` (no warnings)
- `cargo fmt --all --check` (clean)
- `cargo check -p rustfs` (downstream binary builds)
- `scripts/check_logging_guardrails.sh`, `scripts/check_layer_dependencies.sh` (pass)

## Impact

- Deployment: Kubernetes/orchestrated multi-node startups no longer exit on transient DNS/topology errors, so pods stay Running with readiness false and stop accumulating kubelet restarts. Operators should keep a generous `startupProbe` `failureThreshold`, consider `publishNotReadyAddresses: true` on the headless service, and `podManagementPolicy: Parallel` on the StatefulSet; these are recommendations only, not runtime dependencies.
- Configuration: three new optional env vars (`RUSTFS_STARTUP_TOPOLOGY_WAIT_MODE|WAIT_TIMEOUT|RETRY_MAX_DELAY`), all defaulting to `auto` behavior.
- Compatibility: no on-disk or on-wire format change; setup-type classification is unchanged; mixed-version rolling upgrades are unaffected (each node resolves its own topology). One intentional behavior change: the non-Kubernetes distributed default wait grows from the previous fixed 90s to a bounded 180s; CI or environments that want immediate failure can set `RUSTFS_STARTUP_TOPOLOGY_WAIT_MODE=fail-fast`.
- API: no public API signature change.

## Additional Notes

Docker is intentionally not treated as orchestrated by auto-detection (container presence alone does not change behavior); Docker Swarm/compose distributed deployments fall into `bounded` or can opt into `orchestrated` explicitly. Non-transient and configuration errors (malformed `RUSTFS_VOLUMES`, mixed style/scheme, duplicate/root/empty paths, bare `host:port` without scheme, invalid port, local path reuse, shared physical disks, and later auth/RPC-secret/disk-format/IAM-quorum errors) are unchanged and still fail fast.

Adversarial Validation (high risk: init/distributed path) — one-line verdict per role:

- Correctness: attacked orchestrated skip vs setup-type derivation, empty/single-drive early return, and normalize-before-demotion ordering — no break found (covered by `orchestrated_policy_defers_dns_ip_same_path_check`).
- Security: only operator-controlled env parsing, no untrusted input/secret/injection surface — no finding.
- Concurrency/durability: single-threaded startup path, no locks, no shared mutable state, no persistence change — no finding.
- Compatibility: no format/wire change, rolling upgrade safe; documented the intentional 90s->180s bounded-default change. Endpoint-resolution tests inject a deterministic bounded policy so they no longer depend on the CI runner's ambient `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST` (verified by running the suite with that variable set) — no unexpected break.
- Performance: startup-only, O(n) over a small endpoint set, no per-request/per-object hot-path impact — no finding.
- Test coverage: every behavior has a revert-fails test; two end-to-end gaps (indefinite orchestrated wait, fail-fast transient) covered indirectly via `resolve_from` (`Duration::MAX`/`ZERO`) plus the timeout/backoff unit tests to avoid hangs and real DNS.

I have read and agree to the CLA.

Closes #81 (spec #75 / ADR 0015, user story #13).

## What

The background-work UI showed only a bare "Analyzing…" spinner, so a freshly imported recording gave no sense of when it would be reviewable. The Analyzing row now shows a live "~Nm left" / "~Ns left" estimate per recording, updating as the pass progresses.

## How

- **Backend (`media_worker.rs`, `media.rs`)** — motion extraction now streams frames from ffmpeg's stdout (`read_exact` per frame) instead of buffering the whole video, so we can report footage decoded as it goes. The worker emits an `analysis:progress` Tauri event carrying `{ recording_id, processed_ms, total_ms, elapsed_ms }`, throttled to one per 500ms. `total_ms` comes from an ffprobe duration probe; a missing duration degrades to a bare spinner. The wall clock starts at the motion phase (the tracked, long-pole phase) so the frontend's `speed = processed ÷ elapsed` is a clean ratio.
- **Frontend (`analysis-progress.ts`, `use-session-list.ts`, `session-block.tsx`)** — `estimateRemainingMs` derives remaining wall time from measured speed (processed footage ÷ elapsed), never a hardcoded rate; `remainingByRecording` keeps estimates only for rows still analyzing. The session list listens for `analysis:progress` for its lifetime and passes a per-recording ms-left map down to the row.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Remaining-time estimate per recording, updating as the pass progresses
- [x] Derived from measured progress (processed duration vs total), not a hardcoded rate
- [x] No new dialogs or decisions — display only

## Tests

- New pure-logic unit tests for `estimateRemainingMs`, `formatEta`, `remainingByRecording` (TDD). Frontend: 78 pass. Rust: 78 pass. typecheck + eslint clean.
- Reviewed with /code-review (Standards + Spec axes); both review notes (extract inline derivation into a tested helper; start the wall clock at the tracked phase) were applied before opening.

body: ## Problem After #104 merged, production showed **"Unable to read or update the workspace snapshot"** and fell back to browser cache. Signing out/in did not help. **Root cause:** Vercel deployed the new Prisma client (which references `stateCiphertext` / `balanceCiphertext` / …) but never applied migration `20260708195911_privacy_field_encryption`. Every `/api/workspace` call threw Prisma `P2022` (`column … does not exist`). PR #106 (auto-migrate only) was still open and not merged, so production stayed broken. ## Fix 1. **Schema compatibility (immediate recovery):** detect whether encryption columns exist (`server/db/schemaCapabilities.js`). If not, workspace + Plaid handlers use the pre-encryption column set (explicit `select` / plaintext writes) so the app works on the current production DB **without waiting for a manual migrate**. 2. **Auto-migrate on build:** `scripts/prisma-migrate-deploy.mjs` runs during `npm run build` when a real `DATABASE_URL` is present, so the next production deploy applies the migration and encryption turns on automatically. Once the migration is applied, the same code path encrypts at rest again (verified). ## Testing - Against an **un-migrated** Postgres (init-only): workspace GET/PUT round-trip → **200** (`test/workspace-schema-compat.test.js`). - Against a **migrated** Postgres: PUT/GET → **200**, `stateCiphertext` present, plaintext `state` NULL. - Full suite: 66 pass / 13 skip / 0 fail. - Lint clean on changed files. ## After merge Merge this PR → Vercel production deploy will: 1. Apply the pending encryption migration (build step), and 2. Even if migrate somehow lags, the compat path keeps the app working. No new env vars needed — existing `PLAID_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is enough.

body:
## Summary Fixes #549 — assistant messages rendered `/` as the literal HTML entity `/` (e.g. `https://`), starting with 3.4.1/3.4.2. **Root cause:** `semantic_message_builder.dart` reconstructs assistant content (answer text + reasoning/tool `
` blocks) and escaped text with Dart's **default** `HtmlEscape()` — `HtmlEscapeMode.unknown`, which encodes `/`→`/` and `'`→`'` in addition to `& < > "`. The markdown renderer decodes those entities in prose (via the `markdown` package's `DecodeHtmlSyntax`), but **never inside inline code, fenced code blocks, or link destinations** — so slashes there (URLs, paths, `a/b`) leaked to the screen. OpenWebUI's server uses Python `html.escape`, which does not escape `/`, so this over-escaping was Conduit-specific. ## Changes - Switch the shared escaper to `HtmlEscapeMode.attribute` (`& < > "` only) — drops the leaky `/` and `'` while keeping everything needed to neutralize HTML tags and to keep double-quoted `
` attributes intact. - Add `_escapeText`: plain answer text (`SemanticTextBlock`) is now escaped **only outside** code spans/fenced blocks, so `<`, `>`, `&`, `"` no longer leak inside code either (the same failure class, extended). `
` attributes/summaries/bodies keep full escaping — they're HTML-unescaped wholesale by `DetailsBlockSyntax._decode` at parse time and don't leak, and the body must keep escaping `
` for tag-counting. ## Safety The one real risk was UI-spoofing: skipping escaping inside "code" could let a model inject a fake `
` block. Guard: inline-code matching is restricted to a **single line** (`` `[^`\n]+?` ``), a strict subset of real code spans, so a multi-line span can't hide a line-leading tag from the block parser. Validated adversarially against the real `DetailsBlockSyntax` — inline, fenced, multi-line-inline, double-backtick, and indented `
` spoofs all stay neutralized. ## Tests - New `semantic_message_builder_test.dart` (8 cases): slashes, apostrophes, inline-code, fenced-code, tag neutralization, multi-line-inline injection — **8/8**. - `openwebui_stream_parser_test.dart` — **36/36** (updated one assertion that hard-coded the `/`-escaping byproduct: `</details>` → `</details>`). - `conversation_parsing_test.dart` — **44/44** (incl. `
`-neutralization tests). - `flutter analyze` — clean. > [!NOTE] > ### Fix slash rendering in assistant messages by switching HTML escape mode > - Changes `_semanticHtmlEscape` from `HtmlEscape()` to `HtmlEscape(HtmlEscapeMode.attribute)` so `/` and apostrophes are no longer converted to `/` and `'` in assistant message output. > - Adds `_escapeText`, which escapes HTML-significant characters only in prose regions, leaving fenced code blocks (backtick and tilde) and inline code spans untouched. > - Updates `renderSemanticMessageBlocks` to use `_escapeText` instead of the raw `_escape` call for `SemanticTextBlock` content. > - Behavioral Change: `
` and similar HTML tags in plain text are now neutralized via escaping, while the same tags inside code spans/blocks are emitted verbatim. > > > > Macroscope summarized 76e787f. > > ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved HTML escaping for rendered semantic messages to remove unintended extra entities and better neutralize tag spoofing (including `
`/``-style sequences). * Prose is now escaped while preserving URLs (e.g., forward slashes) and apostrophes; inline/backtick and fenced code blocks remain unmodified. * **Tests** * Updated the stream parser test to expect `
` to render as `</details>`. * Added a new regression suite covering escaping and code-region boundary/spoofing edge cases.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes assistant message rendering so slash and apostrophe characters no longer appear as HTML entities. The main changes are: - Switch semantic HTML escaping to attribute mode for generated message markup. - Escape plain answer text while preserving inline code and fenced code regions. - Keep generated `
` attributes, summaries, and bodies escaped for tag safety. - Add tests for slash rendering, code spans, fenced code, CRLF input, and details-block spoofing cases.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Safe to merge with minimal risk. The change is localized to semantic message serialization and tests. The implementation keeps generated details markup escaped while preserving markdown code regions. The tests cover the main rendering and spoofing edge cases reviewed. No files require special attention.

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - We confirmed that Flutter and Dart are not on PATH, based on the semantic-message-availability.log. - The semantic message builder test invocation could not start because Flutter was not found on PATH, with /bin/sh: flutter: not found and exit code 127, as shown in the semantic-message-builder-test-blocker.log. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | lib/core/services/semantic_message_builder.dart | Switches semantic HTML escaping to attribute mode and adds line-aware text escaping that preserves inline and fenced code while escaping prose and generated details content. | | test/core/services/openwebui_stream_parser_test.dart | Updates the escaping expectation for generated details content now that closing slashes are no longer over-escaped. | | test/core/services/semantic_message_builder_test.dart | Adds tests for entity rendering, code preservation, tag neutralization, CRLF handling, and prior spoofing edge cases. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% sequenceDiagram participant Parser as OpenWebUI stream parser participant Builder as renderSemanticMessageBlocks participant Escaper as _escapeText / _escape participant Markdown as Markdown renderer Parser->>Builder: SemanticTextBlock + SemanticDetailsBlock Builder->>Escaper: Escape text blocks line-by-line Escaper-->>Builder: Prose escaped, inline/fenced code preserved Builder->>Escaper: Escape details attrs/summary/body Escaper-->>Builder: Details content tag-safe Builder->>Markdown: Seria

author: waiff
body:
## What
The dedup **candidate-drain lane** (`dedup_engine.py --candidates`, cron `30 */2`) has done
**zero work since 2026-07-05**: `_proposed_candidate_property_ids` bound the float-typed
`dedup_candidate_redecide_hours` setting into `make_interval(hours => %s)`, and Postgres has no
`make_interval(hours => double precision)` overload (only `secs` is `float8`). Every run raised
`UndefinedFunction` ~3s in — roughly half of the 44 "Dedup engine" workflow failures since Jul 5.

This is the **live driver** of the `/dedup` operator review-queue explosion: `property_identity_candidates`
`status='proposed'` grew from ~390 to **15,934** (12,424 past the 24h backoff), and it kept growing
*after* the Jul 5–8 credit outage was resolved — because the lane that re-decides and clears these
pairs was crashing on startup, not because of the outage.

## Fix
Express the backoff as `%(backoff_h)s * interval '1 hour'` (preserves fractional-hour support;
`float8 * interval` is a valid operator). One line in `scripts/dedup_engine.py`.

**Verified against the live schema** (Supabase): the old form raises `UndefinedFunction`, the new
form runs, and the drain's due-set is 12,424 candidates.

## Why it shipped green
The existing SQL-capture test (`test_proposed_candidate_property_ids_due_filter_sql`) **asserted the
broken string was present** — it passed only because the fake connection never executes SQL (the
documented `_FakeConn` gap). This PR corrects that assertion to the interval-multiply idiom plus a
negative guard on `make_interval(hours`. The systemic catch for this whole class is the unmerged
schema-aware SQL gate (**#665**) — recommend merging it next (audit WS6-1).

## After merge
The next scheduled `--candidates` run will start draining the 12.4k due backlog at its budget
(100 compares / 300 floor-plan per run). The large geo `visual_inconclusive` cohort is better
cleared by a one-off batch-API re-decide (audit WS3-2, operator-approved) than by the drain alone.

Part of the 2026-07-09 failure/alerting audit (`docs/design/failure-audit-2026-07-09.md`), workstream WS0-1.

author: innders
body:
Improves and optimises the speed of hierarchy browsing on the overview page by 10x.

## Before

Everytime a folder was expanded, a query would be fired to get the tasks for that one folder.

When multiple folders were opened at once, this would trigger a separate request for every folder. If you opened 100 tasks (not that many) then it would trigger 100 synchronous requests. This would often cause the server CPU usage to spike as it tried to deal with all the requests at once.

As the user expanded and closed folders over time they would build up a cache for each folder. When the user went to filter the tasks, this would trigger a new request for every single folder expanded over that session.

The user story would be a coordinator who is going through lots of shots checking them by expanded in the folder. Now they want to do a filter, ever folder that have expanded and even collapsed up until that point will trigger a new request. All at once. Over an hour of working this could be 100s of folders.

## After

Now we try to batch the folders in one query so instead of 100 requests it's just 1.

- Keep track of previously expanded folders so they are not included in next data fetch.
- Batch all the new expanded folders into batches of 100.
- Make request for the first batch and check if it has anymore pages of tasks.
- Get next pages for batch if required.
- Move onto next batch and repeat.

### Important changes

- Batches expanded folders into single queries. Now 200 expanded folders = 2 requests instead of 200
- Each query runs asynchronously so we not overloading the server in one go.
- There is a hard limit of 5000 folders that they can request at one time and warning banner will show.
- When the user creates a filter, we only need to rerun those batches instead of for every folder.

## Testing

1. Open network tab and filter to graphql
2. Expand one folder
3. Expand 100s in one go (expand children)
4. Check to see number of requests, it should be number of folders / 100. 500 / 100 = 5 requests.
5. Check the requests are made one after another
6. Create a new filter and check the number of new requests is the same in step 4
