body:
## P3 — Whole-block delivery + athlete multi-week view

Fourth phase of the fixed-selection reshape (epic #440, spec `docs/meso/fixed-selection-plan.md`). Delivery moves from **one week at a time** to **the whole block at once**, the athlete home becomes a **read-only multi-week table**, and the delivery diff finally becomes **exception-aware** (the P2→P3 carry-over). No schema changes / no migrations.

### What changed

**1. Block-level delivery (write path).** `plan_deliver` now delivers the whole block — every live week of the target week's `Mesocycle` — stamping `delivered_at` (one shared timestamp) + one `WeekDelivery` snapshot per week; re-delivering re-stamps. `is_current` is untouched (delivering never moves the live pointer). The **group** path is unchanged (a later phase rewrites it).

**2. Block notification.** One email + one push per block delivery — *"your new block is ready (N weeks)"* — via new `_notify_athlete_block_delivered` / `send_block_delivered_email` / `notify_block_delivered` (+ `block_delivered.*` templates). The per-week variants stay for the group path.

**3. Block deliver screen.** `deliver_screen` + `deliver.html` reframed from single-week to the block: per-week "Wk N" change sections, *"Deliver block (N weeks)"*, block-flavored success copy. (Kept on Alpine deliberately — per the designer-framework plan the deliver screen stays Alpine; only the designer grid became a React island.)

**4. Delivery diff is now exception-aware (P2→P3 carry-over).** `skipped` joins `_PRESCRIPTION_DIFF_FIELDS` and renders **off/on** (not the `default` em-dash); `_diff_exercises` is athlete-facing — an *add-this-week* skipped placeholder no longer reads as a phantom **added** on non-target weeks, a row skipped in both snapshots suppresses its field edits, and a skip flip still surfaces.

**5. Athlete multi-week home + `is_current` re-meaning.** `/meso/me/` now shows the whole delivered block as a **read-only multi-week table** (exercises × delivered weeks, one horizontally-scrolling table per day, focus week highlighted, skipped = em-dash, swaps named) plus the focus week's tappable log rows. Pure server-rendered HTML/CSS — **no JS added**. `is_current` now means *the week the athlete is on*; the home anchors on it (block + focus) when it's a single, delivered current week, falling back to the latest delivered week for group snapshots (which flag every delivered week current) and still-undelivered current weeks.

### Design decisions (all spec-supported)
- **"Block" = one mesocycle** (all its live weeks). Group delivery stays per-week (deferred to P5). `append_week` clean-cell behavior unchanged (documented P0 decision).

### Verification
- **Full suite: 2240 passed** (+4 new regression tests, no regressions). Red/green throughout; each of the three implementation slices was TDD'd.
- **Drove the real app** (seeded demo, port 8034): coach block-deliver screen renders block framing → delivering stamps all 4 weeks + a `WeekDelivery` each (`is_current` preserved) → athlete home renders the 4-column table with the current week highlighted, the seeded skip (em-dash) and swap (Cable Crunch) visible, deload marked. This caught a real bug the unit tests missed — a multi-line `{# #}` comment leaking onto the athlete's screen (Django's `{# #}` is single-line only) — fixed + guarded (`b972f7d`).

### Review
Converged through a **Codex review loop** (`codex review`, local): 4 nits fixed across 3 iterations (build-ahead row leak; deterministic latest-week selection; group-plan focus regression; earlier-block current pointer), 1 declined with rationale (non-atomic block delivery — `ATOMIC_REQUESTS=True` already wraps the request). Final pass: **CLEAN**.

Part of #440 (P0–P2 shipped; P4 agent rescope + P5 group remain).

author: igogo-x86
body:
LoopVectorize decides whether to attach llvm.loop.unroll.runtime.disable metadata to the vector loop based on a single target-wide bit, UnrollingPreferences::UnrollVectorizedLoop (AMDGPU sets it unconditionally since D149281). To read this bit, it called getUnrollingPreferences on the newly created vector loop and passed the vectorizer's ScalarEvolution, so SCEV was queried on IR in the middle of the transform.

This has a visible side effect: any SCEV query at this point fills the SCEV caches with expressions for the new loop skeleton, and this changes which existing values SCEVExpander reuses later when it expands the minimum-iteration checks for the epilogue. As a result, if a target's getUnrollingPreferences queries SCEV (ARM already does, AArch64 will in llvm/llvm-project#205102), the emitted IR depends on when the hook runs.

UnrollVectorizedLoop is a target constant, so query it earlier, on the original loop - before the plan executes and before the original loop's SCEV is forgotten. At that point the query is a cache hit and does not add any new vector-loop expressions to the caches.

author: claude[bot]
body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Tim Diekmann** · [Slack thread](https://hashintel.slack.com/archives/C02TWBTT3ED/p1783607320868589)_

> [!WARNING]
> **Experimental spike** for [H-6664 "Create Python monorepo infrastructure"](https://linear.app/hash/issue/H-6664/create-python-monorepo-infrastructure) _(internal)_, opened so the approach can be picked apart before the real implementation. Totally fine to close this and start over.

## 🌟 What is the purpose of this PR?

Demonstrate proper Python monorepo infrastructure, borrowing internal-infra's uv-workspace pattern and wiring it into turborepo.

**Before:** Python packages are invisible to turbo and CI. There is no shared lint/type-check/test configuration and no lockfile policy — e.g. #8989 adds a uv package with no `package.json` (so turbo never sees it), no CI, and a gitignored `uv.lock`.

**After:** `turbo run lint:ruff lint:basedpyright test:unit --filter '@local/python-example'` runs ruff, basedpyright, and pytest for Python packages via uv — with shared config and one committed `uv.lock` at the repo root — and the existing Lint/Test CI pipelines pick Python packages up like any other workspace package.

### How it works

- **uv workspace:** the new root `pyproject.toml` is a virtual workspace root (`[tool.uv] package = false`) listing Python packages as members, with `requires-python = ">=3.14"`. A single `uv.lock` is committed at the repo root (do not gitignore it). Shared tooling lives in one root `dev` dependency group: `ruff`, `basedpyright`, `pytest`, `pytest-asyncio`. Per org Semgrep policy (`uv-missing-dependency-cooldown`), `[tool.uv] exclude-newer = "7 days"` applies a dependency cooldown — releases younger than a week are ignored during resolution (recorded in `uv.lock` as `exclude-newer-span = "P7D"`; adding it changed no resolved versions).
- **Centralized tool config** in the root `pyproject.toml`:
  - ruff: `select = ["ALL"]` with internal-infra's short, documented ignore list (`COM812`, `D203`, `D213`, `FIX002`, `TD003`) plus per-file ignores for tests; `line-length = 100` (matches the Rust width used here); `target-version = "py314"`.
  - basedpyright: `typeCheckingMode = "all"`.
  - pytest: `--import-mode=importlib`, `asyncio_mode = "auto"`.
- **The `package.json` shim (the key part):** each Python package carries a `package.json` whose scripts wrap uv, e.g. `"test:unit": "uv run --frozen --all-packages pytest"`. Turbo then treats the package like any other workspace member — task graph, caching, `--filter`, remote cache all work. Two subtleties:
  - `--all-packages` is required: `uv run` from a member directory only syncs that member's dependencies, so without it the root `dev` group tools would be missing from the shared venv (verified with a fresh `.venv`).
  - basedpyright is pointed at the root config via `--project ../../..` because pyright, unlike ruff and pytest, does not search parent directories for configuration.
- **Example packages (temporary scaffolding):** `libs/@local/python-example` (hatchling build backend, src layout, `py.typed`, fully typed module, pytest suite incl. an async test for the pytest-asyncio wiring) and `libs/@local/python-example-two`, which depends on the first via `[tool.uv.sources] hash-python-example = { workspace = true }` (mirrored as a `workspace:*` dependency in its `package.json` so turbo's graph matches) and imports from it in module + tests — so cross-package uv workspace dependencies and the prune path are exercised on every CI run, not just coexistence. Both are marked as temporary in their READMEs: they validate the infra and should be deleted once the first real Python package (e.g. petrinaut-opt) joins the workspace.

### CI (mostly the zero-new-workflow path)

- **`test.yml`: zero changes needed.** It discovers packages via `turbo query` on `TASK_NAME == "test:unit"`; verified locally that `@local/python-example` shows up in exactly that query. Runners get uv 0.11.18 via mise (`install-tools`), and `uv run --frozen` syncs the venv on first use.
- **`lint.yml`: small addition.** It enumerates tools per package (`lint:eslint`, `lint:tsc`, clippy, …) rather than running a generic `lint` task, so it genuinely can't pick Python up unaided. Added `lint:ruff` / `lint:basedpyright` detection + run steps mirroring the existing ESLint/TSC pattern.
- **`prune-repository` action:** the action keeps the root `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` (they aren't part of `turbo prune`'s output), and `prune.py` treats every uv workspace member as an always-included prune scope (directory-copy fallback for members without a `package.json`) — Python is effectively exempt from pruning, since uv resolves the whole workspace (see open question 4).
- `check-license-in-workspaces` now ignores `.venv/` (uv creates it at the repo root).
- `turbo.json` already listed `pyproject.toml` and `*.lock` in `globalDependencies`, so Python task caching invalidates correctly with no changes.

## 🔗 Related links

- [H-6664: Create Python monorepo infrastructure](https://linear.app/hash/issue/H-6664/create-python-monorepo-infrastructure) _(internal)_
- #8989 — adds `libs/@hashintel/petrinaut-opt` (unwired uv package, base branch `cf-petrinaut-python`)
- [uv workspaces documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/)

## 🔍 What does this change?

- New root `pyproject.toml` (uv workspace + shared ruff/basedpyright/pytest config) and committed root `uv.lock`
- Two temporary example packages, `libs/@local/python-example` and `libs/@local/python-example-two` (pyproject.toml, package.json shim, LICENSE.md, typed module, tests each; the second depends on the first through the uv workspace)
- `turbo.json`: new `lint:ruff`, `lint:basedpyright`, `fix:ruff` tasks
- Root `package.json`: matching `lint:ruff` / `lint:basedpyright` / `fix:ruff` scripts, so `yarn lint` includes Python
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml`: ruff/basedpyright detection + run steps
- `.github/actions/prune-repository/`: `action.yml` keeps `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`; `prune.py` always preserves uv workspace members
- `libs/@local/repo-chores` license check: ignore `.venv/`
- `yarn.lock`: registers the new workspace

## ❓ Open questions for Bilal

1. **Python version floor — resolved:** `requires-python = ">=3.14"` per Bilal, matching internal-infra (initially shipped as `>=3.13`). Note a workspace resolves on the intersection of all members, so #8989's `>=3.10` package could only join by raising its own floor.
2. **Placement/naming:** `libs/@local/python-example` with dist name `hash-python-example` / module `hash_python_example`. Should Python packages live under a different convention (e.g. alongside `@hashintel`), and should the npm-scope name mirror the dist name?
3. **petrinaut-opt (#8989):** should it join the workspace (member entry + package.json shim + un-gitignore its lock into the root `uv.lock`) when `cf-petrinaut-python` lands?
4. **CI pruning — reproduced; interim fix shipped (the remove-prune-entirely discussion stays open).** With a temporary second workspace member (`libs/@local/python-example-two`, not committed) and the prune-repository action's steps run locally scoped to `@local/python-example`, the pruned tree lacks the sibling member and:
   - `uv sync --all-packages --locked` exits 1 — `The lockfile at 'uv.lock' needs to be updated, but '--locked' was provided.` (uv re-discovers the workspace from `members` and resolves 12 packages against a 13-package lock)
   - `uv run --frozen --all-packages pytest` exits 2 — `error: Failed to determine installation plan` / `Caused by: Distribution not found at: file:///…/out/libs/@local/python-example-two`

   i.e. the *first additional* Python package would have broken every pruned Python CI job.

   **Interim fix (in this PR):** `prune.py` resolves the uv workspace members from the root `pyproject.toml` and adds them to the `turbo prune` scopes, so every pruned tree keeps the full Python workspace — including the me

body:
## Summary
Implements a fallback mechanism to use National Weather Service (NWS) gauge observations when USGS readings are missing or stale (>2 days old). This addresses cases where USGS stations have been discontinued but NWS still maintains live observations for the same location.

## Key Changes
- Added NWS provider integration to fetch live gauge readings as a fallback
- Implemented staleness detection: readings older than 2 days trigger NWS lookup
- Maps USGS site IDs to NWS LIDs (Location IDs) for cross-provider correlation
- Filters out placeholder zero discharge values from NWS stage-only gauges (those without rating curves)
- Gracefully handles NWS fetch failures with warning logging
- Prioritizes NWS readings over stale USGS data when available

## Implementation Details
- Uses existing `siteToRiver` mapping to find NWS LID for each USGS site
- Batches NWS requests by deduplicating LIDs across multiple sites
- Only applies NWS fallback when USGS reading is missing or stale AND NWS provides fresh data
- Preserves null discharge values for stage-only gauges to avoid misleading zero-flow indicators
- Wrapped in try-catch to prevent NWS failures from breaking the entire response

author: mikemott
body:
Fixes four of the six launch blockers found by a `/ship` audit (code review + security + test coverage personas, plus independent verification).

## The headline: iCloud sync has never worked

SwiftData requires every relationship to be optional — a synced record can arrive before its inverse exists. `Capture.images`, `Capture.tags` and `Tag.captures` were not optional, so the `cloudKitDatabase: .automatic` container threw on **every launch**, and `QuillStackApp`'s `catch` silently fell back to `cloudKitDatabase: .none`.

Reproduced with a probe test before fixing:

```
CloudKit integration requires that all relationships be optional, the following are not:
Capture: images
Capture: tags
Tag: captures
```

Every install has been local-only while `AppStore/metadata.md:33` advertised "ICLOUD SYNC". A `catch` that downgrades a feature is indistinguishable from that feature working.

Property names are unchanged, so lightweight migration still applies.

## Also fixed

**`fatalError` on container init.** Both `ModelContainer` attempts failing hard-crashed on launch. Now a `StoreState` in `@State` with a non-destructive recovery screen — deliberately *not* an in-memory fallback, which would look healthy while every new capture vanished on quit. Retry genuinely re-attempts (`exit(0)` is an App Store rejection).

**Missing `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`.** `UserDefaults` is a required-reason API (`CA92.1`); an app-target manifest has been mandatory since May 2024 and its absence is an automated rejection. Audited the full required-reason list — UserDefaults is the only category used. Verified the manifest is copied into `QuillStack.app`.

**Nutrition label contradiction.** `metadata.md` declared User Content "not collected" while `CrashReporting` sent literal tag names and document content-signals to Sentry, plus raw `Error.localizedDescription` (which can embed file paths or OCR fragments). Breadcrumbs now carry counts and a stable `OCRFailureCode` only. Added `beforeBreadcrumb` allowlist scrubbing and `beforeSend` IP nulling.

**Recognized text had no home in the UI.** `ocrText` was written once and read only by search and Obsidian export, so a capture whose OCR succeeded but whose FoundationModels enrichment failed (which returns `nil` silently) looked identical to one where OCR produced nothing. `CaptureDetailView` now has a collapsible RECOGNIZED TEXT section.

**Card accessibility identifiers.** `.accessibilityIdentifier` on a container propagates to every leaf: the card button's identifier had become `capture-card-capture-card-capture-card-capture-card-capture-card`, and Share also answered to `capture-card`. `testEmptyStateShowsNoCards` queried `otherElements`, which never matched — it passed regardless of behaviour.

## Not fixed here

- **#5 silent OCR failure UI** — `CaptureFlowView.swift:159` still has `if result.success` with no `else`. Groundwork is in: `ProcessingResult.failure` now carries a content-free code ready to persist. Needs a product decision on what the user sees.
- **#7 CloudKit schema deploy** — Production doesn't auto-create record types. Must run a Development build on device, then Deploy Schema Changes in CloudKit Console, before any TestFlight build can sync.
- `DATALAB_API_KEY` removed from local `Secrets.xcconfig` (never committed; verified against full history). Revoke on DataLab's side.
- Sentry: enable "Prevent Storing of IP Addresses" and an Advanced Data Scrubbing rule `Remove` / `Anything` / `$user.geo.**` (geo survives the IP toggle — getsentry/sentry#92201).

## Verification

- Debug **and** Release builds (Release matters: `--seed-ocr-capture` and `--fail-store` are `#if DEBUG`)
- 48 unit tests, 19 UI tests (9 new), swiftlint clean
- CloudKit container load verified by probe before and after the fix
- Recovery path driven end-to-end via `--fail-store`; one test asserts `app.state == .runningForeground`, which `fatalError()` made impossible

Note: `ea749e1` (empty-state copy) rides along — this branch was cut from `quillstack-empty-state`.

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**

allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)

author: kalwalt
body:
Closes #61. Designed via `/brainstorming` — full understanding-lock and decision log below.

## What this adds
1. **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — triggered by a bare `X.Y.Z` tag push (our convention, never `vX.Y.Z`) or `workflow_dispatch` (manual retry without re-tagging). Runs `npm ci` → `npm test` → `npm run build-ts` (rebuilds `dist/`+`types/` fresh from the tagged commit — a safety check, doesn't trust whatever's committed) → `npm pack --dry-run` (informational, ties into #60) → generates release notes via **git-cliff** → creates the GitHub Release → `npm publish --provenance --access public`.
2. **`cliff.toml`** — Conventional Commits parser config, bare `X.Y.Z` tag pattern, grouped changelog sections (Features/Bug Fixes/Refactoring/etc.).
3. **`MAINTAINERS.md`** — maintainer list, review mandates (from `AGENTS.md`), the full two-phase release runbook, and one-time `NPM_TOKEN` setup steps. Adapted from the [WebARKitLib-rs template](https://github.com/webarkit/WebARKitLib-rs/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md) you linked, corrected for jsfeatNext's actual conventions.

## Scope (confirmed during brainstorming)
- **Automates only from the tag onward** (Phase B). Version bump, `dist/` rebuild-and-commit, and `dev`→`main` promotion stay manual — same control you have today, just no more manual changelog writing / GitHub Release creation / `npm publish`.
- **No `CHANGELOG.md` committed to the repo** — release notes live on the GitHub Release page only, avoiding branch-protection friction on `main` (which requires 1 review).
- **No `release-please`-style version-bump automation** — noted as a possible future addition, explicitly out of scope here.

## A real bug caught during local testing
My first `cliff.toml` draft used `commit.remote.*` for PR-number linking, which makes git-cliff fetch commit metadata from the GitHub API — and it **crashes hard** (not gracefully) without network access, rather than just skipping the links. Removed that entirely; commit subjects read fine on their own, and it's now been verified working locally against this repo's real history with `git-cliff` 2.13.1.

## ⚠️ Action required from @kalwalt before this can actually publish
The workflow needs an **`NPM_TOKEN`** repository secret (I can't create this myself — no access to npm credentials or repo secrets):
1. On npmjs.com, generate a **Granular Access Token** scoped to publish only `@webarkit/jsfeat-next`.
2. Add it as a repo secret named `NPM_TOKEN` (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions).

Full steps are in `MAINTAINERS.md` §3. Everything else in the workflow (test, build, changelog, GitHub Release) runs and is useful without the token — only the final `npm publish` step needs it.

## Verification
- `release.yml` YAML syntax validated
- `cliff.toml` tested locally against real repo history — clean, correctly-grouped output, no crash
- `npm test` → 57/57
- `npm run build-ts` succeeds
- `prettier --check .` clean

## Decision log
| Decision | Alternative | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Tag push + `workflow_dispatch` fallback | Tag-only | Retry a failed publish without re-tagging |
| Automate Phase B only | Also automate version-bump PR (release-please) | Keeps your existing control over what becomes a release |
| GitHub Release notes only, no `CHANGELOG.md` | Auto-PR a CHANGELOG.md | Avoids branch-protection friction on `main` |
| `npm pack --dry-run` informational only | Hard-coded size threshold | Avoids a brittle baseline (YAGNI) |
| No `commit.remote.*` PR linking in cliff.toml | Keep PR-number links | Requires GitHub API network access; crashes hard without it |
| Add `MAINTAINERS.md` | Skip / rely on issues only | User request; durable runbook |

author: dario2801
body:
## What

The sign-in and sign-up cards rendered as a clipped ellipse instead of a rounded rectangle.

## Why

`clerkAppearance.variables.borderRadius` was set to `9999px`. That variable is not the button radius: Clerk derives the radius of every element from it, the card included, and injects it as an inline custom property. With a radius far larger than the card, the browser applies the CSS rule for that case and scales all radii proportionally until they fit, turning the card into an ellipse. The curve then cut across the form, which is the jagged edge visible around the heading and the Continue button.

The `card` element already declared `rounded-[10px]`, but an inline custom property beats a Tailwind class, so it never applied.

## How

Set the base radius to the `10px` used by the brand's other surfaces. The social button, the inputs and the primary button keep their pill shape from the explicit `rounded-full` classes already present in `elements`, so nothing else changes.

## Verifying

Open `/sign-in`. The card is a rounded rectangle; the Google button, both inputs and Continue stay pills.

`tsc --noEmit`, `next lint` and `jest` (60 tests) all pass.

## Scope

One file, one variable. Two related issues in the same file are deliberately left out:

- `colorDanger` is the brand copper, so login errors render in the same colour as links.
- The card is `bg-onyx`, darker than the page it sits on, while the landing hero card now uses `bg-carbon`.

# Description

New template for **Tooldrop** (tooldrop.app), a workspace platform that serves customer workspaces from hostnames they own. The template has two records: an A record in the `routing` group pointing the connected FQDN at our edge, and an ownership-verification TXT (`vc-domain-verify=%vctxt%`) at `_vercel` in the `ownership` group, marked `essential: OnApply`. Apply URLs are always signed (`syncPubKeyDomain: tooldrop.app`, key published at `_dck1.tooldrop.app`).

## Type of change

Please mark options that are relevant.

- [x] New template
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue in the template)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality to the template)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing template behavior to be not backward compatible)

# How Has This Been Tested?

Please mark the following checks done
- [x] Template functionality checked using [Online Editor](https://domainconnect.paulonet.eu/dc/free/templateedit)
- [x] Template file name follows the pattern `<providerId>.<serviceId>.json`
- [x] resource URL provided with `logoUrl` is actually served by a webserver — *no `logoUrl` in this template*

# Checklist of common problems

Mark all the checkboxes after conducting the check. Comment on any point which is not fulfilled.
See [Template Quality Guidelines](../README.md#template-quality-guidelines) for details and rationale on each rule.

- [x] `syncPubKeyDomain` is set — **this is mandatory**; omitting it requires explicit justification in the PR description or the PR will be rejected
- [x] `warnPhishing` is **not** set alongside `syncPubKeyDomain` — the two must not appear together
- [x] `syncRedirectDomain` is set whenever the template uses `redirect_uri` in the synchronous flow
- [x] no TXT record contains SPF content (`"v=spf1 ..."`) — use the `SPFM` record type instead
- [x] `txtConflictMatchingMode` is set on every TXT record that must be unique per label or content prefix (e.g. DMARC) — *intentionally not set on the `_vercel` TXT: multiple `vc-domain-verify` tokens must be able to coexist at the same label (other services hosted on the same infrastructure keep their own tokens there), and the verifier tolerates multiple TXT records*
- [x] no variable is used as a bare full record value (e.g. `@ TXT "%foo%"`) unless necessary — prefer `@ TXT "service-foo=%foo%"`; if bare, justify in the PR description — *the `vc-domain-verify=` prefix is fixed in the template; `%vctxt%` carries only the token*
- [x] no bare variable is used as the full `host` label — the non-variable parts are fixed to limit misuse (e.g. `%dkimkey%._domainkey`, not `%dkimhost%`); if bare, justify in the PR description
- [x] no variable is used in the `host` field to create a subdomain — use the `host` parameter or `multiInstance` instead
- [x] `%host%` does not appear explicitly in any `host` attribute
- [x] `essential` is set to `OnApply` on records the end user may need to modify or remove without breaking the template (e.g. DMARC)

## What's in this PR

**Admin restyle** — aligns the admin section's look with the customer login/dashboard, per request:
- Login screen: centered on white (no card box), shared `PasswordInput` (show/hide eye), same heading/subtitle pattern.
- Admin layout: the same wrap-around white "chrome" the customer portal uses — one seamless L-shape (sidebar + top bar joined by a concave swoop, drawn via a single clip-path) with a soft drop shadow. The 6 tabs (Overview, Activity, Referrals, CRM, Performance, Connections) moved into a left sidebar with icons; top bar shows the active tab title + Refresh/View site.
- **Neutral, not branded**: no per-brand accent colour or glow — white/grey only, active nav item uses `bg-gray-100`, as requested.
- Scope: only `app/admin/page.tsx` was touched (imports `PasswordInput` read-only). The customer login/dashboard files are untouched, so this doesn't clash with other in-flight work on those pages.

**Rex CRM integration scaffold** — `lib/rex.ts`, mirroring the existing Atlas integration for the property-family brands (Property, Lettings, Fine & Country, Auction):
- Token-cached login (`Authentication/login`, auto re-login on expiry/`TokenException`).
- `findOrCreateContact` — search by email, reuse the id, else create.
- `pushLeadToRex` — creates a Lead referencing the contact, with note / `lead_type` / `lead_source` / `assignee`.
- `rexPing` — health check for a future admin Connections card.
- Config entirely via env (`REX_API_EMAIL`/`PASSWORD`, per-brand `account_id`, etc.) — nothing secret in the repo.
- Built against the documented Rex API shapes; a few specifics are marked `TODO(rex-demo)` to confirm once demo credentials are available. **Not yet wired** into the leads-push route or the admin Connections tab — that's the next step once we can authenticate against the demo account.

- `tsc --noEmit` clean on both files.

## #️⃣ Issue Number

- resolved #397

## 📝 요약(Summary)

- `V14__populate_i18n_partnership_description.sql`의 모든 UPDATE 문(506줄)에 하드코딩되어 있던 `dev.partnership` 스키마 접두어를 `partnership`으로 수정. prod 배포 시 스키마명이 `dev`가 아니면 마이그레이션이 실패하거나, 동일 인스턴스에 `dev` 스키마가 존재할 경우 엉뚱한 스키마가 갱신되는 위험이 있었음.
- main(prod) DB의 `flyway_schema_history`에는 V13, V15가 이미 적용되어 있으나 V10~V12, V14는 적용되지 않은 상태였음. `application-prod.yml`에 `flyway.out-of-order: true`를 임시로 추가하여, 다음 prod 배포 시 누락된 V10~V12, V14, V16, V17이 순서 검증 실패 없이 백필되도록 함.

## 💬 공유사항 to 리뷰어

- `out-of-order: true`는 main의 누락된 마이그레이션을 한 번 따라잡기 위한 **임시 설정**입니다. prod 배포 후 `flyway_schema_history`가 V17까지 정상 적용된 것을 확인하면, 후속 PR에서 해당 설정을 제거(원복)할 예정입니다.
- V14 수정으로 인해 prod에 실제로 반영되는 partnership 다국어 설명 데이터가 이번에 처음 채워집니다. 배포 전 prod DB의 partnership 테이블 스키마명을 한 번 더 확인해주시면 좋을 것 같습니다.
- 로컬/CI에서 실제 마이그레이션 실행 테스트는 하지 않았습니다. prod와 동일한 flyway_schema_history 상태(V13, V15만 적용된 상태)를 재현해 out-of-order 백필이 의도대로 동작하는지 별도 검증이 필요합니다.

author: zmeireles
body:
## T-8.5.1 — BFF geocode proxy (Plan-008 Slice 5)

Owner-only BFF proxy for **Geoapify** geocoding so the API key stays server-side. Backs the Slice-5 `LocationPicker` (T-8.5.2). Mirrors the `admin-translate` house pattern (owner-auth, 503-when-key-unset, upstream→502/429).

### Contract (frozen — the PWA picker builds against this)
```
POST /v1/admin/geocode          { query, limit? } -> 200 { results: [{ label, lat, lng }] }
POST /v1/admin/geocode/reverse  { lat, lng }       -> 200 { label: string|null, lat, lng }
errors: 400 invalid_body | 401/403 auth | 429 geocode_rate_limited | 502 geocode_failed | 503 geocode_unavailable
```
- Hard-filter `countrycode:pt`; **soft** São Miguel proximity bias (mainland PT stays reachable).
- `AbortSignal.timeout(8s)` bounds the whole op (fetch + body read). In-memory TTL cache (5 min, 500-cap, insertion-order eviction; only 200s cached). API key never logged (only `{err}`/`{status}`).
- 503-when-unset → the picker degrades to numeric lat/lng inputs. `GEOAPIFY_API_KEY` wired into `config.ts`, compose bff env, `gen-env-qual.sh`, `.env.example`, `.env.qual.example`.

### Acceptance
- PT-biased suggestions; no key in bundle/logs; choice recorded (Geoapify) in EXECUTION. ✅

### Verification
- lint ✅ · typecheck ✅ · bff tests **147 passed** (12 new geocode). Re-run locally by the orchestrator (not just agent-claimed).
- **Fable-5 gate**: caught a 🔴 (GEOAPIFY_API_KEY not passed to the bff container in compose → silent 503-forever; fixed) + a 🟡 (body-read unbounded by timeout; fixed → AbortSignal.timeout) + a 🟢 (blank-label rows; filtered). Confirmed clean on key-leakage, owner-auth, error contract, input safety, cache.

author: rookiewu417
body:
全库 review 用**变异注入**实证了四处「绿但抓不到任何回归」的测试。它们不是风格问题——**它们让本次修复的其它部分失去了保护网**。

## 1. PBO 恒真

```python
assert state.pbo is None or isinstance(state.pbo, float)   # nan 也是 float
```

而且该测试只放 **1 个 attempt** → 候选 <2 → `pool_pbo` 本就返回 nan。所以它连「PBO 是不是一个概率」都没验证过。

**变异实证**：`pool_pbo → -999.0`，测试仍绿。

改为：候选 ≥2 时断言 `0 <= pbo <= 1`（PBO 是过拟合概率）；候选 <2 时断言 `isnan`——而不是 0.0 之类**会被误读为「无过拟合」**的值。

## 2 & 3. turnover 恒真（两处）

同样的 `is None or isinstance(float)` 写法。变异 `-999.0` 仍绿。

改为断言单边换手率 `∈ [0, 1]`（0 = 从不换仓，1 = 每日全部换掉）。

（`_factor_turnover` 本身**有**真判别力的 ground-truth 测试：常数排序→0、每日重排→>0.5。弱的只是集成断言。）

## 4. M5 patience 只有 signature 断言

```python
assert "patience" in inspect.signature(run_llm_agent).parameters
```

**参数存在 ≠ 参数被真正使用。** 单 Agent 路径的 patience **行为**从未被测（只有 team 有行为测试）。改为行为测试。

## 并补上两条路径都缺失的「计数器重置分支」

唯一的行为测试用 `_fn_invalid`（候选**永不增长**）。在那个退化场景下，「正确逻辑」与「计数器永不重置」的变异体行为**完全一致**：

```
growth=[0]*8, patience=2:  正确 → 停在 iteration=2 ；never-reset → 也停在 2    ← 零判别力
growth=[1]*6, patience=2:  正确 → 跑满 6           ；never-reset → 误停在 2    ← 分歧
```

**「每轮持续产出候选却被误早停」这个真实 bug，此前没有任何测试能抓到。** 现在两条路径都覆盖了。

## 顺带修 P3：`--patience 0`

早停判据是 `no_improve >= patience`。patience=0 时它在第 2 轮开头**恒成立**——**即使刚产出新候选**——于是 `--patience 0` 静默变成「只跑 1 轮」，无视 `--iterations`。

而 help 文案说的是「连续 N 轮无新候选则早停」，用户传 0 期望「不早停/更激进」，得到的却**相反**。

CLI 现在拒绝 `patience < 1`（不早停请省略该参数，默认 `None`）。

## 验证

**变异验证**（这批测试的全部意义就是判别力，必须证明）：
- `pool_pbo → -999.0` → 2 例变红
- `_factor_turnover → -999.0` → 2 例变红
- patience 重置分支：由上表的仿真对照证实（旧场景两者相同，新场景 6 vs 2）

全库：`lint` 绿 / `typecheck` 绿(255 files) / `pytest` **1775 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed**。

写这个 PR 时我自己也差点犯同样的错——写了一个 `assert "inspect" not in globals() or True` 的占位测试。已删。

author: vickzdrip
body:
Amplia o backteste de BTC-only para **multi-ativo**, aumentando muito a amostra.

## O que muda
Roda os 7 combos de entrada em **6 ativos** (BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP, DOGE) nos mesmos 30 dias, em 1m/3m/5m, com a mesma saída fixa. Isso testa se o edge é **real ou sorte de um ativo**.

**Como agrega (pra não enganar):**
- **Acerto** e **R médio** (expectância) juntam TODOS os trades de todos os ativos — métricas scale-free, a comparação honesta entre combos.
- **Retorno** e **Máx. queda** são a **média das curvas por ativo** — mantém o número na mesma escala de um ativo só, em vez de inflar por ter ~6× mais trades.

## Backend (`dvl-scanner-backend/src/btcBacktest.js`)
- `ASSETS` + helpers `mexcSym`/`binSym`; `fetchMexcKlines` e `fetchSeries` recebem o símbolo por parâmetro.
- `simulate()` dividido: `simulateTrades()` devolve os R crus (por ativo, em ordem cronológica); `simulate()` = `summarize(simulateTrades())` (contrato antigo intacto).
- `run()` faz loop nos ativos, simula por ativo e agrega conforme acima. Payload ganha `assets[]`; `coverage` soma candles por timeframe.

body:
👤 **User Story:**
"As a Data Engineer, I want to subscribe to a real-time stream of all mutations (inserts, updates, deletes) occurring in the database, so that I can synchronize AletheiaDB with downstream systems (like Snowflake, Elasticsearch, or Apache Kafka) without running expensive polling queries."

🧐 **The "So What?":**
Currently, users are forced to rely on inefficient polling mechanisms to detect changes, which wastes resources and causes data pipelines to lag behind. Adding Change Data Capture directly off the WAL allows real-time integration into enterprise data ecosystems and event-driven architectures.

✅ **Acceptance Criteria:**
- Must provide a WAL tailing API yielding structured transaction events (`NodeCreated`, `EdgeDeleted`, etc.) with LSNs.
- Must support resumability using a starting LSN.
- Real-time streaming latency `< 5ms`.

🚫 **Out of Scope:**
- Native sink connectors (e.g., native Kafka Producer) are deferred to Phase 2.
- Complex Event Processing (CEP) logic over the stream.

## Summary
Fixes the state streaming parameter naming mismatch in LangGraph and DeepAgents predictive state updates documentation examples.

## Problem
The docs examples had **three related issues**:

1. **Parameter name mismatch**: Tool parameter name (`steps`) didn't match state key (`observed_steps`)
2. **Configuration mismatch**: The `tool_argument` configuration fields still referenced `steps` even after the tool parameter was renamed to `observed_steps`
3. **Tool schema mismatch**: DeepAgents prebuilt agent TypeScript example had `schema: z.object({ steps: ... })` while `toolArgument` was `observed_steps`

According to the working example in `showcase/integrations/langgraph-python/src/agents/shared_state_streaming.py`, the tool parameter name MUST match the state_key for per-token state streaming to work correctly:

> the frontend `usePredictStateSubscription` hook indexes the (partial-JSON-parsed) tool args by `state_key`, so the tool's argument name MUST match `state_key` for per-token deltas to land in state.

## State Streaming Invariant

For each state-streaming example, this invariant must hold:
**state_key == frontend_read_key == middleware_tool_argument == tool_parameter**

All 8 code sections now pass this invariant:
- ✅ LangGraph custom graph (Python + TypeScript)
- ✅ LangGraph prebuilt agent (Python + TypeScript)
- ✅ DeepAgents custom graph (Python + TypeScript)
- ✅ DeepAgents prebuilt agent (Python + TypeScript)

## Changes

### Initial Commits
- Renamed tool parameter from `steps` to `observed_steps` in Python and TypeScript examples
- Updated all `tool_argument`/`toolArgument` configuration fields to use `observed_steps`
- Added clarifying comments explaining the parameter name constraint
- Added `pass` statements to Python tool function bodies (required syntax)
- Used safe dictionary chaining (`.get('args', {})`)

### Final Fix (this commit)
- **Fixed DeepAgents prebuilt agent TypeScript schema**: Changed `schema: z.object({ steps: ... })` to `schema: z.object({ observed_steps: ... })` on line 525
- This was the last remaining state streaming invariant violation

author: cajasmota
body:
## Summary
Fixes item 2 of #5675 — the **fd-exhaustion crash-loop**. Under a worktree storm the daemon could exhaust file descriptors and die while persisting its store; launchd/systemd `KeepAlive`/`Restart` relaunched it and boot re-discovery restarted the storm — an unbreakable loop. (Note: the `worktrees.json.tmp` persist failure the reporter saw was already non-fatal — a symptom, not the crash site; the real sink was unbounded fsnotify subscriptions.)

This is **defense-in-depth** — the companion dedup fix (#5678) removes most of the fan-out at the source; this makes an fd-crash-loop structurally impossible.

## Changes (4 areas)
1. **Raise `RLIMIT_NOFILE` at startup.** New `internal/daemon/fdlimit` package: `Raise(target)` reads the soft limit, computes `max(target, current)` (**never lowers**), and tries a descending, hard-max-clamped candidate list `[desired, 65536, 10240]` (handles the Darwin `EINVAL` quirk where only `Cur` can be set). Wired into `runDaemon` **non-fatally** (Warn + continue). Default 65536, overridable via `GRAFEL_DAEMON_FD_LIMIT`. No-op stub on non-linux/darwin.
2. **Bound the activation fan-out.** `poll()` is serialized with a dedicated `pollMu` (distinct from `store.mu`, always wraps it — no lock-order inversion), so the ticker and debounced-fsnotify polls can't overlap. `OnActivate`'s `watcher.AddRepo` is gated by a bounded semaphore (`GRAFEL_WORKTREE_ACTIVATE_CONCURRENCY`, default 8). Both are uncontended/immediately-available in the common case — zero steady-state change.
3. **Harden the store persist (still non-fatal).** `Store.save()` retries a transient `.tmp` write once (removing the stale tmp first); the caller's log is demoted `Error`→`Warn` and rate-limited to once/5min. No `os.Exit`/`log.Fatal` anywhere on the persist path.
4. **Service-unit fd limits.** systemd `LimitNOFILE=65536` in `[Service]` (Linux — the primary deployment target); launchd `SoftResourceLimits→NumberOfFiles=65536`. Each on the correct `_linux.go`/`_darwin.go` build-tag side.

## Tests
- `fdlimit`: never-lowers, raises-from-lowered, new≥old, candidate list — all pass.
- `worktree`: `TestWatcher_poll_serialized` (4 concurrent polls, asserts max in-flight == 1) and `TestStoreSave_RetriesTransientTmpFailure` — **both fail when the fix is reverted, pass with it**; verified under `go test -race` (no data race on `lastSaveErrLog`).
- `service`: systemd `LimitNOFILE` + launchd `NumberOfFiles` generation asserted.
- `daemon`: activate-concurrency env override + safe default (bad/0/negative → 8, never a deadlocking 0-cap channel).

## Verification
`go test ./cmd/grafel/... ./internal/daemon/...` all pass, `-race` clean. `GOOS=darwin` builds clean; changed packages build clean for `GOOS=linux`/`windows` (only pre-existing unrelated tree-sitter cgo cross-compile noise). Independently reviewed: APPROVE-WITH-NITS, **no deadlock, no semaphore leak** (race-detector confirmed).

### Known nits (non-blocking, from review)
- `fdlimit_unix.go` doc-comment overstates the "target below current → unchanged" case: the 10240/65536 fallbacks still raise when the current limit is very low (the never-lower safety property holds regardless). Follow-up: tighten the comment or drop fallbacks when `target < old`.
- Semaphore uses explicit release rather than `defer` (panic-safety only; moot since an `AddRepo` panic crashes the daemon anyway).

Completes the #5675 set (with #5676, #5677, #5678).

author: blueibear
body:
## Summary

Closes the **reminder / scheduled-job ownership** portion of #303 (per-user isolation). Follow-up to #312 (SuggestionEngine isolation).

### Reproduced defects (against master, before this change)

A repro script against `080add0` demonstrated all of the following:

1. `list_reminders()` with no `user_id` returned **every user's reminders** (GUI bridge list used exactly this path).
2. `mark_done` / `cancel_reminder` / `delete_reminder` operated on a bare `reminder_id` with **zero ownership checks** — user A could complete/cancel/delete user B's reminder.
3. `get_reminder` disclosed any user's reminder by ID.
4. `bridge/rex_reminders_bridge.py` **hardcoded `user_id="default"`** on save, so every GUI-created reminder was misattributed.
5. `create_reminder` with an existing `reminder_id` **silently overwrote** another user's reminder.

### Ownership model

- Every reminder has one validated canonical owner `user_id` (validated via `rex.identity.validate_user_id`, enforced at the Pydantic model and at every service entry point).
- `get / list / update (snooze) / mark_done / cancel / delete` — and the `add_reminder / cancel / get` compat aliases — require the requesting `user_id`; non-owned reminders behave as nonexistent (no existence oracle).
- Missing, blank, malformed, or traversal-style identity **fails closed** (`ValueError` / error response). No path falls back to `default` or the currently active user.
- `create_reminder` rejects caller-supplied IDs that already exist (blocks cross-user overwrite via the bridge save flow).
- **Background execution:** `fire_due_reminders()` with no `user_id` remains the system context used by the `reminder_check` scheduler job — each due reminder executes as its **stored owner** (notification metadata and follow-up cue are attributed to `reminder.user_id`, regardless of who is currently active). User-initiated firing must pass `user_id` and only fires that user's reminders.
- **Bridge:** resolves the caller from an explicit `user` payload field or the standard identity chain (`rex identify` session → `runtime.active_user` → `runtime.user_id` ≠ `default`); fails closed otherwise.
- **CLI:** `rex reminders add|list|done|cancel` gain `--user` and resolve identity via `rex.commands._helpers._resolve_cli_user`; fail closed with guidance when no user is set.
- Audit trail: create/update/done/cancel/delete/fire log lines now include the owner.

### Legacy migration behavior (conservative, per #303 owner guidance)

- Persisted records **without** a `user_id` load as owned by the distinct `default` profile. They are **not shared**, **not reassigned** to James/Cole/the active user, and remain accessible only to callers explicitly operating as `default` (`rex identify --user default`, `--user default`, or `"user": "default"` in the bridge payload).
- Persisted records with an **invalid** `user_id` (e.g. traversal strings) are **quarantined**: preserved verbatim in `data/reminders/reminders.json` across saves and restarts, but excluded from every operation for every user. Nothing is deleted.
- Manual reassignment / an administrative migration tool can be added separately if desired.
- **Behavior note:** on a fresh install (`runtime.active_user: null`, `runtime.user_id: "default"`) the GUI reminders panel and bare CLI now fail closed with an actionable message until an active user is set — set `runtime.active_user` (e.g. to `default`) or run `rex identify`. This is the intended fail-closed default; single-user use keeps working by explicitly selecting the `default` profile.

### Tests added (`tests/test_reminder_isolation.py`, 35 tests)

- Cross-user denial for list, get-by-ID, complete, cancel, delete, and update/snooze at the **service**, **bridge**, and **CLI** layers.
- User-scoped manual firing cannot trigger another user's due reminders.
- System-context (scheduler) firing executes as the stored owner even when a different user is active in the identity chain.

body:
## Review guide

| Tier | Files (review first) |
|------|----------------------|
| **Core** | `middleware.py`, `middleware_builtins/*`, `http_config.py`, `network_runner.py`, `worker.py`, `plugin_wiring.py`, `plugin_rpc.py`, `runner.py`, `skills-api-guard.ts`, `url-safety.ts`, `route.ts` |
| **Supporting** | `docs/security-audit.md`, `docs/distributed.md`, `deploy-local.ps1`, CI workflow, scenario trace JSONLs |

## Review responses

| Feedback | Fix |
|----------|-----|
| **Collaborator: merge conflicts** | Merged `main` (`eac3375`); resolved `skills/page.tsx`, `communication.md`, `payments.md` |
| **Collaborator: whitespace noise** | Removed interleaved blank-line churn across 113 files; added `.editorconfig` (`end_of_line = lf`); `ruff format` on touched paths (`0441ed1`) |
| **Collaborator: PR size** | Review guide above — core ~15 files vs supporting |
| **Copilot: metadata_filter** | Restored in `InMemoryRegistry.lookup` / `_matches` + test (`2f9b6d0`) |
| **Copilot: RPC 413** | Early return before routing oversized bodies + test |
| **Copilot: plugin_wiring** | Lazy `nest_plugins_reference` import |
| **Copilot: deploy-local.ps1** | Merge `.env.local` keys; only update `DATABASE_URL` |

## Motivation

A July 2026 red-team audit of Nanda Town found three weak clusters in an otherwise strong Tier-1 simulation engine:

1. **Distributed HTTP surface** — worker bridges accepted any caller when `NEST_HTTP_SHARED_SECRET` was unset; health checks omitted auth headers when a secret was configured.
2. **Next.js `/skills` API** — public `POST` with no rate or body limits; server-side reachability probe vulnerable to SSRF.
3. **Simulator regressions** — `partition_heal_at_tick` not forwarded to worker simulators; JwtAuth not bound to the virtual clock; `auth_scope` silently passed when no auth plugin was present.

This PR is **hackathon platform infrastructure** (middleware seam, distributed runner hardening, dashboard deploy tooling, and documentation). Full findings register: [`docs/security-audit.md`](docs/security-audit.md).

## What changed

### Middleware layer

Composable inbound/outbound message hooks resolved from built-ins or `nest.middleware` entry points:

| Name | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `resilience` | Isolate `on_message` failures |
| `observability` | Structured per-message logging |
| `auth_scope` | Enforce bearer tokens; **denies** when auth plugin is missing |
| `latency` | Deterministic per-hop delay via virtual clock |

Key files: [`packages/nest-core/nest_core/sim/middleware.py`](packages/nest-core/nest_core/sim/middleware.py), [`packages/nest-core/nest_core/sim/middleware_builtins/`](packages/nest-core/nest_core/sim/middleware_builtins/), [`packages/nest-core/nest_core/middleware_registry.py`](packages/nest-core/nest_core/middleware_registry.py).

### Distributed HTTP hardening (P0/P1)

- `require_http_shared_secret()` — fails fast when `workers > 1` or `worker_bind` is not localhost
- `hmac.compare_digest` in `http_auth_valid` (timing-safe secret comparison)
- `check_health()` and `RoutedTransport` send `http_auth_headers()` when secret is set
- Worker stack: [`network_runner.py`](packages/nest-core/nest_core/sim/network_runner.py), [`http_config.py`](packages/nest-core/nest_core/sim/http_config.py), [`worker.py`](packages/nest-core/nest_core/sim/worker.py), [`partition.py`](packages/nest-core/nest_core/sim/partition.py), [`trace_merge.py`](packages/nest-core/nest_core/sim/trace_merge.py)

### Worker simulator fixes

- `partition_heal_at_tick` forwarded to each worker `Simulator` (partition scenarios heal in distributed runs)
- `wire_auth_to_sim_clock()` binds JwtAuth to `sim.clock.now` in runner and worker ([`plugin_wiring.py`](packages/nest-core/nest_core/sim/plugin_wiring.py))

### Skills API security (P0)

- `NEST_SKILLS_API_KEY` required for `POST /api/skills` in production (`503` when unset)
- Rate limit: 30 req/min/IP; max body: 256 KB
- SSRF blocklist for private/internal hosts in API route, server action, and page hrefs

Key files: [`apps/nest-dashboard/src/lib/skills-api-guard.ts`](apps/nest-dashboard/src/lib/skills-api-guard.ts), [`apps/nest-dashboard/src/lib/url-safety.ts`](apps/nest-dashboard/src/lib/url-safety.ts).

### Deploy and documentation

- [`scripts/deploy-local.ps1`](scripts/deploy-local.ps1) — one-command Dev/Prod local stack
- [`docs/distributed.md`](docs/distributed.md), [`docs/security-audit.md`](docs/security-audit.md), [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md), [`docs/roadmap.md`](docs/roadmap.md) Phase 6 backlog

## CI evidence (local, head `dd1ca00`)

```
uv run ruff check .          -> All checks passed
uv run ruff format --check . -> 218 files already formatted
uv run pyright               -> 0 errors, 0 warnings
uv run pytest -q             -> 1047 passed, 1 skipped, 1 deselected; 93.89% coverage (gate: 75%)
cd apps/nest-dashboard && npm run ci -> green (typecheck, eslint, build)
uv run nest doctor           -> 7/7 checks passed
```

## Manual verification

| Check | Expected |
|-------|----------|
| `nest doctor` | 7/7 |
| `GET /` `/hackathon` `/visualizer` | 200 |
| `POST /api/skills` without key (`NODE_ENV=production`) | 503 |
| `POST /api/skills` with `source_url: http://127.0.0.1/...` | 400 |
| `nest run --workers 2` without `NEST_HTTP_SHARED_SECRET` | `ValueError` |
| `nest run --workers 2` with secret set | trace merged successfully |

## Scope and duplicate-work check

This is a **platform upgrade PR**, not a single hackathon-problem submission. It does not re-implement existing merged work (HotStuff BFT #33, cid_facts #31, escrow #38, comms versioning #18). It hardens the **host runtime** those plugins run on.

**P2/P3 backlog** (not in this PR): trace `auth_token` redaction, graceful `/skills` without `DATABASE_URL`, CSP headers — tracked in [`docs/roadmap.md`](docs/roadmap.md) Phase 6.

body:
**MC Task:** n/a for this PR — MC board (PC) unreachable; Lucas waived the MC number for this desktop-lane work.

Stage 1 (Gate A) — the **Electron shell half**. Adds automatic backend startup, a readiness handshake, crash recovery, and graceful shutdown so the desktop app launches with no manual terminal step. Pairs with the backend-runtime PR (loopback bind + `/api/health`), which follows.

## What changed (`desktop/` only)
- **`backend-supervisor.js`** (new) — Electron-free, unit-testable supervisor: `pickFreePort()` (ephemeral `127.0.0.1:0`), `start()` (spawn backend with the desktop env contract), `waitForReady()` (poll `GET /api/health` → 200), `stop()` (SIGTERM → 5s timeout → SIGKILL; `taskkill /f /t` on win32), `restart()`, and an `onExit()` hook that fires only on *unexpected* post-ready exits.
- **`main.js`** — desktop-runtime mode (`PARSE_DESKTOP=1`): splash → supervise → load the ephemeral-port URL; recovery page with a Retry affordance; backend stdout/stderr teed to `<userData>/logs/backend.log`; graceful shutdown on quit. **The existing dev/scaffold flow is preserved byte-for-byte** when `PARSE_DESKTOP` is unset.
- **`preload.js`** — exposes `parseDesktop.retryBackend()` for the recovery page.
- **`package.json`** — `test` script + `backend-supervisor.js` added to `check`.

## Shell↔backend contract coded against
Shell sets `PARSE_DESKTOP=1`, `PARSE_API_PORT=<ephemeral>`, `PARSE_HOST=127.0.0.1`, `PARSE_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, `PARSE_USER_DATA`; polls `GET /api/health` for a 200 readiness signal. The backend-runtime PR implements that side.

## Tests
`node --check` on all four JS files, and `node --test` — **5/5 pass** (`pickFreePort`, `waitForReady` resolve/timeout, idempotent `stop()`, full `start()`→`stop()` against a stub backend). No new npm deps (Node built-in test runner).

## Gate mapping
Covers Gate A1 (auto-start + readiness handshake + graceful shutdown + crash recovery). Gate A5 (loopback + non-wildcard CORS) is the paired backend PR. Full live boot integration runs where the backend deps are installed (CI / the PC), since this Mac lacks the runtime stack.

## Scope / safety
Additive, `desktop/` only. Does not change the web app or the Python backend.

author: spokvulcan
body:
## What

Extensive, durable, **local-only** telemetry for the Browser MCP tools, covering **both** consumption paths through the one server choke point (`MCPBrowserServer.handle(request:origin:)`):

- the in-app Tesseract agent (in-process transport, `origin=in_process`), and
- external coding clients like OpenCode / Claude Code (loopback `/mcp`, `origin=http`).

Purpose: gather real usage evidence to improve the tools — screenshot resolution, result phrasing, call budgets, error recovery — instead of guessing. Nothing ever leaves the Mac.

## Design (ADR-0031)

Grounded in a research pass over current industry practice:
- MCP's own `logging` capability is **deprecated** (SEP-2577) in favor of OpenTelemetry-shaped observability → field semantics follow the **OTel GenAI `execute_tool`** conventions (tool name, arguments, error type, session id), so the corpus stays OTLP-convertible.
- Playwright MCP's `--save-trace` is the closest prior art for on-disk per-session tool traces; Anthropic's tool-improvement guidance (collect transcripts; analyze call counts, latency, errors, retries offline) is the stated purpose.
- Format is **JSONL** — the OTLP file-exporter spec's own choice — via the repo's existing `RotatingJSONLWriter` + `TelemetryEnvironment` substrate (32 MB/day size cap, 30-day retention, crash-safe `O_APPEND`, test-runner isolation per #159).

## What gets recorded

`Application Support/BrowserMCPTelemetry/mcp-<yyyy-MM-dd>.jsonl`, schema-versioned header line, then one event per:

| Event | Fields |
|---|---|
| `session_start` | session id, origin, `clientInfo` name/version (e.g. `tesseract-agent`, `opencode`) |
| `tool_call` | tool, verbatim arguments (long strings capped, original size kept), duration ms, ok/error, error message, result text chars + capped preview, **per-image pixel dimensions + bytes**, total payload bytes, per-session sequence number |
| `protocol_error` | method, JSON-RPC code, message |
| `tools_list`, `session_end`, `server_shutdown` | lifecycle bookkeeping with final call counts |

Every event also emits one `Log.browser` line (`log stream --level info --predicate 'category == "browser"'`) for live visibility.

New setting `browserMCPTelemetryEnabled` (default **on**), consistent with the existing local diagnostics (prefix-cache traces, http-completions recordings).

## Verified

- `xcodebuild test`: 10 new tests in `BrowserMCPTelemetryTests` pass (plus `BrowserMCPWireTests`, `MCPClientManagerTests` untouched-green) — recorder fields, argument/preview capping, PNG dimension extraction, both origins through the real server, disabled-recorder no-op, schema header.
- **Live** against the running Release app: external `curl` client + the app's own in-process agent both landed in the corpus with correct origins and client identities; a real screenshot recorded as `2000×1520 px, 88,761 bytes` — the screenshot-resolution question is now answerable from data.
- `log stream` shows the per-call `Log.browser` line; `scripts/check-docs.sh` passes.

## Acceptance checklist (manual)

- [ ] Use the in-app agent with browser tools once; confirm `mcp-<today>.jsonl` gains `origin=in_process` events with `clientName=tesseract-agent`.
- [ ] Use OpenCode against the server; confirm `origin=http` events carry OpenCode's `clientInfo`.
- [ ] Toggle `browserMCPTelemetryEnabled` off (defaults write / settings when surfaced) and confirm no new events.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Settings UI toggle + "Open Telemetry Folder" affordance on the Server dashboard (recorder already exposes `directoryURL`).
- First analysis pass over a week of corpus → concrete tool tweaks (screenshot sizing, result phrasing, call-budget hints).

author: davermaltby
body:
Fixes #329. A **reporting** fix layered on #326 — the halt DECISION is left exactly as #326 designed; only WHAT a non-converged structural `.claude/`-wall halt reports changes.

## The bug

#326 made the structural `.claude/`-wall halt outcome-aware. But when a non-converged attempt hit a `.claude/` wall **and a guardrail then genuinely ran and FAILED** (the deliverable landed — the agent recovered from a read-source `cp ".claude/…"` detour — but dropped required content), the halt was reported as the permission wall, hiding the guardrail failure. A human reading `run.json`/the summary had no way to know a guardrail even ran, and reasonably concluded the #325 fix hadn't shipped.

## Before / after

For a recovered `.claude/`-wall attempt whose guardrail then fails (issue #329's own case, task `03b`):

| field | before (#326) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| `outcome` | `permission-denied` | `guardrail-failed` |
| `failedGuardrails[]` | `[]` (empty) | `[{ name: "01-worklist-fence-present", reason: "…missing required substrate-worklist fence…" }]` |
| summary | `needs human: write to .claude/ blocked by the runtime (structural) — …` | `guardrail(s) failed: <name> — needs human; a .claude/ write was blocked this attempt (<path>), which may be why (see feedback)` |
| `feedback.md` | permission-wall remedies only | LEADS with the failed guardrail(s) + reasons; the `.claude/` wall is SECONDARY context (explains the staging/recovery detour; points at `needsHarnessWrite`/`stagingOutputs` when the failure is a missing `.claude/` deliverable) |

The task still settles `needs-human` on that **one** attempt (unchanged).

## Preserved #326 behavior (nothing about WHEN it halts changed)

- **Converged attempt → GREEN** — untouched.
- **#104 fast-halt** — the non-converged structural halt still fires on **one** recorded attempt, no retry-budget burn (proven: budget 3, runner invoked once).
- **Pure permission wall stays `permission-denied`** — the *action-failed* site (`!action.Succeeded` + `.claude/` wall = the classic #104 first-attempt wall, **no guardrail ran**) and the **eager #86** repeated-wall halt both still report `permission-denied` with empty `failedGuardrails[]`. Deliberately not touched.

Scope precedence, in one line: `permission-denied` is reported only when the wall is the honest PRIMARY cause with nothing more specific to say; a guardrail that actually ran and failed IS more specific, so it wins.

## Why `AttemptJournaler.cs` and `RetryPolicy.cs` changed (beyond #326's TaskExecutor-only footprint)

Both edits are **strictly necessary** to emit the new outcome + populated `failedGuardrails[]`; the reporting fix cannot be expressed with existing helpers:

- **`AttemptJournaler.StructuralWallHalt` (new method).** The existing `AttemptJournaler.PermissionWall` hard-codes `AttemptOutcome.PermissionDenied` and records **no** `FailedGuardrails` — by construction it cannot report `guardrail-failed` with a populated list. The other candidate, `AttemptJournaler.FailedAttempt`, journals `needs-human` only when `isFinal` — on a non-final attempt it journals `running` and the loop RETRIES, which would **break the #104 fast-halt** (burn the budget re-hitting the unclearable wall). Neither existing method both (a) fast-halts to `needs-human` on this one attempt AND (b) carries a caller-chosen outcome + `failedGuardrails[]`. `StructuralWallHalt` is the smallest method that does — it is the same fast-halt-to-needs-human shape as `PermissionWall`/`RateLimitExhausted`, parameterized by the true primary outcome.
- **`RetryPolicy.ForStructuralWallHalt` (new method).** `ForPermissionWall` composes wall-first feedback (wrong lead for #329); `ForGuardrailFailures` composes retry-oriented feedback ("try again", attempt N) — wrong for a `needs-human` halt and it never mentions the `.claude/` wall. The new composer is the only way to produce guardrail-led-primary + `.claude/`-wall-secondary halt feedback. No existing method could be reused without misreporting.

Neither is dead/speculative: both are called only from the one changed `TaskExecutor` site.

## Tests (red-bar verified)

In `HarnessWriteRunTests` (worktree-mode, OS-picked `.ps1`/`.sh`):
- `Worktree_RecoversClaudeWall_UnrelatedGuardrailFails_ReportsGuardrailFailed` — faithful #329: deliverable lands (recovers from the wall) but an UNRELATED content guardrail fails → asserts `outcome == guardrail-failed`, `failedGuardrails` names the content guardrail, summary is guardrail-led + names the `.claude/` path.
- `Worktree_UnrecoverableClaudeDeliverable_HaltsNeedsHuman_ReportsGuardrailFailed` — deliverable never lands (exists-guardrail fails), budget 3 → `guardrail-failed` + **fast-halt** (single attempt, runner once).
- `Worktree_ActionFailsWithClaudeWall_NoGuardrailRuns_StillReportsPermissionDenied` — companion (no over-correction): action itself fails + `.claude/` wall, no guardrail runs → still `permission-denied`, empty `failedGuardrails[]`.

Red-bar: reverting **only** the one `TaskExecutor` `guardrails.AnyFailed` site (back to `PermissionWall`) fails both guardrail-failed tests (`Not found: "guardrail(s) failed"`) while the companion keeps passing — the tests are non-tautological.

## Verification

- `dotnet build Guardrails.sln -c Release` → **0 warnings / 0 errors**
- `Guardrails.Core.Tests` → **990 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**
- `Guardrails.Integration.Tests` → **548 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped** (RealClaude* — normal, token-gated)
- SSOT `docs/plans/02-schemas-and-contracts.md` §7 (`permission-denied`) + §9.3 updated with the outcome precedence; `guardrails-domain-knowledge` halt/hatch bullet synced.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103021: Discord forum/media threads created by `message action=send` ignored the parent channel's `default_auto_archive_duration`. When the field was omitted from the thread-create request, Discord used 4320 minutes instead of the operator's configured value such as 1440 minutes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reported send path does not call `createThreadDiscord`; it calls `sendMessageDiscord`, which fetched the target channel only to classify its numeric type and then built the forum thread request directly in `send.outbound.ts`.

The revised fix carries that existing lookup forward as a typed Discord channel. Once narrowed to a forum/media parent, the send path copies its `default_auto_archive_duration` into the same thread-create request. This avoids another API request, preserves the field-absent fallback, and leaves the explicit `thread-create` action and its `autoArchiveMinutes` override unchanged.

## User Impact

- Implicit forum/media posts now use the parent channel's configured archive duration.
- Non-forum sends and component handling retain their existing behavior.
- The explicit `thread-create` action remains unchanged.
- No new config, environment variable, or message-tool parameter is introduced.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head: `fcb7c056d7b8bd4489e6565eef3a8c83abd889d2`.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kx4hyrjn05y5r8ttcn8sykfh`: 206/206 focused Discord tests passed across the production send, explicit thread-create, component, and action-runtime surfaces.
- `pnpm check:changed`: extension production/test typechecks, lint, dependency/architecture guards, and runtime import-cycle checks passed.
- Fresh Codex autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; patch correct at 0.87 confidence.
- Discord's [channel resource contract](https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/channel) exposes `default_auto_archive_duration` and accepts `auto_archive_duration` on forum/media thread creation; the pinned `discord-api-types@0.38.49` types match that contract.

author: orthory
body:
## What

The [follow-the-head handoff](../blob/dev/.claude/handoffs/follow-the-head.md)'s hydration redesign, riding the unified-node epic's per-block continuity:

- **Scoped hydration**: a block event costs one `status()` read; the module-root diff names what the block changed, and only those slice groups re-query (`hydration.ts` owns the pure pieces — diff, module→group map, group fetchers). An idle stride re-queries nothing but the explorer ring. The wholesale refresh remains for boot/reconnect/op-completion, recomposed from the same fetchers.
- **Read-your-writes floor (the handoff's bug B)**: `receiptFloor(ops)` — no snapshot below a height this console holds a receipt for ever applies, so a node whose local fold trails a relayed receipt can't un-render a confirmed write. Wedge-free by construction (monotonic heights per connection; ledger resets on node switch).
- Preconfirmation gates preserved: fresh-pending stream gate, pages hold, tab-eviction guards (extracted, shared by both paths).

## Verification

- `tsc` clean; vitest **646 passed / 14 skipped** including the provider + simnode scenario suites (they drive the store against simulated nodes through block events)
- The floor's first catch was the page-preconfirmation test's own mock — static status height below its issued receipts, exactly the lagging-node pathology; the mock now tracks its receipts like an honest node

## Remaining from the handoff (not this PR)

Bug A (self-identity: `state.author` literal `"operator"` used as self everywhere instead of deriving from `status.publicKey`) — its fix direction is spelled out in the handoff; separate seam, tracked.

Re-lands the widget reverted in #57. Root cause of the #55 outage: loadData eagerly fetched every PILOT widget's HTML at cold start (2 subrequests/widget); at 15 widgets buildServer was already ~49-50 of the Free-plan 50-subrequest cap, so run_kernel_vm (widget #16) tipped it over, and a poisoned cold isolate throws before dataCache is set → persistent /mcp tools/call outage.

The streaming branch of `ModifyResponseException` handler in `chat_completion` read `logging_obj` from `_data` after that call, always receiving `None`. `CustomStreamWrapper.__init__` then crashed: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'model_call_details'`. ### After the fix: streaming pre_call block returns HTTP 200 with valid SSE ```bash curl -sS -w "\n---HTTP %{http_code}---\n" http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-nova-micro","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"how do I become an admin"}],"guardrails":["bedrock-guard-pre-call"],"stream":true}' ``` ``` data: {"id":"chatcmpl-88bb06b8-...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":"Sorry, the model cannot answer this question."}}]} data: {"id":"chatcmpl-88bb06b8-...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}]} data: [DONE] ---HTTP 200--- ``` All other cases confirmed working against live Bedrock: - pre_call block non-streaming: HTTP 200, `finish_reason=content_filter`, zero usage - during_call block non-streaming/streaming: HTTP 200, block message, real LLM not leaked - post_call block non-streaming: HTTP 200, real upstream usage preserved (675 completion tokens) - post_call block streaming: HTTP 200, usage preserved, no real tokens emitted - Allowed prompts: normal LLM response, not blocked - flag=false: HTTP 400 with guardrail policy error (unchanged behavior) - Python openai SDK parses both blocking shapes correctly ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py`: capture `logging_obj` from `_data` before calling `post_call_failure_hook` (which pops it). author: mattdhill
body:
## Summary

`hermes-agent-startos`'s release job [failed](https://github.com/Start9-Community/hermes-agent-startos/actions/runs/29031061474) at **Add GitHub release mirrors**, after the package had already been tagged, built, released, and published to the registry:

```
Network Error: registry.package.add-mirror: error sending request for url
(.../releases/download/v2026.7.1_1/hermes-agent_x86_64.s9pk):
client error (SendRequest): connection closed before message completed
```

`registry package add-mirror` downloads the **entire** s9pk and hashes every file body (`serialize(sink, verify: true)` → `serialize_body(w, hash.filter(|_| verify))`) to prove the mirror serves an intact package. For `hermes-agent` that's ~750 MB per arch in one un-retried HTTP body, pulled from GitHub's release-asset CDN. The aarch64 mirror went through; x86_64's connection was closed mid-stream.

It's throughput-bound, not a timeout — the *same* aarch64 asset took 13.5s in the prior release and 27.2s in this one. There is no retry anywhere in the step, so a single dropped connection fails the whole release.

This adds 3 attempts with linear backoff (30s, 60s) around `add-mirror`.

## Why not `--no-verify`

It would halve the transfer, but it's not safe. The registry's own `add_mirror` handler resolves the s9pk via `S9pk::deserialize` → `S9pk::archive`, which fetches only `MAGIC_AND_VERSION.len() + header_size()` bytes from offset 0 — **the header/TOC only**. It validates the root sighash and never reads a file body. A truncated or corrupted upload would sail past server-side validation and get registered as a mirror. The client-side verify download is the only thing that catches that, so it has to stay — which means it has to be retried instead.

## Drive-by

Documented why range requests are disabled in `HttpSource::new`. The `&& false` reads as dead code and invites removal, but `fd7c2fbe9` introduced it together with the entire `HttpReader::Rangeless` reader-pool path — it's a deliberate workaround for GitHub's poor range-request performance, not a leftover. Comment only, no behavior change.

author: yskms
body:
## 概要
手動更新の連打を防ぐ「最低更新間隔」設定を追加。あわせて、同期実行中の手動更新が無反応だった問題を修正した。

## 変更内容
### 最低更新間隔
- データ管理に「連打防止の最低更新間隔」ドロップダウンを追加（制限なし / 1 / 3 / 5 / 10分）。Coming Soon を実機能に置換
- `SyncService.getMinRefreshIntervalMinutes()` / `getManualRefreshCooldown()` を追加
- 制限中の手動更新は残り時間を案内して中断。「制限なし」「同期履歴なし」「経過済み」はすべて許可（フェイルオープン）

### 同期実行中の手動更新が無反応だった問題を修正
起動直後の自動同期中に手動更新すると、`refresh()` の多重実行ガードが `{ fetched: 0, newArticles: 0 }` を返すだけで**何も起きずに終わっていた**（この時点では `lastSyncTime` が未更新なのでクールダウンも効かない）。`SyncService.isRefreshing` を先に判定し「更新中です」と案内する。

**手動更新の判定順序**：同期実行中 → 最低更新間隔 → モバイル回線の確認 → 取得
いずれも取得処理の前に `return` するため、プル更新のスピナーが無駄に立たない。

### レビュー起因の修正
- 選択肢に無い値が保存されていると、ラベルが「制限なし」と表示される一方で実際には制限がかかっていた（表示と実挙動の食い違い）。0より大きい値はその分数を表示するよう修正
- 同一定義だった `wifiOnlyHint` / `minRefreshHint` スタイルを `sectionHint` に統一
- 説明文を修正：「引っ張って更新」の限定を削除（ヘッダーの更新ボタンも対象のため）、「更新をスキップします」→「更新を制限します」

## 確認
- `tsc --noEmit` パス
- 実機確認済み：起動直後の手動更新で「更新中です」／完了後の手動更新で「約N分後に…」／「制限なし」では両ダイアログなし／更新ボタン・プル更新の両方
- コードレビュー実施（ブロッカーなし、指摘は本PR内で修正）

## 補足
保存キーの定数集約（`constants/storageKeys.ts`）は本PRのマージ後に実施予定。

author: martin3zra
body:
#31 was merged into `refactor/unit-reads-playsql` ~24 seconds *after* #30 merged that branch into `main`, and #30 was a squash merge. The company work therefore landed on a branch that had already been merged away and never reached `main`.

This re-targets the same two commits onto `main`. `main`'s tree was byte-identical to the branch state just before them, so the cherry-pick applied clean. No new work — the diff is exactly #31.

| Commit | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| `8d04712` | company reads, `storeCompany`, `linkCompanyDefaultSequences`, all five `companies_settings` statements |
| `5a728b6` | `upload_sessions` and `imports` — the CSV import pipeline |

## Bugs fixed (unchanged from #31)

**Settings writes silently no-op'd across tenants.** Every `companies_settings` statement inlined `WHERE company_id = (SELECT id FROM companies WHERE account_id = $1 AND uuid = $2)`. For an unknown uuid — or one belonging to another account — the subquery yields `NULL`, `company_id = NULL` matches nothing, and the three `UPDATE`s affected zero rows and returned `nil`. The lookup is hoisted into `resolveCompanyID`; all five now fail with `ErrNotFound`.

**`failUpload` never recorded a failure.** It passed `message, id` to a query whose `$1` was the id and `$2` the error message, so it ran `WHERE id = <the error message>`, matched zero rows, and returned `nil`. `TestFailUpload` fails against the old code with `got uploading, want failed`.

**Dead code:** `COALESCE(handles_variants, false)` — the column is `NOT NULL DEFAULT false`.

## Verification

`go test ./app/ -count=1` green on this branch, on top of current `main`.

author: hleserg
body:
## Проблема (репорт с поля, фест идёт)

При запуске в **авиарежиме** приложение виснет на `$ ./программа --загрузка` — `boot()` не стартует, вечная загрузка.

## Причина

На **проде** CI инжектит `<script src="config.js">` (пинг «установили»). `config.js` **не прекэшируется** SW (свежий токен, #61) — офлайн его сетевой запрос может **зависнуть** (в поле wifi без интернета: коннект не падает мгновенно). Скрипт подключался **`defer`**, а defer-скрипты исполняются **по порядку** → зависший `config.js` навсегда блокирует следующий `app.js` → `boot()` не запускается → «вечная загрузка».

`offline.js` это не ловил — `config.js` существует только на проде (локально его нет).

## Фикс

1. **`pages.yml`: config.js инжектится `async`, не `defer`** → `app.js` от него не зависит и не ждёт. `APP_CONFIG` нужен лишь к `appinstalled` (жест юзера, сильно позже) — порядок не важен.
2. **`boot()`: `loadProgram`/`loadGeo`/`loadBasemap` стартуют параллельно.** Офлайн с зависшей сетью каждый data-fetch ждёт таймаут SW ~3.5с; последовательно ≈10с «загрузки», параллельно — один таймаут ≈3.5с. Логику не переставлял, только раньше запускаю fetch.

`CACHE` v76→v77 (менялись `index.html`/`app.js` — дойдёт до установок, как только телефон окажется онлайн хоть раз).

## Проверки

- `tests/e2e/config-offline.js` (новый регресс-гард): читает форму инжекта из `pages.yml` (возврат к `defer` → тест падает), «сеть зависает» (сокет висит, как в поле), холодный офлайн-запуск обязан подняться из кэша ≤8с. **Мутационно: `defer` → виснет >12с; `async` → 4с.**
- `offline.js` — ВСЁ ЗЕЛЁНОЕ (параллелизация boot не сломала офлайн);
- `npm test` 91 зелёный (4 TZ); `geo.js` зелёный.

⚠️ **Важно про доставку:** установленные копии подхватят фикс только когда телефон окажется **онлайн хоть раз** (SW обновится с v76 на v77). Пока телефон офлайн со старым кэшем — баг остаётся (это неизбежно для cache-first PWA).

author: vxfemboy
body:
## What

Phase 1 of **[A·M4] API & operations (#4)**: an authenticated, tenant-aware, **read-only** HTTP control API for Blackwall, plus its config directive and the `Store` reads that back it. Mutation endpoints, daemon supervision, and the bench harness are Phases 2–4 (separate PRs) by design.

Includes the approved design spec and Phase 1 implementation plan under `docs/superpowers/`.

## Components

- **New `blackwall-api` crate** (axum): `ApiError`→`IntoResponse`, the `AppState` trait + `*View` types, SHA-256 **bearer-token auth** middleware (constant-time via `subtle`), 9 response DTOs, 10 read handlers, and a **generated OpenAPI 3.1 doc** (utoipa) served at `/v1/openapi.json` with a route-coverage contract test.
- **Endpoints** (all behind auth, tenant-aware URLs): `/v1/tenants[/{name}[/services|/ip-assignments]]`, `/v1/mitigations/{rtbh,flowspec,xdp}`, `/v1/detections`, `/v1/sessions`, `/v1/audit`, `/v1/openapi.json`.
- **Config:** `api listen=<ip:port> token-file=<path>` directive (`blackwall-core::ApiConfig` + `Policy.api`), mirroring the existing `metrics listen=` shape.
- **State:** five thin `Store` read methods (tenants, ip-assignments, active detections, recent sessions, recent audit) with DB integration tests.
- **Daemon:** concrete `StoreAppState` + `serve_api` mounted as a task in `blackwalld run` when `api` is configured; token-load/bind failures log and disable the API (no panic). Glue is coverage-excluded like `metrics.rs`.

## Design decisions (see spec)

Single-admin control plane, tenant-*aware* URLs so per-tenant self-service is a later increment; in-process with `run` (shares `Store`, no split-brain); bearer token with TLS at a reverse proxy.

## Quality

- Built via subagent-driven development: 7 tasks, each spec+quality reviewed, plus a final whole-branch review (**ready to merge, no Critical/Important**).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` clean; `cargo fmt` clean; **workspace coverage 95.92%** (blackwall-api ~96.3%).

## What changed

- Production deploys intentionally skip Prisma migrations.

- Workflow is manual-only via `workflow_dispatch`.
- After merge, go to GitHub Actions and run `Run Production Prisma Migrations` on `main`.

## Screens/pages affected
- GitHub Actions only. No app UI changes.

## Tenant-safety considerations
- The workflow uses existing tenant-safe Prisma migrations.
- It relies on the guarded `db:migrate:production` script and production environment secrets.

## Known limitations
- GitHub `production` environment must have `DATABASE_URL` and `PRODUCTION_DATABASE_SIGNATURE` secrets configured before the workflow can run successfully.
