author: amiller
body:
## What it does
Adds `reddit-karma/` — a sample OAuth3 relying-party app (static `index.html`, same shape as `timeline-peek`). **Connect** initiates the OAuth3 login flow and renders the connected Reddit account's karma — **total, with comment / post breakdown** — read through a scoped, revocable `reddit:read` token from the OAuth3 node. The app never sees the Reddit cookie; the TEE pod does the authenticated read.

- Two login paths (matches `timeline-peek` / `calendar-share`): the browser extension (`window.oauth3.connect({plugin:"reddit"})`), or — with no extension — self-provisioning an Ed25519 `did:key` wallet in-browser and running the `/api/login` → `/api/connect` → `/approve` handshake.
- Defines the plugin contract it expects: `GET /oauth3/api/reddit/karma` (Bearer) → `{ data: { name, total_karma, comment_karma, link_karma, created_utc } }` — for the reddit plugin tracked in `teleport-computer/oauth3-server#83`.
- **Mock fallback (honest, not masked):** #83 is still open. On any instance where the plugin isn't registered yet, the live connect/read fails and the card falls back to clearly-labelled **MOCK** karma — but the real error + HTTP status go into an evidence block under the number, and the card is stamped `MOCK`. A failed read never silently becomes "0 karma." When #83 ships, real karma renders with **no code change**.
- A **View demo (mock)** button shows the mock without attempting login, so the demo is viewable end-to-end today.
- Styled through the pod design system (constructivist overprint, grape-acid webhost inking), light + dark.

## What you get by merging
The concrete sample OAuth3 app the operator asked for — the app side of the app+plugin story for Reddit Karma, ready for the reddit plugin (#83) to land against a published contract. Registered in `REGISTRY.md`.

## Risk
Low. New static subdirectory + one `REGISTRY.md` row; no change to existing apps or shared code. The wallet self-provision block is duplicated from `timeline-peek`/`calendar-share` (a third copy) — flagged as share-kit-style extraction debt in the README, left inline here to match the existing convention rather than refactor siblings in this issue.

## Verification (parse/smoke-level — not a full test suite)
- `node --check` on the extracted `<script>` → **OK** (no syntax errors); HTML tag balance checked → clean.
- Served the static dir and `curl`ed: `GET /` → **HTTP 200** (18453 B, `text/html`); `GET /index.html` → 200; `GET /nope.html` → 404. Expected content strings present (`Reddit Karma`, `Connect with OAuth3`, `View demo (mock)`, `reddit:read`, `window.oauth3.connect`, `/api/reddit/karma`).
- Did **not** exercise a live OAuth3 connect or a real reddit karma read — the reddit plugin (#83) isn't landed, and no browser E2E was run. The connect/read path is adapted verbatim from the proven `calendar-share`/`timeline-peek` flows; the mock fallback is the path exercised today.

<details>
<summary>diff</summary>

```diff
A  reddit-karma/index.html   (static app: connect → /api/reddit/karma → karma card + evidence block; mock fallback)
A  reddit-karma/README.md    (flow, plugin contract for #83, mock policy, deploy, debt notes)
M  REGISTRY.md               (+1 row: reddit-karma)
```
</details>

Closes #34.

body:
## Contexte

Issu du diagnostic « zéro inscrits » : la vraie cause s'est révélée être un **problème de trafic mal ciblé** (Search Console : ~55 clics/mois, majoritairement des requêtes de résultats de hockey LNH/NHL, pas des profs d'ÉPS). En chemin, deux bugs concrets ont été trouvés et sont corrigés ici.

## Changements

### 1. `analytics.js` chargé site-wide via `zts.js`
`analytics.js` (GA4 `G-C2L5PD388L`) n'était inclus que sur ~52 pages (blog/articles). **Ni la home ni les 1 440 fiches de jeux** (la surface SEO dominante) n'étaient mesurées → GA4 affichait « 4 utilisateurs / 28 j », ce qui a longtemps masqué la réalité du trafic.
- Chargé désormais partout via `zts.js` (donc home + fiches + apps), avec **garde anti-double-chargement** pour les 52 pages qui l'incluent déjà en dur.
- **Consent Mode v2 inchangé** (default deny, opt-in RGPD géré dans `analytics.js` + `cookie-consent.js`) → aucun cookie sans consentement.

### 2. Meta-descriptions des fiches coupées sur un mot entier (`gen-jeux-fiches.js`)
`clip()` tronquait à 155 caractères en plein milieu d'un mot (« …deux **cadres-rebon** », « …la gestion **d** ») sur les 1 440 fiches → rendu peu engageant dans les SERP (nuit au CTR). Coupe désormais sur une frontière de mot + ellipse.
- ⚠️ N'affecte que les fiches **régénérées** via `gen-jeux-fiches.js`. Les 1 440 fiches existantes gardent leur description actuelle jusqu'à une régénération (gros diff — à décider séparément).

## Tests

- `node --check` OK sur `shared/zts.js` et `scripts/gen-jeux-fiches.js`.
- **Chromium headless** : une fiche `/jeux/*` injecte bien `analytics.js`, qui charge le tag `googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-C2L5PD388L` ✅.
- `clip()` vérifié sur le texte réel de tchoukball : « …marquer sur les deux… » (mot entier) au lieu de « …cadres-rebon ».

## Hors périmètre (volontairement)

- Les **titres** des fiches sont déjà corrects (`Tchoukball — règles et déroulement | Jeu d'éducation physique`) — pas de changement cosmétique injustifié ici.
- Le vrai levier reste **l'acquisition de trafic ciblé profs** (ranking + promotion), qui n'est pas un changement de code.

## Summary

- Adiciona `studyMilestoneService.js` — serviço puro (sem I/O, sem IA, sem persistência) que deriva **Marcos da Evolução** (`buildMilestones(entries)`) a partir das mesmas `entries` já carregadas pelo Diário de Estudos: primeira sessão, limiares de sessões/horas/questões, primeira reflexão/revisão, matérias distintas, recordes (maior sessão, mais questões em uma sessão, maior tempo diário) e constância (dias consecutivos, reaproveitando o mesmo conceito de `studyStreakService.js`/F6.11).
- `studyJournalView.js` passa a renderizar um novo bloco somente-leitura "Marcos da Evolução" antes dos grupos de dia, recalculado a cada `_render()` a partir de `filtered` (F8.4) — nenhuma consulta nova, nenhum evento publicado, nenhum outro domínio (Dashboard, Insights, Conquistas, IA) tocado.
- Ícones dos marcos reaproveitam os mesmos glifos já usados na navegação lateral (`index.html`) — nenhum SVG, imagem ou biblioteca de ícones nova.
- Estilos novos (`.sj-milestones*`) seguem o mesmo padrão visual dos cartões de resumo já existentes (`.sj-week-summary`).

## Estratégia adotada

- Nenhuma tabela, migration, coluna ou policy nova — marcos nunca são persistidos, sempre recalculados em memória (mesma arquitetura da F6.1: Sessão/Questão/Revisão/Reflexão são fatos, Marco é interpretação derivada).
- Nenhuma consulta adicional a serviços (`activitySessionService`, `questionService`, `reviewSessionService`, `studyReflectionService`, `studyStreakService`, `subjectProgressService`, `achievementService` etc.) — o novo serviço só opera sobre as `entries` já resolvidas pelo Diário.

author: thecyclecoder
body:
## Problem
migrate-to-internal flips an Appstle sub to internal by **renaming** `shopify_contract_id` (numeric → `internal-…`). Its own cancel step fires an Appstle `subscription.cancelled` webhook that arrives async carrying the **old numeric id**. The webhook's migrated-internal guard matched only on `shopify_contract_id` — no longer matching the renamed row — so it fell through and **inserted a fresh `is_internal=false` cancelled shell** bearing the old id. The portal's `resolveSub` then resolved a migrated customer's stale numeric id to that dead shell → false "out of stock" on order-now (ticket 183d28b9 / Ellyn).

## Fix
- New nullable `subscriptions.migrated_from_contract_id` (+ partial index) retains the origin id on the flipped row.
- Both flip paths in `migrate-to-internal.ts` write it.
- Appstle webhook guard + portal `resolveSub` match `shopify_contract_id OR migrated_from_contract_id` (raw `.or()` charset-gated against PostgREST filter injection) and prefer the live internal row.

## Data repair (prod, already applied)
`scripts/_fix-migration-dupes.ts`: backfilled 154 migrated subs, deleted 24 pre-existing dead cancelled shells. Verified 0 shells remain; Heather (`27902050477`) now resolves to her active internal sub (bills tomorrow).

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- `order-now-guard` tests 5/5 pass
- Live prod verify: 0 non-internal rows carrying a claimed origin id; the old id resolves to the active internal sub.

Brain: `tables/subscriptions`, `libraries/migrate-to-internal`, `integrations/appstle`.

<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Chris Feijoo** · [Slack thread](https://hashintel.slack.com/archives/C02TWBTT3ED/p1783595334963669)_

## 🌟 What is the purpose of this PR?

**Before:** the monorepo type-checked with TypeScript 5.9.3, leaning on long-deprecated compiler options — `baseUrl`-based `paths` resolution, `moduleResolution: "node"` (node10), an `ignoreDeprecations: "5.0"` escape hatch — and on TS 5.x's implicit inclusion of every `node_modules/@types` package.

**After:** the whole repo type-checks, lints, and builds with **TypeScript 6.0.3** (typescript-eslint 8.62.1). The legacy base tsconfig is cleaned of deprecated options, workspaces resolve modules with `bundler`/`nodenext`, and ambient type packages are declared explicitly. This absorbs the TS 6 defaults now, so the follow-up TS 7 (Go-native) side-by-side compiler flip is a much smaller diff.

## 🔗 Related links

- Linear: [H-6679](https://linear.app/hash/issue/H-6679/migrate-monorepo-to-typescript-603) _(internal)_
- Related: [SRE-381 — Migrate from internal tsconfig base to community-maintained](https://linear.app/hash/issue/SRE-381/migrate-from-internal-tsconfig-base-to-community-maintained) _(internal)_
- Supersedes #8942 (Renovate's bare `typescript` v6 bump)
- Requesting Slack thread _(internal)_: https://hashintel.slack.com/archives/C02TWBTT3ED/p1783595334963669

## 🔍 What does this change?

**Dependency bumps** (`chore: bump TypeScript to 6.0.3 and typescript-eslint to 8.62.1`)
- `typescript` 5.9.3 → 6.0.3 in every workspace manifest; `typescript-eslint` resolution → 8.62.1.
- Changeset for `@blockprotocol/graph`, whose codegen module depends on `typescript` at runtime.
- **petrinaut runtime LSP deliberately frozen at TypeScript 5.9.3**: `@hashintel/petrinaut-core` now depends on `"typescript5": "npm:typescript@5.9.3"` with a matching Vite `resolve.alias` (`/^typescript(\/.*)?$/` → `typescript5$1`), because the in-browser language service uses the TypeScript JS API (`createLanguageService`), which TS 7 no longer ships. Source files keep importing plain `typescript` so they type-check against the workspace-wide version. `yarn.config.cjs`'s `allowedUnscriptedDevDependencies` carve-out updated accordingly, and the root workspace now pins `typescript` so `node_modules/.bin/tsc` deterministically resolves to 6.0.3 rather than the alias's `tsc` bin.

**tsconfig burn-down** (`chore: rework tsconfigs for TypeScript 6.0`)
- `libs/@local/tsconfig/legacy-base-tsconfig-to-refactor.json`: dropped `baseUrl` (bare-`paths` resolution retired), `moduleResolution: "node"` → `"bundler"`, removed the root `ts-node` block and `outDir`, fixed the stale `@local/status/type-defs/*` path mapping.
- TS 6 no longer auto-includes every `node_modules/@types` package, so the base config declares `"types": ["node"]` explicitly; workspaces needing more ambient globals extend it (e.g. frontend adds `gapi`/`google.accounts`/`google.picker`, plugin-browser adds `chrome`).
- Kept TS 5.x behavior for `noUncheckedSideEffectImports: false` (bundler-handled asset imports like `import "./styles.css"`).
- Removed the now-rejected `ignoreDeprecations: "5.0"` from `@hashintel/ds-components`; added explicit `rootDir: "./src"` to build configs.

**Source fixes** (`fix: adjust sources for TypeScript 6 and typescript-eslint 8.62`)
- Replaced deep `dist/cjs` type imports (`react-pdf`, `@blockprotocol/type-system`) with public/esm entry points — stricter exports-map enforcement under `moduleResolution: "bundler"` blocks the old paths (`apps/hash-frontend/src/pages/shared/pdf-preview.tsx` and friends).
- `libs/@hashintel/design-system/src/e-chart.tsx`: derive `GraphNode`/`GraphEdge` from the public `GraphSeriesOption` instead of reaching into `echarts/types/src/*`.
- Temporarily disabled `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-type-assertion` in `@local/eslint`: 8.62 mis-reports assertions as unnecessary under TS 6.0 (removing them breaks `tsc`). To be re-enabled once typescript-eslint officially supports TS 6.0.

**What surfaced**
- `@local/effect-dns-hickory` lint failed in the migration container only because the `napi` CLI (provided in CI via mise, `npm:@napi-rs/cli`) isn't available there, so the napi-generated `dist/impl.d.ts` was missing and the package import resolved to an error type. With the build artifact present, `lint:tsc` and `lint:eslint` pass unchanged under TS 6.0.3 — no code change needed.
- `@apps/plugin-browser:build` requires `SENTRY_DSN`/`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` for production builds (hard error in `webpack.config.js`); these are CI-provided secrets (Vault, see `deploy.yml`) absent in the migration container. `tsc --noEmit` for plugin-browser passes under 6.0.3.

## Pre-Merge Checklist 🚀

### 🚢 Has this modified a publishable library?

This PR:

- [x] modifies an **npm**-publishable library and **I have added a changeset file(s)**
  - `@blockprotocol/graph` (runtime `typescript` dependency bump — changeset added); `@hashintel/petrinaut-core` is touched but the `typescript5` alias is a bundled devDependency, not a published-consumer-facing change.

### 📜 Does this require a change to the docs?

The changes in this PR:

- [x] are internal and do not require a docs change

### 🕸️ Does this require a change to the Turbo Graph?

The changes in this PR:

- [x] do not affect the execution graph

## ⚠️ Known issues

- `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-type-assertion` is temporarily off repo-wide (false positives against TS 6.0); re-enable when typescript-eslint ≥ 8.63 lands.
- typescript-eslint 8.62.1 does not yet declare official TS 6.0 support — expect a warning banner, behavior verified across the repo lint run.

## 🐾 Next steps

- Step 2 of the migration plan: TS 7 (Go-native) side-by-side compiler flip — this PR intentionally absorbs the TS 6 config defaults to keep that diff small.
- Re-enable `no-unnecessary-type-assertion` once typescript-eslint officially supports TS 6.
- SRE-381: replace the legacy base tsconfig with the community-maintained base.

## 🛡 What tests cover this?

- Full `turbo` run (build / lint:tsc / lint:eslint / unit tests) across all workspaces under TS 6.0.3 — green except the two environment-only items called out above.
- `@hashintel/petrinaut-core`: 665 unit tests pass; `vite build` output verified to bundle TypeScript 5.9 (`versionMajorMinor = "5.9"`) into the LSP worker; `tsgo --noEmit` clean.
- `yarn constraints` passes.

## ❓ How to test this?

1. Checkout the branch, `yarn install`.
2. `yarn tsc --version` → 6.0.3; run `turbo run lint:tsc lint:eslint` — repo-wide green.
3. `yarn workspace @hashintel/petrinaut-core test:unit --run && yarn workspace @hashintel/petrinaut-core build` — LSP worker still bundles TS 5.9.3.

author: the-obstacle-is-the-way
body:
## Problem

`.github/dependabot.yml` has two security-only entries (npm + github-actions, the `applies-to: security-updates` ones). Neither sets `target-branch` (so they default to `main`) and a Dependabot entry performs **version updates as well as security updates** by default — the group's `applies-to` only controls grouping. Result: a second, unconfigured pipe emitting ungrouped version-update PRs straight at `main`, with no cooldown and the default `increase` versioning strategy.

Evidence this pipe is live and harmful:
- #604/#605 (superseded by #610): opened Thu 09:13 ET matching the daily security schedule, 8 days after publish (bypassing the 7-day cooldown would-be-Monday sweep), with #605 rewriting the `lucide-react` range `^1.16.0` → `^1.23.0`.
- #465: `actions/checkout` 6.0.3 → 7.0.0 — a **major** — merged to `main` through this pipe, ungrouped, which `docs/dev/dependency-update-protocol.md` explicitly disallows.
- 14 of 16 resolved `main`-targeted Dependabot PRs were manually closed; the intended `dev` grouped flow merged 6 of 7.

## Solution

`open-pull-requests-limit: 0` on both security-only entries. Per GitHub docs this disables **version updates only**; security updates run under a separate internal limit of ten open PRs that this setting cannot change, and they keep targeting `main` un-delayed — which is exactly the design intent recorded in `docs/dev/dependency-update-protocol.md` → Dependabot Config Policy (DEBT-393).

## Verification

- YAML parses; 4 entries: npm→dev limit 5, npm→main limit 0, actions→dev limit 5, actions→main limit 0.
- Full local gate green: typecheck ✅ lint ✅ unit 3162 ✅ browser 363 ✅ integration 159 ✅ build ✅ e2e 36 ✅ (config-only diff; gate run per protocol).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Chores**
  * Updated automated dependency update settings to limit security-related pull requests and prevent unintended ungrouped version-update requests targeting the main branch.
  * Added configuration notes explaining the updated behavior.

body:
Fixes the concrete CLI blockers filed in `abc-universe/brainstorms/abc-cluster-cli/2026-07-09-remote-run-blockers-mtb.md`, surfaced trying to run a multi-stage MTB-resistotyper genomics pipeline on the `compute` pool. Each is small; together they made remote batch work undebuggable (couldn't see why a job failed, nor retrieve a successful job's output).

## Observability
- **B1** `job show` → new **FAILURE DETAIL** section prints the last task-event message (driver error / exit code / OOM) for failed/lost allocs. A fast-failing `exec2` job no longer says "N failed" with no cause.
- **B11** `job trace` **implemented** (was advertised in `--help` but "not yet implemented"): placement, per-task lifecycle events, and a stdout/stderr tail — the command to reach for when `job logs` is empty.
- **B2** `job logs --alloc <id>` now works with no job positional (was rejected `accepts 1 arg(s), received 0`); streams straight from the allocation.
- **B9** a blocked eval / `FailedTGAllocs` now surfaces the placement reason (constraint / resource / class) in the watch loop **and** `job show` (**PLACEMENT BLOCKED**), instead of an infinite silent "pending, 0 allocs".

## job run staging
- **B3** staging bucket was blindly = Nomad namespace, which became `default` under a `--namespace` override → `NoSuchBucket`. Now resolves an `su-<group>` bucket, adds `--stage-bucket`, and **fails fast at submit** with guidance.
- **B4** only stage a default `data/` when it exists; allow `--out` without `--in` (was aborting `given object .../data not found`).

## namespace / config / cluster
- **B6** honor `NOMAD_NAMESPACE` in read commands; submit output shows the **namespace** and track-progress hints include `--namespace`, so `show`/`logs`/`status` find the job instead of 404ing against the context default (`abc-services`).
- **B8** `config set`/`config list` **redact** credential values (`secret`/`password`/`token`/`*_key`) instead of echoing them.
- **B5** `cluster capabilities sync` picks the **S3/api** port, never the console port (MinIO exposes both → "must be made to API port"); warns non-destructively when a stored endpoint disagrees.
- **B10** `job stop -y` short alias (`--yes` already existed).
- **B7** verified **already covered on main** (`ResolveS3Creds` falls back `access_key→user`, `secret_key→password`, reaching `cred_source.local`) — no change.

Unit tests added for the pure helpers (redaction, placement-failure summary, port picker). Build + vet + full touched-package tests green.

**Cluster-side (out of scope, for abc-deployments):** C1 provision the `default` staging bucket, C2 finish the persistent-job-logs pipeline, C3 validate/repair the `exec2` driver on compute nodes.

author: simon-xydt
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Assistant and local-user identity fields were truncated with raw UTF-16 code-unit slicing. When a supplementary character such as an emoji crossed a field boundary, the result could contain a lone surrogate instead of valid text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original patch replaced the shared helper's slice operation. Maintainer review found that the shared `coerceIdentityValue(value, maxLength)` API also accepted arbitrary limits and preserved accidental negative-limit behavior, so this branch was rewritten at the owning boundaries instead:

- Gateway identity fields now use a closed name/avatar/emoji limit map.
- Control UI assistant identity fields use their own closed field-to-limit map.
- Local-user names use the fixed 50-code-unit product limit.
- Every bounded field uses `truncateUtf16Safe` after optional-string normalization.
- The ownerless shared helper and its tests are deleted.

The rewrite reduces production code by 11 lines and preserves contributor credit in the commit history.

## User Impact

Identity values keep their existing trimming, limits, precedence, and fallback behavior. Values containing supplementary Unicode characters at a boundary now remain valid text: a complete character is retained when it fits, and an incomplete surrogate pair is dropped.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head: `f98c7d2fab678bb8bbfe55d61dce54decd5072e3`
- Exact diff hash: `cf081ed5bdb71c6536a2fa1a52beb85d6ca74941c04ccd1bbdfe43c766a4c52a`
- Gateway regression uses schema-reachable `agents.list[].identity.name` through the public resolver.
- Gateway, assistant UI, and local-user tests cover both sides of the 50-code-unit surrogate boundary.
- `git diff --check`: pass.
- Fresh full-diff autoreview, root re-review, and independent exact-content review: clean; no actionable findings.
- Exact-head hosted CI: [run 29045831776](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29045831776), all executed jobs successful.
- Exact-head CodeQL: [run 29045831824](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29045831824), successful.
- Sanitized direct AWS focused proof: [run `run_5a0495db40af`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_5a0495db40af) on fresh public/no-Tailscale lease `cbx_02c395ea71cb`; 32 Gateway and 10 UI assertions passed.
- Source-blind public CLI/RPC proof: [run `run_77c720e392a9`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_77c720e392a9) returned the padded short name exactly trimmed as `Alpha β`, with valid UTF-8, no replacement character, and a clean round-trip. Supplementary-character boundary live clauses remained harness-blocked after a leaked prior listener; exact sanitized regressions and hosted CI cover both boundary outcomes.

author: zoubeir23
body:
## Résumé
Troisième agent conversationnel actionnable (après OKR et Onboarding), suivant le même pattern DRY : le chat peut désormais valider ou refuser une demande de congé, en langage naturel, sans dupliquer la logique métier existante.

## Fonctionnement
- `detect_action_intent()` reconnaît en priorité les formulations de **validation/refus** ("valider le congé de X", "refuser la demande de congé de X"...) avant celles de simple demande de congé (les deux contiennent le mot "congé").
- `extract_leave_approval_parameters()` (LLM) extrait l'employé concerné et la décision (approve/reject).
- `_execute_leave_approval()` résout l'employé par nom exact (rejette les homonymes), retrouve sa demande PENDING la plus récente, puis invoque **directement le ViewSet REST existant** (`LeaveRequestViewSet.approve`/`.reject` via `APIRequestFactory` + `force_authenticate`) — aucune logique de permission (RH/Admin/manager du département), de solde de congé ou de notification n'est dupliquée.
- Point technique important : comme `ATOMIC_REQUESTS=True`, DRF marque `connection.needs_rollback=True` sur toute réponse d'erreur (403/400) même hors du cycle requête/réponse normal. L'appel est donc enveloppé dans son propre `transaction.atomic()` pour consommer ce flag localement et ne pas corrompre la transaction de l'appelant.

## Exemple
> "Valide le congé de Awa Diallo" → ✅ Demande de congé de **Awa Diallo** validée : **Congé annuel** du 01/08/2026 au 05/08/2026.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest smart_hr/ai` (86 tests) — intent detection (priorité approval vs request), extraction LLM (succès/erreur/décision invalide), exécution (succès approve/reject, décision manquante, employé introuvable, aucune demande en attente, employé sans droit ne peut pas approuver, demande déjà traitée)
- [x] `pytest smart_hr` complet (580 tests) — aucune régression
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` — tous les hooks verts

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Nouvelles fonctionnalités**
  * Ajout de la prise en charge des décisions de congé dans le chat IA.
  * Un responsable RH peut désormais approuver ou refuser une demande de congé d’un autre employé directement depuis l’interface.

* **Améliorations**
  * La détection des intentions distingue mieux les demandes de congé et les validations/refus.

author: dragonstyle
body:
Adds a Slack notification when a release awaits publish approval, because GitHub's deployment-review notifications are unreliable (notably suppressed for the actor who triggered the run).

## Approach (given the app is incoming-webhook only)
`meridian-slack-notifications` has only the `incoming-webhook` scope — no bot token — so it **can't DM**. Instead we post to a **dedicated approvals channel** and **@-mention** the approvers, which pings them personally.

- **`SLACK_APPROVALS_WEBHOOK_URL`** (optional secret) → the approvals channel, separate from any general `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` update stream.
- **`approvers`** input (space/comma-separated GitHub logins) → resolved to Slack member IDs via a shared **`slack-ids.json`** (login → `U…`), and `@`-mentioned. Unmapped / `TODO` entries are skipped.
- Fires from the **release-please job** (before the environment gate — a step in the gated publish job wouldn't run until after approval). No-ops if the webhook secret is unset.

## Your setup
- [x] Create a `#release-approvals` channel + an incoming webhook for it (via `meridian-slack-notifications`); store the URL as org secret **`SLACK_APPROVALS_WEBHOOK_URL`**.
- [x] Fill in **`slack-ids.json`** — the `TODO`s → each approver's Slack member ID (Slack profile → ⋯ → Copy member ID).
- Callers pass e.g. `with: { approvers: "dragonstyle jjallaire epatey" }`.

author: ignaciomagana
body:
## What

Adds an optional per-survey redshift depth that truncates the completeness correction's
missing-galaxy budget to `zgrid <= z_depth`, instead of the full `[0, DARKSIRENS_ZMAX]`
grid (default 5.0). For a survey complete to z<=1.5 the full-grid budget inflates
`N_miss` ~5x and dilutes the per-pixel catalog term to `N_obs/(N_obs+N_miss) ~ 0.15`
(measured on a GLASS mock during the gw_agn reproduction campaign).

`z_depth = None` (the default everywhere) is the legacy full-grid budget and is
**bit-identical**: the `None` branch takes the original expression verbatim (no mask is
even constructed).

## Design

- `SurveyParams.z_depth: Any = None` (core/types.py); concrete Python float at trace time
  (closure constant), never a tracer — the branch is a Python-level `if`.
- `_assemble_curves` masks `dN_miss` (and the diagnostic `N_exp`) beyond `z_depth` before
  the trapezoids; threaded through `_completion_curves_row{,_q}` and
  `_completion_member_row` (ensemble members mirrored).
- Sources & precedence: `--survey_z_depth` (CLI, all catalogs) > per-catalog file attr
  `z_depth` (new optional attr, written by `darksirens_pixelate --z_depth`) > `None`.
  Clamped to `zMax` with a warning. Loud per-catalog config line + banner row; provenance
  attrs in results HDF5 (mirrors `complete_empty_pixel_policy`).
- `load_survey` returns the attr (all 5 call sites updated); decoder carries per-catalog
  depths onto `SurveyParams` in both `decode` and `decode_mixture`.

## Validation

- New `tests/test_completion_depth.py` (6 tests): `None` ≡ full-depth bit-identity (`==`),
  truncation equals an independent NumPy trapezoid + monotonicity, clamp-warns,
  `load_survey` round-trip, decoder threading.
- Full fast suite on the branch: **617 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed** — identical to the
  origin/master baseline (611 passed + the 6 new tests; baseline measured same machine,
  GPU, 0 failures). Bit-identity canaries (`test_multitracer_likelihood`,
  `test_complete_catalog_empty_pixel_policy`) green.
- End-to-end: `pixelate --z_depth` -> `load_survey` round-trip -> `make_likelihood` run
  confirming `z_depth=None` == `z_depth=zMax` bitwise and finite change for finite depth.

## Notes

- The `--validate_completion` diagnostic path intentionally untouched (out of the hot
  likelihood path); a follow-up can mirror the mask there.
- Groundwork for the field-convention catalog-sky-weighting PR (stacked next), whose
  global normalizer must respect the survey depth.

author: ascaramutti
body:
## Qué

Agrega CI de tests del backend en GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/backend-tests.yml`):
corre `mvn test` en un runner GitHub-hosted (`ubuntu-latest`) contra un Postgres 16
efímero, en cada `pull_request` que toque `backend/` y en `push` a `develop`.

Flyway migra el schema completo sobre la BD virgen y el `DevDataSeeder` siembra la data de
desarrollo; el par de claves JWT de test se genera al vuelo con `openssl`. Permisos de solo
lectura y credenciales de test no sensibles (viven en el bloque `%test.` de
`application.properties`).

## Config de test vía perfil `%test.`

Los overrides que usan los tests estaban en `src/test/resources/application-test.properties`,
que Quarkus no cargaba (un `application-{perfil}.properties` solo se activa si hay un
`application.properties` base en la misma ubicación). Localmente lo suplía el `.env`; sin él
(en CI) el arranque de Quarkus fallaba al expandir los `${VAR}`. Se movieron a un bloque
`%test.` en el `application.properties` base y se eliminó el archivo muerto, así el CI no
necesita `.env` ni env vars.

## Tests que dependen de la BD de desarrollo

Correr la suite sobre una BD virgen destapó que los tests de recurso de cotizaciones (y
casos puntuales de cargotypes/pdf) asumen la data acumulada del entorno de desarrollo y su
layout de IDs (client=1, cargoType=1, service types en posiciones fijas, cuentas en
`system_settings`), que no se puede sembrar en una BD limpia. Se marcan con
`@Tag("requires-dev-data")` y se excluyen de la corrida del CI (`-DexcludedGroups`),
manteniendo la exclusión visible en el workflow. La suite completa se sigue corriendo
localmente. Hermetizarlos y quitar el tag queda como trabajo aparte.

También se ajusta el nombre que el seed asigna a `lcampos` para que coincida con lo que
espera `AuthResourceTest`, de modo que el login test pase sobre una BD virgen.

## Verificación

- BD virgen + exclusión del tag: 693 tests en verde (lo que corre el CI).
- Suite completa local (BD de desarrollo): 867 tests en verde.

## Nota

Cuando se mergee, marcar el check `Backend tests` como required en la branch protection de
`develop` (Settings, Branches).

author: kristoffeys
body:
Closes #194.

Rebuilt on current `main` (which now has #192's three-way `resolveBrain` and #195's PreCompact), resolving the conflicts — and extended with prompt-time capture per the follow-up ask.

## 1. Per-prompt context injection (original #194)

New **`UserPromptSubmit`** hook: every turn it reads the prompt, resolves the brain via the same single ADR-0024 §3 pass as `SessionStart` (which is the scope gate — `denied`/`none` inject nothing), and injects the notes relevant to *this turn* via the existing query path (`context --query` → `selectRelevant({query})` → FTS). Complements `SessionStart`'s session-wide context.

**Per-turn latency (the crux):**
- `realDeps` resolves the curate binary **once** and prefers the vendored `vendor/curate/index.js` — no `npx -y` cold start per turn (falls back to npx when vendor/ is absent).
- The query is capped (`--limit 5`) and **hard time-bounded (10s)**.
- **Hard relevance gate**: renders nothing without a real match → no per-turn noise. Silent no-op when out of scope / no brain / no prompt. Honors `DISABLE_HOOKS_ENV`.

## 2. Throttled capture on UserPromptSubmit (follow-up: "capture stuff … if needed")

The hook **also** launches the same detached SessionEnd worker — but **throttled**: at most once per `$COMMONWEALTH_PROMPT_CAPTURE_MS` **per session** (default **15m**; `0` disables). So a long session's knowledge is captured periodically, not only at PreCompact/SessionEnd — closing the gap where a session is abandoned mid-flight.

- **Fire-and-forget** (detached worker) → zero turn-latency cost.
- The worker **self-gates** on scope/brain, so an out-of-scope prompt does no real LLM work; the throttle is the "if needed".
- **Safe**: curate dedups staged notes, so overlapping prompt/PreCompact/SessionEnd captures never duplicate. Per-session throttle marks live beside the receipt file.

## Testing

`pnpm lint` ✓, prettier ✓, plugin suites green (82). New: `lib.test.ts` (userPromptSubmit gates + `buildUserPromptSubmitOutput` + `shouldCaptureNow`/interval parsing), `manifest.test.ts` (all four hooks registered), `realdeps.test.ts` (recursion no-op, capture-mark round-trip, real throttled worker-launch + disabled-no-launch). Plugin README updated.

author: manganite
body:
Resolves the Table-4f **STOP** from the previous work order (findings §8.3). The maintainer supplied Birss's own pairing convention.

## The rule — lockstep (recorded in `table-4f.md`)
> "Notations of the type xz(2), xxy(3), yxxx(x.3), xxxz(4), xxyy(x:3), xxyz(c4) and zzxy(xy:6) indicate certain permutations which must be applied to every component in the column. Thus … the same permutation must be applied to all the components listed in that column for the various crystal classes." (Birss, printed pages 62–66)

A header annotation defines a set of **index-position** permutations; the **same** permutations expand the cell value → one relation per family member. It is **not** an axis relabel (why that candidate failed) and **not** "all members = one component" (why that failed). Worked example — `K4`, `xxyz(c4) = -yyyz` (cyclic shifts): `T_xxyz=-T_yyyz`, `T_zxxy=-T_zyyy`, `T_yzxx=-T_yzyy`, `T_xyzx=-T_yyzy`. Sum cells (e.g. `xxxx = yyxx+xyyx+yxyx`) are direct equalities.

## Guard — `tables4f.reference.test.ts` (34 tests, all green)
For all **32 classical groups × both parities**, compares `computeTensorForm(…, {rank:4, i, none})` to the parsed Table-4f row (via the Table-4a even-rank class letters) by **subspace equality**: the engine span satisfies every parsed relation **and** its rank equals the table's independent-component count. Also asserts the classical **i-form ≡ c-form**. No per-class exceptions.

### Engine note (comparison uses rank, not length)
For a *general* (intrinsic-none) rank-4 tensor, `computeTensorForm(...).basisResults` is a **non-minimal spanning set** (deduped only by proportionality — e.g. 11 vectors spanning a 10-dim space for class P). The guard therefore compares the **rank of the engine span** to the table dimension. Unaffected: ED/MD/EQ and ranks 0–3 (projection already minimal). A future Tables UI displaying an independent-component *count* for general rank-4 must apply the same reduction.

### 6/mmm P4 — Birss's own worked example (eq. 2.23), for a book eyeball
The parsed P4 (polar) equalities, all reproduced by the engine:
```
T_yyyy = T_xxxx      T_yyzz = T_xxzz      T_zzyy = T_zzxx
T_yyxx = T_xxyy      T_yzyz = T_xzxz      T_zyzy = T_zxzx
T_yxyx = T_xyxy      T_yzzy = T_xzzx      T_zyyz = T_zxxz
T_yxxy = T_xyyx
```
plus the sum cell `T_xxxx = T_yyxx + T_xyyx + T_yxyx`; independent leads: `xxxx xxzz xzxz xzzx zxxz zxzx zzxx zzzz` (+ the two constrained families) → 10 independent.

## Docs / gates
- findings §8.3.1: STOP → resolved (rule + engine-spanning-set note); ROADMAP-next V1 Table-4f sub-gap marked **done**.
- Canonical `manganite/birss-tables` gets the identical Notation note via its own PR (Part A).

author: m0nd0r
body:
## Summary

In `MULTI_USER_MODE`, app ownership is tracked by the admin app's `db.app` table, but application `appadmin` controllers authorize through the shared admin session via `gluon.fileutils.check_credentials(request)`. A non-manager admin user with a valid admin session could therefore reach another application's `/appadmin` controller because the credential check only verified that the admin session was fresh.

This patch makes the shared credential check enforce the multi-user app boundary before authorizing appadmin access:

- global admin-password sessions without multi-user `auth.user` data keep the existing behavior
- manager users, including user id 1, keep cross-app access
- non-manager multi-user admin sessions are accepted only when `db.app` records show they own `request.application`
- missing ownership metadata fails closed for multi-user admin sessions

## Security impact

`appadmin` can read, insert, update, delete, import, export, and inspect an application's database tables. In a shared `MULTI_USER_MODE` deployment, allowing one non-manager admin user to access another user's appadmin crosses the intended app ownership boundary and can expose or modify another application's data.

## Tests

- `python3 -m unittest gluon.tests.test_appadmin`
- `python3 -m py_compile gluon/fileutils.py gluon/tests/test_appadmin.py`
- `git diff --check origin/master..HEAD`

author: peytonhobson
body:
## Why

apple.com's demo shipped a **"TV & Home" nav glyph** as its logo. The bounding-box + IoU-matching design failed (tiny navbar mark; one run's screenshot was covered by an app-store modal), and the fallback — the probe's hand-tuned heuristic score — picked a nav label. Score-based selection is overfit by construction: every constant was tuned reactively to one site (West Hills, Pizzeria Bianco, now Apple).

## What

Selection now happens by **looking at the candidates**, in the same single vision call that picks the brand color:

- New `rasterize-logo.ts`: renders each candidate to a ≤256px PNG (sharp) — flattened onto light grey so white-ink marks stay visible, SVGs rasterized at high density so a 14×44 mark is legible.
- `detect-brand.ts`: candidates are attached as numbered images, each captioned with one line of DOM context from the probe (`alt`, wrapping anchor label, links-home, recurrence). The model returns `logoIndex`; `logoBox`/IoU matching is deleted.
- Fallback when vision abstains or errors: schema.org-declared logo → apple-touch-icon → heuristic top pick.
- The full candidate list is logged per run, so the next misfire is diagnosable from logs alone.

Companion web-crawler PR fixes collection (the real Apple mark was dropped by a size floor before selection ever saw it) and adds the context fields.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` + build clean.
- Replayed a live apple.com scrape through the new `detectBrand` with a real vision call: picked the **real 14×44 Apple mark (#3)** over seven nav-glyph decoys that all outscored it heuristically ("TV & Home" was still #0 at score 320). Color selection unaffected (`#0066cc`).

author: gilbert-barajas
body:
Following up on #2 with the predicted-vs-measured data from the oMLX / M-series stack. Two real measurements from an **M5 Max 128GB** running **oMLX 0.4.5.dev1 (MLX 0.31.2)**. Both resident-byte figures come straight from oMLX's own per-engine accounting (the `actual_size` field it exposes for each loaded engine — the same metric #2 read via the fork's `/engine/loaded`).

### 1. Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (MLX 8-bit) — `30.4 GiB`
- **How measured**: oMLX `/engine/loaded` actual resident bytes (the #2 table). oMLX estimates the full 8-bit MoE weights at 31.72 GiB; the 30.4 GiB resident reflects dFlash SSD expert offload (only active experts held in RAM).
- `ctx 32768` / `kvBits 16` are oMLX defaults; the figure is weight-residency-dominated and effectively ctx-independent.
- Figure taken from #2 (closed — the `parseHfConfig` bit-width fix landed) — not re-measured this session because the model wasn't resident at the time.

### 2. Qwen3.6-27B-4bit (Gated DeltaNet) — `15.33 GiB`  ← the linear-attention datapoint asked for in #2
- **How measured (live this session)**: `GET /admin/api/models` → `Qwen3.6-27B-4bit.actual_size = 16,457,805,464 bytes = 15.33 GiB` (oMLX's own formatted label). This is the per-engine resident-bytes field — identical to what `/engine/loaded` reports.
- Architecture: `qwen3_5`, hybrid 16 full-attention + 48 Gated-DeltaNet (linear) layers → the recurrent state is ctx-independent, so resident memory does **not** scale with context length. A useful calibration point for the linear-attention path.
- `ctx 32768` = oMLX global default `max_context_window` (per-model `null` → inherits default). `kvBits 16` from the loaded engine's settings (`turboquant_kv_enabled=false` → unquantized fp16 KV).
- Idle measurement (no active generation) — treat as a floor, not peak-during-gen.

**Units**: both figures are GiB, matching #2's convention and oMLX's own labels. Decimal-GB equivalents: 30.4 GiB ≈ 32.64 GB; 15.33 GiB ≈ 16.46 GB. Happy to switch the field to decimal GB — raw bytes are in each entry's `notes`.

**On the 4-bit variant**: I measured the 4-bit Qwen3.6-27B because it was the one resident at the time. The oQ8-mtp (8-bit) variant is registered but wasn't loaded, so I reported no number for it rather than guess one.

The `source` field on entry 2 points at this PR; repoint to the upstream PR URL if you'd prefer.

### Tests
`node --test test/*.test.mjs` → **8/8 pass** · `node vectors/run.mjs` → **14/14 pass**.
Heads-up (pre-existing, unrelated to this data PR): the `npm test` wrapper `node --test test/` errors under Node ≥23 because Node now resolves a bare directory argument as a module. `node --test test/*.test.mjs` (or `"test/**/*.test.mjs"`) works.

Thanks for the engine — the per-layer-type modeling is exactly right.

author: 91jaeminjo
body:
## Summary

Tears down a server's **in-memory** session state when a *different* user signs in on it within the same app session, and scopes document-filter selections per server so they can be cleared cleanly.

Persistent device-local state is already partitioned by user identity. But four in-memory caches would otherwise carry the prior user's state into the next session:

- `AgentRuntimeManager` (keyed on the live `ServerConnection`, which re-auth reuses)
- `RunRegistry` (keyed on the stable `serverId`)
- `UploadTrackerRegistry` (keyed on `serverId`)
- `DocumentSelections` (a single shared map, previously not partitioned by user)

The new `UserSwitchTeardown` watches each server's `AuthSession.currentUserId` and evicts all four when a server's identity moves from one non-null user to a different non-null user. Reading identity state (rather than intercepting sign-in call sites) covers every auth path — silent restore-on-launch, token refresh (no teardown), and expiry-then-different-user (a switch).

## Changes

- **`DocumentSelections`** now keys on `(serverId, roomId, threadId)` via a named record, isolating selections per server, and gains `clearServer`.
- **`AgentRuntimeManager` / `RunRegistry` / `UploadTrackerRegistry`** expose `evictServer(serverId)` via a shared predicate-driven `_evictWhere`; `UploadTrackerRegistry` hardens disposal with remove-before-dispose + swallow-and-log.
- **`RemovedServerCleanup`** now also clears a removed server's document-filter selections.
- **`UserSwitchTeardown`** (new) coordinates the four evictions, each isolated so one throw can't strand the rest or unwind the sign-in.

## Known limitation

Servers whose IdP issues **opaque (non-JWT) access tokens** report a `null` identity for every user, so a switch between two such users is undetectable — the next user inherits the prior in-memory session. This mirrors the shared unauthenticated bucket those servers already use for persistent state, and is documented in the `UserSwitchTeardown` class doc.

## Test plan

- `flutter analyze` — clean across the project.
- `flutter test` on the affected suites — all green:
  - `test/modules/room/user_switch_teardown_test.dart` (10 tests: switch/refresh/first-sight/logout/disposed/per-server-isolation/expiry-then-switch/switch-back/late-signin baseline, and step-isolation under a throwing eviction — mutation-verified).
  - `test/modules/room/document_selections_test.dart`, `test/core/removed_server_cleanup_test.dart`.
- CHANGELOG updated (Fixed + Security).

author: lucasccordeiro
body:
## What

`format(value)` / `format(value, "")` on a **float** threw `format() spec '' is not supported for this value` instead of folding, e.g. `format(1.0)` and `format(-1.0)` both errored. CPython's `format(x, "")` is `x.__format__("")` = `str(x)`, so they should fold to `"1.0"` and `"-1.0"`.

The cause: `handle_format` routes numeric values through `py_format_number`, which models only the explicit float presentation types (`f`/`e`/`g`/`%`) and returns `std::nullopt` for the repr-like *default* float format (the fail-closed boundary added in the earlier `format()` mini-spec work). With an empty spec that `nullopt` fell through to the string-only fallback and then the reject.

## How

- Extract the `str()`/`repr()` float renderer that already lived in `handle_float_to_str` into a shared free helper `py_str_from_double(double)` (`std::to_string`'s `%f`, trailing-zero strip, `".0"` restored for whole numbers, under a `round_to_nearest_guard`) and route `handle_float_to_str` through it.
- Add a `spec.empty() && is_float` branch to `handle_format` that folds `py_str_from_double(dval)`. `dval` comes from `const_double_from_json`, which already carries the `UnaryOp(USub)` sign, so the positive and negative literal branches share one path.

Deliberately **not** reusing `string_method_handler.cpp`'s `format_value_from_json` (the `"{}".format` renderer): that uses a default `ostringstream` (six *significant* digits, `format(1234.5678)` → `"1234.57"`), whereas `str()` uses `%f` (six *fractional* digits, `str(1234.5678)` → `"1234.5678"`). `format(x) == str(x)` requires the `str()` renderer.

This is a **restore-working-behaviour** fix — the prior behaviour was a clean error / spurious `FAILED`, never a false `SUCCESSFUL`. It shares `str()`'s exact renderer, so it introduces no new divergence beyond `str()`'s known 6-fractional-digit / no-scientific-notation gap (`str(1/3)`, `str(1e16)`), which remains a separate follow-up.

## Tests

New regression pair (CORE), both included in this PR:
- `regression/python/builtin_format_empty_spec_float` — liveness witness for the new branch: whole-number floats (±, `-1000000.0`), signed zero (`-0.0` → `"-0.0"`), dyadic fractionals, an explicit empty spec (`format(1.5, "")`), and the unaffected int/string empty-spec paths.
- `regression/python/builtin_format_empty_spec_float_fail` — pins the previously-erroring `format(-1.0) == "-1"`, now correctly `FAILED`.

Every positive assertion was differential-tested bit-for-bit against CPython (14/14 match; the `_fail` claim is genuinely false). The focused `format`/`fstring`/`percent`/`str`/`repr` ctest subset (168 tests) passes 100%. Solver-agnostic (a frontend constant fold — assertions simplify to `assert(true/false)` with zero remaining VCCs).

Closes the first deferred candidate in `docs/python-issues-triage-report-2026-06-02.md` §83b (documented as §84).

author: psamiton
body:
## Problem

`sharp` was listed in `devDependencies`, so it was absent from production installs of the published package. The avatar code that inlines participant images into every mind's context did `import("sharp")`, caught the `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, and silently fell back to inlining the **full-size original bytes** — potentially megabytes of base64 — into every mind's context on every message. This class of bug (an optional dep present in dev but absent in prod, behind a silent fallback) is invisible to every other test.

## Changes

- Move `sharp` from `devDependencies` to `dependencies` (root `package.json` + refreshed `package-lock.json`) so downscaling actually runs in production.
- Refactor the two duplicate `import("sharp")` avatar loaders into a single exported `renderAvatarBlock()` in `packages/daemon/src/lib/util/avatar-image.ts`. It resizes to `AVATAR_CONTEXT_DIM` (128) and returns `null` — **omitting the avatar entirely** — when sharp is unavailable, the format is unsupported, resizing fails, or the encoded block exceeds a 64 KB ceiling (`MAX_AVATAR_BLOCK_BYTES`), rather than inlining full-size originals.
- `delivery-manager.ts` `loadAvatarBlocks()` now calls `renderAvatarBlock()` while keeping its own path-escape / symlink checks and cache.
- `loadSharp()` warns **once per process** (was debug) when sharp is unavailable.
- Tests: `renderAvatarBlock` unit tests, plus a repo-guard asserting sharp is a `dependency`, not a `devDependency`.

## Review triage

Three reviewers surfaced four findings; triage:

- **Once-per-process warning only covered the missing-module branch** (minor) — **fixed**. `loadSharp()`'s guard now covers the broken-native-binary branch too (a real risk now that sharp ships platform-specific prebuilds), so an unusable install warns once instead of once per participant per delivery.
- **Omit-on-failure path untested** (important) — **addressed**. Added a `renderAvatarBlock` test: a supported-extension file (`.png`) holding non-image bytes returns `null` (omits the block) instead of inlining the original. This exercises the exact regression contract — on processing failure, drop rather than inline full-size — for the realistic failure mode. The literal sharp-completely-absent branch is left to structural review (a trivial `return null` in `loadSharp`) plus the packaging guard test, rather than adding a test-only injection seam to production code.
- **`MAX_AVATAR_BLOCK_BYTES` ceiling drop-path untested** (minor) — **skipped**. Verified empirically that a 128×128 output is inherently a few KB; even a 200-frame noise GIF resizes to ~30 KB (sharp collapses to a single page on resize here), so the ceiling cannot be tripped by any realistic avatar. It is defense-in-depth; a deterministic fixture that trips it would be disproportionately contrived. Existing test still asserts a resized block stays under the ceiling.
- **Resize-throws catch untested** (minor) — **addressed** by the same non-image-bytes test above (a `.png` extension passes the MIME check and reaches sharp, which throws).

## Testing

Full `npm test` passes: **1927 tests, 1927 pass, 0 fail**. Targeted `test/avatar-image.test.ts` passes (10/10) including the new omit-on-failure case.

Fixes #535

author: eduvhc
body:
First slice of the admin dashboard (decisions from our discussion: separate InteractiveServer host, HTTP client to /api/staff, Refitter codegen, scaffold+login scope).

## What's here
A new **`src/Iedora.Dashboard`** Blazor Web App — a *pure client* of the API's admin surface, no DB of its own.

**Aspire** — new `dashboard` resource with `WithReference(api)` (service discovery resolves `https+http://api`) + `AddServiceDefaults` (OTel/health/resilience), same as every other service.

**Typed client** — Refitter's source generator emits `IIedoraApiv1` from the committed `openapi/Iedora.Api.json`, over Refit + `IHttpClientFactory`. A `BearerHandler` attaches the admin's token. The generated client is **committed and regenerated in-place on build** — same posture as the OpenAPI doc it derives from (a Refitter clean-build ordering quirk also makes committing it the robust choice).

**Auth (the important part)** — the dashboard runs its **own cookie session**; the API JWT stays **server-side, never in the browser**:
- `POST /login` → API `/auth/login` → `/auth/whoami`, and **requires the `admin` role** before signing in (front-office admins only; non-admins are rejected).
- Anonymous requests bounce to `/login`; default authorization policy is `RequireRole(admin)`.
- Reuses `Iedora.Identity.Contracts.Roles.Admin` (no duplicated "admin" string); everything else is over HTTP — the API stays the single enforcement point.

## Layout
`Auth/` (AccessToken, BearerHandler, AuthEndpoints), `Api/` (Refitter settings + generated client), `Components/` (Login, Home shell, RedirectToLogin). Program.cs at root per the host convention.

## Verification
- Full solution builds **0 warnings**; the AppHost **e2e test still boots healthy** with the dashboard added (17s).
- Booted standalone: anonymous `GET /` → **302 → /login**; `/login` renders the form with email/password + antiforgery token.
- Live credential login against a running API + DB + seeded admin is the **next slice** (it also brings the first real screen, the Staff Overview, and per-request token hydration from the cookie for interactive API calls).

## Notes / next
- The per-request token hydration (so interactive components can call `/api/staff`) is stubbed for now — `AccessToken` is only populated during the login round-trip. That gets wired when the Overview page lands.
- `Policies.Admin` on the API side is unchanged; the dashboard enforces the same `admin` role via its own cookie policy.

author: jeswr
body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent (Claude Fable 5). Implements `sq-1ivw7`, closing #1785's honest null result.

## What

Widens the opt-in, OFF-by-default `id-filter-fastpath` (on `sparq-engine`, added in #1785) to
**object-position IRI/bnode variables** via a **snapshot-aware predicate-range term-kind inference** —
the missing piece #1785 documented as its null result on the SP2Bench **q08/q12b** shape.

#1785's position-only static analysis (`nonliteral_vars`) proves a variable non-literal only when it
is bound in subject/predicate slots. q08/q12b's FILTER variables (`?author`, `?erdoes`, `?author2`,
`?document`, `?document2`) appear only as `dc:creator` **objects**, so the analysis correctly declined
and path (a) did not fire — even though those objects are provably IRIs at DATA level.

This PR credits an **object** variable as non-literal when its predicate is a **constant IRI** whose
object column has **no literal** in the **current store snapshot**.

- The requirement is **NO LITERALS**, not IRI-only: bnode ids are identity-comparable exactly like
  IRIs for `=`/`!=` (`sameTerm` coincides; distinct non-literals compare **FALSE** per §17.4.1.7), so a
  predicate with IRI **and bnode** objects still fires.
- Declines conservatively: any **literal** object for the predicate (string, inline-integer, any
  datatype), a **variable** predicate, a **quoted-triple** object, or **mixed** use of the variable
  (also an object of a literal-having predicate anywhere) → the exact path, unchanged.

New always-compiled `sparq-core` public API (each with a **direct** unit test):
- `dict::is_literal_id(dict, id)` — id-level term-kind (inline integers always literal; else
  `TermParts::Lit`).
- `Graph::predicate_has_literal_object(pred)` — **overlay-aware, early-exit** scan of a predicate's
  objects against the **live** snapshot. Answers for the **receiver graph only** (scans `self.store`,
  never `self.named`) — documented so callers don't misuse it across a graph boundary.

Also wires the **fused conjunctive** residual-FILTER sites (`eval_flat_conjunctive`,
`eval_bgp_binary_capped`) — deliberately not wired in #1785 — to install the same snapshot-aware
non-literal column set. **Drain-safe** via `with_idfast_nonlit_cols`: the set drains on the first
consuming `apply_filter`, so a nested `EXISTS` on a different `Bindings` layout sees the empty default
(the #1785 round-2 EXISTS-re-entry defence, commit `36d59f1d5`).

## Cross-graph soundness fix (addresses the request_changes on this PR)

The escalated-tier reviewer found — and empirically reproduced — a result-correctness hole: the
predicate-range object credit was unsound across a `GRAPH` boundary. `collect_kind_positions`'
`G::Graph` arm recursed into the inner BGP with the **outer** graph's `obj_may_be_literal` classifier.
But a plain object variable inside `GRAPH <g>`/`GRAPH ?g` is bound from the **named sub-graph** (a
self-contained sub-`Graph` with its own store/dict), not the graph the outer FILTER dispatches
against. A FILTER sitting **outside** the GRAPH block therefore credited a named-graph object off the
**default** graph's literal-free column and id-compared literals for `=`/`!=`.

Counterexample (default `<creator>` literal-free; named graph `<http://ex/g>` has
`"1"^^xsd:integer`/`"1.0"^^xsd:decimal` creator objects; `GRAPH <g>{ ?d creator ?a . ?d creator ?b }
FILTER(?a=?b)` **outside**): feature **OFF = 4 rows** (`=` is value equality, `1 = 1.0` holds), feature
**ON was 2 rows** (unsound id credit). This hole could not exist under #1785 (subject/predicate credits
are graph-independent); the predicate-range credit is the first place *which graph is scanned* matters.

**Fix (minimal, preserves the q08/q12b default-graph win):** in `collect_kind_positions`, the
`G::Graph` arm now recurses with the always-conservative classifier (`&|_| true`) so object slots
under **any** GRAPH block stay literal-risk at an outer dispatch. The **inside-GRAPH** dispatch is
already correct and unchanged: when the FILTER sits inside the block, `eval_translated` evaluates the
inner pattern with `graph = sub`, so its own `nonliteral_filter_cols` scans the right (named) store.
`Graph::predicate_has_literal_object`'s doc now states its receiver-graph-only scope.

## Snapshot lifecycle (the soundness question — answered, cited)

The inference is valid **only** for the snapshot the query runs against. I traced the lifecycle:

- A prepared query is **parse-only**: `PreparedQuery` (crates/sparq-engine/src/lib.rs) carries the
  `spargebra` algebra — **no compiled plan, no store metadata**. Execution entry points acquire the
  `&Graph` **fresh at execution time**.
- Evaluation holds a **shared immutable** `&Graph` borrow for its whole duration, so Rust's borrow
  rules forbid a coexisting `&mut Graph` — **the snapshot cannot mutate mid-eval**. Computing
  `predicate_has_literal_object` at the FILTER dispatch is therefore valid for the entire eval.
- There is **no plan cache**. The only cache is a **result** cache keyed by `(query, version)`; a
  mutation bumps the version and orphans old entries.
- The server pins a lock-free **generation** snapshot per request; an UPDATE publishes a **new**
  generation. A query built against gen G1 is never re-run against G2's data.

**Conclusion:** the check is computed against the **live** `graph` handed to each eval, so an UPDATE
inserting a literal object simply makes the **next** query decline — the verdict **never outlives its
snapshot**. Proven by `predrange_snapshot_update_flips_credit` and
`predicate_has_literal_object_reflects_overlay_update`.

## Tests (real path, load-bearing invariants)

`sparq-core` (direct unit tests for the two new public fns):
- `is_literal_id_classifies_each_kind` — IRI / bnode / string-lit / inline-int / dict-int / `NO_ID`.
- `predicate_has_literal_object_iri_only_vs_literal_vs_bnode` — IRI-only + bnode fires; title/year
  decline; absent predicate vacuously literal-free.
- `predicate_has_literal_object_reflects_overlay_update` — the snapshot-lifecycle flip.

`sparq-engine` (`idfast_unit`, feature-on):
- `predrange_credits_iri_only_object_declines_literal`, `predrange_mixed_use_of_same_var_declines`,
  `predrange_variable_predicate_declines`.
- `predrange_fires_on_q08_shape_witness` — **witness** the q08 `?a = ?b` compiles to
  `CompiledExpr::IdEqNonLit` (fires; under #1785 it declined). **Still fires after the fix** —
  default-graph credit is preserved.
- `predrange_end_to_end_q08_result_unchanged`, `predrange_snapshot_update_flips_credit`.
- **NEW (cross-graph regression, the reviewer's counterexample):**
  - `predrange_graph_block_declines_object_credit_at_outer_dispatch` — analysis-level decline witness:
    an object var bound under `GRAPH <g>` gets **NO** credit at the outer (default-graph) dispatch.
  - `predrange_cross_graph_filter_result_identical` — end-to-end feature-ON differential asserting
    **4 rows** (equal to OFF). **Verified RED on the pre-fix code** (`left: 2, right: 4`) and GREEN
    after the fix.

## Gates (both feature states)

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — GREEN (default) **and** with
  `--features id-filter-fastpath`.
- `cargo test -p sparq-engine` — GREEN default **and** `--features id-filter-fastpath` (all
  `idfast`/`predrange` tests). `cargo test -p sparq-core` — GREEN.
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features` — GREEN.
- W3C SPARQL conformance ratchet — **≥1229, 0 fail** (feature OFF in the conformance build →
  behaviour-identical FILTER path; the fix only tightens the feature-ON classifier).
- `scripts/check-readme-template.py --enforce` — **0 deviations**; `sparq-engine/README.md` at the
  120-line cap.

`origin/main` merged (was 1 commit ahead: #1787 cluster-materialize) — clean.

## Honest performance finding (NON-CANONICAL work box — not a baked-in number)

SP2Bench **q08** / **q12b** at 250k, `materialize`, this shared/noisy work box. Row counts identical
(q08 = 358, q12b

author: drodriguezatcci
body:
## El bug (real, reproducido en pruebas con el sandbox)

Crédito en B2 (2 cuotas atrasadas). Se paga **solo la mora** de una cuota, CONTA valida, corre el job → el crédito baja a B1 **aunque la cuota sigue sin pagarse**. También afecta la mora del sistema viejo: `cuotas_atrasadas` baja 2→1 y el monto se recalcula de menos.

## Causa raíz

1. Un pago de **solo mora/otros/convenio** se inserta colgado de la primera cuota pendiente con `pagado: true` y `monto_aplicado: 0` (`getSpecialPaymentInstallmentFields` — ese `pagado` significa "fila de pago completa", no "cuota cubierta").
2. Al validar, la cuota correctamente NO se marca pagada (suma aplicada 0 < cuota), pero la fila conserva `pagado=true` y pasa a `validated`.
3. El `hasPaidPayment` del job (`EXISTS pagado=true AND validated/no_required`) la toma como cuota cubierta → la cuota desaparece del conteo → BAJADA falsa + mora sub-calculada.

## El fix

`AND COALESCE(pc.monto_aplicado, 0) > 0` en el EXISTS — una fila solo "vouchea" la cuota si aplicó plata real. En dos lugares para que no se contradigan:
- `procesarMoras` (el job) — `hasPaidPayment`
- `createMora` — guard de `cuotasReales` (misma lógica documentada "Misma lógica que procesarMoras")

## Radio de impacto (medido en dev/sandbox con SELECTs)

- 16 cuotas vencidas hoy excluidas del conteo por el EXISTS.
- **Solo 3 se re-incorporan** con el fix (2 solo-mora + 1 solo-otros — exactamente el bug).
- Las otras 13 tienen pago real validado que cerró la cuota con el flag desincronizado → siguen contando como pagadas (para eso existe el EXISTS; sin regresión).

## Letra chica

- Filas solo-mora **legacy** guardaban `monto_aplicado = mora+otros` (>0) → siguen comportándose como hoy (no distinguibles de plata real con seguridad).
- Hay EXISTS con el mismo patrón en `reports.ts` / `reportes.ts` / `paymentAgreement.ts` (conteos de reportes y convenios): **no se tocan aquí** (fuera del alcance pedido), pero queda anotado que pueden mostrar conteos distintos al job en estos 3 casos borde.

## Pruebas

- `bun test latefee.test.ts`: 17/17 pass (incluye los E2E del motor con DB fake).
- `tsc --noEmit` sin errores nuevos.
- Verificación manual del escenario en el sandbox pendiente de re-correr el ciclo (pago solo mora → validar → job → debe seguir B2 con 2 cuotas).

**Nota:** este error existe en prod (sistema viejo de moras, sin buckets) — sigue un hotfix aparte con base `main` con el mismo cambio.

body:
## Summary

Monthly rewards distribution for the **2026-07-15 → 2026-08-15** calendar epoch (31 days), generated by the reward-automation worker (calendar-epochs build, [PR #94](https://github.com/moonwell-fi/moonwell-reward-automation/pull/94) + [#95](https://github.com/moonwell-fi/moonwell-reward-automation/pull/95)) and executed through `RewardsDistributionV2Template` — first monthly MIP to rely on the template's generic auto-batching (#678), no hand-tuned chunk boundaries.

Additionally (Moonbeam wind-down): sets the **stkWELL withdrawal cooldown on Moonbeam to 0** (was 7 days) via `setCoolDownSeconds(0)` on the Safety Module. Stakers can activate the cooldown and redeem immediately; the 2-day unstake window is unchanged. Verified on-chain that the Safety Module's `EMISSION_MANAGER` is the Temporal Governor (executor of the proposal's Moonbeam actions) and that the live cooldown is 604800s; `build()` asserts both, `validate()` asserts cooldown 0 and unstake window intact.

## Epoch contents (worker output)

- **Ethereum (source + destination)**: Foundation funds the governor with 10,311,362.67 xWELL (bridged to the Base TG via the on-chain-quoted Wormhole path) and the Ethereum MRD directly with ~4,160,470.94 xWELL. First epoch with Ethereum mainnet markets as a reward destination.
- **Base**: TG → MRD 5,671,249.40 WELL, 21 MRD speed updates, 5 merkle campaigns.
- **Optimism**: 13 MRD speed updates only (no transfers this epoch).
- **Moonbeam**: fully wound down — 16 comptroller speeds zeroed, `stkWellEmissionsPerSecond: 0`, no bridges or transfers, plus the cooldown removal above.

author: jonathansick
body:
## Summary

- Add a caching proxy for Sphinx `objects.inv` intersphinx inventories so the Rubin documentation toolchain resolves inventories through Ook instead of hammering upstream docs sites. A new `intersphinx_inventory` table (migration `c2a2c14c0e60`) keys cached inventories by origin URL with content, validators (`etag`/`last_modified`), fetch/request timestamps, and last-fetch status.
- Serve inventories from `GET /ook/intersphinx/inventory?url=...`: a cold miss fetches the origin synchronously, stores it, and returns the bytes with an `Age` header; a populated entry is served from Postgres without contacting upstream — fresh within `OOK_INTERSPHINX_TTL`, otherwise stale — so the request path never blocks on the origin once a copy exists.
- Guard every upstream fetch with an SSRF check (https-only; host must not resolve to a private, link-local, or loopback address, including IP-literal and IPv4-mapped IPv6 hosts) and negatively cache cold-miss failures for `OOK_INTERSPHINX_NEGATIVE_TTL` so a repeat request returns the error without re-contacting upstream. The negative-cache write is gated at the store (`ON CONFLICT ... WHERE content IS NULL`), so a concurrent request's freshly stored good copy can never be displaced by a failure row.
- Harden every upstream fetch against a hostile or misbehaving origin: redirects are never followed (explicitly, so the SSRF guard cannot be bypassed one hop at a time — a redirecting origin is treated as an upstream failure), each request carries an explicit 30 s timeout, and the response body is streamed under a 50 MB cap so an oversized inventory is abandoned (and treated as a fetch failure) rather than buffered into memory. DNS rebinding between guard time and connect time is backstopped by TLS hostname verification on the https-only fetch, documented in the guard.
- Add `IntersphinxCacheService.refresh_inventories()` and the `ook refresh-intersphinx` CLI command (a scheduled cron job): conditional GETs revalidate inventories past the TTL that were requested within `OOK_INTERSPHINX_ACTIVE_WINDOW` (default 30 days). A 304 keeps stored content and bumps the fetch time; a 200 replaces content and validators; inventories outside the active window are skipped, not deleted; per-inventory failures are logged and don't abort the batch. The batch owns its transaction boundaries: each inventory's outcome is committed as soon as its refresh completes, so no DB transaction spans an HTTP fetch and a mid-run crash preserves prior progress. Refresh writes leave `date_requested` untouched so a concurrent client request's activity bump is never reverted, and the CLI echoes the summary counts (considered/refreshed/revalidated/failed) for self-describing cron output.

## Validation steps

- `GET /ook/intersphinx/inventory?url=<https objects.inv URL>` twice and confirm the first response fetches upstream while the second is served from cache (rising `Age` header, no second upstream hit).
- Request a `http://` URL, a URL whose host resolves to a private address, and an IP-literal URL such as `https://169.254.169.254/objects.inv`; confirm all are rejected with a 400 and never stored.
- Take the origin offline after a successful fetch and confirm the cached inventory is still served stale past the TTL.
- Request an unreachable/`5xx` origin on a cold miss; confirm a 502 and that a repeat request within the negative TTL returns immediately without re-contacting upstream.
- Request an origin whose response exceeds the 50 MB cap (or declares an oversized `Content-Length`); confirm a 502 whose detail mentions the cap, and that the failure is negatively cached without buffering the body.
- Run `ook refresh-intersphinx` with a stale-but-active cached inventory and confirm a 304 keeps content while bumping the fetch time, a 200 replaces it, and an inventory last requested outside the active window is left untouched; confirm the command echoes the summary counts.
- Confirm `ook refresh-intersphinx` is registered (`ook --help`) and that a per-inventory upstream failure is logged and rolled back without aborting the rest of the run.

author: elirc
body:
## Context
Sprint 04 makes issues orderable and the product keyboard-first: fractional indexing so a drag is a
single-row update, a move endpoint that changes state + reorders in one mutation, a kanban board, and
the keyboard registry + command palette that define Tracer's feel.

Playbook: `docs/sprints/sprint-04.md` · Closes #16 · Closes #17 · Closes #18 · Closes #19 · Closes #20

## Approach
- **Fractional indexing (`@tracer/shared/order.ts`, ADR-0005):** `keyBetween(a, b)` → a base-62 string
  strictly between two keys (ascending-ASCII alphabet, so plain `<` sorts). Property-tested for the
  ordering invariant across random insertion sequences.
- **Move = one mutation (`routes/issues.ts`):** `PATCH /issues/:id/move { stateId, afterId? }` — the
  **server** computes the between-key; only the moved row is written.
- **Board (`web/Board.tsx`):** columns by workflow state, drag to reorder/move, optimistic-ish reload.
- **Keyboard (`web/lib/keyboard.tsx`):** a global registry whose active set mirrors mounted components;
  plain keys don't fire while typing, `mod`-combos do.
- **Command palette v1 (`web/CommandPalette.tsx`):** Cmd/Ctrl+K, substring filter (frecency is S11).

## Verification (local)
`pnpm install && pnpm db:generate` → **typecheck ✓ · 23 tests pass (incl. fast-check property tests)
· lint clean · build ✓**.

## Tradeoffs considered
- **Fractional indexing vs integer resequencing** → ADR-0005 (one-row moves, merge-friendly). See debate.
- **Native HTML5 drag** for the board (no dep) vs a DnD library — keyboard-parity + a11y DnD is Sprint 14.

## Deferred
- Rebalancing fractional keys (flaw #2 → Sprint 12), scoped shortcut stacks, accessible keyboard DnD
  (Sprint 14), palette frecency ranking (Sprint 11).

## Learning objectives
Ordered collections via fractional indexing · move-as-one-mutation · keyboard registries · command
palettes · property-based testing of an ordering invariant.

## How to review this PR
1. `packages/shared/src/order.ts` (+ property tests) — `keyBetween`, and why keys can grow (flaw #2).
2. `apps/api/src/routes/issues.ts` — the move endpoint (one intent = one mutation, server owns the key).
3. `apps/web/src/lib/keyboard.tsx` — the registry + the typing-vs-mod rule.
4. `apps/web/src/CommandPalette.tsx`, `apps/web/src/Board.tsx`.
5. `docs/adr/0005-fractional-indexing.md`, `docs/curriculum/sprint-04.md`.

author: ajit-zer07
body:
Guarantees every published AITP crate stays at the **same version** and is **released together** — mirroring the sibling `acdp-rs` release config.

## 1. Lockstep guard (blocks drift)

- **`scripts/check-versions.sh`** — fails if any crate under `crates/` doesn't inherit via `version.workspace = true`, or if any `aitp*` path pin isn't exactly `=<workspace version>`.
- **`Makefile`** — `make check-versions`, also in the `make ci` gauntlet.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — new `versions` job on every PR/push (now a required check on `main`).

## 2. Force-full-republish (release-plz)

release-plz has no native "release everything" flag; it publishes any crate whose manifest version isn't yet on crates.io. To make full-family release deterministic, `release-plz.toml` now mirrors `acdp-rs`:

- **`version_group = "aitp"` on all 10 published crates** → release-plz assigns them the same next version and bumps/publishes the **whole family together, even unchanged crates**. crates.io never holds a subset at a stale version.
- **Exact inter-crate pins** — `version = "=0.4.0"` (was `"0.4.0"`) so a fresh resolver can't mix release generations.
- **`[workspace]` block** — `semver_check = true` (blocks the release PR on an API break, where the bump happens), `pr_labels = ["release"]`, `git_release_enable = true`.

`version_group` and `version.workspace = true` coexist (each crate still inherits the single `[workspace.package]` version), so the `versions` guard stays valid.

## Verification

- ✅ `check-versions.sh` green: `13 crates inherit version.workspace = true`, `44 inter-crate pins are exact =0.4.0`.
- ✅ `release-plz.toml` parses: 10 crates in `version_group = "aitp"`; workspace opts set.
- ✅ `cargo metadata` resolves with the exact pins.
- ✅ Negative-tested: guard rejects both a crate with its own version and a loosened (`0.4.0`, non-`=`) pin.

## Not in this PR

- **Independent second implementation** (`aitp-verifier-py`-style): AITP's `VERSIONING.md` promotes surfaces to Final only once "two independent implementations interoperate," and `bindings/aitp-py` wraps the same Rust core so it doesn't count. Tracked separately — it's a whole implementation, not a config change.

## Summary

Fixes #919. Two `[keybindings]` fields shipped in the default config but had no handler wired anywhere — pressing them did nothing.

- **`rename_session`** (default `,`): opens the name-input overlay and renames the current session via the `rename` control message. The new name is validated client-side (`daemon.ValidateSessionName`) before the round-trip, mirroring `gr rename`.

Both are driven by their configured key bytes through `PassthroughKeys`, so the config values are respected rather than hardcoded. The `default_config.toml` comments are updated to reflect the now-wired set.

- `internal/client/passthrough.go`: new `ResultRenameSession`/`ResultScrollMode` + `PassthroughKeys` fields + switch cases; help bar updated.

## Summary

Behavior-preserving refactor that removes the duplicated OIDC code path between the shared `micromegas-auth` crate and `analytics-web-srv`.

- **Consolidate login-flow OIDC client construction into `micromegas-auth`.** New `rust/auth/src/oidc_client.rs` module holds the `ConfiguredCoreClient` type alias and a `DiscoveredProvider` (`discover` + `build_client`) that owns provider discovery and client construction. `analytics-web-srv` no longer defines its own `build_oidc_client` / `ConfiguredCoreClient` / `OidcProviderInfo` — `AuthState::get_oidc_provider` now delegates to `DiscoveredProvider::discover`.
- **Split the 909-line `analytics-web-srv/src/auth.rs`** into a focused `auth/` submodule directory: `config` (web `OidcClientConfig`), `state` (`AuthState` + methods), `cookies`, `claims`, and `handlers` (Axum routes, middleware, admin extractors). `mod.rs` re-exports the flat public API so every caller (`web_server.rs` and all tests) compiles unchanged.
- Dropped two dead `let _client = state.build_oidc_client(...)` bindings in `auth_callback`/`auth_refresh` (their result was never used — those handlers do manual HTTP token exchange).

Public API (`analytics_web_srv::auth::*`) and runtime behavior are unchanged; error-message wording and discovery semantics are preserved.

author: pnewsam
body:
## Problem

On Windows, a non-admin user without Developer Mode cannot create symlinks. `Path.symlink_to()` raises `OSError [WinError 1314] A required privilege is not held by the client`. This crashed **server boot**: `reconcile_all()` in `run_dev_setup()` propagated the raise, so the FastAPI lifespan startup aborted with *"Application startup failed. Exiting."* It also broke the DB→files skill migration.

Reported from a Windows test build (preinstalled machine): the server never came up, `/health` timed out.

Fixes: https://linear.app/mindsdb/issue/ENG-717/desktop-app-cowork-backend-fails-to-start-health-timeout-on-v207

## Fix

`cowork/services/skill_links.py`:

- **Junction fallback** — when `symlink_to` fails on Windows, create a directory **junction** (`_winapi.CreateJunction`), which any user can create and is equivalent for our read-only skill fan-out. POSIX still gets a real symlink (unchanged).
- **Junction-aware detect/remove** — junctions are reparse points that `is_symlink()` reports `False` for (checked via `st_reparse_tag`); a directory reparse point is removed with `rmdir`, not `unlink`, on Windows.
- **Boot can't die on this** — `reconcile_all` now reconciles each skill under try/except and logs+skips failures. Per-project skill links are a convenience; the server must boot regardless.

## Tests

`tests/test_skill_links.py`: link create/remove round-trip + idempotency/retarget, and the boot-safety regression (one unlinkable skill doesn't abort the full reconcile). Green on macOS CI (exercises the symlink path).
