author: jchris
body:
Adds a **Side Meetings** tab to the IETF 126 picker, fed by the community side-meetings board at sidemeetings.ietf.org — which the datatracker agenda doesn't cover.

## Data path (the interesting part)

The board's `/_data` endpoint has **no CORS headers**, so the app can't fetch it from the iframe — and the board also **403s the platform's worker egress** (IP/ASN-level; browser headers don't help — verified live on `qa/ietf-picker`, same class as DEF CON's `info.defcon.org`). So this adopts the DEF CON db-snapshot pattern:

- an owner-side refresher (vibes.diy repo: `scripts/vibe-ops/refresh-ietf-side-meetings.mjs`) writes the raw `/_data` JSON into the `ietf126` db as owner-gated `side-snapshot` chunk docs (it refuses to overwrite if the board flips to meeting 127 or serves zero bookings)
- the backend's 1-minute scheduled tick assembles a COMPLETE chunk set into module state
- `GET /_api/side-meetings` serves it (direct upstream fetch kept as the fast path in case the block lifts)

## App integration

- Bookings flatten into the standard event shape with `side-<booking id>` eventIds (prefixed — booking ids and datatracker `session_id`s are both bare numbers), so side meetings are **first-class everywhere downstream**: hearts, notes, My Faves, Right Now / Up Next, the friends schedule, super-mode counts.
- The ics subscription lane splits a user's picks and joins `side-*` ids against the snapshot, so favorited side meetings reach subscribed calendars; either upstream failing 502s the refresh rather than serving a calendar that clients would treat as deletions.
- New `SideMeetingsView`: day-grouped cards with the teal SIDE lane chip, organizer-tagged area chips, room + organizer, description, and the remote-participation (webex) link when the organizer provided one.
- `access.js`: `side-snapshot` writes are owner-only (creates AND updates), so ordinary signed-in users can't poison the served board.

Tests: 75 → 97 (flattener, proxy + snapshot assembly + poisoning defense, subscription join, access rules).

Validated on `qa/ietf-picker`: full loop refresher → chunk docs → tick assembly → proxy 200 (37 bookings) → rendered lane.

author: oveddan
body:
The agent-comprehension layer: a **hash-keyed semantic catalog** of what patterns/effects *do*, so an external MCP-connected agent can understand components without reading source every session — with staleness mechanically detectable when the code changes.

Design principle: structural truth (parameter names/ranges/options) stays live via `get_parameter` / `list_available_*` and can never drift; the catalog covers **behavior only**, and every entry is a *cache of source understanding* keyed by content hashes — never hand-maintained.

## What's here

- **[`docs/catalog-format.md`](../blob/pr-7a-semantic-catalog/docs/catalog-format.md)** — the contract: one markdown file per class (FQCN filename) under `package/src/main/resources/catalog/`; flat frontmatter carrying `sourceSha256` (the generator's incremental key) and `classBytesSha256` (the runtime staleness key); three fixed sections (Summary / Parameter interactions / Usage tips). Three-tier runtime resolution — `~/.lx-mcp/catalog/` overlay → **the class's own jar** → the lx-mcp jar — so a drop-in content jar (e.g. Apotheneum) can ship its own docs and arrive documented.
- **`.claude/skills/lx-mcp-catalog/`** — the generation skill: portable `sources.json` (git URLs + maven coordinates; machine paths in git-ignored `sources.local.json`), live-or-offline class discovery, skip-if-source-hash-unchanged incrementality, Sonnet summarizers, bytecode hashes from the pinned artifact.
- **24 generated entries** — all 10 stock LX patterns + all 14 effects.
- **Dev-loop integration** — catalog freshness is now a standing step in `/lx-mcp-loop`: the incremental pass runs every iteration (hash no-op when clean), so staleness is fixed at the PR that caused it.

## Quality process

An adversarial review of the first generation pass found a **~50% factual-error rate** (6 sampled, 3 wrong — including a confidently stated wrong transform order). Response: the content rules were tightened (every mechanism claim source-verified; never reference nonexistent parameters), and **all 24 entries were then fact-checked line-by-line against LX source** — 9 corrections total (DynamicsEffect pipeline order, ChasePattern/SparkleEffect nonexistent parameters, NoisePattern inverted scale, SoundObjectEffect invented mode, PatternRack buffer semantics, GateEffect level-vs-time, TransparifyEffect inverted threshold, BlurEffect half-life wording, ColorizeEffect alpha semantics). All 48 hashes verified mechanically against the LX checkout and the pinned `lx-1.2.1.jar`.

## Verification

- Mechanical validation: all 24 entries pass the format check (frontmatter keys, FQCN=filename, 64-hex hashes, section headings) — this check becomes `CatalogFormatTest` inside `mvn package` in PR-7b.
- `mvn package` green (no Java changes in this slice).
- Re-running the skill on the unchanged tree skips all 24 as fresh (the incremental key works).

PR-7b (stacked): `get_component_doc` tool + bytecode-hash staleness at runtime. PR-7c: modulators + Apotheneum batches.

## What & why

Replaces the legacy pre-Aurora `TemplatePickerView` sheet (opened from the Trackers **"New"** button and the Home empty-state **"Add tracker"**) with the designed **2-step full-screen Aurora wizard** per `ios/specs/views/add-tracker.md` (PR 2 of the receivers→add-tracker management-loop pass). No backend work — `GET /tracker-templates` + `createTracker` already exist.

## Flow

**Step 1 — Choose template:** 2-col `StrideTemplateCard` gallery from `GET /tracker-templates` (hue icon + raw `kind` badge) + a **Custom** card (visible; "coming soon" — blank-config deferred per decision 5).
**Step 2 — Configure:** pre-filled **name**, Aurora **color swatch** picker, **read-only field rows**, and an editable **ALERT min/max row for every `number` field**, then Create → `createTracker` against the active receiver.

body:
## Summary

PR 3 of the React Flow migration (stacked on #99). The canvas becomes a full authoring surface.

- **Drag-to-connect**: connection handles appear on node hover (editable canvases only). Drops are hit-tested against node rects in flow coordinates — React Flow's own drop detection uses `document.elementFromPoint`, which can't see into the shadow root — so dropping anywhere on a node body connects. The gateway-routing invariant holds by construction: state→state connections route through the source's Split gateway (created on demand via `findOrCreateSplitGateway`), state routes may target gateways directly, gateway routes target anything. Duplicates are announced and skipped; the inspector opens on the new route. `autoPanOnConnect` is off so the canvas never slides out from under a drop.
- **Shift-marquee multi-select** (partial-intersection): group drags commit as one undoable update; selection renders as a dashed outline, distinct from the semantic single selection which stays on the inner buttons.
- **Subgraph copy/paste**: a marquee selection copies through the editor's existing clipboard as a subgraph — stages and gateways get fresh unique keys, routes internal to the copied set are remapped to the copies, external targets are kept, pasted nodes land offset from their sources. One paste, one undo entry.
- **MiniMap** (pannable/zoomable, bottom-right) and **animated simulation-path edges**.
- **Stability hardening** found along the way: the wrapper reuses array references in prop snapshots when contents are unchanged (the editor maps simulation arrays inline every render, which otherwise loops the host render via React Flow's fresh-array `onSelectionChange` reporting), and local node reseeds carry the RF selection across so host re-renders don't dissolve a marquee.

## Tests

- New `workflow-canvas-connect.spec.ts`: stage→gateway connect + inspector, stage→stage auto-Split creation, read-only handle absence, marquee copy/paste/undo ✅
- Full suites: Playwright **167 passed / 0 failed**, Storybook **56 passed**, `dotnet test` **865 passed** ✅

body:
`govulncheck` went red on `main` (and on the #178 PR): **GO-2026-5856** — an Encrypted Client Hello privacy leak in `crypto/tls` — is reachable through Helena's WebSocket/TLS paths (`internal/websocket`, `internal/httpclient`) and is fixed in the standard library at **go1.26.5**.

This is unrelated to #178's docs; the advisory just dropped against the pinned go1.26.4 toolchain.

## Fix
Bump the pinned `toolchain` directive in `go.mod` from `go1.26.4` → `go1.26.5` (the `go 1.26` language directive is unchanged). CI's `setup-go` reads this via `go-version-file: go.mod` under `GOTOOLCHAIN: local`, so the vuln/build/test jobs pick up 1.26.5. No source changes.

## Verified locally under go1.26.5
- `govulncheck ./...` → **No vulnerabilities found** (was exit 3 on GO-2026-5856)
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and the non-UI test suite all pass.

author: danielsaska
body:
A package of UI fixes/improvements, split into these areas.

## Publish to SpeleoDB
- **Description now required** — the server's `Project` model rejects a blank description (`blank=False`), which would 400 the create after the click. Gated in the dialog (`*` markers + inline error) with a matching backend guard in `speleodb_publish`.
- **Add collaborators from the create dialog** — queue `(email, level)` pairs via a shared, debounced, server-backed email typeahead; granted best-effort after the project is linked. Partial-grant failures surface a warning toast (rest can be finished from Project Settings) rather than undoing the publish.
- Hardened the success path: a hiccup in the post-publish `refreshLinkStatus()` no longer misreports a succeeded publish as failed, and queued collaborators are named (not silently dropped) if the reopen fails.

## Progressive top-bar condensation
- **SingleSystemView Toolbar** and the **GlobalView start-screen header** drop labels in a fixed priority order as horizontal space runs out, then tighten padding, and restore everything when space returns:
  - Toolbar: `Display` text → `Import` text → Undo/Redo → tight padding.
  - GlobalView header: `Stalagmight` brand → New/Open labels → Map/List labels.
- Condensed controls keep an accessible name (`aria-label`) and their icon, so nothing clickable disappears.

## Menu + recents polish
- Burger menu: badged SpeleoDB **Open** and **Publish** icons; **hide "Open from SpeleoDB" when signed out**.
- Remote (SpeleoDB) recents are framed as a recoverable **"Delete local copy"** (with a warning that unpushed local edits are lost), distinct from a permanent delete.
- **Removing an already-absent recent is now an idempotent success**, so a stale "missing" row can always be cleared (the frontend only refreshes recents on success).

## Refactor / tests
- Extracts `SpeleoUserAutocomplete` as the shared typeahead (Project Settings + Publish).
- Adds component tests (DeleteProjectDialog `isRemote` framing; collaborator add/remove/change-level) and **Playwright specs for both condensation state machines** (priority-order invariant + expand-back).
- Rebaselines `speleodb.rs` for the file-size ratchet.

## Verification
- `/pre-pr` run (10 adversarial lenses + bundled review); two CI-breakers it caught (a stale test asserting old behavior, the file-size ratchet) are fixed, plus the should-fix/nits.
- Green: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy` (deny-level), `pnpm lint:rust-file-size`, `pnpm tsc --noEmit`, frontend suite (1701 passed), Rust suite (2146 passed; the 2 unrelated failures are environmental — leftover dev-server WebKit processes + a load flake), and both new Playwright specs.

author: qwwiwi
body:
## Что и зачем

Вождь 2026-07-09: убрать confirm-карточки гейта на обычных командах — он всё равно жмёт Allow. Первый подход (снести последние два confirm-детектора `git-exec-surface` + `pipe-interpreter`) **отклонён двойным ревью**: Codex GPT-5.6 Sol дал BLOCK — эти детекторы ловят RCE-через-индирекцию (`curl|sh`, `git -c core.sshCommand=evil`), а silent-allow открыл бы обход lexical deny-спайна. Fable дал SHIP, но пропустил это — цена двойного кросс-family ревью.

Вместо сноса — сделал детектор `git-exec-surface` **точным**: убрал ложные срабатывания, сохранив (и усилив) защиту.

## Ложные срабатывания устранены

`git switch -c`, `git commit -c HEAD`, `git branch -c old new`, `git log -c`, `git show -c HEAD`, `git checkout -b`, git-в-строке рядом с `python3 -c`, `git -C /path`, `git help --config`, `git push -u`, `git add -u` — больше **не** поднимают карточку.

## Защита от RCE усилена (позиционно-независимая value/subcommand модель)

- **короткий `-c`**: config-инъекция = глобальный `-c` с любым значением ЛИБО `-c`/`--config` под `clone` (любой ключ, включая URL-scoped `credential.https://...helper=!id`); после сабкоманды benign (имена веток, даже с `=`)
- **длинные exec-флаги**: `--config-env`, `--upload-pack`/`--receive-pack` (+ префикс-аббревиатуры), `--exec`, `--exec-path=<val>` — position-independent, ловят фрагментацию кавычками (`--receive'-pack'`)
- **git-алиасы**: `-u`/`-u<val>` для fetch-семейства = `--upload-pack`
- **индирекция** (`$`/backtick): flatten + ANSI-C decode + fail-closed маркеры
- **сохранены**: `GIT_SSH_COMMAND=` env-config и `.git/hooks` гарды, весь deny-спайн (secrets, own-channel systemctl, force-push) — не переопределяемы

## Ревью

Двойное ревью Codex GPT-5.6 Sol + Fable. **13 кругов** adversarial-упрочнения — каждый круг Codex находил либо реальную дыру (`git clone -c`, фрагментированный `--receive-pack`, ANSI-C `$'git'`, URL-scoped ключи), либо ложный срабат моего же рефактора (`git help --config`), и то, и другое устранялось. Финальный вердикт: **Codex SHIP, 0 находок**.

- `bun test` (plugin/): **2049 pass / 0 fail** (полный прогон 2221/0)
- `bun run typecheck`: 0 ошибок

## Задокументированный остаток

1-символьные сокращения опций git (`--u`) и глубокая per-subcommand неоднозначность аббревиатур требуют полного парсера `parse-options` git — неразрешимо в эвристике, присутствует в baseline v1.1.0. Эксплойт требует специально обфусцированной инъекции.

author: programmingdrak
body:
## What and why

In the itinerary List view, the "Unfinished" section (past-day tasks never completed, carried onto today) rendered through a bespoke, stripped-down builder `unfinishedRow()`. It lacked the notes button, the reschedule arrow, and the other affordances every normal task row has. This makes those rows render and behave like a normal task, using the same code, so there is no divergent builder to keep in sync.

The Unscheduled section already routes through the shared `row()`; Unfinished was the only outlier. Only the Unfinished section is in scope here.

## Changes

All in `public/js/schedule-tab.js` plus two dead CSS rules in `public/css/dashboard.css`.

- Deleted the bespoke `unfinishedRow()`. Unfinished entries now render through the shared `row(ev, idx, mode, node)` via:
  - `_unfToEv(r)`, a block to ev adapter (a raw past-day block is not a `scheduled[]` task).
  - a new `mode === "unfinished"` branch in `row()`, threaded the same way the existing `isDoneRow` / `isPushedRow` modes are (not draggable, no editable start-time, no quick-complete).
- The three Unfinished-specific behaviors are preserved by overriding just those handlers:
  - complete lands on the origin day via `commitDoneOnDate`.
  - the reschedule arrow opens a true-move date picker (`openTaskRadial` gained an optional `opts.unfinished` that routes to the shared `openDatePickPopover` pick-mode), whose pick runs `blockStore.rescheduleBlock`.
  - drop deletes the source block via `blockStore.deleteBlock`.
- Bounty is intentionally hidden on Unfinished rows: `placeBounty` only applies to today's scheduled tasks, and an Unfinished item completes on its origin day, so a bounty could never pay out.
- Removed the now-dead CSS for the old inline Today/Tomorrow/Move carryover controls; kept the shared `.carryover-btn` and `.it-list-unfinished` rules that are still used elsewhere.

## Test plan

Verified end to end in a local browser (headless), logged in, with a synthetic Unfinished entry rendered through the new path:

- Row renders with notes button, reschedule arrow, delete, the amber bar, and the "Unfinished from <date>" chip; and correctly has no bounty button, no carryover buttons, no quick-complete, is not draggable, and has no editable start-time.
- The reschedule arrow opens a "Move ... to..." picker (Today / Tomorrow / date + Move), wired to the true-move handler; duration stepper correctly hidden.
- Renders identically to the Unscheduled rows above it.

Local pre-review (the five-lane clever review pipeline) came back clean, zero findings.

## Summary

- Switches \`run_publish\` from \`HfApi.upload_folder\` to \`HfApi.upload_large_folder\` (with a follow-up \`list_repo_refs\` to resolve the head revision, since \`upload_large_folder\` returns None).

Discovered while trying to close #723 (adapters exist but PRHW HF datasets never published). \`loom datasets publish mmlu-pro\` produced HTTP 504 on the commit endpoint every attempt. author: lciacci
body:
Chunk 2's boot was attempted and blocked on EC2 capacity. **$0 spent, no instance ever launched.** Two real bugs surfaced on the way, both fixed here.

## 1. The contention baseline measured nothing

`fan_out` queries models **one at a time**, so every `latency_s` is a *solo* latency. `baseline()` then compared `sum(solo)` to `max(solo)` and called the ratio a co-residency tax. That is an arithmetic identity — it lands near +150% for any three models regardless of what the GPU does. Nothing ever ran concurrently.

The docstring even asserted the conclusion as a premise ("parallel client threads would not buy real parallelism on one GPU"), which is exactly the claim Chunk 2 exists to test. As written, the boot could not have falsified it.

Adds `fan_out_parallel` (`ThreadPoolExecutor`; blocking `urllib` releases the GIL) and rewrites `baseline()` to run a solo pass then a real concurrent pass:

```
contention_tax = (parallel_wall - max_solo) / max_solo
```

- `~0%` → the L40S timeshares fine, **Chunk 4 multi-GPU is not justified** (~$8-15/measure saved)
- `~+100%` → co-residents serialize, **multi-GPU is justified**

Either answer is worth the boot. `demo()` now asserts the threads actually overlap, so a fan-out that silently serializes fails the offline self-check. The old "+40% over ideal-parallel" datapoint carries the original defect and is discarded.

## 2. EC2 capacity errors stall instead of failing

`InsufficientInstanceCapacity` comes back as **HTTP 500**. The AWS SDK retryer treats 500 as retryable and retries silently, and `timeouts { create = "3m" }` does **not** bound that loop — an apply sat in `Still creating...` for **26 minutes**. The error never reaches normal terraform output.

`gpu.tf` carried a comment claiming that timeout made it fail fast, and `design.md` recorded the same as a v1 lesson. Both were wrong; corrected in place. The working recipe is `TF_LOG=DEBUG` + `grep InsufficientInstanceCapacity` + an external wall-clock guard, which fails a dry AZ in ~20s.

Also documented:
- A cancelled `RunInstances` returns `context canceled` — AWS may have launched a box you never saw. **Orphan-check after every kill.** (Done here; nothing orphaned.)
- g6e.xlarge on-demand was dry in **all four** us-east-1 AZs. AWS's "you can currently get capacity by choosing us-east-1b/1c/1d" error text is generic boilerplate, not a live capacity read — all three were dry.
- G+VT quota is **8 vCPU, on-demand and spot alike**, so `g6e.2xlarge` (same single L40S 48GB, `mem_util` values unchanged) is the only fallback; `g6e.4xlarge` fails `VcpuLimitExceeded`. Spot saves nothing ($1.50-1.85/hr vs ~$1.86 on-demand).

Plus a stale-doc fix: HANDOFF still described the pre-Chunk-1 per-slice `mem_util` scheme (0.36/0.26/0.24) that `variables.tf` replaced with cumulative 0.25/0.55/0.82.

## Verification

`python3 orchestrator/ensemble.py` passes (offline, no GPU), including the new overlap assert. `terraform validate` + `terraform fmt -check` clean. The contention tax itself is **still unmeasured** — that needs the boot.

## Next

Retry Chunk 2's boot; if g6e.xlarge is still dry, `-var gpu_instance_type=g6e.2xlarge`. Harness is boot-and-run.

author: haasonsaas
body: ## Summary PR #96 (GH-64) minted worker-scoped guest tokens and enforced them on guest-facing routes, but the Kubernetes provider never delivered a token into the sandbox pod at all -- the delivery half of GH-64, called out explicitly in that PR's "Deviations from the task's spec" note. This wires it up, following the design the issue sketched: - **Mounted as a read-only Secret file, not an env var or argv.** Mirrors `ssh_authorized_keys_secret`/`vnc_password_secret` (PR #99): `SANDBOXWICH_API_TOKEN_FILE` points at `/run/sandboxwich/token/api-token`, a Secret volume mount. The raw token never appears in the pod spec/status, so it can't leak via `kubectl get pod -o yaml`, `kubectl describe pod`, or `/proc/1/environ`. `SANDBOXWICH_WORKER_ID` travels as a plain env var since it's an identifier, not a credential. - **The worker synthesizes and applies its own per-sandbox Secret**, unlike `ssh_authorized_keys_secret`/`vnc_password_secret` which reference operator-managed secrets assumed to already exist. The worker token is minted fresh at registration (GH-64) and can't be pre-provisioned, so `KubernetesDryRunProvider::worker_token_secret_manifest` renders it and `KubernetesApplyProvider::provision_manifests`/`fork_manifests` apply it alongside the PVC/Pod/Service/NetworkPolicy manifests, ahead of the Pod that mounts it. - **Teardown and RBAC**: `SANDBOX_TEARDOWN_RESOURCE_KINDS` now includes `secret`, so the per-sandbox Secret is cleaned up by the same label-scoped `kubectl delete` that already tears down the pod/PVC/services/network policy -- no separate lifecycle tracking needed. The worker's RBAC `Role` in `deploy/kubernetes/worker.yaml` gains `secrets` access, scoped to the sandbox namespace only (same blast-radius boundary as pods/services/PVCs). - **`sandboxwich-agent` reads the token from the mounted file, with env-var fallback.** New `--api-token-file`/`SANDBOXWICH_API_TOKEN_FILE` flag on `heartbeat`/`daemon`/`exec`; `resolve_api_token` prefers the file's contents over `--api-token`/`SANDBOXWICH_API_TOKEN`, which remains the path for non-Kubernetes deployments with no mounted file. - No new database migration, no new `RuntimeResourceKind` variant, no server-side API changes -- the token-minting/enforcement side (GH-64) already existed; this only wires the existing worker-scoped token into pod provisioning, matching the issue's scope. ## Design notes - `KubernetesDryRunProvider::with_worker_credentials(worker_id, worker_token)` stores `(worker_id, token)` only when `worker_token` is non-empty; a `None`/blank token means no wiring at all (not a fallback to a tenant-wide token). - Threaded `worker_id`/`worker_token` down through `runtime_provider_from_args`/`work_loop` in `sandboxwich-worker/src/main.rs`. For `run`, the freshly-minted worker token from registration is used. For direct `work-once`/`work-loop` invocation, `cli.api_token` is already the worker-scoped token per the existing doc comment on `Cli::api_token`. - Extracted `KubernetesApplyProvider::fork_manifests` (mirroring the existing `provision_manifests`) so both are independently unit-testable without shelling out to a real `kubectl`. ## Test plan - [x] `cargo fmt --check` - [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` - [x] `cargo test --workspace` (134 tests passing across all crates) - New tests in `sandboxwich-worker`: token mounted as a read-only file (not env var, not on argv, not in the serialized pod manifest at all); `workerTokenSecret` manifest content/labels; no wiring when credentials aren't configured; clearing credentials via a blank token; fork's child pod gets its own secret scoped to the child sandbox id; apply-mode `provision_manifests`/`fork_manifests` include the Secret ahead of the Pod; `secret` present in `SANDBOX_TEARDOWN_RESOURCE_KINDS`. - New tests in `sandboxwich-agent`: `resolve_api_token` prefers the file over the CLI token, errors (not silently falls back) on an empty or unreadable file, and passes through the CLI token when no file is configured. Closes #101 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

author: lionsr
body:
## Mathematical correction

The theorem proposed in #2537 is false under the stated horizontal canonical-form hypotheses. On bond space C^2, take

A^(a,b) = c_a E_ab,    c_0 = 3/5,    c_1 = 4/5.

The four doubled-index matrices span M_2(C), satisfy the left-canonical identity, and form a one-block horizontal canonical-form datum with finite-length block separation. Their diagonal restriction consists only of (3/5)E_00 and (4/5)E_11. Every word in the restricted tensor is diagonal, so no blocking length spans the full matrix algebra.

This does not contradict Proposition 4.13. The source uses MPDO positivity and Lemma L to construct an independent canonical form in the vertical direction; it does not obtain the vertical normal tensors by restricting the horizontal blocks to diagonal physical pairs.

Source: Cirac–Pérez-García–Schuch–Verstraete, arXiv:1606.00608, Proposition 4.13, source label `Prop:IV.12`, lines 1863–1921.

## Changes

- formalize the matrix-unit counterexample and the failure of normality at every blocking length;
- expose only the capstone theorem as public API, keeping the proof scaffolding private;
- correct the Chapter 21 proof sketch to follow the source order;
- add a paper-gap note separating the false diagonal-restriction route from the genuine positivity-based vertical decomposition.

## Verification

- targeted build of the counterexample module
- direct check of the BiCF derivation aggregate and `TNLean.lean`
- `leanblueprint checkdecls`
- blueprint declaration synchronization
- blueprint PDF build and visual inspection of Chapter 21
- reader-facing prose, line-length, and proof-integrity checks

Closes #2537.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Mathematical correction and documentation with a self-contained obstruction proof; no changes to auth, runtime, or critical infrastructure paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> Refutes the claim that **horizontal canonical-form data** forces **normality** of diagonally restricted blocks. A new Lean module proves `horizontalCFData_diagBlock_not_isNormal`: a **C²** matrix-unit tensor with coefficients **3/5** and **4/5** is injective, left-canonical, and satisfies finite block separation, yet `diagBlock` stays diagonal at every blocking length and cannot span off-diagonal directions.
> 
> **`VerticalCF.lean`** and the blueprint are updated so Proposition **4.13** is described as building an **independent vertical** canonical form via MPDO positivity (arXiv:1606.00608, lines 1873–1921), not by restricting horizontal blocks to **(i,i)**. Chapter 20 adds theorem **`thm:diagonal_restriction_not_normal`** and revises the horizontal→vertical proof sketch accordingly. A **`docs/paper-gaps`** note records the false diagonal-BNT route versus the genuine positivity-based decomposition.

author: joeytroy
body:
## Problem

The DKMS **package** version is pinned at `0.1.0` in `dkms.conf` — the driver version lives in `VERSION` (currently `9.3.3.00291`). Because the package version never changes between driver updates, re-running `./install-dkms.sh` on a machine that already has `rcraid/0.1.0` registered silently left the **old** module installed:

- `dkms add` errored with *"DKMS tree already contains: rcraid-0.1.0"* — but the error was masked because output is piped through `sed` and the script ran without `pipefail`.
- `dkms build` and `dkms install` saw `0.1.0` already built/installed for the kernel and skipped.

Net effect: the script printed "Install complete" while the previously installed binary stayed in place. Upgrading to the 9.3.3.00291 build (#37) required a manual `dkms install --force`, which is how this was discovered.

## Fix

- **Skip `dkms add`** when the package is already registered (checked by capturing `dkms status` output — see note below).
- **`--force` on `dkms build` and `dkms install`** so the freshly staged sources always replace what's there; a no-op cost on first install.
- **`set -euo pipefail`** in both `install-dkms.sh` and `uninstall-dkms.sh`, so a real dkms failure aborts the script instead of being swallowed by the `| sed` prettifier.
- The registration check deliberately avoids `dkms status | grep -q`: under `pipefail`, `grep -q` exits at the first match, `dkms` catches SIGPIPE, and the pipeline spuriously reports failure (reproduced during verification). Same reason the `lsmod | grep` checks became `grep /proc/modules`.
- Banner now prints `driver 9.3.3.00291, dkms package rcraid-0.1.0` so the frozen package version doesn't read as the driver version.
- If rcraid is currently loaded, the completion message notes the new module (and regenerated initramfs) only take effect after reboot.

## Verification

Ran on the dev box in the exact upgrade scenario (rcraid/0.1.0 registered for two kernels, module loaded, root filesystem on rcraid0):

- `==> dkms add (skipped — rcraid/0.1.0 already registered)`
- Forced rebuild + MOK signing, then reinstall replaced `/lib/modules/6.17.0-35-generic/updates/dkms/rcraid.ko.zst` — `modinfo` shows the working-tree `build_rev` (`3343da9-dirty`), proving the staged sources won.
- initramfs regenerated via `update-initramfs -u`; loaded-module reboot note printed.
- First run also caught the grep-SIGPIPE false negative live (script aborted loudly at `dkms add` instead of silently succeeding — pipefail working as intended), which led to the capture-based check.

author: digibrander
body:
## Summary

This PR was scoped from `docs/billing/2026-07-02-invoicing-implementation-plan-v2.md` (invoicing/tax plan) and `docs/billing/billing-system-overview.html` (billing/discounts/seats review). Both docs turned out to be stale — nearly everything they list as "to build" (seat-billing fix, discount engine, commission snapshotting, code guards, the GST tax-invoicing system) had already shipped on `development` before this branch started. Verified that against the live code before touching anything.

What was actually missing, found by (1) re-verifying the two docs against the current codebase and (2) a follow-up adversarial correctness review of the core financial paths (tax engine, credit ledger/refunds, discount/seat billing, webhook idempotency):

### 1. Audit-log gap (from the review doc)
Affiliate commission/discount split changes were only logged via `logger`, not written to `audit_logs` — no durable "who, when, old → new" trail for money-moving edits. Wired `record_audit()` into code create/update (self-service) and superadmin invite/update/delete on the affiliate.

### 2. Stale documentation
`billing-system-overview.html` described the seat-billing bug, discount engine, and an international-payments plan as open work. All three were already resolved or superseded (Stripe was built then deliberately removed on `development` in favor of a Razorpay-only + contact-sales architecture). Corrected the doc so it no longer describes fixed bugs as open, or a removed integration as a build target.

### 3–6. Four financial-correctness bugs (adversarial review, not in either source doc)
- **Seat add-on orphaned on cancel/upgrade/downgrade** — the operator-seat add-on is a separate Razorpay subscription; nothing cancelled it when its parent subscription was cancelled or superseded, so it kept billing ₹499/seat/month forever. Now cancelled alongside its parent and carried forward onto any replacement subscription.
- **Refund clawback could hit the wrong month** — a subscription's first-period credit grant is made before any invoice exists and never gets linked to one; a chargeback landing on that (long-expired) first invoice fell back to "most recent grant in scope" and could wipe out a later, still-in-use month's credits. Now backfilled the moment the invoice shows up.
- **Credit-note over-reversal race** — two independent reversal events for the same invoice (e.g. a partial refund and a concurrently-processed dispute) could each read "already reversed = 0" and both issue a full-amount credit note. Now serialized with a row lock.
- **Cancelled subscriptions could be resurrected** — an out-of-order/redelivered `subscription.charged` or `subscription.activated` webhook could silently un-cancel a subscription and grant it fresh credits. Also hardened the per-period grant marker from exact-equality to monotonic, closing a replay-triggered double-grant via the superadmin dead-letter replay tool.

## Test plan
- [x] All 4 new/changed correctness fixes have dedicated regression tests, each verified to **fail** with the fix reverted and **pass** with it applied (not just "green by construction")
- [x] Full backend suite: `uv run pytest` — **2,234 passed**, 0 failed
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` — clean
- [x] Alembic migrations verified to apply cleanly to a fresh DB (single head)
- [x] No frontend/widget files touched — those checks don't apply

author: robsyme
body:
Closes #7319.

### Problem

The Fusion license-token cache key in `TowerFusionToken.getLicenseToken` was written with **single quotes**:

```groovy
final key = '${product}-${version}'
```

In Groovy a single-quoted literal is not interpolated, so `key` was always the constant string `${product}-${version}`, identical for every call. All `(product, version)` pairs collided on one Guava cache entry, so the first token cached was returned for any subsequent product/version, and the cached error response was shared the same way. The outgoing request was built correctly; only the cache key was wrong.

It is currently latent because `product`/`version` are constant within a run, but it defeats the intended per-product/version caching and would misfire if a second product or version were ever requested in the same session.

### Fix

Use a double-quoted GString so the value interpolates, typed as `String` so it still satisfies the `Cache<String, ...>` key type under `@CompileStatic`:

```groovy
final String key = "${product}-${version}"
```

### Test

Added `should cache license tokens per product and version` to `TowerFusionEnvTest`, using the existing WireMock harness to return a distinct token per product. It requests two products and asserts each receives its own token and both reach the endpoint. The test fails on the old key (the second product gets the first's cached token) and passes with the fix.

`./gradlew :plugins:nf-seqera:test --tests "*TowerFusionEnvTest"` → 14 passed, 0 failed.

body:
## What

The **fourth M7 player-UI slice**: THE SYSTEM's in-fiction **broadcast feed** at `/play/campaigns/[id]/system`. This realizes the "System messages / notifications" bullet on the player surface (`docs/10-ui-ux.md`).

A System message is just a `SYSTEM_MESSAGE` entity, so **no schema change** — the feed is a new read projection over that type.

## Design decisions

- **Campaign-wide, visibility-projected (not crawler-scoped).** Unlike the crawler sheet/loadout (slices 2–3), every player sees the same feed the DM published. `getSystemMessageFeed` is a plain visibility read: role → `PLAYER_VISIBLE` filter + a belt-and-suspenders `status: CANON` gate (like the Known World), newest broadcast first by `createdAt`. **Invariant #5** made visible again — DM-only and pending messages never leak.
- **No invented "kind."** The mockup's per-message badges (ANNOUNCEMENT / ALERT / PERSONAL / PATCH NOTE) aren't modeled on the entity, so rather than ship a fake classification (AGENTS.md no-filler rule), each card renders the message's real content only — headline + optional summary + Markdown body + date, under a neutral "System broadcast" label. A tier/kind `data.*` field is a plausible future follow-up.

## Changes

- **Service** `src/server/services/system-feed.ts`: `getSystemMessageFeed` + exported `SystemFeedMessage`.
- **UI** `system-feed.tsx` component + `/play/campaigns/[id]/system/page.tsx` (ConsoleScreen + `PlayerSystemBanner`).
- **Nav**: **System Feed** flipped from Planned → a built link with active-highlight.
- **Tests**: DB-backed service (projection + non-member + DM-sees-all), component, page, nav.
- **Docs**: `PROGRESS.md` dated entry + `AGENTS.md` status.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors; pre-existing settings-action warnings only), `npm run build` (route registers).
- Full coverage gate green — **143 files / 1859 tests**; statements 95.37%, branches 88.96%, functions 96.49%, lines 96.96%; `system-feed.ts` fully covered.

author: jakepre
body:
Closes #800.

### Problem
"king of the hill - using an item runs an animation that stops you from moving, which looks weird - allow movement when animations are playing"

The sim never stalls (confirmed — movement input is always processed server-side regardless of the client's animation state). The bug is purely client-side: firing a Shove Blast plays the `interact` flourish and protects it from `update_rig()`'s walk/idle switch for a fixed `SHOVE_HOLD_SEC` (0.6s) window, mirroring `rumble_ring`'s hit/ko `_reaction_hold` idiom. During that window the rig's position still slides to wherever the sim says (via a raw `rig.position =` assignment, bypassing `update_rig()` entirely) — but the walk animation never kicks in, so the character visually looks frozen in the interact pose while sliding across the ground.

### Fix
`update_rig()` (the shared `MinigameView3D` helper) gains an optional `force_animate` param, defaulting to `true` so every existing call site — including `rumble_ring`'s own separate `_reaction_hold` pattern, which is untouched — behaves exactly as before. When a caller passes `false`, the walk/idle switch only yields to a currently-playing one-shot animation *while the player is stationary*; the instant real movement is detected, the walk switch fires regardless of `force_animate`. Position, facing, and interpolation are unaffected either way.

King of the Hill's `_update_players()` now always calls `update_rig()` (no more bypassing it with a raw position assignment), passing `force_animate = not flourishing`. The shove flourish still plays out fully if the player stands still after firing, but can never stall visible movement.

### Tests
Added to `tests/unit/test_king_of_the_hill_view.gd`:
- `test_movement_during_the_shove_flourish_is_not_stalled` — moving mid-flourish switches to walk immediately.
- `test_standing_still_keeps_the_flourish_playing` — the existing (unchanged) stationary-flourish behavior still holds.

The two pre-existing shove-animation tests pass unmodified. `rumble_ring`'s tests (its own reaction-hold pattern, not touched by this PR) also pass unmodified, confirming the new `force_animate` param is fully backward-compatible.

Full local run: 1863/1863 GUT tests pass (no `Failed to load script`/`Ignoring script`), `gdformat --check` + `gdlint` clean on all changed files.

## Test plan

- [x] `gdformat --check` / `gdlint` on changed files

author: fw-bot
body:
# How to reproduce
- Create a new product
- Add a reordering rule to that product with :
	- Trigger : Auto
	- Min : > Forecast
- Activate dev mode
- Go to Seetings > Technical > Automation > Scheduled Actions
- Find the "Procurement: run Scheduler" action & run it manually

# The issue
We get a traceback :
psycopg2.errors.SerializationFailure: could not serialize access due to concurrent update

# Cause
In Odoo, we use an isolation level of "REPEATABLE READ" for transactions :
https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/7c35e183d6cc33a6e5d20e5e97ffef79e03b49d4/odoo/sql_db.py#L373

Even with that isolation level psql can throw a `SerializationFailure` if a transaction
attempts to update a row that was modified by another transaction after the isolation
snapshot was taken.

### Example that will raise an error :

Session 1
```SQL
BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ;
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 1;
```

Session 2
```SQL
BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ;
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 50 WHERE id = 1;
COMMIT;
```

Back to Session 1
```SQL
COMMIT;
```

When running our action, we do this :
https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/dff0835346f30fd1ef77260d94bcceeeab4d9051/addons/stock/models/stock_rule.py#L697-L703

Which correspond exactly to the first example :
We first update some records with their compute

Then `orderpoints.sudo()._procure_orderpoint_confirm(...)` creates a new
transaction, update some rows & commits :
https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/dff0835346f30fd1ef77260d94bcceeeab4d9051/addons/stock/models/stock_orderpoint.py#L716-L719
https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/dff0835346f30fd1ef77260d94bcceeeab4d9051/addons/stock/models/stock_orderpoint.py#L781-L783

Finally, we commit the original transaction with `_commit_progress(1)`

# Proposed solution
Inverse the order of  `_commit_progress(1)` and
`orderpoints.sudo()._procure_orderpoint_confirm(...)` so we commit
the first transaction before starting the second one.

opw-6261675

author: groganz-bot[bot]
body:
Part of the **[Epic - toast-notifications]** epic cinatra-ai/cinatra#1107 (sub-issue S12). Closes #45.

## What a user sees

Before: a failed connect/disconnect (bad token, denied tag scope, rate limit, network error, unconfigured Nango, OAuth dialog failure) showed the SAME error message twice — once as a toast, once as a destructive red banner inline in the setup form.

After: the error shows exactly once, as a toast. The inline banner is gone. Nothing else in the form changed — the token-expiry warning banner and the "disconnecting doesn't revoke the OAuth client" reminder are persistent state, not transient errors, and are untouched.

**Where it appears:** Connectors → Cinatra Ai → Tailscale Connector → Setup (`/connectors/cinatra-ai/tailscale-connector/setup`).

## What changed

- Deleted the dead `friendlyError` state + its destructive `<Alert>` render block from `src/tailscale-connect-form.tsx` — every error path already called `useNotify().addNotification(...)` in parallel, so the banner was pure duplication.
- Two branches previously **only** set `friendlyError` with no toast at all (the Nango Connect-UI `onEvent` "error" case, and the outer `catch` when the OAuth dialog fails to open) — deleting the banner without touching those would have made those two outcomes surface **nowhere**. Both now call `addNotification` so every failure still surfaces exactly once, per the epic's acceptance rule ("error outcomes surface exactly once — as toasts").
- No new toast machinery needed here: this connector already used `@cinatra-ai/sdk-ui`'s `useNotify()` (flyout-backed toasts), unlike the server-component + flash-param pages the epic's `cinatraToast`/`SearchParamToast` island (#1186) targets. Confirmed against the epic body and #1186's merged diff before starting — S12 is dedup-only, not a flash-protocol migration.

## Tests

Added `src/__tests__/tailscale-connect-form-toast-dedup.test.ts` (5 cases). This repo's vitest is node-environment only, and `@cinatra-ai/sdk-ui` (the host of `useNotify`) is a host-internal peer that isn't installable outside the cinatra monorepo (`pnpm install` here 404s on `@cinatra-ai/sdk-ui`) — so a DOM/render test of this specific component isn't runnable from this repo (documented precedent: `tailscale-error-copy.test.ts`). The added tests instead lock in the structural invariants a DOM test would otherwise cover, at the source level:
- no `friendlyError` state/markup remains
- the persistent alerts (`expiryNotice`, the OAuth-disconnect reminder) are untouched
- every `!x.ok` failure branch still calls `addNotification`
- the two previously-silent branches (OAuth event error, dialog-open catch) now call `addNotification`

Ran via the cinatra monorepo's vitest binary against this connector (symlinked in as a workspace package) — all 5 pass; the two pre-existing suites that need `server-only` (`tailscale-connect.test.ts`, `tailscale-oauth.test.ts`) fail the same way standalone as before this change (unrelated, pre-existing).

## Real dev-boot verification

Brought up a real cinatra dev instance (isolated worktree, its own Postgres/Redis, `pnpm dev`) with this fixed connector wired in as the live `@cinatra-ai/tailscale-connector` workspace package (confirmed in the boot log: `tailscale-connector:registered`), signed up the first admin, and rendered the live setup page — screenshot below is the actual running app, not a fixture.

![Tailscale setup page, light mode, real dev boot](https://github.com/cinatra-ai/tailscale-connector/blob/toast-s12-dedup-inline-banner-evidence/screenshots/02-tailscale-setup-light.png?raw=true)

**Screenshot gap (environmental, not a code concern):** the shared build machine this session ran on was under sustained heavy contention for its whole ~45-minute window — load average 15–36 throughout, ~23/24 GB RAM in use, 10+ concurrent `next-server` processes from other epic sub-issue lanes (S1/S2/S3/toast-s1/toast-s2 etc. all doing similar dev boots at the same time). The dev server was killed (silent, consistent with OOM) within 2–30 seconds on ~25 of ~30 boot attempts. I got exactly one clean render through before the next kill — the disconnected/default state above (light mode) — but not the matching dark-mode render, nor the error-toast-in-flight state (I got as far as triggering the save action with a fake token and watching the button read "Connecting…" before the server died mid-request). The code fix itself is small, mechanical, and codex-reviewed (see below); the remaining screenshot coverage is a capture-environment gap, not an open question about the diff.

## Codex convergence

Ran an inline `codex exec --sandbox read-only` review of the diff (model per `~/.codex/config.toml` at run time). Verdict: **MERGE-SAFE** — confirmed all six error paths still notify (four pre-existing, two newly added), no new silent failure path, persistent alerts untouched, diff minimal.

## Not in scope

- Merging (design-surface change — routed to the coordinator, never self-merged).
- Any new toast plumbing — this connector was already on `useNotify()`.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR implements architectural isolation for the formal verification pipeline and eliminates logical gaps within the Trusted Computing Base (TCB) by completing the remaining FFI-layer proofs.

### Rationale & Key Decisions

The primary motivation for these changes was a recurring failure in the audit system. Previously, the auditor attempted to build the entire project environment, which included heavy UI-related dependencies (like `ProofWidgets`) that were prone to cache desynchronization and build failures. Since these dependencies are not required for the core mathematical proofs, I have decoupled the build process to ensure the auditor only targets the essential logic.

Furthermore, several "placeholder" assumptions (marked with `sorry`) existed in the bridge between Rust and Lean. To achieve full mathematical certainty, these have been replaced with formal proofs, specifically targeting U256 subtype properties and fixed-point scaling conservatism.

### Detailed Changes

#### 1. Architectural Isolation & Build Optimization
- **`lakefile.lean`**: Removed the `@[default_target]` attribute from the `UALBF` library. This prevents `lake env` commands from cascading into non-essential targets like Mathlib UI components.
- **`Makefile`**: Updated the `lean` target to explicitly invoke `lake build UALBF`. This establishes a strict compilation boundary, ensuring only the core library and its direct imports are processed.
- **`auditor.py`**: Refactored the tool to perform an isolated build of the `UALBF` target before validating axioms. This prevents the auditor from timing out or failing due to unrelated external dependency issues.

#### 2. Formal Proof Completion (Removal of `sorry` tags)
- **`UALBF/FFI.lean`**: Resolved a hidden edge case where Lean 4's macro generation for `by decide` was silently falling back to a `sorry` definition in the `U256.mk` initializer. I replaced the tactic with `by omega` to provide a native, definitive proof of the `n < 2^256` bounds.
- **Scaling Conservatism**: Formally verified `UALBF.Fixed64.scaleBoundCeil_conservative`. This bridges the gap between Rust’s rational bounds scaling and the Lean model, ensuring that fixed-point operations are mathematically sound.

### Success Metrics
- **Zero "sorry" tags**: All FFI and core proof layers are now fully verified.
- **Audit Stability**: The auditor tool now achieves a 100% success rate across all 12 core theorems in a clean environment.
- **Reduced TCB**: By isolating the build, we have effectively removed UI-heavy libraries from the Trusted Computing Base of the audit process.

author: matheusschmitz
body:
Fixes #9800

## What

Switches the four TunerStudio pin-selection defines in `tunerstudio.template.ini` (`output_pin_e_list`, `switch_input_pin_e_list`, `brain_input_pin_e_list`, `adc_channel_e_list`) from the positional `@@X_fullenum@@` form to the key-value `@@X_enum@@` form already generated by `PinoutLogic.enumToOptionsList()`: dropdown options come out sorted by pin name and the `INVALID` placeholder entries are omitted.

Example from a generated ini (was a positional list padded with `"INVALID"`):

```
#define output_pin_e_list=0="NONE",30="DIR",25="ENABLE",29="Ignition 1",...
```

Stored tune values remain the same enum ordinals, so existing tunes keep their pin selections. Boards without a pinout yaml (or without pins of a given class) keep the positional fallback from `rusefi_config.txt`, where `_enum` and `_fullenum` are identical.

## Console parser support

The java_console ini parser expanded `$define` references positionally (index = ordinal), which would mis-map the new key-value form, so this PR also teaches it the new shape:

- `EnumIniField.EnumKeyValueMap`: a `$define` reference may now hold key-value pairs (alternating ordinal/label tokens as produced by tokenizing `#define x=0="NONE",10="Pin"`), not only a positional label list.
- `ConfigurationImageGetterSetter`: reading an enum ordinal used to bound-check against the entry count, which breaks for sparse lists (e.g. pin ordinal 47 in a 23-entry map). It now renders `"INVALID"` for ordinals falling in a gap (same string the old positional form displayed) and still throws `OrdinalOutOfRangeException` for ordinals beyond the highest known entry.

All `$`-referenced defines in generated inis were audited: only the four pin lists switch to the key-value form; everything else (`gpio_list`, `pin_mode_e_enum`, `gppwm_channel_e_enum`, etc.) stays positional and keeps taking the positional path. TunerStudio already accepts the sparse key-value format for `bits` fields (`engineType` uses it inline).

## Testing

- Regenerated a board config with a pinout yaml and verified the resulting ini defines.
- New unit tests for key-value `$define` expansion (`IniEnumDecoderTest`, `IniFileFieldsTest`) and for sparse-map ordinal reads (`ConfigurationImageGetterSetterTest`).
- `:inifile:test` and `:ecu_io:test` suites pass.

author: bfollington
body: ## Why A production capture of a Mobile Loom boot (25MB, 82s, ~180ms RTT; forensics in the loom repo, `docs/development/projects/mobile-loom-production-performance/findings.md`) showed a ~3k-item derived jump-search list weighing **~1.33MB per copy, re-materialized once per consuming pattern instance** — 58% of the boot payload — plus 140s of cumulative slow client-side `get()` warnings (median 65ms) re-reading unchanged docs. Before assigning blame between the runtime and that usage, this bench measures the runtime's **native dynamics for the shape in isolation**: a flat list of many similar shallow `{name, ref}`-ish items, the way any index/autocomplete list looks. ## What it measures One new bench file, `packages/runner/test/cell-set-flat-index-list.bench.ts`, env-parameterized (`FLAT_INDEX_LIST_SIZES`, default 100/1000/3000), using `tx.journal.novelty()` for stored-bytes/docs accounting printed outside the timed windows: 1. **Write**: one `cell.set(array)` vs one `Writable.for().set()` per item — time, documents created, stored bytes vs raw JSON 2. **Read**: first `get()`, repeated `get()` ×100 on an unchanged doc, `get()` ×100 through a JSON schema (the validateAndTransform path) 3. **Update**: whole-array re-set with ONE item changed vs targeted `key(i).set` — bytes/docs written per transaction (history growth) ## Results (M-series MacBook, emulated loopback storage) ### 1. `cell.set()` of a flat object array creates one document PER ITEM | N | docs created | stored bytes | raw JSON | overhead | per item | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 100 | **101** | 70.3KB | 31.0KB | 2.27× | 703B | | 1000 | **1001** | 717KB | 317KB | 2.26× | 717B | | 3000 | **3001** | 2.18MB | 967KB | 2.26× | 728B | "One flat array in one doc" does not exist for object arrays — every element becomes its own document (per-item `Writable` docs are the same count at 2.8× overhead). Downstream consequence: any watch/query over the list is N per-doc server materializations, and any client traversal is N doc hops. ### 2. Schema-path reads: linear, but ~19µs/item **per read**, no memoization | N | first get() | repeated get() ×100 | schema get() ×100 | schema per-read | |---|---|---|---|---| | 100 | 164µs | 3.3ms | 165ms | **1.7ms** | | 1000 | 554µs | 28.1ms | 1.8s | **18ms** | | 3000 | 2.3ms | 90.1ms | 5.7s | **57ms** | Good news: not superlinear. Bad news: the constant is brutal and **every read re-pays it in full on an unchanged document** — the schema path is ~63× the schemaless path. 57ms/read at N=3000 matches the production capture's median 65ms slow-`get()` on a ~5.6k-entry space almost exactly; production logged 1,876 re-reads of one unchanged doc = the observed 140s of client CPU. ### 3. Update profiles: regenerate-from-scratch rewrites everything; read-modify-write is cheap Three writer profiles for "one item changed" (per-tx averages over 20 txs; accounting outside the timed window): | N | REGENERATE from scratch | READ-MODIFY-WRITE | targeted `key(i).set` | |---|---|---|---| | 100 | 27ms · 61.6KB · 101 docs | 6.9ms · **685B · 2 docs** | 1.6ms · 246B · 1 doc | | 1000 | 445ms · 629KB · 1001 docs | 85ms · **685B · 2 docs** | 16ms · 246B · 1 doc | | 3000 | **2.15s · 1.92MB · 3001 docs** | 220ms · **685B · 2 docs** | 41ms · 246B · 1 doc | Per review (@seefeldb): the original "whole-set" finding modeled a **regenerate-from-scratch** writer — fresh objects carry no doc identity, so every element re-mints. The idiomatic **read-modify-write** edit (get → replace one element → set back) reuses doc identity from the `get()` and lands as a flat 2-doc/~685B change at any N; writing back an unchanged array is a perfect no-op (0 docs). The full-rewrite cost applies specifically to derivation-style writers that rebuild lists from scratch — which is what our production index refresh does. Also pinned in this PR (`patterns-lift.test.ts`): a lifted array-of-objects **result** is stored inline as ONE doc (raw write path) — derived output does not go through the editable-array decomposition. ## Interpretation - The runtime is **efficient at targeted updates** (246B/tx regardless of N) — the primitives for cheap list maintenance exist. - The pathological costs come from (a) the **doc-per-element explosion** on plain `cell.set`, (b) the **unmemoized schema-read path**, and (c) **wholesale re-sets** — which is exactly how derived/lifted lists get refreshed in practice. - Production compounds this by materializing the same derived list **once per consuming pattern instance** (10 copies in the capture). That part is usage/framework layering, not this bench's subject — but it multiplies every number above. ## Test plan - `deno task bench` filtered to the new file; full matrix run attached above. - `deno fmt` / `deno lint` clean. - Env knobs verified (`FLAT_INDEX_LIST_SIZES=50 FLAT_INDEX_LIST_UPDATE_TXS=3` smoke run). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Adds benchmarks for flat index/autocomplete list write/read/update costs and decomposes schema-read overhead by schema depth, plus a test pinning derived array outputs to a single inline document. Helps explain where read costs come from and how update strategies scale. - **New Features** - Added `packages/runner/test/cell-set-flat-index-list.bench.ts` to measure one-doc vs per-item writes, first/repeated/schema reads, and three update profiles at N=100/1000/3000; config via `FLAT_INDEX_LIST_SIZES`, `FLAT_INDEX_LIST_UPDATE_TXS`, `FLAT_INDEX_LIST_REPORT`. - Added `packages/runner/test/cell-schema-read-depth.bench.ts` to read the same 1000-item doc through schemaless, `items: true`, permissive `items: {type: "object"}`, and full item schema to locate schema-path costs. - Updated `packages/runner/test/patterns-lift.test.ts` to assert a lifted array-of-objects result is stored inline as a single doc (no per-element entity docs). - **Performance** - `cell.set()` of an object array creates N+1 documents. - Schema-path reads are ~19µs/item/read (~63× schemaless); depth bench shows merely entering the schema path (`items: true`) is already ~30×, a permissive object schema is worst, and a fully-declared schema is cheaper — field validation isn’t the main cost. - Updates with one changed item: regenerate rewrites all N+1 docs; read-modify-write averages ~685B across 2 docs per tx and stays flat with N; targeted `key(i).set` stays ~246B/tx. Written for commit eaa71fd994f54a53aa538d0688c9097500c97c19. Summary will update on new commits.

author: edwinbetanc0urt
body:
Fix duplicate outbound orders can be generated from the same sales order because the gRPC `generateLoadOrder` service accepts the client-supplied lines without re-checking availability against the database. A double-submit (double-click, network retry, form resend without refresh) creates a second identical outbound order.

## Root cause

`OutBoundOrderLogic.generateLoadOrder` was ported from the ZK form `org.spin.wms.form.OutBoundOrder` without carrying over its `validateQuantity()` guard (checks `QtyOrdered − QtyDelivered − allocated-in-outbound` per line and rejects requested amounts that exceed it). Without that guard, the server trusts the request payload blindly, so a replayed identical payload creates a second outbound order even though the sales order has zero available quantity left.

## Fix

Add a pre-transaction check `validateAvailableQuantities` invoked as the first step inside `Trx.run` in `generateLoadOrder`. For each requested line it:

1. Loads the source order line and caches its parent order's `DeliveryRule` (avoids repeated `MOrder` / `MDDOrder` loads when all lines belong to the same order).
2. Skips the check when the delivery rule is `Force` or `Manual` (matches ZK semantics — those rules explicitly allow over-loading).
3. Computes the fresh available quantity from the database using a **correlated subquery** (see the SQL constant comment; do NOT rewrite as `LEFT JOIN + GROUP BY`).
4. Accumulates all failing lines and throws a single `AdempiereException` listing each violation as `@C_OrderLine_ID@=…, @Qty@=…, @QtyAvailable@=…`.

On the reported case the second request now reads `available = 0` and is rejected before any INSERT happens — the transaction rolls back cleanly, no duplicate outbound order is created.

Formulas replicate `listDocumentLines`:

- Sales Order: `available = QtyOrdered − QtyDelivered − allocated`
- Distribution: `available = QtyOrdered − QtyInTransit − QtyDelivered − allocated`

## Performance

Verified in dyd-dev (61k `wm_inoutboundline`, 285k `m_inoutline`, 276k `c_orderline`) with the exact SQL constants shipped here:

| Scenario | 41-line generation | Per line |
| --- | --- | --- |
| With the three FK indexes (real state) | **17.45 ms** | 0.43 ms | | Without them (simulated `enable_*=OFF`) | 3 267 ms | 79.7 ms |

The correlated form is critical: rewriting as `LEFT JOIN + GROUP BY` (the shape used by `listDocumentLines` for the paginated list) degrades to ~440 ms per line (~18 s for 41 lines) because the planner materializes the aggregate over the whole `m_inoutline` on every call. A code comment on the SQL constants documents this trap for future readers.

## Related migration

The FK-column indexes required by the validation are shipped as `adempiere-migrate-xml` PR `Add performance indexes for OutBoundOrder available-quantity check` (SeqNo `503640`, release `1.5.13`). Names match the canonical `_id` convention already present in most instances, so on dyd-dev it is a no-op.

## Behavior matrix

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Double-submit of the same request | Two identical outbound orders | Second rejected, no dup | | Single request over available quantity | Silently over-allocates | Rejected | | Legitimate partial + saldo generation | Works | Works (unchanged) | | Force / Manual delivery rule | No check (as ZK) | No check (unchanged) | | Non-stocked product | Works | Works (unchanged) |

## Test plan

- [ ] Send `GenerateLoadOrderRequest` twice with identical payload on a consignment sales order → first succeeds, second returns `@Qty@ > @QtyAvailable@`; DB has exactly one outbound order.
- [ ] Rapid double-click on the "Generate" button in the Vue form → idem; one outbound order created.
- [ ] Partial generation followed by a legitimate second generation for the remaining saldo → both succeed.
- [ ] Distribution order (`DD_Order`) path exercises the same guard.
- [ ] Sales order with `DeliveryRule = 'F'` (Force) or `'M'` (Manual): double-submit still creates two outbound orders — semantics preserved on purpose.
- [ ] Non-stocked product line: no regression.
- [ ] `./gradlew compileJava` green (already verified locally).

## Follow-ups (out of scope)

- Data cleanup of duplicated outbound orders already in production (procedure documented in the analysis HTML, §5).
- Secondary issue seen in the third Loom (`listDocumentLines` not returning the pending saldo after a partial generation) — treat as a separate issue.
- With `Query.setForUpdate` now available in the local patched Query class, a follow-up PR could add pessimistic locking on the source order line to also close the millisecond-simultaneous concurrency window; not observed in evidence, deferred.

author: echoofdawn
body:
## ELI16 — Teach instar to accept the just-released GPT-5.6 codex models

OpenAI shipped the GPT-5.6 model family (sol, terra, luna) to general availability on the Codex subscription, and they work today on our account. instar keeps a deliberately short allowlist of the exact Codex model names it will accept, so a typo or a made-up name can never quietly reach a real command line — but that list stopped at GPT-5.5, so the new models were being rejected as unknown even though the operator's config already asked for the flagship. This PR adds the three new names to that allowlist in the two places it lives (the model-tier-escalation resolver and the session-spawn validator, which mirror each other), and registers them in the doorway model registry with pricing. The fail-closed design is unchanged: unknown names still reject. The Pro variants are deliberately left out, and the routing lanes still pick GPT-5.5 until the new models earn their place through benchmarks — this change only makes them acceptable if you choose them.

## What changed

- `KNOWN_CODEX_MODEL_IDS` (src/core/ModelTierEscalation.ts) + `CODEX_MODELS_SUBSCRIPTION` (src/server/routes.ts) gain `gpt-5.6-sol` / `gpt-5.6-terra` / `gpt-5.6-luna`, kept as documented mirrors. `topicProfileValidation` reads the same enum, so it accepts them automatically.
- The Doorway/Model Knowledge Registry (`scripts/model-registry-freshness.manifest.json` → `codex-cli.topModels`) gains the three ids as recognized (`frontier:false`) entries with pricing; the now-false "gpt-5.6-sol is preview-only/unreachable" note is corrected. The CI-gating freshness lint is unaffected (the derived frontier set stays `[gpt-5.5]`; the capable pin stays `gpt-5.5`).
- Codex CLI >= 0.144.0 is required to actually run these models (older CLIs 400 with "requires a newer version").

## Tier

Tier 1 — additive model-id allowlist extension, fail-closed design unchanged. ELI16 (`docs/specs/codex-gpt56-allowlist.eli16.md`) + side-effects (`upgrades/side-effects/codex-gpt56-allowlist.md`) + release fragment (`upgrades/next/codex-gpt56-allowlist.md`) staged with src in one commit.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/modelTierEscalation-resolver.test.ts` — codex-cli escalated accepts each of sol/terra/luna; `gpt-9.9-fake` fails closed (`id-not-in-closed-enum`); the -pro variants asserted absent.
- `tests/unit/route-validation-edge.test.ts` — `POST /sessions/spawn` (framework codex-cli) accepts the three ids, rejects `gpt-9.9-fake` (400).
- `tests/unit/topicProfileValidation.test.ts` — `validateModelId` accepts them via the KNOWN_MODEL_IDS mirror.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run lint` green; adjacent model-tier suites (freshness, codex-model-tier-resolution, frameworkSessionLaunch, model-tier-swap-route, escalation-lifecycle) re-run green.

## Deliberately not done

- The `-pro` variants (likely plan-gated + pricier) — a tracked follow-up.
- No routing-chain / capable-pin / frontier promotion — a model earns its routing lane via benchmarks, not by GA date.

author: rbisecke
body:
## Summary

Replaces `CaptureController.detectMotion`'s positional-span heuristic (12-sample lead-wrist Y span, `> 0.20` starts / `< 0.03` for 15 samples stops) with a causal speed/burst trigger. The span check over-fires on wide practice waggles that never accelerate hard, and under-fires on compact fast swings (punch shots, partial pitches) that don't travel far enough to cross the span threshold.

- `SwingCore/Sources/SwingCore/MotionTrigger.swift`: adds `MotionTrigger.LiveState`/`step`, a pure incremental sibling to the existing `swingWindow` burst detector. Unlike `swingWindow`, which operates on a complete post-hoc array, `step` decides mid-recording from a single new sample plus caller-owned state, so the live recorder doesn't have to wait for the clip to end. The stop condition is gated behind `minRecordingSamples` so a genuine near-zero-speed pause at the top of the backswing (a real physical moment, not noise) can't be mistaken for the swing having settled.
- `ios/Divot/Store/CaptureController.swift`: replaces the `recentWristY`/`settleCounter` span logic with a `recentSpeeds` buffer (frame-to-frame lead-wrist displacement magnitude) and a `MotionTrigger.LiveState`, calling `beginRecording()`/`endRecording()` on the trigger's `recording` false→true/true→false transitions.
- `SwingCore/Sources/SwingCoreCheck/main.swift`: new `[MotionTrigger.step]` checks — flat noisy baseline never fires, the existing synthetic burst fires and stops correctly (never before `minRecordingSamples` elapses), a brief mid-swing pause inside a burst does not false-stop the recording, and two well-separated bursts fire the trigger twice.

`riseFactor`/`settleRatio`/`settleSamples`/`minRecordingSamples` are starting points ported from `swingWindow`'s existing defaults and today's settle cadence; they still need an on-device tuning pass against real waggles and swings before being considered final.

body:
## Why
Investigating the July Vercel Edge Requests alert (75% of the Hobby 1M cap, 95.4% from at-site) surfaced three crawler-hygiene gaps. The traffic growth itself is real (GA4: sessions +196%, $9.3K revenue/30d), but these leaks waste requests and lose visitors.

## What
1. **`app/robots.ts`** — didn't exist; every bot's `/robots.txt` probe server-rendered the full 404 page, and crawlers walked the site unguided. Now serves rules (blocks `/api`, `/preview`, `/v` homepage variants, `/amzn`, `/thank-you`) + sitemap pointer.
2. **`app/sitemap.ts`** — didn't exist; search engines rediscover the site by brute-force recrawling years of dead Squarespace URLs. Now 1,258 URLs: static pages, products, event detail pages, listable blog posts.
3. **Printables handle-prefix redirects** — the finding that reframed the 404 tail: the Shopify migration imported printables under `printable-`-prefixed handles, so the old SQS URLs (Google-indexed, Pinterest-pinned) 404 while the **same products are live** at `/shop/printable-<slug>`. These are not retired products (the t833 styled-404 decision stands for those). GA4 top not_found paths (trailing 7d) matched 1:1 against the live catalog gave 8 exact redirects, plus `/digishop` and an updated `/shop/digital-prints` → the printables category.

## Verification (local prod build)
- `next build` passes; `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` are routes.
- robots.txt: HTTP 200 with correct rules.
- sitemap.xml: HTTP 200, 1,258 URLs.
- All 8 printable redirects: 308 → live twin PDPs.
- `/digishop`, `/shop/digital-prints`: 308 → `/shop?category=printables`.
- Retired handle sample: still 404 (t833 behavior preserved).

## Not included (parked for a merchandising call)
Retired printables with no live twin (`a-good-life-printable`, `november-printable`, `true-strength-printable`, +12 more) stay on the styled 404 per t833. If Amy would rather route them to the printables category, that's a one-block follow-up.

author: leotemtem
body:
## Problem

  Fixes #5 

  RepoMonster did not have a visible GitHub Actions workflow under
  `.github/workflows`, which weakens confidence for a CI/review-focused
  tool. The repo should prove that its own tests, linting, type checks,
  Docker build, formatting, integration coverage, and security scan pass
  before changes are reviewed or merged.

  ## Approach

  Added `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with jobs for:

  - service-free unit tests
  - service-free integration tests
  - Ruff linting
  - Ruff formatting check
  - mypy source type checking
  - Bandit security scanning
  - Docker image build

  The unit test job uses the existing no-container test path:
  `PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests`.

  The integration test job runs the local `review_gate` CLI against
  `examples/review_request.json`, exercising request parsing, bundled pack
  retrieval, deterministic review, and JSON output without PostgreSQL,
  Docker Compose, network calls, or model connectivity.

  Mypy is scoped to `src` for the initial baseline because the current
  tests include untyped test doubles.

  Added URL scheme validation for configured outbound endpoints before
  `urllib.request.urlopen` is used. The GitHub API URL, insight endpoint
  base URL, and embedding endpoint base URL now reject non-HTTP schemes.
  The remaining Bandit suppressions are narrow `B310` suppressions at
  validated `urlopen` calls.

  Formatting changes are isolated in their own commit so the logical CI/
  security changes remain reviewable.

  ## Acceptance Criteria

  - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` exists and is visible in the repo.
  - CI runs on pull requests and pushes to `main`.
  - Unit tests run without requiring Docker, Postgres, or other service
  containers.
  - Integration tests run without requiring Docker, Postgres, network
  access, or model connectivity.
  - Ruff linting runs in CI.
  - Ruff formatting check runs in CI.
  - Mypy type checking runs in CI.
  - Bandit security scanning runs in CI.
  - Docker image build runs in CI.
  - Security scan has no unsuppressed findings.
  - Formatting changes are separated from logical CI/security changes.

  ## Test Evidence

  - `PYTHONPATH=src /tmp/repomonster-ci-venv/bin/python -m unittest
  discover -s tests`
    - Passed: 43 tests
  - `/tmp/repomonster-ci-venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s
  tests_integration`
    - Passed: 1 integration test
  - `/tmp/repomonster-ci-venv/bin/ruff format --check .`
    - Passed: 27 files already formatted
  - `/tmp/repomonster-ci-venv/bin/ruff check .`
    - Passed
  - `/tmp/repomonster-ci-venv/bin/mypy src`
    - Passed: no issues in 17 source files
  - `/tmp/repomonster-ci-venv/bin/bandit -r src`
    - Passed: no issues identified
  - Workflow YAML parse
    - Passed
  - `docker build --tag repomonster:ci .`
    - Passed locally before Docker Desktop’s WSL CLI mount later began
    returning an environmental `Input/output error`
    - GitHub Actions will provide the authoritative Docker build result

### Motivation
- Introduce a central `Company` registry keyed by full 14-digit CNPJ to map invoices' tomador CNPJ to friendly display names and an active flag.
- Allow ADMIN users to manage companies (create, edit, activate/inactivate) and surface company names in lists and invoice details for better usability.
- Ensure seeded initial company data is available for existing environments to avoid mismatches when resolving tomador CNPJs.

### Description
- Adds a new Prisma `Company` model with `cnpj` unique index and an `active` index, the migration SQL at `prisma/migrations/20260709130000_company_registry/migration.sql`, and an initial upsert seed in `prisma/seed.js` to insert the provided companies.
- Implements admin-only REST endpoints: `POST /api/empresas` and `GET /api/empresas` with pagination and filtering, and `PATCH /api/empresas/[id]` for updates, including input validation and Prisma error handling in `src/app/api/empresas/route.ts` and `src/app/api/empresas/[id]/route.ts`.
- Adds UI for company management at `src/app/empresas/page.tsx`, exposes the link in the main header (`src/app/components/main-header.tsx`), and integrates company display (name and formatted CNPJ) into dashboards and invoice lists (`src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` and `src/app/api/notas/minhas/route.ts`) so invoices show resolved company names when available.
- Adds `companySchema` validation to `src/lib/validations.ts` and implements client-side formatting/helpers for CNPJ display and company presentation.

### Testing
- Ran the project's automated test suite via `yarn test`, and the tests completed successfully.
- Performed a type check and production build via `yarn build` which succeeded.
- Exercised the new endpoints with API calls during local seed/migration to verify upsert behavior and error handling (conflict and not-found cases) during development.
