author: kthyng
body:
BoundaryForcing ([#616](https://github.com/CWorthy-ocean/roms-tools/issues/616)/[#626](https://github.com/CWorthy-ocean/roms-tools/issues/626)) and SurfaceForcing ([#629](https://github.com/CWorthy-ocean/roms-tools/pull/629)) already select their horizontal regrid engine and optional source prefill through the shared processing_methods.RegridConfig, defaulting to a NaN-aware xESMF regrid. InitialConditions was the last full-domain consumer still hardwired to the legacy AMG Poisson fill + SciPy interpolation — so the interior initial state and the boundaries it must match at t=0 were built by different machinery. This PR closes that gap and factors the shared logic into one place.

Changes:
* InitialConditions gains prefill, prefill_kwargs, regrid_method, extrap_method, extrap_kwargs (same semantics as BoundaryForcing). No deprecated apply_2d_horizontal_fill alias — IC never exposed one.
* New shared helpers, so the mask-selection, prefill-branch, regridder-construction, and coverage-check logic live in exactly one place:
  * regrid.py: build_lateral_regridder, select_source_mask
  * setup/utils.py: check_source_coverage, apply_source_prefill, apply_scipy_fallback_fill
* BoundaryForcing and SurfaceForcing refactored onto these helpers — behavior-preserving. SurfaceForcing's private _check_source_coverage is removed in favor of the shared one.
* ROMS-restart guard: ROMSDataset has no prefill API, so for a "ROMS" source IC keeps its existing apply_lateral_fill path and the new options are ignored (with a logged note), mirroring the bgc_interpolation_method fallback convention.

Behavior change: 
The IC default is now prefill=None + regrid_method="auto" (masked xESMF bilinear + inverse-distance extrapolation; nearest-neighbor + SciPy fallback when xESMF is absent). Output shifts slightly for users on the defaults — pass prefill="2d_lateral_fill", regrid_method="scipy" to reproduce pre-v4 output byte-for-byte. On the default (extrapolating) path, a grid that extends beyond the source coverage now raises a clear error instead of silently extrapolating.

Testing: 
* New IC tests: default vs. legacy path, per-method prefill (inverse_dist/nearest_s2d/nearest_neighbor), source-coverage error, ROMS-source guard, and an explicit to_yaml→from_yaml round-trip of the new fields.
* BoundaryForcing and SurfaceForcing regression-hash fixtures are unchanged — the byte-identical guard confirming the shared-helper refactor is behavior-preserving.

Docs: 
* releases.md entry.
* initial_conditions.ipynb gains a short "Controlling the horizontal regridding" section documenting the options (referencing the Boundary Forcing tutorial for the full explanation).

Timing:
I was able to run a large domain (1.2 million horizontal cells and 100 vertical levels) on a full Anvil node in about 10 minutes simply inputting the GLORYS relevant file for the initial time and no chunks information so that the internal chunks management handled it. I tried a few versions of the unified BGC dataset with varied chunks and it did change the time but they are all fine. Running on half a node did not work — not enough memory I think.

- [x] Tests added
- [x] Passes `pre-commit run --all-files`
- [x] Changes are documented in `docs/releases.md`
- [x] New functionality has documentation

author: wingedguardian
body:
## Summary

Two isolated memory-retrieval correctness fixes (Tier-2 carry-overs), plus the review-found P1 that made the second one stick end-to-end.

- **MEM-006** — `drift_recall`'s wing-scoped FTS drill-down hardcoded `collection="episodic_memory"` while the sibling vector arm loops `source_collections`. Knowledge-base rows ARE FTS-indexed (`store.py` upserts with the resolved collection), so `source="knowledge"/"both"` recall could never surface knowledge lexically in the scoped phase. Now mirrors the vector arm: one `search_ranked` per collection, order-preserving dedup, wing post-filter unchanged.
- **mem-007** — `_apply_diversity_penalty` mutates `fused` in place (echoes ×0.5, evictions =0.0) and `RetrievalResult.score` fed J-9's `emit_recall_fired` — logging a dedup artifact as retrieval quality (top_scores / mean_score / score_spread / entrenchment corr). New `RetrievalResult.retrieval_score` snapshots the pre-penalty (post-rerank, post-graph-boost) score; J-9 reads it. `score` stays penalized — it drives the returned ordering, which SHOULD demote near-duplicates. Unblocks a trustworthy mem-005 graph-boost A/B baseline.
- **Review P1 (fixed in-PR)** — the MCP MEM-003 enrichment (`memory_recall`/`knowledge_recall`) re-derived top_scores/mean_score from `.score` and `update_event_metrics` overwrites keys — clobbering the raw values on the primary production paths. The enrichment now reads `retrieval_score` (fallback to `score` for paths that don't populate it), `knowledge_recall` carries it through the merge with the authority boost applied (a legitimate quality signal, unlike the echo penalty), and the DRIFT path populates it (no penalty there — raw == final).

## Verification

- TDD with empirical RED for all three changes (each test confirmed failing against the unfixed code).
- 126 tests green across the affected surface (drift, retrieval, types, reranker, MCP memory, recall instrumentation, runtime retriever); ruff clean; subsystem-map guard clean.
- Two independent code reviews: initial review surfaced the P1; focused re-review of the P1 fix came back clean on all five checks (fallback safety, additive-key consumers, boost mutation, test pinning, FTS parity).
- Pre-existing (NOT this PR): 6 `*_requires_init` tests in `tests/test_mcp/test_memory_mcp.py` fail under one specific multi-file local batch on main too — cross-file pollution, tracked as follow-up 05034405.

## Notes

- `knowledge_recall` result dicts gain an additive `retrieval_score` key (all consumers duck-type; verified).
- CHANGELOG (user-visible MEM-006 entry) + `docs/architecture/CURRENT.md` memory entry refreshed (stamp `d3d48d94 2026-07-09`).

Первый из трёх PR спайка LOS-76 (план: ядро → CANopenNode+vcan-риг → ESP32+отчёт). Новый проект `projects/bench_controller/firmware/` — прошивка контроллера прочностного стенда (путь ① [RFC-0004](../blob/develop/docs/RFC/rfc-0004-experiment-control-architecture.md)), архитектурные паттерны — из rc_vehicle.

## Что внутри

**Портируемое ядро `common/`** (без OS/CAN-инклюдов — компилируется хостовым тулчейном):
- `ChannelController` — force/displacement PID с **bumpless-переключением** (пре-загрузка интегратора + рампа захвата цели), feed-forward по производной уставки + **lead-компенсация** лага золотника, slew-лимит команды клапану
- `SpecimenFailureDetector` — детекция разрушения (падение силы при значимой уставке) с **arming** после выхода на режим; латч → мгновенный displacement-hold
- `LinkWatchdog` — политика потери связи из discovery: Running → Grace → **плавная разгрузка** → SafeHold; восстановление только из Grace, возобновление — явной командой
- `SineProgram` (block loading), `HydraulicPlantModel` (золотник τ=8 мс → поршень → образец-пружина), `TickStats`, `BenchControlLoop` (тик 500 Гц + `HostStep` seam для SIL), HAL `BenchPlatform`

**Тесты: 48 GTest** — юниты + интеграционные сценарии замкнутого контура (ядро + модель, без CAN/Python, гоняются в ctest):
- (a) трекинг синуса force-режима: **10 Гц RMS < 6 %**, 20 Гц ≈ 23 %, 50 Гц ≈ 50 % — граница 500 Гц контура зафиксирована (10 отсчётов/цикл; вход для отчёта)
- (b) безударность переключений — скачок команды ограничен slew-лимитом всегда
- (c) разрушение → hold: латч ≤ 2 циклов, runaway за окно детекции ограничен
- (d) потеря связи: grace → монотонная разгрузка без ступеней → SafeHold

**SIL CLI**: `sim_host --fake-plant` (CSV; сценарии разрушения/потери связи флагами)

**Сборка**: `sources.cmake` — единый список исходников для всех потребителей (фикс дублирования rc_vehicle); `make bench-firmware-test` в корне.

## Осознанные решения
- PID/slew-rate **скопированы** из rc_vehicle (namespace bench, PID расширен `SetIntegral` для bumpless) — извлечение общей либы: LOS-107
- CANopen здесь нет вообще: ядро видит только `IValveChannel` — адаптер CANopenNode придёт в PR-B

## Проверка
```
make bench-firmware-test   # 48/48 passed
tests/build/sim_host --fail-at-ms 2000 > run.csv
```

author: lukesantossz
body:
## 1. Context

- **Motivation:** Captured photo originals stored under `soil_images/` retained EXIF (including GPS) — an uncontrolled duplicate of the location the app already records explicitly through `LocationService` — which would exfiltrate once `RemoteSyncBackend.uploadBlob` uploads raw image bytes. The capture-site flag alone does not close this on Android (its `image_picker` plugin ignores `requestFullMetadata`), so the removal is done at the durable-storage boundary.
- **Task Link:** https://github.com/LukeSantossz/visiosoil-app/issues/113
- **Spec Link:** `docs/specs/0002-strip-exif-from-captured-photos.md` (full tier; decision recorded in `docs/adr/0005-strip-exif-at-image-storage-boundary.md`)

## 2. What Was Done

- **Capture site** (`capture_screen.dart`): pass `requestFullMetadata: false` to `ImagePicker().pickImage` as iOS-side defense-in-depth.
- **Storage boundary** (`DefaultImageStorageService.saveCapturedImage`): for a JPEG source, read its EXIF with `decodeJpgExif`, keep only the orientation tag, and rewrite the EXIF APP1 segment with `injectJpgExif` — dropping GPS and all other metadata while preserving the entropy-coded scan. Both `Image.file` (display) and `img.decodeImage` (the classifier) apply EXIF orientation, so keeping the tag holds display and inference identical to before. The strip runs only on data starting with the JPEG SOI marker, and a parser failure on a corrupt JPEG is logged and falls back to a raw copy, so a malformed source never aborts the save. Non-JPEG sources are raw-copied unchanged.
- Recorded ADR 0005; no new dependencies (`image ^4.3.0` already present).

**Known residuals (accepted, out of scope):** XMP metadata is not stripped (camera GPS lives in EXIF); a non-JPEG source (only reachable via a gallery source, which is out of scope) is raw-copied; a malformed JPEG whose EXIF parser overruns is raw-copied rather than stripped (not camera-producible and not read as valid EXIF by standard decoders).

## 3. How to Test

1. Check out the branch.
2. Install dependencies: `flutter pub get`.
3. Run the checks: `flutter analyze && flutter test`.
4. Verify the build runs without errors.

## 4. Evidence

Backend/data-privacy change; no UI change (display orientation is deliberately preserved). Covered by tests in `test/services/image_storage_service_test.dart`: GPS stripped from a stored JPEG, EXIF orientation preserved, decoded pixels byte-identical to source, non-JPEG raw-copied; plus `test/features/capture/capture_screen_test.dart` asserting the capture flag. `flutter analyze` clean; `flutter test` 166 passing.

## 5. Self-Review Checklist

- [x] Self-review done in the Files Changed tab.
- [x] Spec approved at the Gate before implementation, and the change matches its Scope (per `spec_method.md`).
- [x] Each Acceptance Criterion has a passing test; tests were written before their implementation.
- [x] Commented-out code and unnecessary debug statements removed.
- [x] Code follows the project style guide.
- [x] New dependencies work without breaking the build (none added).
- [x] Review layers recorded — **Author:** Claude Opus 4.8. **R1 (internal):** Opus 4.8 subagent, read-only adversarial review; it caught that stripping the EXIF orientation tag would rotate Android captures and change the classifier input, which drove the orientation-preserving fix, then re-verified the fix. **R2 (cross-provider):** Codex / gpt-5.5 pre-push gate; it flagged that the capture-site flag does not strip camera EXIF on Android (drove moving the strip to the storage boundary) and that the parser could overrun on malformed JPEG-like input (drove the SOI-signature guard and parser-failure fallback); the final R2 run is clean. **R3:** CodeRabbit on this PR.

author: apholmes7-bot
body:
<!-- Hidden Harbours PR. Keep PRs small and single-purpose. See ../agents/coordination.md §6. -->

## What & why

The owner's delegated aesthetic pass (2026-07-08, verbatim: *"feel free to tune the water in whatever fashion you think will lead to better looking waves, better clumping of foam, deep blues"*). Three additive levers, one per ask, each a named tunable ON at a modest default and an **exact passthrough at 0** — built on his #183 baseline (his tuned values are byte-identical; his locked `_Flow`/`_WindChop` untouched) and composed with the #182 swell-read (nothing washes it out).

**Backlog item:** owner mandate 2026-07-08 (water aesthetic pass)
**Pillar(s) served:** P1 Sea Has Moods
**Owning role:** lead-architect (the serialized water-shader lane), art-pipeline look

## The look I went for

The same cold North Atlantic sea, but *gathered and modelled*: swells read as directional forms with a lit face and a shaded back instead of flat brightness bands; whitecaps collect into wind-aligned rows and crest-shed rafts with clear water between, instead of an even sprinkle; and the deep water settles into a rich navy that the owner's hand-painted shallows melt into — KTC-cozy, still his sea.

## Every tunable added/changed (old → new, with reasoning)

### 1. Deep blues — `_DeepBlueStrength` / `_DeepBlueColor` / `_DeepBlueStart` (new)

**The trap, resolved:** the shipped `Water.mat` has `_USE_DEPTHRAMP` ON, so the base colour comes from the owner's **hand-painted `_DepthRamp`** (its deep end is a muted slate-teal) — `_DeepColor` is inert, and repainting his ramp would bulldoze his art. The lever chosen: a **bounded pull of the settled base colour toward a rich navy**, keyed to the read-only deep fraction, applied *before every additive layer* (the #182 swell-read, swell bands, spec, foam ride on top at full amplitude) and *before the palette guard-rail* — **the ADR 0015 rail stays the single final colour owner** and bounds this like every other layer. Pre-grade water colour (not light content), so it dims correctly with the night overlay; the post-grade compensated block is untouched.

| Tunable | Old → New | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `_DeepBlueStrength` | (none) → **0.45** | Master pull. Dialing up = deeper navy; **0 = the painted ramp exactly.** |
| `_DeepBlueColor` | (none) → **(0.02, 0.09, 0.30)** | The navy target — the deeper-saturated cousin of the owner's own `_PaletteDeep` anchor (0.02, 0.08, 0.26), so the guard-rail's anchor pull agrees with it (sits under his sat-cap 0.78, above his value floor 0.08 — the rail neither greys nor lifts it). |
| `_DeepBlueStart` | (none) → **0.25** | Where (in the deep fraction) the pull begins — shallows and mid ramp untouched. |

### 2. Foam clumping — `_FoamClumpStrength` / `_FoamClumpScale` / `_FoamClumpStretch` (new)

A second, much **broader and slower** evolving field (reuses the existing `EvolvingField`/`Pixelize` helpers — no new noise machinery, no texture fetches), **stretched along the wind** and drifting with the same foam drift, **redistributes** the whitecap coverage: in-patch coverage lifts ×1.25 (saturated), between-patch coverage thins toward bare water. The same foam, gathered into **windrows and rafts** instead of sprinkled. Applied to both whitecap paths (live wave trains + legacy); the shoreline fringe is deliberately untouched (the "even sprinkle" is an open-water read; the fringe already has swash/churn character).

| Tunable | Old → New | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `_FoamClumpStrength` | (none) → **0.55** | How strongly foam gathers. 0 = today's even sprinkle; 1 = hard patch-gating with bare lanes. |
| `_FoamClumpScale` | (none) → **0.10** | Patch frequency — smaller = broader rafts and wider clear lanes (~10 m patches at the default). |
| `_FoamClumpStretch` | (none) → **2.5** | Wind anisotropy — 1 = round rafts; higher = long thin windrows down the wind. |

### 3. Better waves — `_SwellFaceShade` (new)

The shared wave field's **analytic slope** (`waveSlope` — already computed by `WaveFieldSample` for twin parity, previously unused in the composite) shades each swell against the **one implied sun** (`_SunDir` → `_LightDir` fallback, the specular's exact convention — ADR 0006 single-light discipline): lit face brighter, back of the crest shaded. Where the #182 swell-read is *symmetric* (crest bright / trough dark), this is *antisymmetric* — the two **compose into a modelled, directional wave** instead of doubling one band into glare (combined worst-case crest add ≈ 0.16 pre-grade, inside the rail's ceiling). Self-gating: glass ⇒ zero amplitude ⇒ zero slope ⇒ zero term (the calm mirror is untouched); the legacy no-trains path leaves `waveSlope` at 0 (edit-mode/bare-scene look unchanged). **No C# twin needed:** it consumes `WaveFieldSample`'s existing outputs without changing the field math (the #182 precedent) — `WaveMath`/`ShaderTwinSample` untouched.

| Tunable | Old → New | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `_SwellFaceShade` | (none) → **0.22** | Lit-face/shaded-back contrast (±0.033 swing at default — shading, not glare). 0 = flat bands. |

### 4. Serialization + mood coherence (no owner value changed)

| File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Water.mat` | new keys serialized at the defaults above; also pins `_SwellReadStrength` **0.35** / `_SwellReadBands` **0** | These two were riding shader defaults un-serialized (his tuning session predates #182) — pinning makes his Inspector state explicit. **Every owner-tuned value is byte-identical; `m_LockedProperties: _Flow _WindChop` untouched.** |
| `Water_FoggySmother.mat` | `_DeepBlueStrength` **0**, `_SwellFaceShade` **0** | A pale flat smother has no rich navy and no lit faces — the fog anchor must kill both if the weather blend eases toward it. |
| `Water_StormGrey.mat` | `_DeepBlueStrength` **0.1** | Grey gloom keeps only a hint of navy. |
| `Water_DeepBlue.mat` | `_DeepBlueStrength` **0.7** | The saturated open-ocean variant leans the enrichment in. |
| `WaterSurface.cs` | new float keys join `MoodFloatNames`, `_DeepBlueColor` joins `MoodColorNames` | The §12 preset library / §14 weather blend ease the new look props per mood — look props only, disjoint from the physics set (no double-drive). |
| `docs/design/water-rendering.md` | new §20 | The pass, the trap resolution, placement, and every tunable documented. |

## Hard-rule compliance

- **P1 / rule 5:** all three terms are `col.rgb`/`col.a` dressing only — `depth`, `clip()`, `dt`, `_WaterLevel`, the height read, and the wave-field sample are untouched; the waterline and the wave the boat feels are byte-identical. No new randomness anywhere sim-adjacent.
- **Rule 6:** every new strength/scale/colour is a named material property with a sensible default; internal shaping constants follow the shader's documented-constant idiom (the swell-read's 0.25-ceiling precedent).
- **Rule 7:** +1 `EvolvingField` (4 value-noise taps) per whitecap-branch pixel when clumping is on, one smoothstep for the deep pull, one dot/clamp for the face shade — **no new texture fetches**.
- **Pre-grade vs post-grade:** all three are pre-grade water colour (they dim with the night like the sea they colour); the post-grade overlay-compensated light bucket is untouched.

## How I tested

- **Full EditMode suite headless** (Unity 6000.5.0f1, this worktree's own project path) — including `WaterShaderCompileGuardTests` (force-compiles the shipped `Water.mat` + every `WaterPresets/` variant — the magenta gate) and `ArtRenderingTests`. Results: **1132/1132 passed, 0 failed** (`WaterShaderCompileGuardTests` passed; `ArtRenderingTests` 41/41 passed).
- Shader-trap checklist: no `+` in any `[Header]`, no `[unroll]` over a runtime bound, degenerate-smoothstep guarded (`_DeepBlueStart` capped below 1), all new props in the `UnityPerMaterial` CBUFFER (SRP batcher).
- No C# twin required: no shader math with an existing twin changed (`WaveFieldSample`/`SwashOffset` untouched); the new terms consume already-sampled values, per the #182 pr

The Helm/K8s install path silently deployed a **degraded stack**. The README's services table and architecture describe reranker (30084) and rag-admin (30085) as part of the stack, and the quick start says bootstrap "deploys every service" — but:

author: elirc
body:
## Sprint 15 — Production readiness → v1.0.0 🎉

The final sprint. Operate a stateful, real-time system: measure the promise (not the process), trace a
mutation across four systems including the browser, survive infra loss, and ship v1.0.0 with an honest
retrospective. **This closes the course.**

### What changed
- **Observability primitives** (`packages/shared`, pure + property-tested):
  - `latency` — nearest-rank percentiles + a percentile-based SLO. The metric users feel is p95, not
    the mean; an average of 245ms can hide a p95 of 2000ms.
  - `trace` — a **client-inclusive** mutation lifecycle. The browser is a first-class service in the
    trace, so we estimate each client's clock offset (NTP-style) and correct before subtracting —
    otherwise a client whose clock is 5s fast reports its teammate's edit arriving *before it was sent*.
  - `redact` — offline-first error context (connection state, pending count, `lastSeq`) with PII
    scrubbed at the trust boundary before it reaches a third-party tracker.
- **API:** request-ID correlation (`x-request-id`, reused or minted, echoed on every response),
  structured logs in prod, and `GET /metrics` exposing `slo.p95WithinBudget` — a boolean an alert pages on.
- **Graceful deploys:** SIGTERM drains WebSockets (notify → stop accepting → close HTTP); the client
  treats a `draining` message as an ordinary reconnect. Deploys become a controlled version of the
  network failure the system already survives (S07).
- **Ops docs:** six runbooks, a blameless postmortem of the Redis fanout-loss drill, and **ADR-0012**
  (accept a proven degraded mode + alert on it, rather than carry pub/sub-redundancy weight).
- **Release:** CHANGELOG, root README, and the **Course Retrospective** — which reveals the flaw ledger
  (author-private until now) and tallies the "spine dividend."

### How to review this PR
Follow one mutation across four systems, then the drill story:
1. `feat(shared): observability primitives` — start with `trace.ts` (the clock-skew correction) and
   `latency.ts` (why percentiles).
2. `feat(api): request-id + /metrics` — the SLO verdict endpoint.
3. `feat(api): WS drain` — drain-as-reconnect; note how little new code this needed (S07 did the work).
4. `docs(ops): runbooks + postmortem + ADR-0012` — read `postmortems/2026-07-09-redis-fanout-loss.md`.
5. `docs(release): retrospective` — the flaw ledger, revealed.

### Why the incident drill is the centerpiece
We killed Redis pub/sub mid-collaboration on staging. Clients kept working and converged on reconnect —
**zero data loss** — confirming the S06 sentence "the log is truth, the fanout is a hint." The real
finding wasn't the outage; it was that **no alert fired** (API stayed green while the promise broke).
That gap became the fix. *Test the failure and you may find you don't need to prevent it — you need to
observe it.*

### Verification
- `pnpm run lint` clean · `pnpm turbo run typecheck test build` green (property tests included) · web
  bundle builds. New tests cover percentiles (bounds/monotonicity), clock-skew recovery, redaction,
  `/metrics`, and request-id echo.

### Deferred (named, not dropped — see the curriculum note)
- Real Prometheus/OTel export, a tracing backend, Redis-backed fanout at scale (ADR-0012's revisit
  trigger), load testing at 10k concurrent, and the client beacon that feeds `observeFanoutLagMs`. The
  *shapes* are built and tested; wiring them to real infra is the next repo.

Closes #63
Closes #64
Closes #65
Closes #66
Closes #67

author: pa-arth
body:
`{{label}}` was the only free-text branch-template variable substituted without sanitization. `{{description}}` goes through `extractDescription` (kebab-case, stripped to `[a-z0-9-]`), but `generateBranchName` passed the label straight through as `label || entityType`. A scoped label like `area:permissions` therefore lands a `:` in the branch name, which `validateBranchName` rejects — and because the branch setup block catches that error and calls `process.exit(1)`, the whole run dies rather than degrading. This repo's own labels (`area:permissions`, `provider:1p`) trigger it.

This adds a small `sanitizeLabel` helper and applies it before substitution. Unlike `extractDescription`, which drops invalid characters, it replaces runs of them with a hyphen so scoped labels stay readable (`area:permissions` → `area-permissions`, `needs review` → `needs-review`). If a label sanitizes to nothing (e.g. an emoji-only label), it falls back to `entityType`, matching the existing no-label behavior.

I deliberately kept this to the label variable and left the custom-template return path untouched — it intentionally skips the lowercase/truncation that the default path applies, so I didn't want to change those semantics.

Tests: added regression cases in `test/branch-template.test.ts` covering a scoped label, a label with spaces, and a label that sanitizes to empty, each asserting the result also passes `validateBranchName` (so the `process.exit(1)` path can't regress). Full suite green (`bun test`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`).

Fixes #1491

author: sawyerhood
body:
## Summary

- enforce one absolute execute-request lifetime across browser-lock queueing, browser setup, sandbox initialization, script execution, and teardown
- cancel on deadline or socket disconnect, suppress late output and duplicate terminal frames, and await each active Playwright progress controller before lock release
- keep cancellation scoped to the per-script bridge so existing named pages and externally connected browsers survive
- make page-title discovery concurrent, add injection-safe snapshot refs including iframe refs, and remove default CUA navigation grace latency
- update the agent guide and add first-class Codex skill installation

## Measured behavior

- Three non-settling page titles previously consumed three serial 1500 ms windows, or 4500 ms total. The fake-timer regression now starts all three title calls together and returns all summaries at exactly one 1500 ms window.
- Non-navigation CUA actions previously paid roughly 1 second of grace on every click. Focused sandbox timings now assert default CUA click, CUA doubleClick, DOM-CUA click, and DOM-CUA doubleClick complete in under 900 ms. Explicit `waitForNavigation: true` still settles the expected main-frame navigation.
- A queued request now expires at its absolute 50 ms test deadline and never starts after the prior lock holder exits.
- A running missing-element Playwright action now aborts within the focused test bound of 2 seconds, emits no late output, and the next request reuses the same named page and existing element without relaunch or content reset.
- Boundary coverage advances the clock to the exact hard deadline without running the timer callback and confirms timeout wins over success.

## Validation

- `cd daemon && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`
- `cd daemon && pnpm vitest run` — 19 files, 145 tests passed
- focused cancellation, title concurrency, snapshot ref, iframe ref, CUA, DOM-CUA, browser late-return cleanup, and finalization regressions
- `cd daemon && pnpm format:check`
- `cd daemon && pnpm bundle`
- `cd daemon && pnpm bundle:sandbox-client`
- `cd cli && cargo fmt --check`
- `cd cli && cargo build`
- `cd cli && cargo test` — 6 tests passed
- `git diff --check`

## Compatibility notes

- Playwright remains the browser engine; no Puppeteer migration.
- Existing selectors and role locators remain available. `page.getByRef()` only accepts `eN` or `fNeN`, preventing selector injection.
- Named-browser locking remains exclusive. Cancellation does not release the lock until active Playwright controllers stop and cleanup completes.
- The timeout flag now covers total request lifetime, including queue wait and setup, rather than only guest script execution.
- `Cua.click`, `Cua.doubleClick`, `DomCua.click`, and `DomCua.doubleClick` now default `waitForNavigation` to false. Callers can preserve settling with explicit true or pair known navigation with `Promise.all([page.waitForURL(...), click()])`.
- Noninteractive `install-skill` now updates Claude, Agents, and Codex targets. Explicit flags remain available for selecting only desired targets.

## Intentionally deferred

- snapshot depth protocol mismatch
- target-id caching
- daemon/client version handshake
- optional CLI read watchdog

This PR is intentionally left unmerged.

## Summary
- `actions/checkout` unconditionally runs `git config --global --add safe.directory <workspace>` on every job, with no dedup check (upstream behavior since the CVE-2022-24765 fix). Across 70+ self-hosted runners and thousands of job runs this bloated the operator's real `~/.gitconfig` — a symlink into the dotfiles SSoT — to 16,302 duplicate lines (found 2026-07-09 while reconciling a stuck Spartan dotfiles sync).
- Sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` in the shared runner env hardening to a node-local scratch file, seeded once from the real `~/.gitconfig` so identity/credential settings still resolve. All future `--global` writes from CI jobs land in the scratch copy instead of the tracked source.
- An earlier fix attempt (inverting the `~/.gitconfig` symlink into an `[include]`-only file) was tested and reverted by the dotfiles agent: `git config --global <key>` as a plain CLI read does not follow includes by default in git 2.43, so that approach would have silently broken any tool doing a bare config read. This fix is scoped entirely to the CI runner job environment and leaves the interactive shell's config untouched.

author: mikelward
body:
A systematic bug hunt across the whole codebase (client data/sync layer, core UI, client libs/pages, Edge Functions/SSRF/sanitizer, migrations/RLS). Every finding below was traced through the code before fixing; each fix is its own commit with a regression test. Baseline was green; the branch adds 19 JS tests + 2 SQL checks and stays green (`npm test` 2292 passed, lint, typecheck).

## Fixed (one commit each)

**Security / server**
- **Poller absolutized relative feed links against `secret_url`** — a relative channel/item `<link>` in a tokenized feed persisted the token into subscriber-visible `feeds.site_url` / `items.url` (guardrail #7), and diverged from `refresh/index.ts` (which uses `feed.url`), splitting the `(feed_id, url)` dedup key between the two writers. Poller now parses against the public `feed.url`.
- **`assertSafeUrl` echoed the raw URL in its `Invalid URL` error** — the message lands in client-visible `feeds.last_error`, and a malformed pasted feed URL can carry a token.

**Client**
- **Infinite reload loop in the `index.html` boot guard** — its listener lives for the tab's lifetime and matches any `/assets/` failure, while `main.tsx` clears its one-shot budget on every boot; a persistently failing lazy-route asset (broken deploy) reloaded forever. The guard now stands down after boot (`window.__readmoBooted`), leaving post-boot failures to the fail-closed CHUNK budget.
- **Stale mouse/pen gesture starts in `useSwipeToDismiss` / `usePullToRefresh`** — capture is only taken once a gesture arms, so a press released outside the element never delivered its pointerup; a button-less hover then resumed the "gesture" (rows dragging under hover, a later plain click able to commit Done/Pin or a spurious refresh). Both hooks now drop the tracked start on a button-less mouse/pen move.
- **`ItemList`'s More scroll anchor was never disarmed on a failed/empty fetch** — it then fired on any later items change (PTR, TTL re-materialization, same ids in another view), yanking the viewport. Now cleared when nothing appends and on view change.
- **Two divergent `formatDisplayDomain` implementations** — the live copy (itemMeta.ts) lacked the compound-eTLD list and half the ccTLD set of the dead-code copy (format.ts): `jasoneckert.github.io` → "github.io", `author.substack.com` → "substack.com", `x.or.kr` → "or.kr". itemMeta now delegates to format.ts.
- **`ensureFeeds` swallowed title-override read errors** — a transient 401/5xx silently cached raw feed titles for the whole session (renames vanished). It now throws before touching the permanent cache so the query retries.
- **Legacy cache migration orphaned the pre-scoping outbox** — queued offline writes at the unscoped key were never replayed and never purged. The one-time migration now moves the outbox with the state map.
- **OPML import mangled numeric character references** — `&`/`&` in `xmlUrl` subscribed a literally wrong URL that parked the feed. `decodeXmlEntities` now decodes them (invalid code points stay literal).
- **OPML export failures died silently** — no catch, caller doesn't await; now surfaces a toast like import.
- **`/debug` labeled a backend outage "Network: offline"** — the row used the two-state online boolean; it now reports the three-way connectivity status (`backend unreachable` vs `offline`).

**Database (migrations 0055–0057 — verified against a local PostgreSQL 16 with all migrations applied and the repo's SQL tests)**
- **0055**: `upsert_feed_items` aborted the whole per-feed batch on a guid/url cross-collision (row A holds the incoming guid, row B the url) — the fallback's guid adoption hit `unique (feed_id, guid)` with no handler, and the identical publisher data re-aborted every poll (a stuck feed). A nested handler now updates the url survivor without the guid adoption. Regression test added as T6 in `supabase/tests/canonicalize_item_url.sql`.
- **0056**: the orphan-feed reaper race 0043 claimed to close is still open — EvalPlanQual doesn't fire on lock-only conflicts, so a subscription committing while the reaper's DELETE waited was silently cascade-deleted (reproduced with two sessions). The reaper now locks candidates `FOR UPDATE`, then re-checks both conditions under a fresh snapshot.
- **0057**: `set_item_state` stored client LWW timestamps unclamped — a far-future device clock permanently locked a field and held the Done/Hidden/Opened TTLs open (protection 0003 documented and 0023 dropped). Clocks past a 10-minute tolerance are now replaced with `now()`; within it they store verbatim so the client's exact-echo loss detection doesn't re-pull on ordinary skew.
- **Fixed `supabase/tests/access_rpcs.sql` T13** — `(fi.item).id` errors against `feed_items`' single-composite-column shape (PostgreSQL flattens it to `SETOF items`), so the file aborted under `ON_ERROR_STOP` before T13–T17 ever ran.

## ⚠️ Manual deploy required

Merging alone does not ship the backend half:
- `make migrate` — migrations **0055, 0056, 0057**
- `make deploy-poll` (or `make deploy`) — poller/ssrf changes (`_shared/poller.ts`, `_shared/ssrf.ts`)

The client changes are independent of the backend ones (no new RPC/shape dependencies), so auto-deploying the frontend before the manual backend deploy is safe in both directions.

## Found but NOT fixed (reported for a decision)

- **Auth-transition purge gate opens early** (`useUserCacheScope`): during an in-tab uid→uid switch there is a window where the old user's state store/outbox are live under the new JWT (guardrail #8). Needs a gating rework, not a spot fix.
- **Two same-user tabs overwrite each other's persisted outbox** (whole-blob localStorage writes, no cross-tab merge) — offline writes from a closed tab can be lost.
- **Hydration paging assumes PostgREST serves exactly 1000 rows** (`ITEM_STATE_PAGE`); a lower `db-max-rows` would truncate hydration and mass-drop local state. Config-conditional.
- **Grouped `limit` semantics differ between `MockDataSource` and `SupabaseDataSource`** (latent contract mismatch; no current caller hits it).
- **Allowlist/admin gates key on unverified JWT email** — exploitable only if email confirmation is off in the project's auth config.
- **Direct PostgREST reads of `items` expose `full_content_html`/`ai_summary` to any subscriber** — already acknowledged as accepted in 0025/0035 comments; fixing means the `feeds`-style revoke+column-grant treatment, which could break old cached clients (guardrail #11).
- **`vault.decrypted_secrets` reads in the 0012/0053/0054 triggers sit outside their exception handlers** — an unreadable vault would break signups/pin writes despite the stated fail-open intent (config-dependent).
- **`admin_set_user_blocked` doesn't revoke live sessions** — a blocked user keeps working until their JWT expires (~1h).
- Pre-existing: `deno check` fails on `_shared/redditImages.ts` / `_shared/sanitize.ts` (CI only gates `ssrf.ts`).

author: hyperpolymath
body:
Follow-up to #67. The e2e workflow has been red on `main` for weeks — first at compile (`--warnings-as-errors`), which #67 fixed; with compile green, the `runtime-api` job then failed on `{:error, {:no_plugin, "zig"}}` from tests that were never meant to run there. Two pre-existing defects, both fixed at source:

## 1. Tag taxonomy — download tests ran in PR CI despite the exclusion

The live-download tests carried **both** `@tag :external_api` and `@tag :live_download`. ExUnit's `--include` re-includes tests dropped by `--exclude`, so

```
mix test --include external_api --exclude live_download
```

ran the ~10–50MB download tests that `e2e.yml`'s own header reserves for manual dispatch. They now carry only `:live_download` (run manually via `--include live_download`), matching the taxonomy defined at the top of the test file.

## 2. Plugin search path — `Manager.install` couldn't resolve plugins from a checkout

`@plugin_search_dirs` was a **module attribute**, so `:code.priv_dir(:opsm)` was frozen at *compile* time, pointing inside whatever `_build` compiled the module — its own comment said "resolved at runtime", an intent that never held. Result: `runtime/core/*.ncl` plugins were unreachable from any repo checkout (this also breaks the `opsm runtime install` dogfooding path that reads `opsm.toml [runtime]`).

Search dirs are now computed per call, with repo-checkout fallbacks (`cwd/../runtime/core` under mix, `cwd/runtime/core` as escript) and a fail-safe guard on `:code.priv_dir/1`. `find_plugin_ncl/1` is `@doc false` public with unit tests covering checkout resolution.

Also hardened: `System.cmd("nickel", …)` raises `ErlangError :enoent` when nickel isn't installed — now returns `{:error, {:nickel_not_installed, tool}}`.

## Verified (OTP 28.3.1 / Elixir 1.19.5)

- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` — green
- `mix test test/opsm/runtime/manager_test.exs` — 17/17 (2 new `find_plugin_ncl` tests)
- The exact `runtime-api` CI command — **9 tests, 0 failures, 6 excluded**, live against ziglang.org / go.dev / nodejs.org; both previously-failing tests correctly excluded

Note: the branch was restarted from `main` after #67's squash-merge (the old remote branch was auto-deleted on merge), so this PR contains only the follow-up commit.

author: jhowtkd
body:
## ⚡ Bolt: Throttle Waveform Mousemove Event

### 💡 What
Implemented requestAnimationFrame throttling for the mousemove event handler in the Waveform component. Extracted the `clientX` property synchronously to avoid accessing stale event data from React's event pool, and properly cancel pending animation frames when requesting a new one or upon unmounting the component.

### 🎯 Why
High-frequency UI events like mousemove cause severe performance bottlenecks when performing synchronous layout calculations (like `getBoundingClientRect()`), leading to main-thread blocking and layout thrashing.

### 📊 Impact
**Expected improvement:** Prevents main-thread blocking during rapid mouse movements over the waveform.

**Metrics:**
- Before: Synchronous DOM measurements and state updates on every `mousemove` event tick.
- After: State updates and DOM measurements batched efficiently to the browser's refresh rate (~60fps).
- Improvement: Elimination of layout thrashing and smoother UI responsiveness during hover interactions.

### 🔬 Measurement
1. Open the application and navigate to an audio item with a waveform.
2. Open Chrome DevTools -> Performance tab.
3. Start recording and move the mouse rapidly back and forth across the waveform.
4. Stop recording and verify that event handling is batched to animation frames, without long tasks blocking the main thread.

### 🧪 Testing
- [x] All tests pass

author: pal-tamas
body:
Follow-up to #302. I investigated the "value-returning `InvokeAsync<T>` read is occasionally unreliable" note and found it was mis-attributed.

**The read is fine.** A bridge trace shows the read's result marshals back correctly — `jsResult id:5 success:true result:"hello-native"` — and on a passing run the handler updates the DOM (`#demo-status` → `Read: hello-native`).

**The real flake is one level down: the native full-HTML re-render.** On a complex guide page, `Raw`/CodeSample content defeats the trusted diff, so `Auto` mode falls back to a **full-HTML render** for the update. The native full-HTML morph then occasionally drops content — the morph races the frame's scoped-JS invokes (a component's `OnRendered`/`OnUnmount` hooks, e.g. `Rask.GuideChrome.stop`) and the in-dispatch render-coalescing budget, and an element (`#demo-status`) can vanish.

So it's a native full-render robustness issue in the morph + concurrent-frame-invoke + coalescing pipeline — not an interop bug. This PR just reframes the `docs/native.md` follow-up accordingly (docs-only). The native E2E already proves the #302 fixes via the surgical-diff paths (element-ref focus, history/Todos); hardening the full-HTML re-render of heavy pages is the next native task.

author: korjavin
body:
Closes bd `med-he3`. **The bug.** `web/static/index.html` is shared between bot mode and the cloud origin. Bot mode sends `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`; the cloud origin sends `style-src 'self'` (`internal/cloudserver/router.go:155`). So the six literal `style="…"` attributes in the HTML were refused on every cloud page load. Runtime `.style.foo=` setters do **not** trigger `style-src` — the console noise was entirely static attributes. **The fix.** Five were `display:none` and one was a static margin/font/color. - The five could **not** become the `hidden` utility class: `.hidden` is `display: none !important`, and `workout/groups.js`, `workout/variants.js` and `health.js` reveal these elements with `.style.display = 'block'`, which cannot beat `!important`. Their initial hidden state moves into `styles.css` as plain id/class rules instead. - The `

` at 1615 reuses the existing `.hint` class. CSP is not weakened — this page holds the in-memory DEK and `docs/cloud-crypto.md` rates on-origin XSS as catastrophic. **Regression guard.** `architecture.design-tokens.test.js` walked only `web/static/js`, so its inline-style scan never looked at `index.html` (where the offenders lived) or at `web/cloud/js` at all. Two new scans close that: served HTML (`web/static/index.html`, `web/cloud/*.html`) and `web/cloud/js`. Verified the HTML guard fails when an attribute is re-added. Full frontend suite green (3046 passed).

author: elberteplinio
body:
Adds the cookie-gated `grok.web` provider: PickGauge reads Grok's real weekly usage (the shared "Weekly SuperGrok Limit") from `GET grok.com/rest/grok/credits` using the opt-in managed browser profile, and gives Grok a distinct tray/float accent. Ollama's existing web scrape is untouched; both services' web rows now inherit the plan detail from their zero-setup sibling.

Refs #26 (PR 3 of the 4-PR plan; PR 4 = headless `usage --json` + skill remains).

**Endpoint provenance:** discovered from grok.com's own JS bundles (proto descriptors for `grok_api_v2.GetGrokCreditsConfig` embed the `google.api.http` annotation `/rest/grok/credits`); response shape is the proto3-JSON of `GrokCreditsConfig` (`creditUsagePercent`, `productUsage[]{product, usagePercent}`, `currentPeriod.billingPeriodEnd`). Verified live that the route exists and is cookie-session-gated (CLI bearer → Connect NOT_FOUND; same bearer works on `/rest/subscriptions`).

**What changed**
- Sidecar: grok allowlisted with pinned URLs only (`grok.com/` for browser passes, `/rest/grok/credits` for the cookie HTTP fast path); credits JSON parsed inside the sidecar; sanitized `products` array added to the response contract; absent `creditUsagePercent` = 0 used; HTML body/401/403 → `logged_out`; missing `config` → `unexpected_ui`. Cookies and raw bodies never leave the sidecar.
- Rust: `UsageProviderId::GrokWeb` (`grok.web`), fail-closed registration + headless override (the ollama pattern), grok managed browser profile (`grokPath`), login flow, weekly-only window (no 5h slot anywhere).
- Merge: web-source snapshots now prefer percentages > parsed > newest, and the chosen row inherits `plan`/`billingPeriodEnd` from siblings — grok.web keeps grok.cli's plan, ollama.web keeps ollama.local's plan.
- Distinct Grok accent: tray `[156,163,175]` neutral gray, float `var(--muted)` (was Claude's ember — flagged in #28).
- Frontend: grok web actions (refresh/login/official page) when web readings are on; weekly gauge card; Grok Build segment shown as a detail; Settings profile path row.
- Docs: README privacy/web sections, parser contract doc, UNRELEASED.md.

**Tested**
- `cargo test --locked --all-targets`: 261 passed, 1 ignored.
- `bun run check` clean; `bun run test`: 66 Vitest + 21 sidecar Node tests (new grok cases: happy path, absent-percent, missing-config, HTML body, 401/403).

**Not tested yet**
- Live cookie flow (no grok.com session exists on this machine by design — tokens/cookies are user-owned). The owner's one-tap "connect web session" is the remaining manual validation; failure modes degrade to `logged_out`/`unexpected_ui`, never wrong numbers.

**Risks**
- `rest/grok/credits` is an undocumented surface; shape drift → honest `unexpected_ui`.
- The on-demand $ credits bucket is deliberately not read (out of scope per #26).

author: forktrucka
body:
## What & why

`BoseCloudServer` is an unauthenticated fake-Bose-cloud HTTP server that LAN
speakers call to resolve TuneIn stations. The station-id path segment was
interpolated raw and unencoded into five outbound/reflected URLs and fields
in `_resolveTuneIn`, letting any LAN client inject extra query params
(`123&render=xml`) or path segments into requests the plugin makes to
radiotime.com, and reflect junk into the JSON response.

This adds a strict `STATION_ID_PATTERN` (letter-type prefix + digits, e.g.
`s24939`, matching real preset ids) enforced with a 400 rejection before
`_resolveTuneIn` runs, plus `encodeURIComponent` at all five interpolation
points as defense in depth. Bind address and XML handling are unchanged (XML
layer already confirmed safe — xml2js escapes by default, sax doesn't
resolve external entities).

Delivers `.claude/plans/2026-07-10-bose-cloud-server-hardening.md` in full.

- `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` — all green (338 tests)
- `npm run build` — clean

## 概要

「①出す → ②検証・改善 → ③育てる」を人手最小で回し続ける自動アプリ工場（App Factory）。
1年後に全アプリ合計で月5〜10万円が目標。

- 全体設計: `docs/app-factory.md`
- Before/After 概要: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/dacc0ef1-5643-40dc-9f43-0afdc73f9a6b

## 変更内容

### 新プラグイン `app-factory` — ライフサイクル全スキルを集約

**新規4本**: portfolio-review（計測→KPI判定→週報）/ factory-build（issue自律実装・条件付きauto-merge）/ store-release（release-train issue による24h拒否権付きApp Store提出）/ growth-advisor（多軸グロース提案）

**移動+強化5本**（`~/.claude/skills` と dev-workflow-tools から集約、直接編集で運用）:
- **app-idea-hunt**: JTBD 分析（ジョブ分解・人気の因果・日本への移転可能性）、KPI の具体的数値目標（根拠必須）、**モック/トンマナページ生成**（prd-vault の showcase サイト = Next.js→Vercel、PRD と同じ PR でレビュー、一覧ページがカタログになる）
- **app-kickoff**: 計測実装 issue の MVP 必須化、**docs/architecture.md / docs/test-strategy.md のキックオフ時書き切り**（以後の無人実装のブレ防止）
- **xcode-cloud-setup / feature-hunt / quality-release-cycle**: パス参照をプラグイン内に修正して移動

### ship-issue の「無人モード」明文化（dev-workflow-tools）

プランモードは使わず、**計画を issue コメント（🤖 実装計画:）+ PR 本文に記録してから実装**。計画→実装の順序は維持し、承認ゲートだけを外す。factory-build はこの契約に加えアーキテクチャ文書への整合を必須とし、逸脱 issue は `needs-clarification` で人間へ。

### 定期実行テンプレート（`plugins/app-factory/cron/`、深夜帯中心）

平日 3:00 dispatch（割当表で1日1リポジトリ）/ 毎日 5:00・23:00 factory-build / 毎日 6:00 store-release（bash 事前判定）/ 金 17:00 portfolio-review。`install.sh --migrate` で旧ジョブを置き換え。ホームスキルからの移行手順は `cron/README.md`。

### 公開リポジトリ対策

- シークレットスキャン実施（webhook 実URL・キー・トークン: 検出なし）
- Apple Team ID をテンプレートから除去 → `.env` の `APPLE_TEAM_ID` から注入
- `__pycache__` / `.DS_Store` 除去 + `.gitignore` 追加

## テスト

- 全 cron スクリプト `bash -n` green / plist 4本 `plutil -lint` OK
- 最終シークレットスキャン green

## 導入手順（マージ後）

author: lsuarez-ekline
body:
## What

`ContextTracker._handle_result` logs the turn's token metrics from `ResultMessage.usage`, which is the cumulative usage for the **orchestrator agent only**. On a turn that spawns subagents (the `Task`/Agent tool), the subagent tokens are billed but missing from the trace, so the logged totals under-count — often heavily.

This prefers the token counts from `ResultMessage.model_usage` (the per-model breakdown, which is per-agent and includes subagent calls), summed across models, for the logged metrics. Metadata (service tier, inference geo) still comes from `usage`. When `model_usage` is missing or unusable it falls back to `usage`, so single-agent turns and older SDKs are unchanged.

Fixes #564.

## Details

- New helper `_aggregate_model_usage()` sums `model_usage` into an Anthropic-usage-shaped dict, then reuses `extract_anthropic_usage` for the metric mapping — so cache-read / cache-creation / completion all flow through the same path as before.
- Single-agent turns are unaffected (`usage == model_usage`).
- A model that only ever runs as a subagent has no dedicated LLM span; its tokens now land on the turn's LLM span via the aggregate, so the trace's token total matches the SDK's `model_usage`.

## Testing

- `nox -s "test_claude_agent_sdk(latest)"` — 50 passed (existing suite + 2 new unit tests for `_aggregate_model_usage`).
- `ruff format` / `ruff check` clean.

## Notes

Alternative considered: attribute tokens onto per-subagent spans instead of aggregating onto the turn's LLM span. Happy to take that direction if you'd prefer — this PR takes the minimal approach that makes the trace-level token total correct.

author: wingedguardian
body:
## What

First stage of the ambient session-awareness layer (WS-C): the system that watches what a session is *about* and — in later PRs — volunteers relevant memories the per-prompt keyword lane misses. PR1 is **record-only**: no worker spawn, no injection, no output change.

New package \`src/genesis/session_awareness/\` (pure functions, no clocks, zero DB/Qdrant access):
- **accumulator.py** — EMA (α=0.25) over genuine user-prompt embeddings, renormalized each fold. Outlier-skip guard: a vector at cosine < 0.05 vs the current EMA (cross-backend/off-family response) is counted and skipped, never folded. Dimension changes are absorbed by the same branch. Decaying entity ledger (prompt keywords ×1.0, file keywords ×0.3, decay 0.9/turn, alias-normalized); file paths never touch the EMA.
- **trigger.py** — pure \`check_fire\`: theme must exist ≥3 turns, be stable (min pairwise cosine ≥0.90 across the last-3 EMA ring), sit ≥0.35 from every previously fired region, respect a 3-turn cooldown, ≤3 fires/session, and honor a pending-worker claim with a 120s stale override. Every "no" returns its reason for shadow logs and the replay harness.
- **statefiles.py** — \`~/.genesis/sessions/<id>/session_theme.json\`: traversal-guarded, atomic mkstemp→replace, corrupt/stale (>24h) degrades to empty, saves never raise.
- **hook_api.py** — \`hook_fold\`: the one fail-open entry point the hook calls.

Hook integration (\`scripts/proactive_memory_hook.py\`): \`_ambient_fold\` runs at the very end of \`_run\`, after all stdout flushes AND all existing metrics — deliberately outside the \`total_ms\` window so new work cannot skew the H-1 latency baselines. Skips harness envelopes and embed-less turns. Kill switch: \`GENESIS_SESSION_AWARENESS_DISABLED=1\`. Dispatched sessions never run it (existing \`GENESIS_CC_SESSION\` guard).

## Zero-behavior-change proof

Subprocess integration test (real embedding backend, skipif-gated) runs the hook exactly as CC does, 5 same-theme turns, in two isolated HOMEs: **stdout is byte-identical enabled vs disabled, turn by turn**. The enabled home accumulates \`session_theme.json\` (theme settles → one fire recorded); the disabled home writes nothing. Envelope prompts don't fold.

## Also fixes: hook tests were touching the production vector store

Both hook subprocess tests pointed \`QDRANT_URL\` at live Qdrant, so every backend-enabled test run had the hook's \`_increment_retrieved\` bumping \`retrieved_count\` on real memory points — quiet pollution of retrieval baselines. Both now use a dead port (also makes stdout deterministic for the byte-identical assertion).

## Measured hot-path cost

Package import 18ms; first fold 48ms (one-time alias YAML load); steady-state fold 0.7ms — all after the final stdout flush, user-invisible.

## Verification

- 41 tests green: accumulator (12), trigger (11), statefiles (8), hook_fold orchestration (4), subprocess integration (2), plus the fixed learning-hook test.
- \`check_subsystem_map.py\` clean — package claimed under ambient-cognition in \`docs/architecture/CURRENT.md\`.
- Deviation from the design doc, on purpose: fires are recorded only in \`session_theme.json\` (already compaction-durable), not double-written into the hook-owned intent trail — one owner per file, fewer failure modes in a hot path.

PR2 (detached worker + ranking + shadow logs), PR3 (arbiter), PR4 (OMI-replay kill criterion) follow.

author: myinisjap
body:
## Problem

WebSocket auth passes the long-lived API token as `?token=` (`ws/client.go#ServeWS`). Query strings are logged by reverse proxies, access logs, and browser history — a durable credential shouldn't travel there.

## Proposal

Ticket pattern:

- `POST /api/v1/ws-ticket` (under normal bearer auth) returns a random, single-use ticket valid ~30s, stored in memory.
- Client connects with `?ticket=...`; `ServeWS` validates and consumes the ticket.
- Keep `?token=` support behind a deprecation window (or a config flag) for existing setups.

Low urgency for single-user self-hosted deployments, but cheap to do and removes the main credential-leak path once people put this behind a reverse proxy.

_Imported from https://github.com/myinisjap/agent-task-editor/issues/51_

### What changed

## Code review agent — PASSED

### Scope reviewed
- `backend/internal/ws/ticket.go` + `ticket_test.go` (ticketStore: issue/consume, TTL, single-use, sweep-on-issue, Hub wrapper methods)
- `backend/internal/api/handlers/ws_ticket.go` + `ws_ticket_test.go` (`POST /api/v1/ws-ticket` handler)
- `backend/internal/api/router.go` (route registration: `/ws-ticket` inside bearer-gated `/api/v1` group; `/ws` remains outside that group but does its own auth via `ServeWS`)
- `backend/internal/ws/client.go` (`ServeWS` auth logic: ticket-first via `hub.ConsumeTicket`, `?token=` deprecated fallback via constant-time compare, `slog.Warn` on fallback use)
- `frontend/src/api/ws.ts` (`WSClient.connect()`: fetches ticket via bearer-authed POST before opening the WS URL with `?ticket=`, falls through gracefully on fetch failure so existing reconnect loop still works)
- `openapi.yaml`, `docs/websocket.md`, `backend/internal/ws/CLAUDE.md`, `frontend/src/api/CLAUDE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — all updated consistently and accurately describe the new flow, including the deprecated fallback.

### Verification performed
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (no new formatting issues), `go test ./...` — all pass.
- `npm run build` (tsc + vite) — passes, no type errors.
- Manually traced the full auth path end-to-end: frontend mints ticket via bearer header → `ServeWS` consumes it via `hub.ConsumeTicket` → single-use enforced (delete-on-lookup regardless of validity) → deprecated `?token=` fallback still works and logs a warning → `/ws-ticket` correctly bearer-gated (not reachable without holding the token).
- Confirmed no regression: `/ws` route itself was already outside bearer middleware pre-change (correctly, since browsers can't set Authorization headers on WS handshakes) and still performs its own auth check inline.

### Findings
- **Low**: No existing (pre- or post-change) Go test exercises `ServeWS`'s HTTP-level auth branch end-to-end (e.g. spinning up an httptest server and asserting 401 vs 101 for valid/invalid/expired ticket and token). This is a pre-existing test gap (no `client_test.go` existed before this change either), not a regression introduced by this task. The ticketStore and handler logic that this branch depends on are well covered by unit tests. Non-blocking.
- **Low** (already noted by prior testing agent, re-confirmed): `frontend/src/api/types.ts` (generated from `openapi.yaml`) is stale and missing the new `/ws-ticket` path — it isn't imported anywhere in `frontend/src` so this is dead generated-artifact drift, not a functional issue. Worth a follow-up `npm run gen:api` commit.

No medium/high/critical issues found. Implementation is correct, complete, matches the issue's proposal (ticket-based auth with 30s single-use tickets, `?token=` deprecated fallback retained with logging), and is well documented.


### Commits

- WS auth: move token out of the query string (ticket-based auth) (safety-net commit)

author: pradeepmouli
body:
## Summary
- TypeScript 7 shipped as the stable `typescript` package (`7.0.2`) — the Go-native compiler this repo already ran via the `@typescript/native-preview` dev-snapshot (`tsgo`) is now `typescript`'s own `tsc` binary. Bumped every workspace package's `typescript` devDependency from `^6.0.3` to `^7.0.2`, dropped the now-redundant `@typescript/native-preview` devDependency, and renamed every `tsgo`-invoking script (`type-check`, plus `codegen`'s and `design-system`'s `build`) to `tsc`.
- **Verified the native compiler is genuinely what `tsc` runs in 7.0.2** (a reviewer flagged this as worth confirming, not just asserting — good catch): `typescript@7.0.2` declares per-platform `optionalDependencies` (`@typescript/typescript-darwin-arm64`, `@typescript/typescript-linux-x64`, etc.), `bin/tsc` resolves the current platform's package via `lib/getExePath.js` and execs its `lib/tsc` binary, and on this machine that file is confirmed via `file`: `Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64` (23.6MB) — the same native binary `@typescript/native-preview`'s `tsgo` resolved, just named `tsc` under the `typescript` package. Not a JS reimplementation, not a staged/preview-only feature behind a flag.
- TS7 restructured the package: the classic synchronous Compiler API (`createProgram`/`getPreEmitDiagnostics`/etc.) is no longer the default export — it moved to a new, explicitly-`unstable/sync` RPC-style API (spawn/connect to the native process, `Snapshot`/`Project`/`Program`/`Checker` objects, requires disposal). Six oracle tests under `packages/codegen/test/emit/` use the classic API to compile+typecheck the codegen's own generated `.ts` output as a self-verification step. Rather than depend on the unstable surface (or lose that coverage), they now import a scoped `typescript-classic` alias (`npm:typescript@6.0.3`, `packages/codegen`-only) instead of the workspace-wide `typescript`.
- No CI workflow or `.vscode/settings.json` changes needed — CI only ever calls `pnpm run type-check`/`pnpm run build:ci`, never `tsgo` directly, and there's no `typescript.tsdk` pin.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm run type-check` — all 18 workspace projects pass under `tsc` (TS7 native)
- [x] `pnpm run build:ci` — real `tsc -b`/`tsc -p` emit succeeds (design-system, codegen), no tsc errors
- [x] `pnpm run test` — 3700+ tests pass across every package, including the 6 repointed oracle tests in `packages/codegen`
- [x] `pnpm peers check` — one non-blocking peer mismatch flagged: `typedoc@0.28.19` doesn't yet declare TS7 support (no stable typedoc release does); `docs` is excluded from `build:ci`, so this doesn't gate CI
- [x] Confirmed the installed `tsc` binary is the native compiler (`file` → Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64 on darwin-arm64), resolved via `typescript@7.0.2`'s per-platform `optionalDependencies`, not a JS fallback

body:
## Link por cliente (link mágico assinado) ⭐

Dá ao cliente do cardápio uma **identidade persistente sem senha** — o item marcado como alta prioridade para retomar ao fim da revisão de menus.

> **Requer a migration `071_cliente_cardapio.sql` no Supabase.** *(Nota: já aplicada em produção no dev — idempotente.)*

### Como funciona
- **Identidade "link mágico"**: o cliente informa o telefone → o servidor gera um **token HMAC assinado** (`cliente-token.ts`), guardado no navegador. Os endpoints públicos validam a assinatura **e o tenant** (não vale em outra loja). Reidentificar o mesmo telefone **não duplica** (único por tenant+telefone).
- **Endereços salvos** (CRUD + principal), usados no checkout ("usar este endereço").
- **Histórico** dos pedidos + **"pedir de novo"** (reconstrói o carrinho a partir do snapshot do pedido — `produtoId/variação/qtd`; complementos pagos o servidor recalcula).
- **LGPD**: consentimento no cadastro + **"esquecer meus dados"** (apaga cliente/endereços e desvincula os pedidos).

### Implementação
- **Backend** módulo `cliente` (público sob `/publico/cardapio/:token/cliente`): identificar, perfil, endereços, esquecer, pedir-de-novo. `receberPedido` associa `pedido_externo.cliente_id` quando o `clienteToken` vem no pedido.
- **Front**: `ClientePanel` (loja) — entrar, endereços, histórico, reordenar, esquecer; botão **"Entrar / Meus dados"** no cabeçalho; `clienteToken` guardado por cardápio e enviado no pedido.

### Testes (smoke backend)
```
identificar (telefone novo) → clienteToken assinado
reidentificar mesmo telefone → acha, não duplica (nome/tel preservados)
endereço → principal automático no 1º
perfil → nome + endereços + histórico
token adulterado → 401
esquecer → 201, acesso revogado (perfil 401)
```
Builds verdes nos dois lados. **Requer migration 071.**

Addresses a logical desynchronization bug in the timetable generation algorithm. 

During the 'Ultimate Fallback' phase, the algorithm previously nullified the `teacher` reference to forcefully place lessons into available classroom slots, causing critical data loss. Furthermore, it failed to update scheduling caches after these forced placements, resulting in overlapping lessons (collisions). 

This patch removes the dangerous nullification of the teacher property and ensures `_addToCache` is immediately invoked when a lesson is temporally placed, maintaining robust internal state synchronization and adhering strictly to data preservation principles.

author: xerhab
body:
Makes the phone side of the glasses app match the mobile web UI: a login page identical to the web dashboard's, then the **real dashboard embedded in an iframe**. The glasses keep rendering via the SDK in parallel (navigating the WebView away would blank them, so the dashboard is embedded, not navigated to).

### Login
- Matches `agent-hub/public/login.html` (branded card, palette, dark mode, inline errors); collects only username + password.
- **Hub URL hardcoded** to `agents.xerktech.com` (`config.ts` `DEFAULT_HUB_URL`/`resolveHubUrl`; `VITE_HUB_URL` overrides for dev; stored URLs ignored).
- Sign-in POSTs `/api/login` (credentials included) exactly like the web login — validating the password **and** planting the session cookie the iframe rides — then persists the Basic creds (the glasses app polls with Basic) and reloads.

### Embedded dashboard
- Signed-in view is a full-bleed iframe of the hub dashboard + a Sign out bar. `main.ts` tags `<body>` `backend-bridge` (device → iframe) vs `backend-dom` (`npm run dev` → the green-text glasses mirror).
- **Hub cookie change:** the `hub_session` cookie is now `SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned` over HTTPS (was `Lax`, which browsers drop in a cross-site iframe). Partitioned/CHIPS keys it to the embedding top-level site, so it works even where third-party cookies are blocked and is never shared with other embedders — no broad cross-site widening. Plain HTTP (LAN/dev) stays `Lax`.

### Known risk (acknowledged)
The embed relies on the WebView honoring the partitioned cookie. If the Even Hub WebView blocks it, the iframe falls back to showing the hub's own login page (still usable). Verified the hub sends no `X-Frame-Options`/CSP `frame-ancestors`, so framing itself is allowed.

### Verification
215 glasses tests (login-flow: view toggle, cookie-refresh on load, offline fallback, 401 vs network, sign-out) + 74 hub tests (new: HTTPS cookie is None/Secure/Partitioned) pass; `tsc --noEmit` + `vite build` clean; iframe-of-hub and login page both confirmed rendering in a browser (screenshots in session).

Those agents' current prompt mode refuses these flags, so a run failed before the agent even started.

Dropping the two flags lets prompt runs reach the Kimi and Qwen agents again.

## Review Claim

Approve dropping the `--yolo` and `--prompt` flags from how Invoker routes prompt runs to the Kimi and Qwen agents.

## Review Lane

behavior

## Review Unit

routing

## Safety Invariant

Change is limited to two execution agents' argument builders and their unit tests. No shared runtime, gating, or persistence path is touched, so a reviewer can confirm correctness from the four-file diff alone.

## Slice Rationale

This slice only changes how prompts route to the Kimi and Qwen agents. It stays isolated from the wider needs-attention effort so the agent fix is easy to approve on its own.

## Non-goals

Does not change the OpenAI or Claude execution agents. Does not change the needs-attention inspector UI. Does not alter approval or worker lifecycle behavior.

author: mgh3326
body:
## Summary

Fixes the two crosswalk defects from the 2026-07-10 crypto retro (ROB-802) and adds the post-hoc manual-fill ingestion path (ROB-801). Base: `robin` (= `robin-v0.3.5-r6`).

### ROB-802 — crosswalk fail-closed
- `validate_order_approval_crosswalk` no longer degrades to an unfiltered approval dump when a `ticket_id` / `broker_order_id` / `approval_receipt_id` filter matches nothing. The old `elif ticket_ids:` fallback was the root cause of the 27-unrelated-approvals incident.
- Broker-order lookup failure → fail-closed payload: `status: "error"`, `success: false`, `error: "broker_order_lookup_failed"`, `failure_reason`, `rows: []`, `terminal_inference_allowed: false`.
- Filtered lookup with no match → `status: "no_match"`, `no_match: true`, `no_match_reasons`, `rows: []` (never unrelated approvals).
- `VOIDED` added to lineage terminal states; a VOIDED ticket with no replacement, no `superseded_by_ticket_id`, and no manual-execution link raises the `voided_without_successor` anomaly (DOT canary case).

### ROB-801 — unattributed fill ingestion (evidence-based, post-hoc only)
- `sync_broker_account` scans `adapter.get_fills()` per account and exposes fills with no canonical ticket as an explicit `unattributed_fills` list (silent no-op removed); fills persist as `unattributed_fill` `PortfolioLedgerEvent` rows (hash-deduped). Fill-endpoint failures surface as explicit warnings.
- New MCP tools:
  - `list_unattributed_fills` (read; head-manager / portfolio-manager / risk-manager / execution-operator, safe-home read scope)
  - `annotate_manual_execution` (write; head-manager / execution-operator) — links an unattributed fill to an existing **VOIDED** ticket only, requires non-empty `evidence`, and hard-rejects on symbol/side/currency mismatch, unknown fill, non-VOID ticket, or duplicate link.
- A linked fill becomes a `manual_execution` node in `replacement_lineage` (with `provenance: "manual"`), which resolves the `voided_without_successor` anomaly. No canonical `Fill`/`BrokerOrder` rows are fabricated — manual executions are never disguised as canonical; realized amounts (`gross_notional`, `fee`, `net_amount`, optional `realized_pnl` given `cost_basis_price`) come from broker fill data.
- `FillDTO` gains optional `symbol`/`side` fields for the evidence match.

### resting_lifecycle (r6) consistency
- Panel continues to exclude `VOIDED` tickets (`PANEL_TICKET_STATES` unchanged) and passes the extended lineage shape (`manual_executions`) through; covered by a dedicated test.

## Tests
- `tests/test_manual_fill_lineage.py` (new, 8 tests, written TDD red→green):
  - ROB-802 regression 3-case set: lookup failure fail-closed / no-match empty rows / `voided_without_successor`
  - sync exposes + dedupes unattributed fills; fill-lookup failure becomes a warning
  - annotate links a VOID ticket, resolves the anomaly, keeps manual provenance, computes realized amounts; rejection matrix (no evidence, unknown fill, non-VOID, symbol mismatch, duplicate)
  - resting lifecycle panel consistency
- Full suite: 143 passed (`uv run --with pip --with 'pytest>=8' pytest tests/`).

author: gesellc90
body:
Der aufgeschobene Folge-PR zum Review: hebt die Dev-/Test-Toolchain auf aktuelle Majors und behebt damit die 5 verbliebenen `npm audit`-Schwachstellen (esbuild, vite, vitest, @vitest/coverage-v8). Betrifft ausschließlich Dev-/Build-Abhängigkeiten — kein Produktions-Runtime-Code, kein API-Verhalten.

## Upgrades
- **backend**: `vitest` & `@vitest/coverage-v8` → `^4.1.10`
- **frontend**: `vite` → `^8.1.4`, `vitest` → `^4.1.10`, `@vitejs/plugin-react` → `^6.0.3`, `jsdom` → `^29`, `@testing-library/{jest-dom,react,user-event}` auf aktuelle Versionen
- **root `engines`**: `node >=20.19.0` (Mindestanforderung von vite 8 / plugin-react 6)

## Nötige Anpassungen durch die Majors
- **`@testing-library/jest-dom` → 6.9**: Voraussetzung für vitest-4-Kompatibilität (6.4 konnte das `vitest`-Paket nicht mehr auflösen).
- **Coverage-Baseline gesenkt** (Backend-Gate: Stmts/Lines 78, Branches 70): `@vitest/coverage-v8` v4 misst per AST-Remapping strenger → ~8 Punkte niedriger bei **identischen** Tests. Reine Mess-Änderung, keine echte Regression.

## Node-Verträglichkeit
vite 8 / plugin-react 6 verlangen Node `^20.19 || >=22.12`, vitest 4 ab Node 20. Die CI nutzt `setup-node@20` (neuestes 20.x ≥ 20.19), der **Pi-Runtime nutzt kein vite** (läuft `node dist/server.js` + statische Assets). Kein Node-Bump in CI/Prod nötig.

## Residuum
`npm audit`: **5 → 1**. Verbleibt eine **low-severity** esbuild-Meldung (arbitrary file read, nur **Dev-Server auf Windows**), via `tsx` und `vite` auf esbuild 0.27.7 gepinnt. Bewusst **kein** Override auf esbuild 0.28 — das würde das gesamte Build-Toolchain riskieren, während der Angriffsvektor hier (Linux-CI, Pi ohne esbuild, kein Windows-Dev-Server) nicht greift. Dependabot meldet einen sauberen Fix, sobald vite/tsx nachziehen.

## Verifikation
- Backend: **268 Tests** + Coverage-Gate grün (vitest 4)
- Frontend: **91 Tests** grün (vitest 4 + jsdom 29)
- vite-8-Build & `vite preview` funktionieren (standalone verifiziert)
- Lint & Typecheck sauber

E2E-Specs und Playwright sind unverändert; das lokale Ausführen der E2E ist in der Sandbox durch das Server-Spawning blockiert — die **CI liefert die E2E-Endbestätigung** (nur vites Preview-Server ist neu und läuft nachweislich).
